parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 25
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=25|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] announces that they have recaptured [[Sowdari District|Sodri]], [[North Kordofan]]. [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/sudan-army-announces-capture-of-sodari-area-in-north-kordofan (Radio Tamazuj)]
***Two civilians are killed in a [[drone strike]] by [[Rapid Support Forces]] in [[El Obeid]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/319268 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[Sudanese refugee crisis]]
***The [[United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees]] reports a sharp increase in refugees fleeing from [[Sudan]] to [[Chad]] in a effort to escape the civil war and dire conditions, with 400 people a day crossing eastern Chad. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/number-sudanese-fleeing-chad-surges-20-fold-aid-runs-dry-un-says-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]], [[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reports that [[United States president]] [[Donald Trump]] has rejected [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]]'s proposal to reopen the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and halt regional fighting within seven days in exchange for easing [[United States sanctions against Iran|U.S. sanctions]] and releasing [[Iranian frozen assets|Iranian frozen funds]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/allies-unite-behind-saudi-arabia-houthis-step-up-attacks-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]], [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] and missile strikes on residential buildings and other civilian sites in [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]], kill seven people, including a 14-year-old boy, and injure 46 others. [https://www.news.com.au/breaking-news/daytime-russian-attacks-kill-seven-in-kyiv/news-story/0e54173b829569bb9c750c436505de26 (AFP via News.com.au)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Piracy off the coast of Somalia]], [[Anti-piracy measures in Somalia|Anti-piracy measures]]
***The [[Puntland Maritime Police Force]] successfully frees the [[oil tanker]] ''Sibu 1'' following a multi-day counter-piracy operation near [[Garacad]], [[Mudug]], [[Puntland]], after it was seized by [[Piracy off the coast of Somalia|Somali pirates]] in August. [https://www.idilnews.com/degdeg-ciidanka-badda-puntland-oo-soo-furtay-markabka-mtt-sibu1/ (''Idil News'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/us-sanctioned-oil-tanker-sibu-1-rescued-somali-pirates-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war]]
**[[Pakistan]] says that [[Pakistani Armed Forces|its military]] has killed 13 [[Afghan Armed Forces|Afghan security forces]] during [[shootouts]] at [[Durand Line|the border]]. [[Afghanistan]]'s [[Government of Afghanistan|government]] denies the claim. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/25/pakistani-forces-kill-afghan-taliban-fighters-in-border-escalation (Al Jazeera)] [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-afghanistan-overnight-border-fighting-southwest-787f857b24c3737c1cdfbabc2086657e (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Gambling in Brazil]]
**[[Brazilian president]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] issues a [[provisional measure]] banning [[online betting]] in [[Brazil]], immediately halting new deposits. Users may withdraw remaining funds until October 5, and [[Brazilian National Congress|Congress]] must approve the measure within 120 days for it to remain in force. The ban occurs just days before the [[2026 Brazilian general election]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260925-lula-bans-sports-betting-days-ahead-of-brazil-s-election (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c914ddj21rzlo (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|military]]-leased [[Let L-410 Turbolet|Let L-410]] carrying 17 people, including two generals, crashes near [[Kenge, Kwango|Kenge]], [[Kwango]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], while on route to [[Kinshasa]], killing all passengers. [https://www.aa.com.tr/fr/afrique/rdc-17-morts-dans-le-crash-d-un-avion/4069936 (AA)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-military-plane-crash-kills-13-including-three-officers-official-says-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)]
*At least eight people are killed and 12 others are injured when a bus overturns on a road near [[Iraquara]], [[Bahia]], [[Brazil]]. [https://g1.globo.com/ba/bahia/noticia/2026/09/26/acidente-com-onibus-deixa-mortos-e-feridos-na-bahia.ghtml (G1)]
*Six people are killed and two others are found injured after a suspected [[gas leak]] causes an explosion and collapses a two-storey building in [[Plaka]], [[Athens]], [[Greece]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260925-six-missing-after-building-blast-in-historic-athens-district (AFP via France 24)] [https://apnews.com/article/greece-explosion-athens-plaka-acropolis-f5b20571f39d635832dde89b792f01d5 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6p3kk78l4l1o (BBC News)]
*Two people are killed and 13 more injured in a fire at a residential building in [[Lucca]], [[Tuscany]], [[Italy]]. [https://www.ansa.it/english/newswire/english_service/2026/09/25/two-killed-in-blaze-in-lucca-children-among-13-injured_f4cdcec7-7bfc-478f-8e2b-a102348f831a.html (ANSA)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023–2026 mpox epidemic]]
**A laboratory-confirmed [[mpox]] case from a 21-year-old woman is reported in [[Bunia]], [[Ituri Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/mpox-case-confirmed-northeastern-congolese-city-center-ebola-outbreak-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Mary Jane Veloso drug smuggling case]]
**Mary Jane Veloso is released from [[Correctional Institution for Women (Mandaluyong)|a prison]] in [[Mandaluyong]], [[Philippines]], after [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]]'s absolute [[pardon]] of her was approved yesterday. [https://www.arabnews.com/world/philippines-pardons-death-row-inmate-mary-jane-veloso-after-16-years-behind-bars-3003118 (''Arab News'')] [https://www.rappler.com/philippines/overseas-filipinos/mary-jane-veloso-released-detention-september-25-2026/ (Rappler)]
*A [[Judiciary of France|court]] in [[Paris]], [[France]], sentences Loik Le Priol to 26 years in prison and Romain Bouvier to 19 years for [[Murder in French law|murdering]] former [[Rugby union in Argentina|Argentine rugby union]] player [[Federico Martín Aramburú]] in 2022. Le Priol and Bouvier had links to the dissolved [[Far-right politics in France|far-right]] group [[Groupe Union Défense]]. [https://apnews.com/article/aramburu-rugby-killing-paris-796a8a4b3e5032340f36807ef27e3a12 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c639mm1mrv94o (BBC News)]
*[[Sri Lanka]]'s [[Parliament of Sri Lanka|parliament]] approves a [[Constitution of Sri Lanka|constitutional]] [[Constitutional amendment|amendment]] extending the terms of [[Judiciary of Sri Lanka|senior judges]] by two years as part of efforts to reduce an estimated 1.1 million-case backlog. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lankas-parliament-approves-constitutional-amendment-extend-judge-terms-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Asian Games]]
**[[China at the 2026 Asian Games]], [[Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games]]
***In [[Competitive swimming|swimming]], [[China]]'s [[Zhang Zhanshuo]] becomes the first athlete to win seven gold medals at a single [[Asian Games]], securing his seventh title in the [[Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games – Men's 400 metre freestyle|men's 400-metre freestyle]] with a [[List of Asian Games records in swimming|Games-record]] time of 3:41.28. [https://www.afp.com/en/chinas-zhang-wins-record-seventh-asian-games-swimming-gold (AFP)]
*In [[association football]], an independent [[Premier League]] commission finds [[Manchester City F.C.]] guilty of 114 of 115 alleged [[UEFA Financial Fair Play Regulations|financial-rule]] breaches spanning the [[2009–10 Manchester City F.C. season|2009–10]] to [[2022–23 Manchester City F.C. season|2022–23 seasons]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/25/sport/manchester-city-charges-premier-league (CNN)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 24
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=24|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]], [[France–Saudi Arabia relations]]
***[[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]]
****[[2026 Yemen offensives]]
*****[[France]] announces that it will deploy [[French Armed Forces|its soldiers]] and [[Anti-aircraft warfare|air defense systems]] to [[Yanbu]], [[Saudi Arabia]], to support the [[Saudi Arabian Armed Forces|Saudi military]] against the [[Houthis]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/cia-did-not-warn-france-about-possible-russian-drone-attacks-macron-says-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] and [[Shin Bet]] say that they have killed [[Hamas]]'s chief financial officer in the [[Khan Younis]] area of the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/433578 (''Israel National News'')] [https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/israel-news/2602708/hamas-finance-chief-idf-says-muhammad-abu-alwan-killed-in-khan-younis-strike.html (''The Yeshiva World'')]
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**[[2026 Ethiopian offensive]]
***[[Fano (militia)|Fano fighters]] launch several attacks in the [[Amhara Region]]. [[Shootout]]s with the [[Ethiopian National Defense Force]] are ongoing, causing several casualties, while a [[colonel]] is captured. [https://africa.dailynewsegypt.com/ethiopian-army-colonel-reportedly-captured-by-fano-forces/ (''Daily News Egypt'')]
*[[2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s [[Pakistan Armed Forces|military]] launches ten [[Airstrike|air strikes]] on [[Afghan military]] sites, claiming they were used to store and launch drones. At least four people are killed in the strikes. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-afghanistan-border-fighting-66402ffe6fc48608ea4c32a099774c4c/ (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[beatification]] ceremony for the late [[American Catholic]] [[prelate]] and [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Rochester|Rochester Archbishop]] [[Fulton J. Sheen]] is held at [[The Dome at America's Center]] in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]], [[United States]]. [https://www.bastillepost.com/global/article/6188152-famed-radio-and-tv-priest-fulton-sheen-is-beatified-in-st-louis-putting-him-a-step-from-sainthood (''Bastille Post'')] [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/church/news/2026-09/cardinal-tagle-homily-beatification-mass-fulton-sheen-missionary.html (''Vatican News'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war fuel crisis]]
***The [[European Commission]] reports that the average [[Diesel fuel|diesel]] price across the [[European Union]] reaches a record [[Euro|€]]2.23 ([[US$]]2.54) per litre, up from €2.16 ($2.46) the previous week. Nineteen [[Member state of the European Union|member states]] record new highs. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/general/3325430/average-eu-diesel-price-hits-record223-euros-a-litre-afp-analysis (AFP via ''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[Economic D-Day]], [[United States sanctions against Iran]]
***The Emirati [[General Civil Aviation Authority]] announces the suspension of all flights between [[Iran]] and the [[United Arab Emirates]] amidst [[Economic D-Day|new]] [[U.S. sanctions]] until further notice. [https://gulfnews.com/business/aviation/uae-suspends-all-iranian-airline-flights-until-further-notice-1.500686774 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[Economic impact of the Gaza war]]
**[[UN Trade and Development]] reports that [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] is experiencing the most severe [[economic crisis]] on record, with 92% of [[Economy of the Gaza Strip|economic]] establishments damaged or destroyed, daily [[per capita GDP]] at US$0.58, and unemployment exceeding 90% among working-age residents. [https://www.afp.com/en/gaza-suffers-worlds-worst-ever-economic-crisis-un (AFP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least nine people are killed and many others are injured after a [[sleeper bus]] catches fire on the [[Yamuna Expressway]] in [[Greater Noida]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://www.deccanherald.com/india/uttar-pradesh/9-killed-as-sleeper-bus-catches-fire-on-yamuna-expressway-in-greater-noida-newsalert-4157568 (''Deccan Herald'')] [https://www.dw.com/en/india-news-9-killed-after-bus-catches-fire-outside-delhi/live-79405879 (DW)]
*Twelve [[Armed Forces of the Republic of Kazakhstan|Kazakh military]] personnel are killed, three are rescued and two are missing after being swept into the [[Caspian Sea]] during a [[Kazakh Naval Forces|naval]] [[training exercise]] in the [[Mangystau Region]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/nine-kazakh-military-personnel-dead-after-being-washed-out-sea-during-exercises-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Hungary]]'s [[National Food Chain Safety Office|food chain safety office]] confirms the [[European Union]]'s first detection of the [[Invasive species|invasive]] [[spotted lanternfly]] in [[Bács-Kiskun County]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260924-hungary-detects-invasive-spotted-lanternfly-for-first-time-in-eu (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Chromebook procurement scandal]]
**A [[Judiciary of Indonesia|court]] in [[Jakarta]], [[Indonesia]], reduces former [[Ministry of Education and Culture (Indonesia)|education minister]] and [[Gojek]] co-founder [[Nadiem Makarim]]'s prison sentence from 10 to nine years for [[Corruption in Indonesia|corruption]] involving [[Chromebook]] procurement, while lowering [[Restitution and unjust enrichment|restitution]] from [[Indonesian rupiah|Rp]]809 billion ([[US$]]45 million) to Rp548 billion ($30 million). [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-court-reduces-gojek-founders-sentence-9-years-appeal-hearing-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Croatia–Germany relations]], [[Nord Stream pipelines sabotage]]
**A [[Judiciary of Croatia|Croatian court]] approves [[Ukrainians in Germany|Ukrainian national]] Volodymyr Zhuravlov's [[extradition]] to [[Germany]] over his alleged involvement in sabotaging the [[Nord Stream 1]] and [[Nord Stream 2]] [[Natural gas pipeline|pipelines]] in 2022. [https://apnews.com/article/croatia-germany-suspect-nord-stream-explosion-7bf007025930ca0833ad054356a6887b (AP)]
*[[Donald Trump's conflict with the news media]]
**[[News media in the United States|American news]] outlets [[CNN]], [[MS NOW]], and ''[[Politico]]'' regain [[White House press corps|access]] to the [[White House]] after [[U.S. federal judge]] [[Timothy J. Kelly]] temporarily [[Injunction|blocked]] the ban by [[President of the United States|President]] [[Donald Trump]], ruling that the outlets are likely to show that their [[press pass]]es were revoked without adequate [[Due Process Clause|due process]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cqe8ek7608mlo (BBC News)]
*[[Mary Jane Veloso drug smuggling case]]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]] grants an absolute [[pardon]] to Mary Jane Veloso, a former [[overseas Filipino Worker|overseas worker]] in [[Indonesia]] who was arrested for [[drug trafficking]] and [[Capital punishment in Indonesia|sentenced to death]] in 2010, but was later granted a reprieve and [[extradition|extradited]] back to the Philippines. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-president-pardons-drug-convict-mary-jane-veloso-2026-09-25/ (Reuters)] [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2311536/marcos-grants-mary-jane-veloso-absolute-pardon (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[President of Belarus|Belarusian president]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says that he has [[pardon]]ed 15 [[political prisoner]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/belarus-president-lukashenko-pardons-15-prisoners-state-media-says-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Priesthood in the Catholic Church|priest]] is killed and four other people are injured in a [[mass stabbing]] by a [[Ukrainians in Poland|Ukrainian national]] at a [[Benedictines|Benedictine]] abbey in [[Jarosław]], [[Podkarpackie Voivodeship]], [[Poland]]. [https://apnews.com/article/poland-stabbing-convent-jaroslaw-9592a9fc8b97b815d9ee647c0fa7c15f (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/one-dead-four-injured-polish-abbey-knife-attack-local-media-report-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Moroccan general election]]
**[[Morocco]]'s [[Authenticity and Modernity Party]], led by [[Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri]], wins the most seats in yesterday's [[Parliament of Morocco|parliamentary]] election, taking 97 of 395 seats, followed by the ruling [[National Rally of Independents]] with 66 and the [[Istiqlal Party]] with 65, according to preliminary official results. [https://www.reuters.com/world/pam-party-wins-most-seats-moroccos-parliamentary-election-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Hijab and burqa controversies in Europe]], [[Islam in Italy]]
**[[Italy]]'s [[Meloni government|government]] approves a [[Law of Italy|decree]] capping [[Education in Italy|foreign students]] with limited [[Italian language|Italian]] proficiency at 30% per classroom and banning [[burqa]]s and [[niqab]]s in schools. The measure takes effect immediately but requires [[Italian Parliament|parliamentary]] approval within 60 days. [https://apnews.com/article/italy-school-foreign-students-classrooms-veil-migrants-education-3d7cf97f62c8e9a3f8855ef018fc6112 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Asian Games]]
**[[Japan at the 2026 Asian Games]], [[Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games]]
***In [[Competitive swimming|swimming]], [[Japan]]'s [[Shin Ohashi]] wins gold in the [[Swimming at the 2026 Asian Games – Men's 200 metre breaststroke|men's 200-metre breaststroke]] at the 2026 [[Asian Games]] in 2:04.83, breaking [[China]]'s [[Qin Haiyang]]'s 2023 [[200 metres breaststroke|world record]] of 2:05.48 by 0.65 seconds. [https://www.afp.com/en/japan-swimmer-ohashi-17-shrugs-covid-smash-world-record (AFP)]
*[[2026 Major League Baseball season]]
**In [[baseball]], the [[Major League Baseball]]'s [[Chicago White Sox]] clinches the upcoming [[2026 Major League Baseball postseason|playoffs]] for the first time since [[2021 Chicago White Sox season|2021]], following three-straight [[List of worst Major League Baseball season win–loss records|100-loss seasons]]. [https://apnews.com/article/white-sox-royals-score-clinch-25f0e5288dd7165e3a8f94f1185433fd# (AP)]
<!-- All news items above this line -->

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=24|bottom=yes}}

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 23
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=23|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***[[2026 United States naval blockade of Iran]]
****The [[United States Central Command]] says that the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] has redirected 115 [[commercial vessel]]s since the reinstatement of its [[blockade]] on July 14. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/115-iran-linked-ships-redirected-us-naval-blockade-on-iran-continues-1.500685751 (''Gulf News'')]
***An Indian [[Wiper (occupation)|wiper]] is killed during an [[List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war|attack]] on the [[bulk carrier]] MV ''Cape Dao'' near the [[Strait of Hormuz]], with [[Oman]]'s [[Royal Navy of Oman|navy]] confirming that 27 crew members have been evacuated. [https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/one-indian-killed-in-attack-on-ship-heading-toward-india-says-embassy-in-oman-says-3002803 (AFP and Reuters via ''Arab News'')] [https://indianexpress.com/article/world/indian-national-killed-mv-cape-dao-attack-gulf-of-oman-10891112/ (''The Indian Express'')]
**[[Iran]] reopens [[Education in Iran|schools]] and [[Higher education in Iran|universities]] after months of closures caused by the war. About 16.5 million schoolchildren begin the new academic year, with reopening ceremonies held across the country. [https://www.channelstv.com/2026/09/23/iranian-children-back-to-school-after-war-closures/ (AFP via Channels Television)]
**Acting [[United States Navy]] [[United States Secretary of the Navy|secretary]] [[Hung Cao]] reports that eight sailors on the {{USS|Abraham Lincoln|CVN-72|6}} have [[Suicide attempt|attempted suicide]] during its long deployment including during the Iran war. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cr3wj0px283xo (BBC News)]
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**[[2026 Ethiopian offensive]]
***The [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] (TPLF) seizes several airports in [[Tigray Region|Tigray]], while clashes are ongoing in [[Regions of Ethiopia|the nearby regions]] of [[Afar Region|Afar]] and [[Amhara Region|Amhara]]. The TPLF says that it has started a "[[defensive war]]" against the [[federal government of Ethiopia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ethiopian-airlines-suspends-flights-tigray-region-2026-01-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Kharkiv strikes]], [[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]], [[Odesa strikes (2022–present)|Odesa strikes]]
***[[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] and missile attacks across [[Ukraine]] kill at least eight [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|civilians]], including six [[Agriculture in Ukraine|agricultural]] workers in [[Kharkiv Oblast]] and two people in [[Kyiv]], while strikes also hit [[Odesa]]. [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukraine]] says it intercepts or suppresses 119 of 161 drones. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-attacks-un-81b243e8493f4de852da4497e211dadd (AP)]
**[[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Poland]] deploys [[Polish Air Force|fighter jets]] into its [[airspace]] after a [[Russian Air Force|Russian]] helicopter intruded near [[Braniewo]], [[Warmian–Masurian Voivodeship]]. [https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/uk-news/poland-scrambles-military-action-after-34660021 (''Chronicle Live'')]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Threats and attacks by the [[Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada]] (ACSN) bring [[Santa Marta]], [[Magdalena Department]], [[Colombia]], to a standstill, closing businesses and [[Transport in Colombia|public transport]]. The group orders the shutdown after [[Military Forces of Colombia|security forces]] kill 13 ACSN members. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260924-colombians-in-santa-marta-stay-inside-after-violence-wracks-the-city (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/threats-armed-group-bring-colombias-santa-marta-standstill-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Communal conflicts in Nigeria]]
**Fifteen people, including a village head, are killed in an armed [[Demographics of Nigeria|ethnic]] clash in [[Bagudo]], [[Kebbi State]], [[Nigeria]]. Six suspects are arrested following the attack. [https://dailypost.ng/2026/09/22/ethnic-clash-kills-15-in-kebbi-as-residents-flee-homes/ (''Daily Post'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]], [[United States sanctions against Iran]]
**[[List of airlines of Iran|Iranian airlines]] suspend services to [[Azerbaijan]], [[Baghdad]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]], [[Muscat]], and [[Qatar]], after [[Economic D-Day|new]] [[U.S. sanctions]] target Iran's aviation sector. [https://www.afp.com/en/iran-airlines-cancel-flights-us-sanctions-hit (AFP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season#Tropical Storm Fay|Tropical Storm]] [[List of storms named Fay|Fay]] re-emerges as a tropical depression with a sustained wind of 35 mph amidst a unusually quiet [[Atlantic hurricane season]] caused by [[2026–2027 El Niño event|El Niño]]. [https://www.sun-sentinel.com/2026/09/23/tropical-depression-atlantic/ (''Sun Sentinel'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026–2027 El Niño event]]
**The [[Atacama Desert]] in [[Chile]] reports blossoms of flowers amidst the ongoing [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation|El Nino]] event in the [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific]]. [https://phys.org/news/2026-09-chile-atacama-blossoms-life-el.html (Phys.org)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly]]
**[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
***[[Africa–United States relations]]
****The [[United States]] and [[African Union]] hold the first joint Quad-Quintet talks at the [[United Nations General Assembly]] sidelines in a effort to end the [[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|ongoing]] [[civil war]] in [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/319224 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[Belarus–Poland relations]]
***[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Poland)|Polish Foreign Minister]] [[Radosław Sikorski]] and [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Belarus)|Belarusian Foreign Minister]] [[Maxim Ryzhenkov]] meet at the [[United Nations General Assembly]], making it the first meeting between [[Poland]] and [[Belarus]] in a decade. [https://ua.news/en/world/glavi-mzs-polshchi-ta-bilorusi-vpershe-za-desiatilittia-zustrilisia-v-niu-iorku-notes-from-poland (UA News)] [https://notesfrompoland.com/2026/09/23/poland-and-belarus-seek-thaw-in-relations-as-foreign-ministers-meet-for-first-time-in-a-decade/ (Notes from Poland)]
*[[Azerbaijan–France relations]]
**[[President of Azerbaijan|Azerbaijani president]] [[Ilham Aliyev]] pardons a [[France|French]] national who served a 10-year prison sentence for [[espionage]], and orders his release as one of 20 [[pardon]]ed prisoners. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwp84rrrymd0o (BBC News)]
*[[Cross-strait relations]]
**[[Taiwan]]'s [[Coast Guard Administration (Taiwan)|coast guard]] increases patrol capacity around the [[Territorial disputes in the South China Sea|disputed]] [[Pratas Island]] in the [[South China Sea]] by stationing a new 100-tonne [[patrol boat]] and regularly deploying larger vessels, citing increased [[China Coast Guard]] activity near the Taiwan-controlled outpost. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/taiwan-upgrades-maritime-patrol-capacity-vulnerable-south-china-sea-outpost-2026-09-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|North Korean involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[South Korea–Ukraine relations]]
**[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says that [[Ukraine]] transferred two [[North Korea]]n [[Prisoners of war in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|prisoners of war]] to [[South Korea]] after capturing them in [[Kursk Oblast]], [[Russia]], in January 2025. [https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/09/24/korea-Volodymyr-Zelensky-North-Korean-POWs-sent-South-Korea/6371790236408/ (UPI)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Harvey Weinstein sexual abuse cases]]
**A [[Judiciary of New York|court]] in [[New York (state)|New York]], [[United States]], sentences former [[Cinema of the United States|film]] producer [[Harvey Weinstein]] to 15 years in [[Incarceration in the United States|prison]] for committing a [[Rape laws in the United States|criminal sexual act]] against former [[production assistant]] Miriam Haley. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm98626n260yo (BBC News)]
*[[Mexican drug war]], [[missing persons in Mexico]]
**Congresswoman Margarita López Pérez reports that, since 2021, [[Madres buscadoras|Searching Mothers]] have found around 1,600 [[milk teeth]], among other skeletal remains, in a [[mass grave]] in [[Zacapu]], Michoacán. The state prosecutor's office denies having reports on the case. [https://guillermoortega.com/pais/1600-dientes-de-leche-y-ningun-nombre-que-hay-detras-del-hallazgo-en-zacapu (Guillermo Ortega)]
*[[War crimes in the Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|War crimes in the Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Human Rights Watch]] reports that [[Women in Myanmar|women]] held as [[political prisoner]]s in [[Myanmar]] face [[Torture in Myanmar|torture]], [[Wartime sexual violence|sexual violence]], and inadequate [[Health in Myanmar|medical care]]. The group says more than 6,600 women and 640 children are among over 30,000 political prisoners detained since 2021. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmar-female-prisoners-face-torture-neglect-rights-group-says-2026-09-23/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Israeli legislative election]]
**The [[Central Elections Committee]] votes to disqualify [[Ra'am]] and all parties on the [[Joint List]] from running, alleging they promoted terrorism against [[Israel]]. [[Balad (political party)|Balad]] leader [[Sami Abu Shehadeh]] and [[List of members of the twenty-fifth Knesset|MK]] [[Ofer Cassif]] are also specifically barred from running. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/election-panel-votes-to-bar-balad-chief-abu-shehadeh-over-alleged-support-for-terror/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*[[2026 Moroccan general election]]
**[[Moroccans]] vote to elect all 395 members of the [[House of Representatives (Morocco)|House of Representatives]]. [https://apnews.com/article/morocco-parliament-elections-king-boycott-e32311d61692137a196fac6a98afca70 (AP)]
*[[Second impeachment of Sara Duterte]]
**The [[Philippine Senate]], sitting as an [[Impeachment in the Philippines|impeachment court]], rules that only senator-judges able to participate count toward the conviction threshold in [[Vice President of the Philippines|vice president]] [[Sara Duterte]]'s trial, reducing the required votes from 16 to 14. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-senate-lowers-number-votes-needed-convict-vp-sara-duterte-2026-09-23/ (Reuters)]
*The [[United Kingdom]] establishes a [[National Centre for Information Defence]] to detect and counter foreign [[disinformation]], including [[AI-generated content]]. [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Andy Burnham]] says the centre will address [[disinformation attack]]s to states such as [[Russian disinformation|Russia]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260923-uk-sets-up-unit-to-combat-disinformation-from-russia-ai (AFP via France 24)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2026 OpenAI infiltration of Medicare]]
**[[Prime Minister of Australia|Australian prime minister]] [[Anthony Albanese]] says that an [[OpenAI]]-deployed [[AI agent|agent]] accessed public and restricted files on a [[Medicare (Australia)|Medicare]] database during testing in June. OpenAI notified the government in September, while investigations continue into the breach. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260923-australian-pm-says-openai-hacked-government-health-website (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/sep/24/anthony-albanese-says-openai-agent-hacked-medicare-extreme-concern-sam-altman (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Croatia]] joins the [[U.S.]]-led [[Artemis Accords]], becoming the 74th country to do so. [https://www.croatiaweek.com/croatia-signs-artemis-accords-us-space-exploration/ (''Croatia Week'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Asian Games]]
**[[North Korea at the 2026 Asian Games]], [[Weightlifting at the 2026 Asian Games]]
***[[North Korea]]n weightlifter [[Ri Song Gum]] wins gold in the [[Weightlifting at the 2026 Asian Games – Women's 49 kg|women's 49kg]] category at the 2026 [[Asian Games]] while setting three [[List of world records in Olympic weightlifting|world records]]: 94kg in the [[Snatch (weightlifting)|snatch]], 121kg in the [[clean and jerk]], and 215kg overall. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260923-north-korea-weightlifter-sets-three-world-records-for-asian-games-gold (AFP via France 24)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 22
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=22|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**[[2026 Ethiopian offensive]]
***The [[Ethiopian National Defense Force]] launches 21 [[airstrike]]s in [[Alamata]], [[Tigray Region]], killing 14 civilians and wounding 22 more. Two empty schools are also hit. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cry8zwwq21pxo (BBC News)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**[[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]]
****[[Saudi Arabian Armed Forces|Saudi]] [[airstrike]]s against the Houthi-held city of [[Mokha]], [[Yemen]], kills six civilians. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/houthis-saudi-arabia-strike-yemen-key-port-city-6402761 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[President of Colombia|Colombian president]] [[Abelardo de la Espriella]] deploys [[Military Forces of Colombia|troops]] to [[Santa Marta]], [[Magdalena Department]], after members of the [[Conquering Self-Defense Forces of the Sierra Nevada]] (ACSN) attack businesses and burn vehicles following a security operation that killed 13 ACSN members, including a senior commander. [https://www.afp.com/en/colombia-president-orders-troops-violence-hit-caribbean-city (AFP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Silver]] [[Roman currency|Roman coins]] dating back to the [[2nd century]] are discovered by an amateur archaeologist in [[Germany]]. The coins are placed on display at the [[Rheinisches Landesmuseum Bonn]] museum in [[Bonn]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/22/roman-coins-germany-amateur-archaeologist-silver-denarii (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Pacific hurricane season]]
**The [[National Hurricane Center]] reports that [[Hurricane Polo (2026)|Hurricane Polo]] has strengthened into a [[List of Category 5 Pacific hurricanes|category 5]] [[Pacific hurricane]]. [https://www.independent.co.uk/weather/hurricane-polo-mexico-category-5-b3054471.html (''The Independent'')] 
*[[2026 Pacific typhoon season]]
** [[Typhoon Dujuan (2026)|Typhoon Dujuan]] kills at least four people and injures 22 others in [[Japan]], while six remain missing after landslides. More than 45,000 households in [[Chiba Prefecture]] lose [[Electricity sector in Japan|power]], and over 460 homes are damaged. [https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2026/09/23/2003864735 (AFP via ''Taipei Times'')]
*[[Moldova]]'s [[Parliament of Moldova|parliament]] approves a 60-day [[state of emergency]] in the [[Energy in Moldova|energy]] and water sectors as low levels in the [[Dniester]] and [[Prut]] rivers threaten water supplies and global conflicts raise energy costs. [https://apnews.com/article/moldova-energy-europe-emergency-a73f807a2a7c2ccd38258d49ac1fbbd3 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**The [[Atlantic hurricane season]] breaks a 112-year [[List of Atlantic hurricane records|record]] without a hurricane, due to a strong [[2026–2027 El Niño event|El Niño event]] in the [[Pacific Ocean|Pacific]]. [https://www.accuweather.com/en/hurricane/atlantic-goes-without-a-hurricane-through-sept-21-breaking-112-year-record/1932278 (AccuWeather)]
*[[Tunisia]]'s [[National meteorological service|meteorological service]] reports that summer 2026 is [[Climate of Tunisia|the country's hottest]] since records began in 1950, with average temperatures {{convert|2.9|C-change|F-change}} above the previous record and repeated [[heat wave]]s contributing to [[Water supply and sanitation in Tunisia|water shortages]] and [[Energy in Tunisia|power cuts]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/tunisia-says-2026-summer-hottest-record (AFP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] and [[United States special envoy|U.S. envoy]] [[Steve Witkoff]] hold three hours of [[Qatar]]-[[Qatar as a mediator in conflict|mediated]] talks at the [[UN General Assembly]] in [[New York City]], the first contact between [[Iran–United States relations|the countries]] since [[U.S. vice president]] [[JD Vance]] met an [[Government of Iran|Iranian delegation]] in [[Switzerland]] in [[Islamabad Memorandum|June]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/22/iran-us-talks-sidelines-un-summit-trump-israel-us (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Sudan–United States relations]]
***Diplomatic sources and the [[United Nations]] say that the [[United States]] refused to issue [[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese military]] chief and ''[[de facto]]'' [[Transitional Sovereignty Council|leader]] [[Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] a [[Visa policy of the United States|visa]] to attend the UN General Assembly. Sudan asks the UN to intervene. [https://www.afp.com/en/us-refuses-give-sudans-de-facto-leader-visa-un (AFP)]
**[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
***[[President of the United States|United States president]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[Venezuela]]n interim [[President of Venezuela|president]] [[Delcy Rodríguez]] meet on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, marking the first in-person meeting between the countries' leaders following the [[2026 U.S. intervention in Venezuela]] and capture of [[Nicolás Maduro]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260923-trump-met-with-venezuela-s-interim-leader-at-un (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Afghanistan–Turkmenistan relations]]
**[[Afghanistan]] and [[Turkmenistan]] agree to establish a joint commission on road transport and to facilitate transit between the two [[Afghanistan–Turkmenistan border|bordering]] countries. [https://www.trend.az/casia/turkmenistan/4226595.html (Trend News Agency)]
*[[Belgium–Rwanda relations]]
**[[Belgium]] and [[Rwanda]] restore [[diplomatic relations]] 18 months after severing ties over the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict (2022–present)|Democratic Republic of the Congo–Rwanda conflict]]. The countries plan to reopen their embassies following months of meetings [[Qatar as a mediator in conflict|facilitated]] in part by [[Qatar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/belgium-rwanda-resume-diplomatic-relations-after-drc-conflict-dispute-2026-09-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[Greenland crisis]]
**[[Denmark]], [[Greenland]], and the [[United States]] sign an agreement expanding [[U.S. military]] access to Greenland, permitting new defence areas and a [[missile defence system]] while reaffirming Greenland's [[self-determination]] and amending the [[Military in Greenland#Cold War|1951 defence agreement]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/trump-signs-tremendous-greenland-security-deal/a-79381148 (DW)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/trump-denmark-greenland-sign-deal-bid-end-arctic-standoff-2026-09-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in South Africa]]
**Eleven people are killed, including a pregnant woman, and three others are injured after three men open fire at a gathering inside a house in [[KwaMakhutha]] township, [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/crgjqxzl097eo (BBC News)]
**Three men are killed in a shooting in [[Gugulethu]], [[Cape Flats]], South Africa. Police are investigating it as a triple [[homicide]]. [https://www.capetownetc.com/news/three-killed-in-gugulethu-shooting-at-ktc/ (Cape Town ETC)]
*[[2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings]]
**[[Sri Lanka]]'s [[High Court of Sri Lanka|High Court]] convicts 15 men involved in the [[Easter]] bombings in 2019.  [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/9/22/sri-lanka-court-convicts-14-over-deadly-easter-bombings (Al Jazeera)]
* [[2026 Turgutlu school shooting]]
**Eleven people are wounded in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[Secondary school|high school]] in [[Turgutlu]], [[Turkey]]. The perpetrator is arrested. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/22/gunman-wounds-eight-in-shooting-near-high-school-in-western-turkiye (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Human trafficking in Papua New Guinea]]
**[[Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary|Papua New Guinea police]] rescue 39 [[Indonesia]]ns allegedly [[Human trafficking|trafficked]] through [[Employment fraud|false job offers]] and held in [[Port Moresby]]. Officers arrest four [[Chinese people in Papua New Guinea|Chinese nationals]] and investigate possible links to a wider [[Transnational crime|transnational trafficking network]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/papua-new-guinea-police-bust-human-trafficking-ring-rescue-39-indonesians (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*Three lawsuits are filed against the [[Six Flags Magic Mountain]] [[amusement park]] in [[Valencia, California|Valencia]], [[California]], U.S., after 100 riders suffered [[Brain injury|brain injuries]] after riding the [[X2 (roller coaster)|X2]] [[roller coaster]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/23/six-flags-x2-roller-coaster-lawsuit (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.cbsnews.com/losangeles/news/six-flags-x2-roller-coaster-lawsuit/ (CBS Los Angeles)]
*[[Cybercrime]] group [[ShinyHunters]] says it has breached the website of the U.S. [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] (FBI) and stolen personal data on current and former employees, including addresses and [[Social Security number]]s. The FBI investigates the claim. [https://www.reuters.com/world/shinyhunters-hackers-say-they-breached-federal-bureau-investigation-no-immediate-2026-09-22/ (Reuters)]
*At least three people are killed in an after-[[curfew]] ambush in [[Mangu, Nigeria|Mangu]], [[Plateau State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://dailytrust.com/plateau-gunmen-kill-3-vigilantes-despite-curfew/ (''Daily Trust'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*Hundreds of flights are delayed at five [[List of airports in the United States#Primary airports|primary airports]] across [[northeastern United States]], namely [[Newark Liberty International Airport|Newark Liberty]], [[Teterboro Airport|Teterboro]], [[Philadelphia International Airport|Philadelphia]], [[LaGuardia Airport|LaGuardia]], and [[John F. Kennedy International Airport|JFK]], due to technological issues after a construction crew accidentally severed numerous cables, including [[Optical fiber|fiber-optic]] ones used for communication with [[air traffic control]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckvgyzzgvv4wo (BBC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/21/us/northeast-airport-delays-equipment-failure (CNN)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 21
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=21|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**[[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]], [[2026 Yemen offensives]]
***[[Saudi Arabia–United Kingdom relations]]
****[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British prime minister]] [[Andy Burnham]] says that the [[United Kingdom]] will offer [[Saudi Arabia]] [[aerial refueling]] in its ongoing conflict with the [[Houthis]]. [https://thehill.com/homenews/ap/ap-international/ap-uk-to-offer-saudi-arabia-aerial-refueling-to-counter-houthi-attacks/ (''The Hill'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Egypt–Sudan relations]], [[Egypt–United States relations]], [[Sudan–United States relations]]
***[[Senior Advisor to the President of the United States|U.S. senior advisor]] [[Massad Boulos]] says that he has held talks with [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Sudan)|Sudanese foreign minister]] [[Mohi El-Din Salem|Mohieddin Salem]] and [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Egypt)|Egyptian foreign minister]] [[Badr Abdelatty]] at the [[United Nations General Assembly]] [[Eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|meeting]] in an effort to end the three-year long [[civil war]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/egypt-sudan-and-us-officials-discuss-ending-sudan-war-3002461 (''Arab News'')] [https://sudanhorizon.com/trump-envoy-held-productive-talks-with-sudanese-and-egyptian-foreign-ministers/ (''Sudan Horizon'')]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese military]] at night launches heavy airstrikes against [[Rapid Support Forces]] targets in [[Nyala, Sudan|Nyala]], [[South Darfur]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/319114 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***An attack on a [[gold mining]] market in [[North Kordofan]] by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] kills five citizens, including a [[goldsmith]] worker. [https://sudantribune.com/article/319070 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**The [[United Nations]]'s [[International Organization for Migration]] reports that 5 million [[Forced displacement|displaced]] people have decided to return to [[Sudan]] despite the civil war. [https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/over-5m-displaced-sudanese-return-home-un-3002595 (''Arab News'')]
*[[2026 Afghanistan–Pakistan war]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s [[Pakistan Armed Forces|military]] launches strikes over the [[Durand Line|Afghanistan–Pakistan border]] in retaliation for the [[2026 Kohat attack]]. [[Afghanistan]]'s [[Government of Afghanistan|government]] and the [[UNAMA]] report that a family of three was killed in the strikes, while Pakistan says the strikes killed 28 [[Pakistani Taliban]] militants. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/least-three-killed-pakistani-airstrike-afghanistan-tolo-news-reports-2026-09-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]]
**The [[Red Sea International Film Festival]] in [[Saudi Arabia]] is postponed to 2027 due to the [[2026 Yemen offensives|ongoing conflict]] with the [[Houthis]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/lifestyle/saudi-arabias-red-sea-international-film-festival-postponed-until-2027-3002534 (''Arab News'')] [https://gulfnews.com/story/entertainment%2Fred-sea-film-festival-2026-in-december-postponed-due-to-logistical-demands-1.500682342 (''Gulf News'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Ceer Motors]] unveils the EXOBOT SUV and sedan in [[Saudi Arabia]], its first [[electric vehicle]]s in the country. [https://electrek.co/2026/09/21/ceer-unveils-exobot-evs-saudi-arabias-first-electric-vehicles/ (Electrek)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 California wildfires]]
**Two pilots are killed in a helicopter crash while [[Firefighting|fighting]] a [[wildfire]] in [[Yosemite National Park]], [[California]], [[United States]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/two-pilots-die-helicopter-crash-fighting-california-wildfire-2026-09-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**The [[Government of Nepal|Nepalese government]] announces that they are discussing resettling victims of flooding from [[Bhotekoshi Rural Municipality]] to safe places in [[Nepal|the country]]. [https://dailypioneer.com/news/slug-lite/nepal-govt-discusses-safe-resettlement-of-bhotekoshi-flood-victims-minister?year=2026 (''Daily Pioneer'')]
*[[Korean conflict]]
**An explosion injures three [[South Korean military]] officers during an operation inside the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone|Demilitarized Zone]], south of the [[military demarcation line]]. The [[Joint Chiefs of Staff (South Korea)|Joint Chiefs of Staff]] says the cause remains unknown. [https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/21/09/2026/three-south-korean-soldiers-injured-in-dmz-blast-military (AFP via ''The Peninsula'')]
*A helicopter crashes in a mountainous area of [[Urubici]], [[Santa Catarina (state)|Santa Catarina]], [[Brazil]], killing the five occupants, including singer [[Rick Sollo]]. [https://www.metropoles.com/colunas/fabia-oliveira/rick-bombeiros-confirmam-morte-dos-cinco-ocupantes-de-helicoptero-leia (''Metrópoles'' {{small|in Portuguese}})] [https://english.news.cn/20260923/92b6db503534403dbb8c284ce4778d5b/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[New Zealand]]'s [[critically endangered]] [[black robin]] wins [[Forest & Bird]]'s [[Bird of the Year]] competition with more than 26,000 votes out of about 105,000 votes. [https://www.afp.com/en/new-zealanders-pick-endangered-black-robin-bird-year (AFP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Russia–European Union relations]]
**[[List of ambassadors of the European Union|European Union ambassadors]] agree in principle to remove [[Russian oligarchs]] [[Mikhail Fridman]] and [[Alisher Usmanov]] from [[European Union sanctions|sanctions]] imposed over [[Russia]]'s [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|invasion]] of [[Ukraine]], while renewing restrictions on about 3,000 other Russian-linked individuals and [[List of companies of Russia|entities]] for three years. However, [[Latvia]] later blocks the deal. [https://www.billionaires.africa/2026/09/21/billionaire-alisher-usmanov-is-set-to-come-off-eu-sanctions-after-four-years/ (Billionaires.Africa)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/latvian-pm-opposes-deal-lift-sanctions-russia-linked-billionaires-usmanov-2026-09-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2023 Vermont shooting of Palestinian students]]
**Jason Eaton is found guilty for [[Violent incidents in reaction to the Gaza war|shooting]] and critically wounding three [[Palestinans|Palestinian]] students in [[Burlington, Vermont|Burlington]], [[Vermont]], [[United States]], who wore [[Palestinian keffiyeh|keffiyehs]] in solidarity with [[Palestine]] in the wake of the beginning of the [[Gaza war]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/21/vermont-man-guilty-attempted-murder-palestinian-students (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.indystar.com/story/news/crime/2026/09/21/guilty-verdict-jason-eaton-vermont-shooting-palestinian-students-burlington/91877036007/ (''IndyStar'')]
*[[Singapore]]'s [[Land Transport Authority]] introduces [[Fine City|fines]] of up to [[S$]]500 ([[US$]]390) for eating on [[Public buses of Singapore|public buses]] or placing feet on seats, while severe cleanliness or safety violations can incur penalties of up to S$5,000 (US$3,900). [https://www.afp.com/en/propping-feet-bus-seats-carries-400-penalty-fine-city-singapore (AFP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Mexico]]'s [[Secretariat of Public Education]] introduces nationwide rules restricting [[Mobile phone use in schools|cellphone]] and [[One-to-one computing|tablet use]] throughout the school day in [[Education in Mexico#Primary school|public primary and secondary schools]], effective November 3. [[Education in Mexico#High school|High schools]] set their own limits for educational use. [https://www.thestar.com.my/tech/tech-news/2026/09/22/mexico-joins-countries-banning-mobile-phones-in-schools (AFP via ''The Star'')]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=20|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]], [[Qatar as a mediator in conflict]]
***[[Qatar]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Qatar)|foreign ministry]] says that they are working to resume [[ceasefire]] [[2025-2026 Iran-United States negotiations|negotiations]] between [[Iran]] and the [[United States]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/qatar-pushes-revival-us-iran-talks-warns-against-cycles-escalation (''Middle East Eye'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] launch a massive [[drone warfare|drone attack]] on [[Moscow Oblast|Moscow]] [[Oblasts of Russia|Oblast]], [[Russia]], with more than 1,600 long-range drones launched from [[Ukraine]]. At least two people are killed with hundreds more [[emergency evacuation|evacuated]] while [[Moscow Refinery]] is on fire following several direct hits. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/20/mass-ukrainian-drone-attack-on-moscow-kills-two-russia-says (Al Jazeera)]
***[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] confirms he ordered the attack on [[Moscow]] in response to [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] targeting [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|civilians]] in [[Ukrainian cities]], saying that [[FP-5 Flamingo]] [[cruise missile]]s and [[ballistic missile]]s were also used in the attack. [https://www.unionesarda.it/en/world/massive-attack-on-moscow-chaos-at-the-airport-zelensky-quot-cruise-and-ballistic-missiles-were-also-usedquot-tcsco6db (''L'Unione Sarda'')]
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**Seven [[List of rebel groups in Ethiopia|Ethiopian armed groups]], including [[Tigray Defense Forces|Tigrayan forces]], the [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] (TPLF), the [[Fano (militia)|Fano militia]], and the [[Oromo Liberation Army]], form an alliance against [[Federal government of Ethiopia|the federal government]]. The TPLF says the coalition seeks to remove the government and establish a [[transitional administration]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/world/ethiopias-main-armed-groups-announce-alliance-against-government-3002456 (AFP via ''Arab News'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**The [[Statistical Center of Iran]] reports that [[Economy of Iran|the country]]'s [[gross domestic product]] [[Recession|contracted]] 10.1% year-on-year from late March to late June, during the war, amid longstanding [[International sanctions against Iran|sanctions]] and [[currency depreciation]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/irans-economy-contracts-by-more-than-10-during-us-war-official-data-shows (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**The [[National Hurricane Center]] reports that Tropical Depression Six strengthened into [[2026 Atlantic hurricane season#Tropical Storm Fay|Tropical Storm]] [[List of storms named Fay|Fay]] amidst an unusually quiet [[Atlantic hurricane season]] caused by [[2026–2027 El Niño event|El Niño]], becoming the sixth named storm of the season. [https://www.accuweather.com/en/hurricane/tropical-storm-fay-becomes-sixth-named-storm-of-atlantic-hurricane-season/1935940 (AccuWeather)] [https://www.wfla.com/weather/tracking-the-tropics/tropical-storm-fay-forms-in-the-eastern-atlantic-national-hurricane-center/ (WFLA-TV)]
*Eight people are killed and another is injured in a fire at a [[Textile industry in China|textile factory]] in [[Guangdong Province]], [[China]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/textile-factory-fire-southern-chinese-city-of-foshan-kills-8-2026-09-21/ (Reuters)]
*Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured after the explosion of a gas cylinder in [[Ashulia]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260921/70763ecf33cd492e94aa5484c2fbc125/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Six people are killed when a bus plunges about fifteen meters into a ravine in [[Cruzeiro, São Paulo|Cruzeiro]], [[Brazil]]. [https://g1.globo.com/sp/vale-do-paraiba-regiao/noticia/2026/09/20/onibus-cai-em-ribanceira-e-deixa-mortos-em-cruzeiro-sp.ghtml (G1 {{small|in Portuguese}})][https://english.news.cn/20260921/5a2c0b2223b246f0b90d6d1289c05984/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] [[Ebola vaccine|launches]] [[vaccine|vaccinations]] for frontline workers amdist the [[Ebola]] outbreak in the country. [https://www.africanews.com/2026/09/20/congo-launches-ebola-vaccination-campaign-for-frontline-workers/ (Africanews)]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–Iran relations]]
**[[Iran]]ian authorities close down a [[France|French]] language centre affiliated with the [[List of diplomatic missions of France|French embassy]] in [[Tehran]] under a [[Judicial system of the Islamic Republic of Iran|judicial]] order. Prosecutors say it operated without a licence and conducted activities [[Anti-Iranian sentiment|against]] [[Iranian culture]] and national security. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-seals-french-language-centre-tehran-accuses-it-illegal-activities-2026-09-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]], [[Haiti–United States relations]]
**[[Haiti]] sends 18 suspects in the July 2021 [[assassination]] of [[President of Haiti|President]] [[Jovenel Moïse]] to the [[United States]] to face federal charges related to the killing. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/suspects-2021-killing-haitian-president-flown-us-face-trial-2026-09-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Pakistani police]] arrest businesswoman [[Aleema Khan]], sister of [[Arrest of Imran Khan|jailed]] former [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|prime minister]] [[Imran Khan]], at her  home in [[Lahore]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], one week before his [[Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf]] party's planned protest march. Police and [[Second Shehbaz Sharif government|the government]] do not state a reason for the arrest. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/police-arrest-pakistan-ex-pm-imran-khans-sister-lahore-ahead-partys-planned-2026-09-20/ (Reuters)]
*Four unauthorized [[Mining industry of Nigeria|miners]] are killed in a shooting targeting a vehicle by unidentified gunmen in [[Barkin Ladi]], [[Plateau State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://dailypost.ng/2026/09/20/four-dead-as-gunmen-ambush-miners-in-plateau/ (''Daily Post Nigeria'')]
*Three people are killed and another is injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a shack in an [[informal settlement]] in [[Philippi, Western Cape|Philippi]], [[Cape Flats]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.sabcnews.com/sabcnews/manhunt-launched-following-philippi-triple-murder/ (SABC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Mecklenburg-Vorpommern state election]], [[2026 Berlin state election]] 
**State elections are held in [[Germany]] for the [[Landtag of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern]] and the [[Berlin House of Representatives]], with an expected decline for the [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Friedrich Merz]]'s party, the [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|CDU]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvwyz29n0nn2o (BBC News)] 

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Asian Games]]
**[[Japan at the 2026 Asian Games]], [[Triathlon at the 2026 Asian Games]]
***[[Japan]]ese [[Triathlon|triathlete]] {{ill|Takumi Hojo|ja|北條巧}} wins the first [[gold medal]] of the 2026 [[Asian Games]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/japan-win-first-asian-games-gold-chinas-13-year-old-yu-sets-pace (AFP)]
*[[2026 UCI Road World Championships]]
**In [[cycling]], [[Belgium|Belgian]] rider [[Remco Evenepoel]] becomes the first man to win four consecutive [[UCI Road World Championships|Road World Championship]] titles in the [[individual time trial]] event and equals [[Fabian Cancellara]] and [[Tony Martin (cyclist)|Tony Martin]]'s joint record for the most titles. [[Switzerland|Swiss]] rider [[Marlen Reusser]] wins the [[2026 UCI Road World Championships – Women's time trial|women's time trial]] event. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/sep/20/cycling-world-time-trial-marlen-reusser-zoe-backstedt-evenepoel-montreal (AFP via ''The Guardian'')]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=19|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
****[[Supreme National Security Council]] [[Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council|Secretary]] [[Mohsen Rezaee]] says that [[Iran]] has set seven conditions for resuming [[ceasefire]] [[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations|negotiations with the United States]]. [https://www.iranintl.com/en/202609192233 (''Iran International'')]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[United States Central Command]] commander [[Brad Cooper (admiral)|Brad Cooper]] says that oil, cargo, and [[liquefied natural gas]] shipments in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] have hit a six-month high. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-19/hormuz-oil-shipments-hit-six-month-high-us-commander-says (Bloomberg)] [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/us-military-says-strait-hormuz-shipping-volumes-hit-six-month-high (''Middle East Eye'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] [[airstrike]]s kill at least three [[Palestinians]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], including the eldest son of the [[Gaza Health Ministry]] director-general. Israel says it targeted militants, while medics report additional deaths in [[Sheikh Radwan]] and [[Shuja'iyya]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-strikes-kill-three-people-gaza-medics-say-2026-09-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Operation Southern Spear]]
**[[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***The [[U.S. military]] strikes a vessel in the [[Caribbean Sea]], killing four people whom the [[United States Southern Command|Southern Command]] says were involved in [[drug trafficking]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-says-it-killed-four-people-strike-vessel-caribbean-2026-09-20/ (Reuters)]
*[[Philippines and the Islamic State|Islamic State insurgency in the Philippines]]
**A series of clashes, involving combined [[Philippine National Police|police]] and [[Armed Forces of the Philippines|military]] forces and remaining wanted members of the [[Maute Group|Dawlah Islamiya]] and the [[Bangsamoro Islamic Freedom Fighters]], erupts in [[Tugunan]], [[Special Geographic Area]] of the [[Bangsamoro]], [[Philippines]]. Seven members from both groups are killed. [https://www.philstar.com/nation/2026/09/20/2557660/troops-brace-terrorist-retaliation-after-deadly-clashes-barmm (''The Philippine Star'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**Tropical Depression Six forms in the [[Atlantic Ocean]] near the [[Azores]] amidst an unusually quiet [[Atlantic hurricane season]] caused by [[2026–2027 El Niño event|El Niño]]. [https://www.foxweather.com/weather-news/tropical-depression-six-forms-atlantic-el-nino-september-2026.amp (Fox Weather)] [https://www.wtsp.com/article/weather/hurricane/our-sixth-tropical-system-has-formed-in-the-atlantic/67-c1324f82-432a-48f0-9104-29ef73166837 (WTSP)]
*[[2026 Indonesia wildfires]], [[Indonesia–Malaysia relations]]
**[[Indonesia]] accepts [[Malaysia]]n assistance to combat [[wildfire]]s in [[Kalimantan]], including a [[Canadair CL-415|Bombardier CL-415MP]] aircraft, three helicopters, and 52 personnel, as the fires cause [[2026 Southeast Asian haze|transboundary haze]] affecting [[Southeast Asia]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260919-indonesia-accepts-malaysia-s-help-to-tackle-wildfires (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Eritrea–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury|U.S. treasury department]] lifts the [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] against [[Eritrea]]'s [[People's Front for Democracy and Justice|ruling party]] previously imposed by former [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Joe Biden]]'s [[Presidency of Joe Biden|administration]]. [https://apnews.com/article/us-eritrea-sanctions-tigray-houthi-red-sea-c3a4056f2c69b841d97b1bdd8d259716 (AP)]
*[[2026 United Nations Secretary-General selection]]
**Chilean [[Michelle Bachelet]] announces that she is withdrawing from the race to become [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|UN Secretary-General]] after losing support, and that in the latest informal poll, Costa Rica’s [[Rebeca Grynspan]] is reported in the lead. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/chiles-bachelet-withdraws-race-lead-un-2026-09-20/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Domestic violence in South Africa]], [[Sexual violence in South Africa]]
**[[South Africa]]ns hold [[Fun run|memorial run]]s and [[Protests in South Africa|protests]] after [[South African Police Service|police]] find the bodies of nine women in [[Ekurhuleni]], [[Gauteng]], over two months. Police investigate possible links between the killings, which renew public concern over [[violence against women]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/after-deaths-nine-women-south-africans-gather-run-mourn-demand-change-2026-09-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Russian legislative election]]
**[[Central Election Commission (Russia)|Russian election commission]] chairperson [[Ella Pamfilova]] reports [[cyberattack]]s targeting [[Russia]]'s [[online voting]] system during the second day of the [[State Duma|parliamentary]] election and says they are repelled. The [[Minkomsvyaz]] separately reports thwarting a sabotage attempt on [[Russian Far East|Far Eastern]] communication lines. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-19/russia-reports-cyberattacks-during-election/107172738 (ABC News Australia)]
*[[2026 South Ossetian presidential election]]
**[[Marat Kambolov]] is declared the winner of the presidential elections in the partially recognized [[South Ossetia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russia-backed-south-ossetia-elects-leader-close-moscow-2026-09-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Donald Trump's conflict with the news media]]
**[[United States president]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[Executive Office of the President of the United States|executive office]] denies [[White House press corps|journalists]] from [[CNN]], [[MS NOW]], and ''[[Politico]]'' access to the [[White House]] and confiscates or disables their [[press pass]]es, citing their coverage of [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|his administration]]. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/338701/cnn-ms-now-politico-denied-access-to-white-house-grounds (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Asian Games]]
**The 20th [[Asian Games]] are opened by [[Emperor of Japan|Emperor]] [[Naruhito]] in [[Nagoya]], [[Aichi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/asian-games-open-nagoya-after-troubled-buildup-2026-09-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 WNBA season]]
**In [[women's basketball]], [[Atlanta Dream]] player [[Angel Reese]] becomes the first player in [[Women's National Basketball Association]] history to reach 500 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] in a single season. [https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25500900-angel-reese-makes-wnba-history-single-season-rebounding-milestone-during-dream-vs-sky (Bleacher Report)]
*[[2026 World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup]]
**In [[rugby union]], hosts [[Japan national rugby union team|Japan]] win their fourth [[World Rugby Pacific Nations Cup|Pacific Nations Cup]] title after defeating the defending champions [[Fiji national rugby union team|Fiji]] 20–15 in the final at [[Chichibunomiya Rugby Stadium|Chichibunomiya Stadium]] in [[Tokyo]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260919-japan-edge-fiji-to-win-pacific-nations-cup (AFP via RFI)]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=18|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***The [[Islamic Republic News Agency|IRNA]] reports that [[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] has [[List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war|hit]] the [[Togo]]-[[Flag state|flagged]] [[oil tanker]] ''Trend'' as it attempted to pass the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/world/2026/09/18/iran-says-struck-oil-tanker-in-strait-of-hormuz (AFP via ''FMT'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/9/18/iran-war-live-trump-weighs-big-decision-on-iran-tanker-hit-in-hormuz (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[2026 Kohat attack]]
***A [[Suicide attack|suicide]] [[car bomb]]ing outside a mosque located inside a police station in [[Kohat District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]], kills at least 31 people, including 16 policemen, and injures at least 100 more. The [[Hafiz Gul Bahadur Group]] claims responsibility. [https://www.afp.com/en/death-toll-attack-police-hq-pakistan-rises-31 (AFP)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2026 Mali offensives]]
***At least 100 [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian soldiers]] are reported to have been killed in a attack on the [[Dioura]] central army base in [[Mali]] over the past weeks. [https://www.arabnews.com/world/death-toll-passes-100-soldiers-in-mali-attack-last-week-sources-3002283 (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] says that they have killed several [[Rapid Support Forces]] militants in [[Sudan]]'s [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] [[States of Sudan|state]]. The country's [[Ministry of Defence (Sudan)|defence ministry]] also confirms the attacks. [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/sudan-army-says-it-killed-rsf-fighters-in-blue-nile (Radio Tamazuj)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war fuel crisis]]
***The [[Bank of Japan]] raises its benchmark [[interest rate]] by 0.25 percentage points to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995, citing [[inflation]] pressures from rising [[Energy in Japan|energy]] costs and a weak [[Japanese yen|yen]], and signals further increases. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260918-bank-of-japan-hikes-rates-to-31-year-high-to-battle-inflation (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Russia]] places the local assets of [[Auchan]] and [[Nestlé]] under temporary administration, transferring their control to [[State-owned enterprises of Russia|Russian firm]] L.E.V. Management, headed by [[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Russia)|interior minister]] [[Vladimir Kolokoltsev]]. The [[Government of Russia|government]] cites the companies' origins in countries it designates as "[[Unfriendly countries list|unfriendly]]" amid broader seizures of foreign-owned businesses. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/18/business/kremlin-seizes-nestle-assets-russia-intl (CNN)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024–2026 Cuba blackouts]]
**Millions of people are left without [[electricity]] in [[Cuba]] as a result of a collapse of the country's energy [[power grid]]. [https://apnews.com/article/cuba-power-outage-0f180c8e414898dbe34875d3d82b8016 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Zealand Pharma]]'s drug Zeydovio receives approval by the [[European Medicines Agency]]'s [[Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use]] to treat [[short bowel syndrome]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/zealand-pharmas-short-bowel-syndrome-drug-wins-backing-eu-panel-2026-09-18/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Denmark–United States relations]]
**[[Greenland crisis]]
***[[Denmark]] and the [[United States]] reach a deal allowing the U.S. to expand [[United States Armed Forces|its military]] presence in [[Greenland]] and granting permanent [[List of American military installations|basing]], [[Flight permit|overflight]], and access rights, while barring non-[[NATO]] countries from establishing bases and restricting sensitive investments on the island. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/us-denmark-close-greenland-deal-sources-say-2026-09-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[United States sanctions against Iran]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] signs the [[Sanctioning Russia Act|Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026]], which authorises and expands statutory sanctions, tariffs, and prohibitions on Russia and [[Iran and Libya Sanctions Act|extends]] existing [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] on [[Iran]] until 2031. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/trump-signs-lindsey-graham-act-extending-iran-sanctions-2031 (''Middle East Eye'')] [https://kyivindependent.com/trump-signs-sweeping-russia-sanctions-bill-into-law/ (''Kyiv Indepedent'')]
*[[Prime Minister of Poland|Polish prime minister]] [[Donald Tusk]] announces that [[Poland]] has joined the [[Anti-Ballistic Missile Coalition]] to develop a joint [[anti-ballistic missile]] [[Missile defense|defence system]] with some other [[Europe]]an countries. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/poland-joins-ukraine-led-anti-ballistic-missile-coalition-announces-tusk-14046939.html (''Firstpost'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[1MDB scandal]]
**[[King of Malaysia|King]] [[Ibrahim Iskandar of Johor|Sultan Ibrahim]] of [[Malaysia]] grants former [[Prime Minister of Malaysia|prime minister]] [[Najib Razak]] a conditional [[pardon]], allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under [[house arrest]] until August 23, 2028, following his [[Corruption in Malaysia|corruption]] conviction linked to [[1MDB]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/malaysia-pardons-board-members-palace-amid-speculation-meeting-najib-clemency-2026-09-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Ceuta migrant crisis]]
**[[Spanish police]] begin moving more than 3,000 [[Immigration to Spain|migrants]] from beaches in [[Ceuta]] to temporary accommodation at [[Port of Ceuta|the port]]. The operation prompts crowding and clashes, with officers firing [[warning shot]]s and several people sustaining injuries. [https://news.az/news/police-begin-moving-migrants-from-ceuta-beaches (News.Az)]
*[[2026 South Cotabato school shooting]]
**Three students, including the perpetrator, are killed ‌and eight others are injured ​in ​a [[Mass shooting|mass]] [[School shooting|shooting]] at a ⁠secondary ​school in ​[[Banga, South Cotabato]], [[Philippines]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/6-students-killed-17-others-injured-in-philippine-high-school-shooting/4060894 (AA)]
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan relations]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s [[Pakistan Medical and Dental Council|medical regulator]] orders [[Afghans in Pakistan#Education and socioeconomic factors|Afghan students]] enrolled in [[Healthcare in Pakistan|medical]] and [[List of dental schools in Pakistan|dental programs]] to leave their [[List of universities in Pakistan|colleges]] and return to [[Afghanistan]]. Dozens challenge the directive in [[Judiciary of Pakistan|court]], while a [[Lahore]] judge temporarily suspends expulsions in [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260918-afghan-medical-students-in-pakistan-hope-court-stops-college-expulsions (AFP via France 24)]
*Protests erupt in [[Minna]], [[Niger State]], [[Nigeria]], after 37 [[Mining industry of Nigeria|miners]] died yesterday in custody of the [[Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps|Security and Civil Defence Corps]] following raids on suspected [[Illegal mining|illegal mines]]. [[List of current state governors in Nigeria|Niger state governor]] [[Mohammed Umar Bago]] imposes a [[curfew]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/nigeria-forces-open-fire-protest-over-deaths-detainees-witnesses-say-2026-09-18/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russia]] designates filmmaker [[Andrey Zvyagintsev]] a [[Russian foreign agent law|foreign agent]], subjecting him to financial restrictions, reporting requirements, and mandatory labels on published material. Zvyagintsev, who [[Russian diaspora|lives abroad]], has [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|criticized]] the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]] and [[President of Russia|president]] [[Vladimir Putin]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/russia-labels-acclaimed-filmmaker-andrey-zvyagintsev-foreign-agent-2026-09-18/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
* [[2026 Russian legislative election]]
** [[Russia]]ns begin voting to elect 450 seats of the [[State Duma]] over a period of three days following [[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Ukrainian attacks]] upon [[Petroleum industry in Russia|oil infrastructure]]. The elections are also held under strict control during the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]], combined with an ongoing crackdown on [[Anti-war protests in Russia (2022–present)|anti-war]] [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|opposition]] and the anti-war party [[Yabloko]] being disqualified from running. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/world/1450225/russians-begin-voting-in-controlled-election-as-war-drags (AFP via RNZ)] [https://apnews.com/article/russia-putin-election-parliament-duma-ukraine-war-a2001537fc104755e071a38217987331 (AP)]
*The [[Senate of Bolivia]] ratifies an agreement to take a [[US$]]1.9 billion loan from the [[International Monetary Fund]] amid a deep [[economic crisis]] in [[Bolivia|the country]], with [[trade unions]] threatening renewed protests in response. [https://apnews.com/article/bolivia-international-monetary-fund-agreement-rodrigo-paz-d5ac4a2558132559e1d544807b89d528 (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Investigation of UFO reports by the United States government]]
**The [[United States Department of Defense|U.S. Defense Department]] releases a sixth batch of [[classified information in the United States|classified files]] related to [[unidentified flying object]]s, including videos of several orbs [[1952 Washington, D.C., UFO incident|flying over Washington, D.C. in 1952]] and orbs flying near [[Tremonton, Utah]], also in 1952. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/videos/cm4glen7dpx9o (BBC News)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/ufo-files-uap-pentagon-6th-release/ (CBC News)]
