parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=17|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israeli government response to the October 7 attacks]]
****Lt. Col. "Aleph", the chief police officer in the [[Southern Command (Israel)|Southern Command]]'s [[Gaza Division]], is dismissed following his role in the failures leading to the [[Hamas]]-led [[October 7 attacks]] on [[Israel]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/chief-intel-officer-of-gaza-division-on-october-7-formally-dismissed-from-the-idf/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] confirm that they have killed a [[Al-Qassam Brigades]] [[Nukhba forces|Nukhba Forces]] commander who took part in the [[October 7 attacks]] in a airstrike and a [[Hamas]] navy officer in another airstrike in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/433325 (''Israel National News'')] [https://www.jfeed.com/news-israel/tlip93 (JFeed)]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[United States war crimes in Iran strikes|US war crimes in Iran strikes]]
****The [[UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission]] finds "reasonable grounds" that the [[United States Armed Forces|United States military]] may have committed [[war crimes]] with attacks on the [[2026 Minab school attack|Minab school]] and [[2026 Lamerd sports hall attack|Lamerd sports hall]] in [[southern Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-mission-finds-grounds-believe-us-committed-war-crimes-iran-tehran-crimes-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]]
****''[[Al Akhbar (Lebanon)|Al-Akhbar]]'' reports that [[Saudi Arabia]] has sent a proposal for [[Oman]] to mediate a two-week [[ceasefire]] with the [[Houthis]]. [https://www.azernews.az/region/264050.html (AzerNews)]
****A [[Yemen]]i resident is reported to be killed by debris from a drone in [[Taif]], [[Mecca Province]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/saudi-arabia/houthi-drone-debris-kills-yemeni-resident-in-saudi-arabias-taif-3002105 (''Arab News'')]
*Aftermath of the [[South Sudanese Civil War]]
**Twenty-six people are killed and 82 more injured during clashes between two rival communities in [[Abyei]], at the border between [[Sudan]] and [[South Sudan]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/9/17/at-least-26-killed-in-clashes-along-sudan-south-sudan-border-region (Al Jazeera)]
*Fifteen civilians are killed during an armed attack by unknown individuals in Madegoua, [[Far North Region (Cameroon)|Far North Region]], [[Cameroon]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/militants-kill-15-overnight-cameroon-raid-village-sources-say-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[France–Mexico relations]]
**The 16th-century [[Codex Azcatitlan]] goes on display in [[Mexico City]] after [[France]] loaned two [[folio]]s nearly two centuries after the [[manuscript]] left [[Mexico|the country]]. Mexico continues seeking the [[codex]]'s permanent [[Repatriation (cultural property)|return]] from France. [https://www.afp.com/en/prized-mexican-relic-returns-loan-two-centuries (AFP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ck980qyy6d2zo (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Seventeen people are killed and two others are injured after a passenger vehicle collided with a truck in [[Inhambane]], [[Mozambique]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260918/2b1ce32658704f7481bf520e32c349a3/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Environmental policy of the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service]] narrows its enforcement of the [[Endangered Species Act of 1973|Endangered Species Act]] by excluding unintentional [[Fauna of the United States|wildlife]] deaths from its definition of prohibited [[Take (hunting)|take]], including foreseeable deaths linked to activities such as [[Fishing industry in the United States|commercial fishing]] and [[History of the lumber industry in the United States|logging]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260917-trump-admin-overhauls-key-protection-for-endangered-species (AFP via France 24)]
*Biologists publish a study in the journal ''[[Current Biology]]'' describing a new species of [[Wildcat|wild cat]] belonging to the genus ''[[Leopardus]]'', commonly called the "[[Tilcayo tiger cat|tilcayo]]", in the [[Bolivian Yungas|Yungas]] [[cloud forest]]s of [[Bolivia]]. This discovery marks the first new cat species in over 100 years. [https://www.doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2026.08.059  (''Cell'')] [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/new-cat-species-identified-bolivia-first-over-century-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*The [[National Institute for Health and Care Excellence]] approves the [[Trastuzumab deruxtecan]] drug for women in [[England]] with [[Metastatic breast cancer|metastatic]] or incurable [[HER2]]-[[breast cancer]] that cannot be removed surgically, making it the first licensed targeted treatment for patients, two years after it was rejected due to its cost effectiveness. [https://news.sky.com/story/life-extending-drug-for-breast-cancer-patients-now-on-nhs-in-england-13588795 (Sky News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/enhertu-breast-cancer-life-extending-drug-b3051691.html (''The Independent'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Eighty-First session of the United Nations General Assembly]], [[Palestine and the United Nations]]
**The [[United Nations General Assembly]] (UNGA) votes 152–3, with four abstentions, to allow [[President of Palestine|Palestinian president]] [[Mahmoud Abbas]] and other senior [[Government of Palestine|Palestinian officials]] to address [[United Nations|UN]] meetings, including the [[General debate of the eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|general debate]] of the eighty-first session of the UNGA, by video for one year after [[Visa policy of the United States|United States visa]] restrictions prevented their travel to [[New York City]], where the [[UN headquarters]] are. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-allows-palestinian-president-again-speak-via-video-after-us-denies-visa-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Serbia relations]]
**[[Serbian president]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] inaugurates a factory for [[Israel|Israeli]]-made [[Military drone|drones]] that will be produced by [[Serbia|the country]]'s [[Krušik (company)|Krušik]] company, with Vučić stating that it will employ 100 people and produce advanced equipment for the [[Serbian military]]. [https://apnews.com/article/serbia-israel-drones-factory-vucic-military-12098645a942e8fef5b58911e37e9fb2 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Human rights in Pakistan]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s [[Supreme Court of Pakistan|Supreme Court]] suspends 17-year [[Prisons in Pakistan|prison]] sentences imposed on human rights lawyer [[Imaan Mazari]] and her husband over [[Anti-Pakistan sentiment|anti-state]] [[social media]] posts, and grants them [[bail]] pending an [[Islamabad High Court]] ruling. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistans-top-court-suspends-sentences-rights-lawyer-mazari-husband-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Malawi Police Service|Malawian police]] rescue a 47-year-old [[British diaspora in Africa|British]] woman after her abduction in [[Blantyre]]. Four suspected kidnappers are killed in a [[shootout]] with officers, while a senior police officer is injured and hospitalized in stable condition. [https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/4-suspects-killed-shootout-police-rescue-kidnapped-british-136551217 (AP via ABC News)]
*Thirty-seven suspected [[Illegal mining|illegal]] [[Mining industry of Nigeria|gold miners]] die in custody of [[Nigeria]]'s [[Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps|civil defence agency]] in [[Minna]], [[Niger State]]. Survivors say [[overcrowding]] and poor ventilation caused breathing difficulties, while an [[National Intelligence Agency (Nigeria)|intelligence]] report links the deaths to those conditions. The government orders an investigation. [https://www.afp.com/en/nigeria-miners-struggled-breathe-cell-37-died-survivors (AFP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
* [[2026 Swedish general election]]
** [[Ulf Kristersson]] announces his resignation as [[Prime Minister of Sweden]] after his [[Conservatism in Sweden|right-wing]] bloc wins 173 seats in the [[Riksdag]], compared to 176 won by the opposition, led by [[Magdalena Andersson]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/17/sweden-prime-minister-to-resign-as-left-wing-bloc-seals-narrow-election-win (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cxr50l3d762po (BBC News)]
*[[Censorship and media control during the Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[Venezuela]] restores access to 17 [[Mass media in Venezuela|news websites]] that were previously [[Censorship in Venezuela|blocked]], including [[EFE]], ''[[El Nacional (Venezuela)|El Nacional]]'', [[NTN24]], and ''[[Semana]]'', as [[Interim government of Delcy Rodríguez|the interim government]] and [[Venezuelan opposition|opposition]] resume [[Negotiations during the Venezuelan crisis|political transition talks]] that include [[Human rights in Venezuela#Press freedom|freedom of expression]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/venezuela-unblocks-some-censored-news-sites-2-1.500678849 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]
*[[Visa policy of Australia]]
**[[Australia]] tightens visa rules for [[International students in Australia|international students]] and [[Working holidays in Australia|working holidaymakers]], restricts visa switching, and increases enforcement against [[Illegal immigration to Australia|overstayers]] as it seeks to reduce [[Immigration to Australia|net overseas migration]] to 225,000 by 2027–28 and ease [[Australian property bubble|pressure on housing]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260917-australia-to-cut-migration-to-fix-housing-crisis-minister (AFP via France 24)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=16|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***Twenty-one people are killed, 45 are injured, and about 100 others are missing after a residential building in [[Gaza City]] collapses after it was previously hit by an [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]]. Twelve children are among the fatalities. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260916-gaza-apartment-block-collapse-leaves-21-dead (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/16/gaza-residential-building-collapses-six-families-reportedly-trapped (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[2026 Americana Music Honors & Awards]]
**The [[Americana Music Honors & Awards]] are held at the [[Ryman Auditorium]] in [[Nashville, Tennessee|Nashville]], [[Tennessee]], [[United States]], with [[Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers|the Heartbreakers]] performing for the first time since lead vocalist [[Tom Petty]]'s death in 2017. [https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/music/news/tom-petty-heartbreakers-reunion-chris-stapleton-b3052046.html (''The Independent'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026–2027 El Niño event]]
**[[Guatemala]] announces [[food aid]] for about 1.2 million families affected by severe [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation|El Niño]]-related drought, which damages crops and livestock across the [[Dry Corridor]]. The programme distributes maize, beans, and rice with [[World Food Programme]] support. [https://www.arabnews.com/world/guatemala-to-provide-food-aid-as-el-nino-causes-severe-drought-3002037 (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*At least 82 people are killed when a [[gold mining|gold mine]] explodes in [[West Kordofan]], [[Sudan]], an area [[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|under control]] of the [[Rapid Support Forces]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/9/16/gold-mine-collapse-kills-at-least-70-people-in-sudans-west-kordofan (Al Jazeera)] [https://news.sky.com/story/gold-mine-collapse-kills-82-people-in-war-torn-sudan-dozens-more-feared-dead-13588822 (Sky News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 United Kingdom heatwaves]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] records its second-best [[butterfly]] season in 16 years amidst record [[heat wave|heat waves]] in the country. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/big-butterfly-count-statistics-uk-heatwave-b3050959.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Fiji]] declares [[HIV]] a national crisis after reporting 2,016 new diagnoses in 2025, sixteen times the 2019 total. The government estimates that one in 60 adults lives with HIV and expands [[Diagnosis of HIV/AIDS|testing]], [[Prevention of HIV/AIDS|prevention]], and [[Management of HIV/AIDS|treatment]] services. [https://www.nst.com.my/amp/world/world/2026/09/1534679/fiji-declares-national-hiv-crisis (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]
*In a study published by the ''[[Nature Medicine]]'' [[Medical journal|journal]], scientists report that the PANXEON blood test helps detect [[pancreatic cancer]] at early stages and treat the disease before it [[Metastasis|spreads]]. [https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/blood-test-shows-promise-in-detecting-pancreatic-cancer-early-a-holy-grail-for-the-field/ (''Scientific American'')] [https://www.discovermagazine.com/new-blood-test-could-catch-pancreatic-cancer-at-its-earliest-stages-helping-fight-the-silent-killer-49684 (''Discover'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Canada–European Union relations]]
**[[European Commission]] [[President of the European Commission|president]] [[Ursula von der Leyen]] invites [[Canada]] to become the first associate member of the [[European Union]] amidst the [[2025–2026 Canada–United States trade war|ongoing trade war]] between [[Canada–United States relations|Canada and the United States]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/canada-eu-associate-member-von-der-leyen.html (CNBC)]
*[[International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] passes a [[Bipartisanship in United States politics|bipartisan]] [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] bill that imposes [[Sanctioning Russia Act|sanctions on Russia]]'s [[Energy in Russia|energy]] revenues, [[Banking in Russia|financial institutions]], [[Government of Russia|officials]], and [[Russian shadow fleet|shadow fleet]], while authorizing [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs]] of up to 100% on major buyers of [[Russian oil]] and [[Natural gas in Russia|gas]]. The bill will head to [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]]'s desk for his signature for it to become [[Law of the United States|law]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/us-house-approves-grahams-russia-sanctions-bill/ (''Kyiv Independent'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-house-passes-sanctions-tariff-bill-raise-economic-pressure-russia-2026-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*The first summit between [[South Korea]] and the five countries of [[Central Asia]] is held in [[Seoul]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/16/silk-road-spirit-meets-supply-chains-at-korea-central-asia-summit (Euronews)] [https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/foreignaffairs/20260916/1st-multilateral-summit-elevates-korea-central-asia-cooperation-to-leaders-level (AFP via ''Korea Times'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/15/south-korea-embraces-central-asian-leaders-looking-to-boost-regional-clout (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[Inter-Korean Liaison Office bombing]]
***[[Seoul Central District Court|A district court]] in [[Seoul]], [[South Korea]], orders [[North Korea]] to pay [[South Korean won|KRW]]{{nbsp}}44.6 billion ([[US$]]32.5 million) in [[damages]] for destroying the [[Inter-Korean Liaison Office]] in [[Kaesong Industrial Region|Kaesong]] in 2020, in South Korea's first damages lawsuit against North Korea. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/court-orders-north-korea-pay-south-korea-blowing-up-office-6387841 (AFP via CNA)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/south-korean-court-orders-north-korea-pay-damages-over-2020-liaison-office-2026-09-16/ (Reuters)]
*[[Human rights in Macau]]
**[[Macau]] begins its first closed-door [[Macau National Security Law|national security trial]] against former [[Legislative Assembly of Macau|legislator]] [[Au Kam San]], who faces charges including [[Inciting subversion of state power|subversion of state power]] and alleged ties with foreign groups and media outlets. He faces up to 25 years in prison. [https://today.rtl.lu/news/world/macau-holds-first-closed-door-national-security-trial-1011972339 (AFP via RTL Today)]
*[[War crimes in the Kosovo War]]
**The [[Kosovo Specialist Chambers]] sentences former [[Prime Minister of Kosovo|prime minister]] [[Hashim Thaçi]] to 25 years in prison after convicting him on charges of murder, torture, cruel treatment and [[arbitrary detention]] committed during the [[Kosovo War]]. [https://apnews.com/article/thaci-kosovo-serbia-war-crimes-0b24b81d6e1ca8f01d8b8b54bb465ee9 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election]]
**The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Commission on Elections (Philippines)|Commission on Elections]] proclaims all 78 elected members of the [[Bangsamoro Parliament]], with four parties given all seats for party representation. The [[Bangsamoro Federalist Party]], earning most of the seats, fails to secure a majority, leading to a [[hung parliament]]. Meanwhile, six sectoral seats are given to the [[United Bangsamoro Justice Party]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/9/15/election-in-philippines-bangsamoro-region-ends-in-hung-parliament (Al Jazeera)] [https://mb.com.ph/2026/09/16/comelec-proclaims-winning-parties-bets-in-barmm-first-parliamentary-polls (''Manila Bulletin'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Astronomers confirm the existence of [[Elias 2-24 b]], the [[List of exoplanet extremes#Planetary characteristics|youngest]] known [[exoplanet]], which is less than one million years old and located approximately 450 light-years from [[Earth]]. The discovery was observed through the [[W.M. Keck Observatory]] in [[Mauna Kea]], [[Hawaii]], U.S., using a [[coronagraph]]. [https://www.space.com/astronomy/exoplanets/scientists-find-youngest-exoplanet-on-record-a-newborn-named-elias (Space.com)]
*[[NASA]]'s [[Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter|Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter]] discovers a recently formed [[Lunar craters|crater]] on the [[moon]] larger than the [[Colosseum]] in [[Rome]], [[Italy]]. [https://phys.org/news/2026-09-nasa-spacecraft-huge-crater-moon.html (Phys.org)]
*A study published by the ''[[Science Advances]]'' [[Academic journal#Content|scientific journal]] find that the [[Tyrannosaurus]] had a temperature of {{convert|97|F|C}}. [https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/t-rex-was-as-warm-blooded-as-humans-new-study-finds/ (''Scientific American'')]

'''Sports'''
*In [[association football]], [[Clearlake Capital]] buys out [[Todd Boehly]] and [[Mark Walter]]'s stakes to gain full control of [[Premier League]] club [[Chelsea FC|Chelsea]]. The deal is valued at around [[British pound|£]]950 million ([[Euro|€]]1.1 billion) for the 25% share. Chelsea is now worth about £5 billion (€5.8 billion). [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvrl6egl1254o (BBC Sport)] [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/17/boehly-and-walter-sell-chelsea-shares-as-clearlake-capital-takes-full-control-of-club (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49960706/chelsea-clarlake-capital-todd-boehly-mark-walter-ownership (ESPN)]
*The [[Women's Tennis Association]] (WTA) announces that [[WTA Finals|its finals]] will move from [[Riyadh]], [[Saudi Arabia]], to the [[Spectrum Center]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina|Charlotte]], [[North Carolina]], [[United States]], for three years beginning in 2027. The WTA also relocates its global headquarters from [[St. Petersburg, Florida|St. Petersburg]], [[Florida]], to Charlotte. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/tennis/articles/cmly495rnkq7o (BBC)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=15|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Oman]]'s maritime security centre reports that two sailors are reported to be missing after the [[Panama]]-[[Flag state|flagged]] [[oil tanker]] ''El Gaia'' was attacked in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] near the [[Musandam Peninsula]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3n07ydqdzlvo (BBC News)]
***[[Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war]]
****The [[Ministry of Electricity, Water and Renewable Energy (Kuwait)|Kuwaiti energy ministry]] reports that [[Kuwait]]'s [[electrical grid]] has held despite attacks from [[Iran]] against it. [https://www.arabtimesonline.com/news/kuwaits-grid-holds-despite-iran-attacks-record-summer-heat/ (''Arab Times Kuwait'')] 
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]] 
****The [[United Nations]] reports that more than 100,000 people have fled their homes in western and southern [[Yemen]] due to the ongoing [[Houthis|Houthi]] offensive against [[Yemeni Armed Forces|Yemeni government forces]], and that 2,400 [[refugee]]s have arrived in [[Djibouti]] in the last four days alone. [https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/939615/yemen-fighting-displaces-more-than-100000-un-says (Kurdistan 24)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A drone crosses from [[Belarus]]ian [[airspace]] into [[Lithuania]] before being shot down by a [[NATO]] fighter jet over the village of [[Pratkūnai|Pratkūnai, Kaišiadorys District Municipality]], near [[Kruonis Pumped Storage Plant]], two days after an unidentified object flew over Lithuanian airspace from Belarus to [[Kaliningrad Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cjx2zgk7edlzo (BBC News)] [https://www.lrt.lt/naujienos/lietuvoje/2/3052578/lrt-is-pratkunu-kaimo-kur-numustas-dronas-teritorija-saugo-karo-policija (LRT)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2026–2027 El Niño event]]
**The [[Panama Canal Authority]] reduces daily ship transits through [[Panama Canal|the canal]] from 36 to 32 as below-average rainfall and a strengthening [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation|El Niño]] lower [[Water supply and sanitation in Panama|water levels]] in reservoirs supplying the waterway. [https://www.dw.com/en/panama-canal-el-nino/a-78453054 (DW)]
*[[Kenya]] announces bans on exports of unprocessed [[gold]] and establishes at least three [[goldsmith|refineries]], seeking to maximize [[Economy of Kenya|its economic value]] by increasing [[Gold extraction|domestic processing]]. [https://nairametrics.com/2026/09/15/kenya-to-ban-unprocessed-gold-exports-plans-three-new-refineries/ (Nairametrics)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Chatsworth Eurocopter AS350 crash]]
**Three people die when a [[telecopter]] operated by [[KNBC]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], [[United States]], crashes while covering a traffic collision in [[Chatsworth, Los Angeles|Chatsworth]]. [https://apnews.com/article/helicopter-crash-los-angeles-7bf9274cd463e4c53b122ff958b0ed9f (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cw4gq0j5jg10o (BBC News)]
*Six people die while 17 others are injured after an Elf truck, with an [[Isabela (province)|Isabela]]–[[Benguet]] route and carrying 27 passengers, plunges into a ravine in [[Bontoc, Mountain Province]], [[Philippines]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2305748/elf-truck-crash-kills-infant-5-others-in-mountain-province/ (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[United Nations]] reports that daily [[Ebola]] cases in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] declined from about 120 to 80, while 10 of 62 affected [[Health zone (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|health zones]] record no new infections for more than 22 days. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/africa/ebola-congo-ourbreak-virus-un-aid-b3050588.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Aging of Japan]]
**[[Japan]]'s [[Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare|health ministry]] reports 107,677 people [[Centenarian|aged 100 or older]], exceeding 100,000 for the first time since records began in 1963. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/16/world/asia-oceania/japan-centenarians-top-100000-for-the-first-time/2426159 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/15/asia/japan-centenarians-population-intl-hnk (CNN)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Denmark–Russia relations]]
**A [[Russian Navy]] warship fires two [[flare]]s at a [[Royal Danish Air Force|Danish military]] helicopter in the [[Baltic Sea]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/15/nato-jets-shoot-down-drone-violating-lithuania-airspace-kaunas (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement]], [[Controversies related to Sheikh Hasina]], [[Capital punishment in Bangladesh]]
**A [[Judiciary of Bangladesh|court]] in [[Bangladesh]] sentences seven [[Awami League]] leaders who were former officials in former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|prime minister]] [[Sheikh Hasina]]'s [[Fifth Hasina ministry|government]] to death ''[[trial in absentia|in absentia]]'' over their role in deadly crackdowns on the [[July Uprising|anti-government protests in 2024]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/bangladesh-court-sentences-7-hasina-allies-to-death/a-79276131 (DW)]
*[[Death of Noah Donohoe]]
**The [[Northern Ireland|Northern Irish]] [[jury]] in the [[inquest]] returns a [[narrative verdict]], criticising the [[Department for Infrastructure (Northern Ireland)|Department for Infrastructure]] for failure to prevent public access to the tunnel Donohoe was found in and the [[Police Service of Northern Ireland|police]] for failures in their investigation. [https://www.rte.ie/news/ulster/2026/0915/1591611-noah-donohoe-inquest/ (RTÉ)]
*[[Femicide in Latin America]], [[Gender inequality in El Salvador]]
**A [[Judiciary of El Salvador|court]] in [[El Salvador]] sentences a man to [[life imprisonment]] for [[femicide|aggravated femicide]] and [[stalking]], the first such sentence for femicide in the country's history. [https://www.dw.com/en/el-salvador-court-hands-down-first-life-sentence-for-femicide/a-79268746 (DW)]
*[[Phillips family disappearances]]
**A [[New Zealand]] inquiry finds that [[New Zealand Police|police]] and [[Oranga Tamariki]] failed to act on warnings that Tom Phillips might abduct his three children and [[Gun law in New Zealand|possessed firearms]], contributing to missed opportunities to prevent or end their nearly four-year disappearance. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260915-new-zealand-agencies-missed-red-flags-in-child-kidnapping-case-inquiry (AFP via France 24)]
*The [[Brazil]]ian [[Public Prosecutor's Office (Brazil)|public prosecutor's office]] files a [[Lawsuit|civil action]] against [[Vale S.A.|Vale]], the world's largest [[iron ore]] [[Refining (metallurgy)|producer]] and one of Brazil's biggest companies, as well as [[Ministry of Mines and Energy (Brazil)|the national mining agency]] and the [[Minas Gerais]] [[Legislative Assembly of Minas Gerais|state governmen]]t. The lawsuit is based on a [[shaft sinking|containment overflow]] of two [[sump (cave)|sump]]s at the Mina de Viga site in [[Congonhas]] in January, which caused the site to be shut down. [https://www.miningreporters.com/noticia/news/2026/01/brazil-orders-vale-viga-mine-shut-erosion-water-overflow-minas-gerais (Mining Reports)] [https://www.riotimesonline.com/vale-mina-de-viga-public-civil-action-2026/ (''The Rio Times'')] 
*[[China]] implements new travel regulations allowing [[Exit bans in China|exit bans]] on [[Chinese nationality law|citizens]] who violate [[Science and technology in China|technology]] import or [[Export Control Law of the People's Republic of China|export controls]] or commit [[National security|national-security]]-related offences abroad. Returned citizens can face bans lasting six months to three years. [https://www.dawn.com/news/2030095 (AFP via ''Dawn'')]
*Former [[Golden Dawn (Greece)|Golden Dawn]] spokesperson [[Ilias Kasidiaris]] is released from [[List of prisons in Greece|prison]] in [[Domokos]], [[Phthiotis]], [[Greece]], after serving part of a 13-year sentence for leading a [[Greek mafia|criminal organization]] and announces plans to return to [[Politics of Greece|politics]], although he remains barred from office until 2033. [https://www.afp.com/es/node/3839944 (AFP)] [https://www.thenationalherald.com/ilias-kasidiaris-released-from-domokos-prison-after-serving-his-sentence/ (''The National Herald'')]
*[[ProRail]] services across northern and central parts of the [[Netherlands]] are disrupted by a [[Rail sabotage|sabotage]] operation after pipes are attached to tracks, resulting in the failure of [[railway signal]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/suspected-sabotage-disrupts-dutch-trains-level-crossings-2026-09-15/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8ly49w9g1edo (BBC News)] [https://www.politico.eu/article/sabotage-suspected-as-parts-of-dutch-rail-network-come-to-a-standstill/ (''Politico Europe'')]
*[[Agriculture in Romania|Romanian farmers]] clash with [[Gendarmerie (Romania)|gendarmes]] in [[Bucharest]] during protests against [[live export]] restrictions due to [[ovine rinderpest]] and other policies. The confrontations leave 24 people injured, including eight gendarmes, while [[Romanian Police|police]] detain 26 protesters. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260915-protesting-shepherds-farmers-clash-with-romanian-police (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-15/romanian-farmers-clash-with-police-in-anti-eu-protests (Bloomberg)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Reactions to the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[United States House of Representatives|United States representative]] [[Thomas Massie]] files [[Article of impeachment|articles for impeachment]] against [[United States Secretary of Defense|defense secretary]] [[Pete Hegseth]] for allegedly violating the [[War Powers Resolution]] by [[Declaration of war by the United States|declaring war]] against Iran without [[United States Congress|congressional]] approval. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/pete-hegseth-impeachment-vote-update-why-does-thomas-massie-want-trumps-defense-secretary-removed-101789496364430.html (''Hindustan Times'')] [https://www.military.com/republican-lawmaker-forces-house-vote-to-impeach-hegseth-over-iran-war (Military.com)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Asian Games]]
**The [[Italy|Italian]] cruise ship ''[[Costa Serena]]'' docks in [[Nagoya]], [[Japan]], to house about 4,000 [[Asian Games]] athletes and officials as delegations report accommodation problems, including undersized beds, leaking sinks, and room shortages. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260915-asian-games-cruise-ship-arrives-as-accommodation-complaints-grow (AFP via France 24)]
*In [[association football]], [[UEFA]] announces that the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] finals in [[2028 UEFA Champions League final|2028]] and [[2029 UEFA Champions League final|2029]] will be held at the [[Allianz Arena]] in [[Munich]], [[Germany]], and [[Camp Nou]] in [[Barcelona]], [[Spain]], respectively. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/sports/2026/9/15/champions-league-final-venues-revealed-munich-2028-barcelona-2029 (Al Jazeera)]
*The [[World Athletics Championships]] in [[2029 World Athletics Championships|2029]] and [[2031 World Athletics Championships|2031]] are awarded to [[Nairobi]], [[Kenya]], and Munich, Germany, respectively. 2029 will mark the first time the event is held on the continent of [[Africa]]. [https://www.the-star.co.ke/news/world/2026-09-15-how-kenya-won-its-bid-for-2029-world-athletics-championships (''The Star Kenya'')] [https://apnews.com/article/world-athletics-kenya-nairobi-africa-munich-96f9e311ee74ec2c9e153f286b49e3a6 (AP)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=14|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]] 
****[[Houthis|Houthi forces]] seize control of the [[Hanish Islands]] in the [[Red Sea]] consolidating the group's control of the strategic [[sea lane]] off [[Yemen]]'s western coast. [https://apnews.com/article/yemen-houthis-saudi-shipping-mandeb-8c18d82c109a8ea91347ce53c0096c53 (AP)]
****Houthi forces advance towards the [[Presidential Leadership Council|PLC]]-controlled cities of [[Marib]] and [[Taiz]] with heavy clashes underway. [https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed/2026/9/14/yemens-houthis-advance-on-government-strongholds-of-marib-taiz (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Iranian support for the Houthis]]
***[[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf states]] call off planned peace talks with [[Iran]] in response to Houthi [[ballistic missile]] attacks on [[Saudi Arabia]] and [[Yemeni Armed Forces|Yemeni government forces]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/diplomacy-stumbles-with-postponement-meeting-strait-hormuz-proposal-2026-09-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**At least seven suspected gunmen are killed and two others are detained after an armed group attacks [[Nuevo León]] police and [[Mexican Army|soldiers]] in [[General Treviño]], [[Mexico]]. Police later arrest three additional suspects. [https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/15/estados/nuevo-leon-caen-tres-por-enfrentamiento-con-fuerza-civil-en-general-trevino (''La Jornada'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Sudan]]'s [[Popular Congress Party]] and [[Sudan Liberation Movement/Army|Sudan Liberation Movement]] [[Liberated Areas (Sudan)|faction]] led by [[Abdul Wahid al-Nur]] agree to broaden talks aimed at ending the three-year [[civil war]] in the country. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318739 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[78th Primetime Emmy Awards]]
**[[Americans|American]] actress [[Jean Smart]] wins a [[Primetime Emmy Awards|Primetime Emmy Award]] for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series|Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series]] for her role in ''[[Hacks]]'', becoming the first actress to win for every [[Season (television)|season]] of a show. [https://ew.com/jean-smart-wins-comedy-actress-hacks-undefeated-emmys-2026-12115795 (''Entertainment Weekly'')] [https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/jean-smart-hacks-wins-emmy-lead-actress-comedy-1236858177/ (''Variety'')]
**[[Canadian Americans|Canadian–American]] actor [[Michael J. Fox]] wins the [[Bob Hope Humanitarian Award]] for his contributions to [[Research in Parkinson's disease|research]] and advocacy on [[Parkinson's disease]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/michael-j-fox-honored-emmys-parkinsons-advocacy-2026-09-15/ (Reuters)]
**American [[comedy horror]] television series ''[[Widow's Bay]]'' wins 14 Emmys including [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series|Outstanding Comedy Series]], surpassing the record set by ''[[The Studio (TV series)|The Studio]]'' [[77th Primetime Emmy Awards|last year]]. [https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/2026-emmy-best-comedy-winner-widows-bay-sets-emmys-record-1236697070/ (''The Hollywood Reporter'')] [https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/awards/story/2026-09-14/widows-bay-emmys-2026-comedy-series-winner (''Los Angeles Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the Catholic Church]]
**[[Pope]] [[Pope Leo XIV|Leo XIV]] restores salaries for [[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|cardinals]] and senior [[Vatican City]] officials to pre-[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vatican City|COVID-19-pandemic]] levels, ending reductions introduced by [[Pope Francis]] in 2021. The change took effect September 1, 2026, without retroactive compensation. [https://thesun.ng/cardinals-to-earn-full-pay-again-as-pope-leo-xiv-ends-covid-austerity-measure/ (''The Sun'')]
*[[Nigeria]]'s [[Dangote Group]] launches an [[initial public offering]] (IPO) of 4.1 billion shares at [[₦]]525 ([[US$]]0.40) each, seeking to raise about ₦2.15 trillion ($1.6 billion) to fund the expansion of the [[Dangote refinery]] in [[Lekki]], [[Lagos State]]. The sale is set to become [[Economy of Africa|Africa]]'s biggest IPO. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260914-nigerian-oil-refinery-dangote-launches-ipo (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Maersk]] and [[Hapag-Lloyd]] announce that they will sail more container ships through the [[Suez Canal]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/maersk-hapag-lloyd-resume-further-services-through-suez-canal-2026-09-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Indonesia]] extends the [[Search and rescue|search]] for eight people, including five [[Mass media in Indonesia|journalists]], after their speedboat disappeared in the [[Sunda Strait]] during a reporting mission on [[Anak Krakatoa]]'s eruption a week prior. [[Indonesian National Police|Police]] await test results to identify a body found on [[Enggano Island]]. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2026/09/14/indonesia-extends-search-for-eight-missing-after-anak-krakatau-mission-boat-vanishes/235229 (AFP via ''Malay Mail'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026–2027 El Niño event]]
**The [[World Food Programme]] reports that [[Sudan]]'s [[Darfur]] region is having its driest rainy season since the [[1980s]], worsening [[Famine in Sudan (2024–present)|famine conditions]] amidst the ongoing civil war. [https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/world/2026/09/15/sudan-s-darfur-faces-driest-rainy-season-in-four-decades-says-wfp (AFP via ''Free Malaysia Today'')]
*[[Chile]] becomes the first country in [[South America]] to eliminate [[Rabies in animals#Dogs|dog-transmitted]] [[rabies]], with the [[World Health Organization]] confirming the milestone. [https://apnews.com/article/chile-rabies-public-health-dogs-b01d6e95338eab23aa76145ec32939ea (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Separatism in the United Kingdom]], [[Decolonization]]
**The [[First Minister]]s of [[Northern Ireland]], [[Scotland]], and [[Wales]] meet in [[Cardiff]] at a [[Summit (meeting)|summit]] to call for their independence from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c62enegxyl9o (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/sep/14/westminster-first-ministers-uk-celtic-nations-wales-northern-ireland-scotland (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]]
**[[United States district judge]] [[F. Dennis Saylor IV]] of [[United States District Court for the District of Massachusetts|Massachusetts]] [[Injunction|postpones]] new rules limiting stays for [[International students in the United States|international students]] and [[News media in the United States|journalists]], preventing the measures from taking effect while a legal challenge proceeds. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260914-us-judge-postpones-new-visa-rules-for-foreign-students-journalists (AFP via France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election]]
**[[Bangsamoro Parliament|Parliamentary]] elections are held in the [[Bangsamoro]] [[Autonomous regions of the Philippines|autonomous region]], [[Philippines]], its first since its establishment in 2018. [https://www.aljazeera.com/opinions/2026/9/13/bangsamoros-parliamentary-election-is-a-turning-point (Al Jazeera)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Militarisation of space]]
**The [[United States]] confirms for the first time that it has deployed a weapon in [[Earth]]'s orbit. [[United States Secretary of the Air Force|Air Force secretary]] [[Troy Meink]] says the [[Classified information in the United States|highly classified]] weapon is necessary to "safeguard [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. forces]]" against potential enemy action. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ck790xg41ygro (BBC News)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=13|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)| Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***The [[Ghana Army]] says that Battalion 92 of the [[United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon]] will return to [[Ghana]] following a year of duty in [[southern Lebanon]]. [https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/NewsArchive/Ghana-Battalion-92-returns-home-after-Lebanon-peacekeeping-mission-2052014 (GhanaWeb)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**A [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] attacks a [[Rail transport in Ukraine|train]] bound for [[Warsaw]], [[Poland]], at [[Yahodyn railway station|Yahodyn  station]] in [[western Ukraine]], shortly after former [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK prime minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] and top [[European Union|EU]] security officials had passed through the airspace. Former [[Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|U.S. CIA director]] [[David Petraeus]] was also at the station at the time of the strike but was unharmed. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cy5zg41dkqwo (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[List of shipwrecks in 2026|Shipwrecks in 2026]]
**[[Sinking of the Virgo Transport 8|Sinking of the ''Virgo Transport 8'']]
***Six people die, 97 are rescued and 140 remain missing after the [[Shipwrecking|sinking]] of the ''Virgo Transport 8'' [[ferry]] in the [[Java Sea]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgykzgljlyo (BBC News)]
**[[Sinking of the MV Matui|Sinking of the MV ''Matui'']]
***One person dies, 12 are rescued, and more than 30 remain missing after the sinking of the MV ''Matui'' ferry off [[Espiritu Santo]], [[Vanuatu]], during rough seas. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-12/passenger-and-crew-missing-after-ferry-sinks-near-vanuatu/107147060 (ABC News Australia)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/13/one-dead-and-more-than-30-missing-after-ferry-sinks-off-vanuatu-coast-in-rough-seas (''The Guardian'')]
*A [[multiple-vehicle collision]] on a major highway in [[Western Cape]], [[South Africa]], kills at least 21 people and leaves four others injured, according to the [[Road Traffic Management Corporation]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-road-crash-21-killed-9ae8e6beeb75cc307be24e15e9ec1fad (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Myanmar]]'s [[Union Government of Myanmar|Union Government]] revokes [[Kyaw Moe Tun]]'s status as the country's [[Permanent representative to the United Nations|permanent representative]] to the [[United Nations]], accusing him of illegal activities, as the [[UN Credentials Committee]] prepares to consider the country's disputed representation. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260913-myanmar-says-un-envoy-illegitimate-ahead-of-credentials-decision (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Datu Usman Mampen Elementary School shooting]]
**Three people are killed and 15 others are injured when gunfire erupted outside a school in [[Cotabato City]], [[Bangsamoro]], [[Philippines]], used as a [[polling station]] for the [[2026 Bangsamoro Parliament election|Bangsamoro Parliament election]] the following day. [[Philippine National Police|Police]] say that members of rival [[political faction]]s clashed while competing to be first in line to vote. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2026/09/14/three-shot-dead-15-wounded-ahead-of-polls-in-philippine-muslim-enclave (AFP via ''The Star'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**[[Law enforcement in Mexico|Law enforcement]] agents rescue eight people who they say were forcibly recruited by the [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel]] from a [[Clandestine chemistry|clandestine clinic]] in [[Tecalitlán]], [[Jalisco]], [[Mexico]]. Police arrest six suspected guards and seize drugs, weapons, and ammunition. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/12/mexican-authorities-rescue-eight-from-violent-cartels-secret-site (Al Jazeera)]
*An attack on the [[Panguna mine]] in the [[Provinces of Papua New Guinea|autonomous region]] of [[Autonomous Region of Bougainville|Bougainville]], in [[Papua New Guinea]], injures personnel and destroys equipment amid opposition to plans to reopen the [[copper mine]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260914-bougainville-leader-says-violence-won-t-stop-panguna-mine-re-opening (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/attack-hits-panguna-camp-bougainville-backs-copper-mine-restart-2026-09-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[Turkish police]] detain at least 63 people in raids targeting [[LGBTQ rights in Turkey|LGBTQ+ organizations]] and venues across several [[Provinces of Turkey|provinces]]. The [[Ministry of Justice (Turkey)|justice ministry]] says investigations involve 162 suspects, nine associations and 13 businesses over alleged offences including [[Prostitution in Turkey|prostitution]] and [[obscenity]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/14/turkish-authorities-launch-anti-lgbtq-raids-detaining-dozens (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock]]
**The [[Assembly of Kosovo|Assembly]] of [[Kosovo]] is declared constituted by [[Acting (law)|acting]] [[President of Kosovo|president]] and [[Speaker of the Assembly of Kosovo|speaker]] [[Albulena Haxhiu]], but without the deputy speaker from the [[Democratic Party of Kosovo|PDK]]. The Assembly then accepts the [[Fourth Cabinet of Albin Kurti|fourth cabinet]] of incumbent [[Prime Minister of Kosovo|prime minister]] [[Albin Kurti]]. The PDK and the [[Alliance for the Future of Kosovo|AAK]] both challenge the legitimacy of Kurti's government at the [[Constitutional Court of Kosovo|Constitutional Court]]. [https://apnews.com/article/kosovo-government-kurti-crisis-5c3727cfbcf04a3cc5734972fa6ea6c0 (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/kosovo-parliament-re-elects-albin-kurti-prime-minister-2026-09-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Swedish general election]]
**[[Swedes]] vote to elect all 349 seats of the [[Riksdag]]. Incumbent [[Prime Minister of Sweden|prime minister]] [[Ulf Kristersson]], who seeks to lead the [[Moderate Party|Moderates]] to a second consecutive government while including the [[right-wing populist]] [[Sweden Democrats]] in his cabinet, is being challenged by the former prime minister and [[Swedish Social Democratic Party|SAP]] leader [[Magdalena Andersson]]. Preliminary results indicate that the [[Red-Greens (Sweden)|Red-Greens]] and the [[Centre Party (Sweden)|Centre Party]] are projected to have a combined total of 175 seats, while the four [[Tidö Agreement|Tidö parties]] are projected to have a total of 174 seats. [https://apnews.com/article/sweden-election-parliament-kristersson-andersson-6671108eecef137f7bb9a9f545983c23 (AP)] [https://www.dw.com/en/sweden-election-far-right-eyes-power-for-1st-time/a-79248599 (DW)]
*[[Disinformation in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] sanctions his former [[press secretary]], [[Iuliia Mendel]], and nine others for allegedly spreading [[Russian propaganda]] and supporting [[Russia]] in [[Russo-Ukrainian war|its war]] against [[Ukraine]]. The 10-year sanctions include [[asset freeze]]s and [[trade restriction]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/ukraines-zelenskiy-imposes-sanctions-former-press-secretary-2026-09-13/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Formula One World Championship]]
**[[2026 Spanish Grand Prix]]
***In [[Formula One]] racing, [[Kimi Antonelli]] wins the inaugural [[Spanish Grand Prix]] at the [[Madring]] in [[Madrid]], [[Spain]]. [https://www.espn.com/f1/story/_/id/49867186/spanish-grand-prix-madring-formula-1-race-report-kimi-antonelli-lando-norris-lewis-hamilton (ESPN)]
*[[2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[United States women's national basketball team|United States women's team]] defeats [[France women's national basketball team|France]] 97–79 in [[2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup final round|the final]] to win the [[FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup]] in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], further extending its lead of 12 total wins. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/wnba/2026/09/13/usa-france-fiba-womens-world-cup-final-channel-highlights-results-score/91738272007/ (''USA Today'')]
**American player [[Breanna Stewart]] is awarded [[most valuable player|MVP]] of the tournament, while [[Belgium women's national basketball team|Belgian]] player [[Emma Meesseman]] is the top [[Basketball scorekeeping|scorer]], averaging 21 [[points per game]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/wnba/2026/09/13/breanna-stewart-wins-fiba-womens-world-cup-mvp-leads-all-tournament-team/91749717007/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[2026 US Open (tennis)|2026 US Open]]
**In [[tennis]], [[Alexander Zverev]] wins the [[2026 US Open – Men's singles|men's singles]] title of the 2026 [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]] after defeating [[Ben Shelton]] in the final, 6–3, 7–6<sup>(7–2)</sup>, 5–7, 6–2. It is his first US Open title and second [[Grand Slam (tennis)|major]] title overall. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260913-zverev-holds-off-shelton-to-win-us-open-title-1 (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 Women's Twenty20 Asia Cup]]
**In [[cricket]], the [[India women's national cricket team|India women's team]] wins its eighth [[Women's Asia Cup|Asia Cup]] title by defeating [[Sri Lanka women's national cricket team|Sri Lanka]] by 72 [[Run (cricket)|runs]], but [[India–Pakistan cricket rivalry|refuses]] to accept the trophy from [[Asian Cricket Council]] president and [[Pakistan]]i [[Ministry of Interior (Pakistan)|interior minister]] [[Mohsin Naqvi]] during the presentation ceremony. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260914-india-cricketers-refuse-asia-cup-trophy-from-top-pakistan-official (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship]]
**In [[sport of athletics|athletics]], British [[Middle-distance running|middle-distance runner]] [[Josh Kerr]] wins the inaugural [[World Athletics Ultimate Championship]] in the [[1500 metres]] [[2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship – Men's 1500 metres|event]] in [[Budapest]], [[Hungary]]'s [[National Athletics Centre (Budapest)|National Athletics Centre]]. [https://www.the-independent.com/sport/general/athletics/josh-kerr-ultimate-championships-1500m-result-b3049477.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Melissa Jefferson-Wooden]] and [[Kenny Bednarek]] win the inaugural [[2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship – Women's 200 metres|women's]] and [[2026 World Athletics Ultimate Championship – Men's 200 metres|men's]] [[200 metres]] at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7590750/2026/09/13/bednarek-jefferson-wooden-world-ultimate-championship-win/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=12|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack]], [[Iran–Iraq relations]], [[Iraq in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[Iraq]] closes three [[Iran–Iraq border|border crossings]] with [[Iran]] after [[Federal government of Iraq|Iraqi]] and [[Government of Saudi Arabia|Saudi officials]] said that a [[drone attack]] on [[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[East–West Crude Oil Pipeline]] originated from Iraq. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/iraq-closes-three-border-crossings-with-iran-after-attack-that-shut-saudi-pipeline-officials-say/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]], [[Iran–United Arab Emirates relations]]
****Iran and the [[United Arab Emirates]] sign a joint statement calling for restraint in the war. Additionally, [[President of Iran|Iranian president]] [[Masoud Pezeshkian]] and [[Emirate of Abu Dhabi|Abu Dhabi]] ruler [[Khaled bin Mohamed Al Nahyan]] meet at the [[18th BRICS summit|BRICS summit]], the highest profile meeting between the two countries since the war started on February 28. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/09/iran-and-uae-back-joint-brics-statement-urging-restraint-war (''Al-Monitor'')] [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/iran-president-meets-uae-crown-prince-on-brics-sidelines-back-joint-statement-urging-restraint-in-west-asia-war-101789226727137.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan]], [[China in the 2026 Iran war]]
****''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reports that Iran had received [[China|Chinese]] [[Satellite imagery|satellite images]] before launching a July 17 strike on the [[Muwaffaq Salti Air Base]] in [[Jordan]] that [[Casualties of the 2026 Iran war|killed]] three [[United States Army]] soldiers. [https://www.arabnews.com/world/iran-got-chinese-satellite-images-before-deadly-strike-on-us-troops-report-3001481 (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]], [[Strait of Bab al-Mandab crisis]]
****[[Yemen]]i [[Yemeni Armed Forces|government forces]] strike [[Houthis|Houthi]] positions near the port of [[Mokha]], [[Taiz Governorate]], and along the Mokha–[[Dhubab]] road, reporting that they destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed Houthi fighters after the group captured the city. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260912-yemen-government-forces-say-hit-houthis-in-red-sea-city (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kryvyi Rih strikes (2022–present)|Kryvyi Rih strikes]], [[Odesa strikes (2022–present)|Odesa strikes]], [[Zaporizhzhia strikes (2022–present)|Zaporizhzhia strikes]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[drone warfare|drone strikes]] across [[Ukraine]] kill eight [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|civilians]], including two people in [[Zaporizhzhia]], two people at a [[grocery store]] in [[Zhytomyr]], one person in [[Kryvyi Rih]], while a "massive attack" targeting the [[Port of Odesa]] and surrounding areas wounds at least 28 people. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-putin-europe-839f5b0fc5217afc4cb34e15b01b6eff (AP)]
**[[Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Eastern front of the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] strikes a civilian vehicle in [[Kramatorsk]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], killing three people. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-putin-europe-839f5b0fc5217afc4cb34e15b01b6eff (AP)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Four gunmen and a [[National Guard (Mexico)|National Guard]] agent are killed and another is wounded after an attempted ambush against authorities in [[Jilotlán de los Dolores]], [[Jalisco]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/11/estados/muere-un-integrante-de-la-gn-y-otro-resulta-herido-tras-enfrentamiento-con-civiles-armados-en-michoacan (''La Jornada'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[83rd Venice International Film Festival]]
**[[May el-Toukhy]]'s film ''[[Woman Unknown (film)|Woman Unknown]]'' wins the [[Golden Lion]] at the [[Venice Film Festival]] in [[Italy]], while [[Lee Chang-dong]]'s ''[[Possible Love]]'' and [[Yuval Abraham]] and [[Rachel Szor]]'s ''[[NAZA (film)|NAZA]]'' win the competition's [[Grand Jury Prize (Venice Film Festival)|Grand Jury Prize]] and  [[Special Jury Prize (Venice Film Festival)|Special Jury Prize]], respectively. [https://japantoday.com/category/entertainment/venice-film-festival-ends-with-golden-lion-at-stake-after-%27naza%27-draws-record-ovation (''Japan Today'')]
*[[Rukidi IV of Tooro|Rukidi IV]], the late [[Omukama of Tooro|king]] of [[Uganda]]'s [[Tooro Kingdom]], is buried. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/king-oyo-once-worlds-youngest-monarch-be-buried-western-uganda-2026-09-12/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2024 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**The [[Sheriff#United States|sheriff's office]] of [[Washington County, Tennessee|Washington County]], [[Tennessee]], U.S., announces that the remains of the last victim of [[Hurricane Helene]] has been found, two years after the hurricane has hit [[East Tennessee]]. [https://www.knoxnews.com/story/news/local/2026/09/15/hurricane-helene-last-victim-found-in-east-tennessee-two-years-after-storm/91773358007/ (''Knoxville News Sentinel'')] [https://www.foxcarolina.com/2026/09/15/remains-hurricane-helene-victim-found-nearly-2-years-later-sheriffs-office-says/ (WHNS)]
*[[MV June Aster ship fire|MV ''June Aster'' ship fire]]
**The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Philippine Coast Guard|coast guard]] confirms that 41 more bodies have been discovered aboard the burned vessel MV ''June Aster'' off [[Coron, Palawan|Coron]], [[Palawan]], bringing the death toll from the fire to 76. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2304154/palawan-ferry-fire-death-toll-climbs-to-76-as-identification-process-begins (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**The [[Atlantic hurricane season]] reaches a 103-day record in the satellite era without a hurricane after the season started on June 1, the first since [[1941 Atlantic hurricane season|1941]], with [[2026–2027 El Niño event|the]] [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation|El Niño]] in the [[Pacific Ocean]] being a big factor. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/12/weather/el-nino-hurricane-storm-atlantic-record-climate (CNN)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/12/weather/atlantic-hurricane-season-latest-record.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/weather/2026/09/12/atlantic-hurricane-season-2026-sets-record/91658860007/ (''USA Today'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[List of North Korean missile tests|North Korean missile tests]]
**[[North Korea]] launches a series of [[Short-range ballistic missile|SRBM]] missile tests from [[Wonsan]] in response to trilateral Freedom Edge [[military exercise]]s conducted by [[Japan]], [[South Korea]], and the [[United States]]. [https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/korea/north-korea-launches-srbms-after-south-koreausjapan-drills/12872273 (''Korea JoongAng Daily'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/north-korea-launches-unidentified-projectile-toward-east-sea-yonhap-reports-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Cléon derailment]]
**[[France|French]] officials investigate if the [[derailment]] in [[Cléon]], [[Seine-Maritime]], was caused by [[Rail sabotage|sabotage]] after a fragment of rail was found on the tracks. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260912-french-police-suspect-train-derailment-was-sabotage (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c33kp533nn6o (BBC News)] [https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2026/0912/1591279-france-trail/ (RTÉ)]
*[[Libya]]'s [[RADA Special Deterrence Forces]] seize about 100,000 [[MDMA]] pills moulded with former [[Brotherly Leader and Guide of the Revolution|leader]] [[Muammar Gaddafi]]'s likeness after tracking a shipment [[Illegal drug trade|smuggled]] from Europe. Officers find the drugs hidden in a cargo van and refer several suspects to prosecutors. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/gaddafi-ecstasy-pills-libya-tripoli-b3049361.html (''The Independent'')]
*Several residents are arrested after [[riot]]s erupted yesterday in [[Kobani]], [[Syria]], over the murder of a [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish citizen]] that was blamed on an [[Arabs|Arab]] man, while a [[prison riot]] and fire at Kobani prison leaves seven inmates dead. The [[Syrian Observatory for Human Rights]] reports the violence erupted over plans to transfer some prisoners to another prison in [[Aleppo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-kurds-prison-kobani-fire-5d8f8b6c2b93ca5d3a079251ffd1d77c (AP)] [https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/prison-riot-fire-northern-syrian-town-kills-7-136385827 (ABC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Protests against Donald Trump]]
**[[Protests against the 2026 Iran war]], [[Gaza war protests]], [[Protests against the second Trump administration]]
***Thousands of demonstrators gather in [[Dublin]] and [[Doonbeg]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], against [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]]'s [[List of international presidential trips made by Donald Trump|visit]] to the country and protest against his role in the wars in Iran and [[Gaza war|Gaza]]. [https://www.irishtimes.com/ireland/2026/09/12/the-only-people-on-the-streets-are-here-to-oppose-him-thousands-protest-trump-visit/ (''Irish Times'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/12/world/europe/trump-irish-open-ireland-doonbeg.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[2026 Saxony-Anhalt state election]]
**Protesters gather in [[Germany]] across 20 cities against the [[Alternative for Germany]] following its victory in the [[Saxony-Anhalt]] state election. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/12/tens-of-thousands-march-across-germany-to-protest-far-right-party-afd (Al Jazeera)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 US Open (tennis)|2026 US Open]]
**In [[tennis]], [[Elena Rybakina]] wins the [[2026 US Open – Women's singles|women's singles]] title at the [[US Open (tennis)|US Open]], her third [[Grand Slam (tennis)#Tournaments|major]] title, after defeating two-time defending champion [[Aryna Sabalenka]] in the final, 6–4, 5–7, 6–2. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260913-rybakina-reigns-serene-as-new-world-number-one (AFP via France 24)]
**[[Christian Harrison]] and [[Neal Skupski]] win the [[2026 US Open – Men's doubles|men's doubles]] title at the US Open without dropping a [[Set (tennis)|set]] in the tournament after defeating [[Kevin Krawietz]] and [[Tim Pütz]], 6–4, 7–6<sup>(8–6)</sup> in the final. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260912-harrison-skupski-win-us-open-men-s-doubles-title (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 Summer Youth Olympics]]
**The [[Olympic flame]] arrives in [[Dakar]], [[Senegal]], ahead of the upcoming [[Youth Olympic Games]], which will be the first [[Olympic Games]] held in [[Africa]]. [https://apnews.com/article/senegal-olympic-flame-youth-games-5a6f4d02447ea59effe1a6a12049ca98 (AP)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=11|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]]
****In [[Yemen]], the [[Houthis]] seize [[Perim Island]] in the [[Strait of Bab al-Mandab]] after [[Yemeni Armed Forces|government forces]] withdrew, completing their takeover of the surrounding area and giving them control of territory overlooking a major [[sea lane]] between the [[Red Sea]] and [[Gulf of Aden]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260911-yemen-s-houthis-complete-takeover-of-bab-al-mandab-area-govt-official-to-afp (AFP via France 24)]
****The Houthis announce the end and the success of their offensive, expelling government forces from six districts and seizing major locations. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/9/11/iran-war-live-irgc-attacks-us-unmanned-vessel-in-hormuz-two-ships-hit (Al Jazeera)]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack]], [[Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[Ministry of Energy (Saudi Arabia)|Ministry of Energy]] temporarily closes the [[East-West Crude Oil Pipeline]] as a precautionary measure following multiple attacks by drones from [[Iraq]] on Thursday. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/11/saudi-arabia-shut-down-east-west-crude-oil-pipeline.html (CNBC)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Unmanned Systems Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian drone]] strikes kill two people and injure three others in [[Tula Oblast]], [[Russia]], while a separate strike kills a 37-year-old man in [[Kursk Oblast]], according to regional officials. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russian-air-strikes-injure-two-cause-fire-9-storey-apartment-building-kyiv-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]], [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] strikes hit two [[Oil in Ukraine|petrol stations]] in [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]], killing two people and injuring 12 others. A separate attack on a residential building injures eight people, while another strike kills a woman in [[Kyiv Oblast]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russian-air-strikes-injure-two-cause-fire-9-storey-apartment-building-kyiv-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Princess Astrid, Mrs. Ferner|Princess Astrid]], an older sister of the [[Death and state funeral of Harald V|late]] [[King of Norway|Norwegian King]] [[Harald V]] and daughter of [[Olav V]], dies at the age of 94. [https://www.nine.com.au/lifestyle/royals/princess-astrid-death-norwegian-royal-family-member-dies-just-days-after-king-harald-funeral-20260911-p60wpz.html (Nine.com.au)] [https://news.sky.com/story/norways-princess-astrid-dies-two-days-after-funeral-of-her-brother-the-late-king-harald-13584441 (Sky News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Kyrgyzstan]]'s [[National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic|central bank]] starts domestically printing [[banknote]]s of the [[Kyrgyz som]], the country's currency, for the first time since [[Independence Day (Kyrgyzstan)|independence]]. [https://24.kg/english/388902_Kyrgyzstan_prints_20-_and_50-som_banknotes_domestically_for_first_time_/ (24.kg)] [https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-09-11/engk-nknk-kyrgyzstan-begins-printing-its-own-banknotes-for-the-first-time/ (Kursiv)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[MV June Aster ship fire|MV ''June Aster'' ship fire]]
**The death toll from the MV ''June Aster'' ferry fire off [[Coron, Palawan|Coron]], [[Palawan]], [[Philippines]], rises from five to 35 after [[Bureau of Fire Protection|firefighters]] boarded the burned vessel and recovered 30 additional bodies. The [[Philippine Coast Guard|coast guard]] continues searching for dozens of missing passengers and crew. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-rescuers-resume-search-survivors-palawan-ferry-fire-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]
*At least 16 people are killed in a fire in a [[retirement home]] near [[Pitrufquén]], [[Cautín Province|Cautín]], [[Chile]]. Ten people are rescued and hospitalized. [https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/least-16-dead-fire-retirement-084833103.html (DPA via Yahoo News)]
*Thirteen people are killed and eight others are injured when a [[minibus]] collided with a car and a [[logging truck]] in [[Kholmogorsky District]], [[Arkhangelsk Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/three-vehicles-collide-northern-russia-12-dead-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)] [https://english.news.cn/20260912/67131efc494043648f361e89ad1326f1/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**A case of [[Ebola]] is reported in the [[Sud-Ubangi]] [[Provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|province]], making it the seventh province in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] the outbreak has spread to. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/africa/ebola-congo-outbreak-spreads-b3048824.html (''The Independent'')] 
*[[2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak]]
**The [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] and [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention]] declares an end to the [[cyclosporiasis]] food poisoning outbreak, which is caused by ''[[Cyclospora cayetanensis]]'' and linked to [[iceberg lettuce]] from [[Taylor Farms]], in the [[United States]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/11/cdc-record-cyclosporiasis-outbreak-over.html (CNBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/us-declares-end-largest-recorded-cyclosporiasis-outbreak-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Endangerment of orangutans]], [[India–Indonesia relations]]
**[[Indonesia]] works with [[India]]n authorities to repatriate five baby [[orangutan]]s found in an [[Odisha]] [[Forests in Odisha|forest]] after suspected [[Wildlife smuggling|trafficking]]. [[Odisha Police]] and India's [[Wildlife Crime Control Bureau]] examine how the apes, which are native to [[Borneo]] and [[Sumatra]], reached India. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260911-indonesia-to-bring-back-baby-orangutans-allegedly-trafficked-to-india (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Nigeria–South Africa relations]], [[Xenophobia in South Africa]]
**[[Nigeria]]'s [[National Assembly (Nigeria)|National Assembly]] suspends all official visits and virtual engagements with [[South Africa]] in protest over repeated [[Opposition to immigration|anti-migrant]] attacks there, including violence against [[Nigerians in South Africa|Nigerians]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/11/nigeria-suspends-official-visits-to-south-africa-over-anti-migrant-violence (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Israel–United Kingdom relations]]
**In retaliation to [[United Kingdom|British]] sanctions on [[Economy of Israel|goods]] from [[Israeli settlement]]s earlier this week, the [[Israel]]i [[Cabinet of Israel|government]] orders a team of [[British Armed Forces|British soldiers]] who train and advise [[Palestinian Authority]] [[Palestinian National Security Forces|security forces]] in the [[West Bank]] to leave the country. [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/09/11/israel-expels-british-soldiers-tracking-settler-violence/?WT.mc_id=tmgoff_reddit_british-soldiers-tracking-settler-violence/ (''The Telegraph'')]
 
'''Law and crime'''
*[[The Gambia]] bans protests without official permits after demonstrations over prolonged [[power outage]]s damaged a [[The Gambia Police Force|police]] post and utility offices. Police arrest 11 people in connection with the unrest and warn that they will disperse unauthorized gatherings. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/gambia-bans-protests-without-permits-after-unrest-over-power-cuts-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Hong Kong]] [[Judiciary of Hong Kong|court]] sentences [[Pro-democracy camp (Hong Kong)|pro-democracy]] activists [[Lee Cheuk-yan]] and [[Chow Hang-tung]] to seven years in [[Prisons in Hong Kong|prison]] each for [[Inciting subversion of state power|inciting subversion]] under the [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law]] for leading the [[Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China]]. [https://www.afp.com/en/hong-kong-tiananmen-vigil-activists-convicted-security-trial (AFP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/hong-kong-court-jails-two-tiananmen-vigil-group-leaders-7-years-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Lebanese Armed Forces|Lebanese Army]] arrests [[Suleiman Hilal Al Assad]], a [[Assad family|cousin]] of former [[President of Syria|Syrian president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]], along with two other men, on [[Illegal drug trade in Lebanon|drug trafficking]] charges. The men are now under the custody of [[Lebanon]]'s [[Ministry of National Defense (Lebanon)|defence ministry]]. [https://apnews.com/article/lebanon-syria-assad-relative-688da8554748d90569a69a157a8b10ae (AP)] [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/bashar-al-assads-cousin-arrested-in-lebanon-drugs-case-1.500672267 (''Gulf News'')]
*The [[Seoul Central District Court]] acquits former [[South Korea]]n [[President of South Korea|president]] [[Yoon Suk Yeol]] on charges that he appointed his [[Minister of National Defense (South Korea)|defense minister]], [[Lee Jong-sup]], as ambassador to [[Australia]] to [[Perverting the course of justice|obstruct an investigation]] into a [[Republic of Korea Marine Corps|South Korean marine]]'s drowning during [[2023 South Korea floods|the 2023 floods]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-korea-yoon-marine-death-martial-law-47e59273e60cbfe9e0243b94d6e4803c (AP)]
*[[South Africa]] extradites six [[Nigeria]]n nationals allegedly belonging to [[Black Axe (confraternity)|Black Axe]] to the [[United States]], where they face [[wire fraud]] and [[money laundering]] charges linked to [[online romance scam]]s that allegedly [[Internet fraud|defrauded]] more than 100 victims. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/south-africa-extradites-us-six-suspected-members-black-axe-gang-2026-09-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[September 11 intelligence before the attacks]]
**The [[Central Intelligence Agency|U.S. Central Intelligence Agency]] releases 71 documents warning of a threat from [[Al Qaeda]] prior to the [[September 11 attacks]], including [[President's Daily Brief|presidential daily briefs]] during the administrations of former [[President of the United States|U.S. presidents]] [[Bill Clinton]] and [[George W. Bush]] from 1998 to [[Aftermath of the September 11 attacks|the day after the attacks]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c17j94ew1lno (BBC News)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/12/what-did-us-intelligence-know-before-the-9-11 (Al Jazeera)]
