{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=10|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Second Intifada#Aftermath|Aftermath of the Second Intifada]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) and [[Shin Bet]] confirm that they have killed [[Hamas]] senior leader Farah Hamed, a senior member who was accused of carrying out the 2003 attack that resulted in the killing of {{ill|Shalom Har-Melech|he|רצח שלום הר מלך}}, the late husband of [[Limor Son Har-Melech]], in a airstrike in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/433030 (Israel National News)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/hamas-terrorist-behind-2003-shooting-that-killed-mks-husband-slain-in-gaza-airstrike-says-israel/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[Israel]]i airstrikes on the [[Gaza Strip]] kill a family of four. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-strike-kills-parents-two-children-gaza-medics-say-2026-09-10 (Reuters)]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***[[2026 Lebanon war]]
****[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] and [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|defense minister]] [[Israel Katz]] say that the IDF has destroyed a [[Hezbollah]] [[Hezbollah tunnels|tunnel]] in [[Ali al-Taher]]. [https://www.ft.com/content/57045557-574a-4bd6-9912-adb64fd6110f?syn-25a6b1a6=1 (''The Financial Times'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/10/israel-says-it-destroyed-hezbollah-base-in-lebanons-ali-al-taher-ridge (Al Jazeera)]
****The [[United States Geological Survey]] reports that a magnitude 4.1 earthquake has been detected after Israel carried out the strike in Ali al-Taher. [https://news.sky.com/story/4-1-magnitude-tremor-recorded-after-israel-destroys-hezbollah-tunnel-network-in-southern-lebanon-13584236 (Sky News)]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 East–West Crude Oil Pipeline attack]], [[Iraq in the 2026 Iran war]], [[Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war]]
****Multiple [[projectile]] explosives launched from [[Iraq]] strike [[pumping station]]s along the [[East–West Crude Oil Pipeline]] in [[Saudi Arabia]], causing a fire. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/11/politics/saudi-arabian-oil-pipeline-hit-by-projectiles-triggering-fires (CNN)]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensives]]
****[[Houthis]] capture the port city of [[Mokha]], as government forces retreat from the districts of [[Hays district|Hays]] and [[Al Khawkhah district|Al Khawkhah]]. A mass exodus of civilians from the area towards [[Aden]] is reported. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260910-yemen-s-houthis-seize-key-city-on-red-sea-military-source (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russia]] [[drone strike]]s across [[Ukraine]] kill at least 15 people and injure 90 others, including victims in [[Dnipro]], [[Mykolaiv]], [[Odesa]], [[Pavlohrad]], and [[Sumy]]. Ukraine also strikes [[Natural gas in Russia|gas facilities]] in [[Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug]], [[Ural (Russian administrative region)|Ural]], Russia. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/10/russian-attacks-kill-7-in-ukraine-as-kyiv-targets-gas-plants-deep-in-arctic (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Foreign fighters in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Amnesty International]] says that [[Russia]] recruited [[Foreign fighter|foreign nationals]] for its war in Ukraine through deception, coercion, and [[Exploitation of labour|exploitation]], including [[Employment fraud|false job offers]] and threats. The organization concludes that many such cases amount to [[Human trafficking in Russia|human trafficking]] under [[international law]]. [https://eastleighvoice.co.ke/world/399260/russias-recruitment-of-foreign-nationals-to-fight-in-ukraine-war-amounts-to-human-trafficking-amnesty (''The Eastleigh Voice'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war fuel crisis]]
***[[Petroleum|Crude oil]] [[Price of oil|prices]] in the [[United States]], including from [[Brent Crude]] and [[West Texas Intermediate]], reach [[United States dollar|US$]]100, the highest since May, amidst the country's [[September 2026 United States strikes on Iran|renewed tensions]] with [[Iran]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/10/iran-us-oil-hormuz-supply-trump-military-brent-wti.html (CNBC)]
***The [[European Central Bank]] raises its three key [[interest rate]]s by 0.25 percentage points, lifting the [[deposit rate]] to 2.50%, as higher energy prices linked to the Iran war increase [[inflation]] pressures across the [[eurozone]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/10/ecb-interest-rate-hike-lagarde-iran.html (CNBC)]
**The [[International Monetary Fund]] reports that the global growth of the global economy is on track to reach 3% in 2026 despite the war in Iran, but also cautioned that risks still remain high. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/imf-say-global-growth-track-reach-3-2026-risks-remain-high-2026-09-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*At least 20 people are killed and five others are reported missing after a fire breaks out on a [[cargo ship]] in [[Qingdao]], [[Shandong]], [[China]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/10/china/cargo-ship-fire-china-port-intl (CNN)]
*Five people are killed and 40 others are injured after a bus carrying [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[Tourism in Switzerland|tourists]] crashes between [[Zernez]] and [[Susch]], [[Switzerland]]. [https://apnews.com/article/switzerland-bus-crash-c3d992fe08ae0608578d073a1828959e (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak]]
**Seven more children die from suspected [[measles]] in [[Bangladesh]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the total number of deaths in the country to 1,009. [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/health/measles-death-toll-reaches-1009-7-more-children-die-24hrs-1538961 (''The Business Standard'')]
**[[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Bangladesh)|Health minister]] [[Sardar Md. Sakhawat Husain]] announces that Bangladesh will resume nationwide [[Measles vaccine|vaccinations]] beginning on September 25 amidst the ongoing measles outbreak. [https://southasianherald.com/bangladesh-to-resume-nationwide-measles-vaccination-campaign-from-sept-25/ (''South Asian Herald'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Algeria–United Arab Emirates relations]]
**[[Algeria]] cuts diplomatic relations with the [[United Arab Emirates]], without specifying a reason. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/algeria-cuts-diplomatic-ties-with-uae-algerian-state-tv-says-2026-09-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[Peru–United States relations]], [[War on drugs]]
**[[President of Peru|Peruvian president]] [[Keiko Fujimori]] announces that [[Peru]] will join the [[U.S.]]-led [[Shield of the Americas]] coalition against [[drug cartel]]s following a [[List of international trips made by Marco Rubio as United States Secretary of State|visit]] from [[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Marco Rubio]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-join-us-anti-drug-coalition-after-rubio-visit-2026-09-10/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Deportation in the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States Alien Terrorist Removal Court]] orders the [[Deportation from the United States|deportation]] of [[Green card|permanent resident]] Nazira Haji Zada to [[Afghanistan]] in its first case, after Haji Zada conceded that she supported an [[Islamic State]]-inspired [[Mass shootings in the United States|mass-shooting]] plot planned for the [[2024 United States presidential election|2024 presidential election]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c3eqpd9zgl9o (BBC News)]
*[[Hutch Organised Crime Gang]]
**An [[Republic of Ireland|Irish]] [[Courts of the Republic of Ireland|court]] charges Jason Hutch, a son of alleged crime boss [[Gerry Hutch]], with facilitating a [[criminal organisation]], the same day he was extradited from [[Spain]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/2026/0910/1591064-jason-hutch-court/ (RTÉ)]
*[[Sri Lanka]]'s [[Supreme Court of Sri Lanka|Supreme Court]] overturns a 2019 [[President of Sri Lanka|presidential]] [[pardon]] granted to [[Buddhism in Sri Lanka|Buddhist]] monk [[Galagoda Aththe Gnanasara]] and orders him to serve the remainder of his six-year prison sentence for [[Crime in Sri Lanka|criminally]] intimidating [[Human rights in Sri Lanka|human rights]] activist [[Sandya Eknelygoda]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260910-sri-lanka-court-revokes-monk-s-pardon-orders-return-to-prison (AFP via France 24)]

'''Science and technology'''
*The first [[robotic surgery|robotic surgical system]] in [[Kyrgyzstan]] is introduced at the [[Kyrgyz State Medical Academy]]. [https://azertag.az/en/xeber/first_robotic_system_unveiled_in_kyrgyzstan-4407544 (Azertag)] [https://akipress.com/news:918148:Kyrgyzstan_unveils_first_robotic_surgical_system/ (AKIPress)] [https://caspianpost.com/kyrgyzstan/kyrgyzstan-unveils-its-first-robotic-surgical-system (''Caspian Post'')]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=9|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensive]], [[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]]
****[[September 2026 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia]]
*****[[Saudi Arabia]] launches 32 [[airstrike]]s in four [[Governorates of Yemen|governorates]] in [[Yemen]] against the [[Houthis]]. [https://ua.news/en/world/khusiti-zaiavili-pro-ponad-40-aviaudariv-saudivskoyi-araviyi-v-emeni (UA News)]
****The death toll from the [[Royal Saudi Air Force|Saudi]] [[airstrike]] against a prison in [[Al-Jawf Governorate]], two days ago, increases to 23 people. [https://apnews.com/article/yemen-saudi-arabia-war-prison-strike-red-sea-ede975f78a1d014092e43d0f2d682b9a (AP)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Second Intifada#Aftermath|Aftermath of the Second Intifada]]
****[[Hamas]] claims that the [[Israel Defense Forces]] has killed Farah Hamed, a senior member who was accused of carrying out the 2003 attack that resulted in the killing of {{ill|Shalom Har-Melech|he|רצח שלום הר מלך}}, the late husband of [[Limor Son Har-Melech]], in a airstrike in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-908211 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/432992 (''Israel National News'')] [https://vinnews.com/2026/09/09/hamas-announces-death-of-senior-commander-farah-hamed-in-gaza-city-strike/ (VINnews)]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan]]
****[[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] launch [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|missiles]] at the [[Muwaffaq Salti Air Base]] in [[Azraq, Jordan|Azraq]], [[Jordan]], reporting damage to maintenance facilities, deployment areas, and [[hangar]]s. Jordan says [[Jordanian Armed Forces|its forces]] have intercepted 18 Iranian missiles, following [[September 2026 United States strikes on Iran|United States strikes]] that destroyed five [[Petroleum industry in Iran|Iranian]] [[oil tanker]]s. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260909-iran-attacks-us-base-in-jordan-as-hormuz-impasse-deepens (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Operation Southern Spear]]
**[[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***The [[United States Southern Command]]'s [[Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere]] kills three people in a strike on an alleged [[Illegal drug trade|narcotrafficking]] drug boat in the [[Caribbean Sea]]. [https://www.stripes.com/theaters/americas/2026-09-10/us-boat-strike-southern-spear-22809838.html (''Stars and Stripes'')] [https://www.southcom.mil/News/PressReleases/Article/4594213/lethal-kinetic-strike-september-9-2026/ (SOUTHCOM)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] strike hits a shopping centre in [[Sumy]], [[Ukraine]], killing two people and injuring 20 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/strike-shopping-centre-sumy-northern-ukraine-kills-three-governor-says-2026-09-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Death and state funeral of Harald V]]
**The [[state funeral]] of [[King of Norway|King]] [[Harald V]] takes place at the [[Oslo Cathedral]] in [[Oslo]], [[Norway]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/09/europe/norway-king-harald-funeral-intl (CNN)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/09/world/europe/norway-king-harald-funeral.html (''The New York Times'')]
*The [[Tooro Kingdom]] in [[western Uganda]] selects Prince Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a television news anchor and editor, as its new [[Omukama of Tooro|monarch]] following the death of [[Rukidi IV of Tooro|Rukidi IV]] last month. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ugandan-kingdom-picks-new-monarch-succeed-king-oyo-nyimba-once-worlds-youngest-2026-09-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[MV June Aster ship fire|MV ''June Aster'' ship fire]]
**Five people are killed and 87 others are reported missing when a fire breaks out aboard a passenger ferry off [[Coron, Palawan|Coron]], [[Palawan]], [[Philippines]]. The [[Philippine Coast Guard|coast guard]] rescues 42 people from the vessel, which carried 117 passengers and 17 crew members. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/ferry-fire-off-northern-palawan-leaves-five-dead-says-philippine-coast-guard (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*[[Sokolniki Suche train collision]]
**A train collides with a truck at a [[level crossing]] in [[Sokolniki Suche]], [[Poland]], killing one person and injuring 20 others. [https://tvpworld.com/95301887/one-dead-20-injured-as-train-derails-in-central-poland (TVP World)] [https://english.news.cn/20260909/1b30eb71f36b4b789325e625ed79ffe3/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Fourteen people are killed and eleven others are injured in an explosion at a weapons depot in [[Sarmada]], [[Syria]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-idlib-explosion-warehouse-sarmada-bfc58aac61599fdf8ac71d964c453037 (AP)]
*Two people are killed and extensive damage is caused after an [[explosion]] at a [[Hydroelectricity|hydroelectric]] [[power station]] in [[Piotta, Switzerland|Piotta]], [[Ticino]], [[Switzerland]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/several-injured-explosion-hydroelectric-station-switzerland-20min-reports-2026-09-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 heat waves]]
**[[2026 European heatwaves]]
***[[Peninsular Spain]] records [[List of extreme temperatures in Spain|its hottest summer]] since the [[State Meteorological Agency]]'s measurements began in 1961, with an average temperature of {{convert|24.5|C|F}} and 61 [[heatwave]] days from June through August. [https://www.arabnews.pk/world/spain-endured-hottest-summer-on-record-weather-agency-3000744 (''Arab News Pakistan'')]
**[[2026 North American heat wave]]
***The [[National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration]] reports that the [[United States]] has experienced its hottest summer on record from June to August with a {{convert|23.6|C|F}}, surpassing the [[Dust Bowl]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/9/9/us-records-hottest-summer-in-132-years (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/us-hottest-summer-on-record-2026-noaa/ (CBS News)]
**The [[Copernicus Climate Change Service]] (C3S) reports that August 2026 is [[List of weather records|the hottest month]] globally since measurements began, with an average temperature of {{convert|16.96|C|F}}, exceeding the previous record set in July 2023. [https://apnews.com/article/heat-record-climate-change-sizzle-el-nino-2a78248322a04b97f417346308d05483 (AP)]
*[[2026 Indonesia wildfires]]
**The C3S reports that [[wildfire]]s in [[Kalimantan]] and [[Sumatra]], [[Indonesia]], produced more than 19.7 million metric tons of [[carbon dioxide emission]]s from September 1 to 7, the world's highest total and more than one-third of global fire emissions. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/indonesian-wildfire-emissions-surge-worlds-highest-data-shows-2026-09-09/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sudanese cholera epidemic (2024–present)|Sudanese cholera epidemic]]
**The [[United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs]] announces that a 10-day [[Cholera vaccine|cholera]] [[vaccine|vaccination]] campaign has been launched in [[Tawila]], [[North Darfur]] in a effort to immunize 95,000 people in the area. Additionally, 16 deaths are reported from [[cholera]] in [[Sudan]]'s [[West Kordofan]] [[States of Sudan|state]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318583 (''Sudan Tribune'')] [https://www.dabangasudan.org/en/all-news/article/16-cholera-deaths-reported-in-west-kordofan-darfur-vaccination-drive-begins (Radio Dabanga)] [https://allafrica.com/stories/202609110005.html (AllAfrica)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Israel–Slovenia relations]]
**[[Israel]] opens its first [[List of diplomatic missions of Israel|embassy]] in [[Ljubljana]], [[Slovenia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/slovenia-israel-embassy-protest-747a067d6d44501bab151480bffcb7ab (AP)]
*[[Syria and weapons of mass destruction]]
**The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] ends its investigation into [[Syria]]'s nuclear activities after [[Syrian transitional government|the new government]] granted inspectors access to nuclear sites. Its board terminates a 2011 resolution that found Syria in non-compliance with [[IAEA safeguards|its nuclear safeguards]] obligations. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260909-syria-no-longer-under-un-nuclear-watchdog-probe (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Reform UK financial allegations]]
**The [[Metropolitan Police]] launch a [[Crime in the United Kingdom|criminal]] investigation into [[Reform UK]] over allegations that it broke [[Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000|foreign funding laws]] in the [[United Kingdom]], following an investigation by [[Channel 4 News]]. [https://apnews.com/article/britain-reform-uk-8dc9d6790e3e06b2bb898f803231bec1 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cp3k72k1y3vo (BBC News)]
*[[Brazil]]ian [[Supreme Federal Court|Supreme Court]] president [[Edson Fachin]] suspends conflicting rulings by two [[List of ministers of the Supreme Federal Court (Brazil)|justices]], allowing [[Federal Police of Brazil|Federal Police]] chief [[Andrei Rodrigues]] to remain in office while the court reviews allegations that police monitored justice [[André Mendonça]] and other government authorities. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/brazil-top-court-judge-orders-reinstatement-federal-police-chief-2026-09-09/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Serbian parliamentary election]]
**[[Serbia]]n [[President of Serbia|president]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] dissolves the [[National Assembly (Serbia)|National Assembly]] and calls a [[Snap election|snap parliamentary election]] for October 25, following a government proposal amid prolonged [[2024–present Serbian anti-corruption protests|political tensions]]. The ruling [[Serbian Progressive Party]] nominates Vučić as its lead candidate and candidate for [[Prime Minister of Serbia|prime minister]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260909/0cdf0a5c00ef43f5bb4167e2fbfa508d/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2026 in archosaur paleontology]]
**Scientists at the [[Denver Museum of Nature and Science]] in [[Colorado]], [[U.S.]], and [[Liverpool John Moores University]] in [[England]] discover the first adult ''[[Tyrannosaurus]]'' [[Fossil track|trackway]] at [[Hell Creek Formation]] in [[North Dakota]], U.S. The study is published in the ''[[Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology]]''. [https://phys.org/news/2026-09-million-year-trackway-captures-adult.html (Phys.org)] [https://www.axios.com/local/denver/2026/09/09/t-rex-trackway-denver-scientists (''Axios'')]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=8|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**[[2026 Yemen offensive]], [[Houthi–Saudi Arabian conflict]]
***[[September 2026 Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Houthis|Houthi]] forces launch [[ballistic missile]]s and [[Drone warfare|drones]] at several locations in [[Saudi Arabia]], injuring 73 people, including civilians, and causing fires that temporarily halt operations at some [[Energy in Saudi Arabia|energy]] facilities. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-says-it-plans-new-gulf-exclusion-zone-threatens-us-with-new-missiles-2026-09-08/ (Reuters)]
***The confirmed toll of the offensive in western [[Yemen]] increases to 500 people killed, including 278 [[Houthis|Houthi fighters]], 216 soldiers of the [[Yemeni Armed Forces]] and 29 civilians. [https://www.lbcgroup.tv/news/middleeastnews/956496/over-500-killed-since-yemen-clashes-began-last-week-sources-to-afp/en (AFP via LBC Group)]
***The toll from yesterday's [[Royal Saudi Air Force|Saudi]] [[airstrike]] against a prison in [[Al-Jawf Governorate]] increases to 17 people killed and seven more wounded. [https://www.saba.ye/en/news3783769.htm (Saba News Agency)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]], [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russia]] launches [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|drones]] and missiles at [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]], following a weekend [[Ceasefire|pause]] in strikes, killing five people and injuring at least 10. The attacks damage civilian [[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure|infrastructure]] at at least 16 locations and cause fires in five [[Subdivisions of Kyiv|districts]]. [https://dailypioneer.com/news/russia-strikes-kyiv-drones-missiles-two-killed (''The Pioneer'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/russian-ballistic-missiles-hit-kyiv-us-envoys-leave-2026-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***Around 13 people are killed in a drone strike by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] on a courthouse in [[Umm Ruwaba]], [[North Kordofan]]. [https://sudanhorizon.com/13-killed-and-22-injured-after-militia-shells-umm-ruwaba/ (''Sudan Horizon'')]
**Peace talks are held by mediators from the [[African Union]], the [[Intergovernmental Authority on Development]], the [[Arab League]], the [[European Union]] and the [[United Nations]], in [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]], in an effort to end the three-year long [[civil war]], with UN envoy [[Pekka Haavisto]] attending the talks. [https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/un-envoy-joins-quintet-representatives-for-talks-in-khartoum-to-push-sudan-peace-process-3000995 (''Arab News'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico]]
***[[Canada]]'s retaliatory [[tariffs]] of 15% to 50% on [[CA$]]27.6 billion ([[US$]]19.9 billion) of [[List of exports of the United States|U.S. goods]], including [[Iron and steel industry in the United States|steel]], [[Dairy industry in the United States|dairy products]], [[Home appliance|appliance]]s, [[Agriculture in the United States|agricultural equipment]], [[Pulp and paper industry in the United States|paper products]], and electronics, take effect in [[Reciprocity (international relations)|response]] to [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|U.S. tariffs]] on [[List of exports of Canada|Canadian imports]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260908-canada-s-counter-tariffs-take-effect-on-various-us-goods (AFP via France 24)]
***In response, the [[United States]] announces a ban on the [[List of imports of the United States|imports]] of [[Alcoholic drinks in Canada|Canadian alcoholic drinks]], motorcycles, and [[Dairy farming in Canada|dairy products]] beginning September 29. [https://www.reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/canadas-retaliatory-tariffs-take-effect-us-trade-talks-stall-2026-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[International sanctions against Iran]]
**[[United States sanctions against Iran]], [[Economic D-Day]]
***The [[United States Department of the Treasury|U.S. treasury department]] imposes [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] against 27 [[List of airlines of Iran|Iranian airlines]], including [[flag carrier]] [[Iran Air]], in an effort to squeeze [[Iran]]'s [[Economy of Iran|economy]]. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/09/us-hits-27-iranian-airlines-latest-sanctions (Al-Monitor)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**The [[National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority]] reports that 13,583 people have been rescued so far since [[flash flood|flash floods]] ravaged [[Nepal]]. [https://risingnepaldaily.com/news/86288 (''The Rising Nepal'')]
* A [[MBB Bo 105]] helicopter operating for the [[Flying Doctors of Malaysia]] crashes near [[Long Lellang]], [[Sarawak]], [[Malaysia]], killing all five onboard. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/flying-doctor-helicopter-crashes-malaysia-authorities-say-2026-09-08/ (Reuters)] [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/09/08/sarawak-heli-crash-all-on-board-confirmed-dead (''The Star'')]
*[[Indonesia]] reopens [[Soekarno–Hatta International Airport|its airport]] in [[Jakarta]] and four others after previously being closed due to ashes from [[Anak Krakatoa]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/8/indonesia-airports-reopen-after-volcanic-ash-disrupts-thousands-of-flights (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 North American heat wave]]
**A third-year student in the [[Hawkeye Marching Band|marching band]] at the [[University of Iowa]] in [[Iowa City, Iowa|Iowa City]], [[United States|U.S.]], dies after collapsing during [[heat wave|extreme heat]] at the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]] [[2026 Iowa Hawkeyes football team|season opener]] at [[Kinnick Stadium]]. Temperatures reached {{convert|94|F|C}} at the time of the game. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/sep/08/university-iowa-marching-band-derek-phillips-heat-collapse (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7575354/2026/09/08/derek-phillips-iowa-marching-band-taken-off-life-support/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')]
*[[Famine in Sudan (2024–present)|Famine in Sudan]]
**A [[famine]] is reported across [[Sudan]]'s [[Jebel Marra]] area in the [[Darfur]] region, with 20 people dying from hunger and diseases. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318503 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Health effects arising from the September 11 attacks]]
**[[Mayor of New York City|Mayor]] [[Zohran Mamdani]] says that [[New York City]], U.S., has released over 170,000 documents detailing that [[Government of New York City|city officials]] knew about the air quality and unsafe conditions at the time of the [[September 11 attacks]] including at [[World Trade Center site|Ground Zero]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/08/us/nyc-sept-11-air-quality-records (CNN)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/08/air-quality-september-11-attacks-documents-release (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Indonesia]]'s [[National Food Agency|food agency]] suspends nearly 2,000 kitchens in [[Free Nutritious Meals|its national free meals programme]] after they fail to register for mandatory sanitation inspections, as the agency strengthens [[food safety]] measures following widespread [[Food poisoning incidents in Indonesia's Free Nutritious Meals Program|food poisoning cases]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-suspends-nearly-2000-free-meal-kitchens-breaching-sanitation-rules-2026-09-08/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Morocco–Spain relations]]
**[[2026 Ceuta migrant crisis]]
***[[Spain]] declassifies around 40 [[National Intelligence Centre (Spain)|intelligence]] reports concerning the July [[migrant crisis]] into [[Ceuta]], during which more than 70,000 people crossed from [[Morocco]], amid scrutiny of whether [[Sûreté Nationale (Morocco)|Moroccan security forces]] facilitated the crossings and whether [[Law enforcement in Spain|Spanish security services]] had prior warning of the influx. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260908-spain-declassifies-intelligence-reports-into-ceuta-migrant-rush (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Israel–United Kingdom relations]], [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank]], [[Legality of Israeli settlements]]
**The [[United Kingdom]] announces it will ban [[Economy of Israel|imports of all goods]] from [[Israel]]i [[Israeli settlement|settlements]] in the [[West Bank]], as well as some services, including financing, construction, infrastructure, real estate, and advertising. [https://www.telegraphindia.com/world/uk-government-bans-goods-from-israeli-settlements-in-the-west-bank/cid/2178981#goog_rewarded (''Telegraph India'')]
**To [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] the UK sanctions, Israel announces it will close the [[Consulate General of the United Kingdom, Jerusalem|UK consulate]] in [[East Jerusalem]]. Israel also forbids the UK from participating in the [[International Gaza Support Center|U.S.-led mission for Gaza]], and bans some British officials, including former [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] leader [[Jeremy Corbyn]], from entering the country. [https://www.northweststar.com.au/story/9346577/hit-with-broad-sanctions-israel-to-close-uk-consulate/ (''The North West Star'')]
*[[Bosnia and Herzegovina–Serbia relations]]
**[[Bosnia and Herzegovina]] declares two [[Serbia]]n embassy diplomats, military attaché Milan Dulanović and [[Security and Intelligence Agency (Serbia)|Security Intelligence Agency]] representative advisor at the embassy Darko Maksimović, as ''[[Persona non grata|personae non gratae]]'' after attending the funeral of [[Trial of Ratko Mladić|convicted]] [[war crime|war criminal]] [[Ratko Mladić]] in [[Belgrade]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/bosnia-expels-two-serbian-embassy-diplomats-protest-over-mladic-funeral-2026-09-08/ (Reuters)]
*''[[Nicaragua v. Germany]]'', [[German support for Israel in the Gaza war]]
**[[Nicaragua]] urges the [[International Court of Justice]] to reject [[Germany]]'s objections to its case, stating that [[List of modern equipment of the German Army|German arms]] exports to Israel breach the [[Genocide Convention]] and [[international humanitarian law]]. Germany responds by saying that the court lacks jurisdiction over parts of the case. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260908-nicaragua-accuses-germany-of-multiple-violations-of-law-in-gaza-genocide-case (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/8/nicaragua-urges-icj-to-reject-germanys-bid-to-throw-out-gaza-genocide-case (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Musée Renoir theft]]
**[[Art theft|Thieves]] steal ''{{ill|Jeune Femme au puits|fr}}'' and ''{{ill|Madame Colonna Romano|fr}}'' by [[Pierre-Auguste Renoir]] from the {{Interlanguage link|Musée Renoir|fr|Musée Renoir}} in [[Cagnes-sur-Mer]], [[Alpes-Maritimes]], [[France]]. The works have an estimated value of [[Euro|€]]9 million. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/cmdx0grlp92gt (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[AI boom]]
**[[OpenAI]] says that it has solved the [[Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness|Navier–Stokes]] [[Millennium Prize Problems|Millennium Prize problem]], with the announcement raising questions about [[Artificial intelligence and copyright|plagiarism]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cy7zygy3rl2o (BBC News)] [https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openai-claims-blockbuster-math-breakthrough-amid-swirl-of-controversy/ (''Scientific American'')]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 7
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=7|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Oman]]'s [[Royal Navy of Oman|navy]] says that they have rescued 16 crew members from a [[Saudi Arabia]]-[[Flag state|flagged]] [[oil tanker]] ''SIDR'' that was attacked a week ago in the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.newarab.com/news/oman-rescues-16-crew-members-saudi-vessel-struck-iran?amp (MENA via ''The New Arab'')]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israeli conflict]]
***[[2026 Lebanon war]], [[Israeli attacks on the Lebanese health sector during the Israel-Hezbollah conflict (2023–present)|Israeli attacks on the Lebanese health sector during the Israel-Hezbollah conflict]]
****Nine people, including two children, are killed, and five others are injured in an [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]] on a residential building in [[Kfar Reman]], [[Lebanon]]. Separately, in the same city, two medics are killed in another airstrike on a vehicle. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/7/israeli-air-attack-kills-at-least-10-people-in-southern-lebanon (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Ecuadorian conflict (2024–present)|Ecuadorian conflict]]
**[[Operation Southern Spear]], [[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***The [[United States Southern Command]] says that they have sunk a vessel allegedly belonging to the [[Los Choneros]]. [https://apnews.com/article/ecuador-us-boat-drug-trafficking-sinking-pacific-fishermen-551b40890fe249597d0236087fed019a (AP)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**[[2026 Yemen offensive]]
***More than 300 people are killed amid the deadliest fighting in the war since 2022. [https://www.barrons.com/news/more-than-140-killed-in-latest-yemen-clashes-military-sources-4ab1faee (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
***Amid the offensive, [[Saudi Arabia]] launches an [[airstrike]] against a prison in [[Al-Jawf Governorate]], killing seven people, including a child, and trapping 35 more under the rubble. [https://apnews.com/article/yemen-prison-houthis-jawf-forces-prison-saudi-arabia-e6d1e1d84c943d2fb1ce186a1e5bd3f8 (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Tourism in Tokyo]]
**The government of [[Shinjuku]], [[Tokyo]], [[Japan]], announces plans to prohibit more than half of its [[vacation rental]]s in residential areas and near [[Education in Tokyo|schools]] after complaints increase over noise, [[Smoking in Japan|smoking]], trespassing, and improper [[Waste management in Japan|waste disposal]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260907-tokyo-s-shinjuku-to-ban-more-than-half-of-vacation-rentals (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Eleven people, including six children, are killed in a fire at a fire at a market in [[Paniai]], [[Central Papua]], [[Indonesia]]. Forty [[kiosk]]s and houses are destroyed. The causes are unknown. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/fire-in-indonesias-papua-kills-11-including-6-children (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]
*The death toll from an explosion at [[Armed Forces of Bolivia|military]] [[barracks]] in [[Viacha]], [[Bolivia]], three days ago, increases to nine people. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bolivia-confirms-7-deaths-others-still-missing-after-military-base-explosion-2026-09-07/ (Reuters)]
*A private [[Piper PA-34|Piper PA-34-200T Seneca]] aircraft goes missing off [[Andros Island]], [[the Bahamas]], with four people on board. A search and rescue operation is ongoing. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/us-coast-guard-joins-bahamas-search-missing-plane-carrying-4-family-rcna596544 (NBC News)]
*A [[PAC P-750 XSTOL]] aircraft operating a passenger flight for [[Niugini Aviation]] crashes near [[Simbai Rural LLG|Simbai]], [[Madang Province|Madang]], [[Papua New Guinea]], during approach. All four people on board are killed. [https://aviation-safety.net/wikibase/579644 (ASN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 East Malaysia haze]]
**[[Malaysia]] lifts the [[state of emergency]] in [[Serian Division]], [[Sarawak]], after [[Air pollution in Malaysia|air pollution]] fell below hazardous levels, although several areas remain "very unhealthy" because of smoke from [[2026 Indonesia wildfires|wildfires]] in [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260907-malaysia-cancels-haze-emergency-but-warns-problems-remain (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Greenland and the European Union]]
**[[European Commission]] [[President of the European Commission|president]] [[Ursula von der Leyen]] announces that [[Greenland]] and the [[European Union]] have reached a [[Euro|€]]200 million ([[US$]]232.5 million) partnership deal. [https://www.reuters.com/business/eu-announces-200-million-partnership-deal-with-greenland-2026-09-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[North Korea–Russia relations]]
**[[North Korea]] and [[Russia]] opens the [[Yakov Novichenko Bridge]] at [[North Korea–Russia border|its border]], the first [[Bridge|road bridge]] connecting the two countries. [https://www.dw.com/en/russia-opens-first-road-bridge-with-north-korea/a-79142595 (DW)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/east-asia/north-korea-russia-bridge-tumen-river-b3046075.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[Serbia–European Union relations]]
**A [[military funeral]] and burial is held for [[Trial of Ratko Mladić|convicted]] [[war crime|war criminal]] [[Ratko Mladić]] in [[Belgrade]], [[Serbia]], despite objections from the [[European Union]] due to concerns that the honors glorify a person convicted of [[genocide]] and [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/7/convicted-war-criminal-ratko-mladic-gets-heros-burial-in-serbia (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/07/ratko-mladic-butcher-of-bosnia-funeral-belgrade-serbia (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Flood control projects scandal in the Philippines]]
**The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Sandiganbayan]] appellate court issues an arrest warrant for [[Leyte's 1st congressional district|Leyte's 1st district]] [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|representative]] and former [[Speaker of the House of Representatives of the Philippines|House speaker]] [[Martin Romualdez]] after the [[Office_of_the_Ombudsman_(Philippines)|Office of the Ombudsman]] filed charges of [[Looting|plunder]] against him for the alleged [[Philippine peso|₱]]7.44 billion (US$118.62 million) worth of [[Kickback (finance)|kickbacks]] he received from [[Flood management|flood control]], infrastructure, and other government projects. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-court-orders-arrest-presidents-cousin-over-alleged-kickbacks-118-2026-09-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Kenya]] grants [[Temporary resident|temporary legal status]] to [[Illegal immigration|undocumented]] [[East Africa]]n nationals who registered with their embassies, after [[President of Kenya|president]] [[William Ruto]] ordered the closure of [[small business]]es operated by [[Foreign trade of Kenya|foreign traders]] without [[work permit]]s. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/burundians-try-leave-kenya-ahead-crackdown-traders-2026-09-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*In [[Australian rules football]], the [[Australian Football League]] introduces limits on [[Australian football tactics and skills|contact]] training from the 2027 [[preseason]] to reduce [[Head injuries in the Australian Football League|concussion]] risk, capping weekly contact at 120 minutes initially and 160 minutes later while prohibiting [[High-intensity training|high-intensity sessions]] on consecutive days. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260907-australian-rules-limits-contact-training-to-reduce-concussion (AFP via France 24)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 September 6
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=6|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
****[[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli]] strikes in [[Gaza City]] kill at least four [[Palestinians]], including an eight-year-old girl and a three-year-old boy, and injure six others. [[Israel]] says one strike targeted a [[Hamas]] member and that it is reviewing the outcome. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-strike-kills-two-people-gaza-medics-say-2026-09-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israeli conflict]]
***Seven people are killed and 20 more injured in a series of Israeli [[airstrike]]s in southern [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/6/israeli-air-attacks-on-lebanon-kill-at-least-four (Al Jazeera 1)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/9/6/iran-war-live-irgc-claims-new-attacks-on-us-warships-over-naval-blockade?update=4923404 (Al Jazeera 2)] 
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[U.S.]] envoys [[Steve Witkoff]] and [[Jared Kushner]] make their first visit to [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]], to meet with [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] for talks amidst renewed efforts to end the war. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/us-envoys-make-first-kyiv-visit-amid-ukraine-war-peace-push-2026-09-06/ (Reuters)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/06/us-envoys-make-first-kyiv-visit-amid-ukraine-war-peace-push.html (CNBC)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] and [[Darfur Joint Protection Force|Joint Forces]] advance in [[Sudan]]'s [[North Kordofan]] [[States of Sudan|state]], and recaptures the town of Hamrat al-Wiz. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318423 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**The [[International Committee of the Red Cross]] reports that over 11,000 people have been reported missing since the [[civil war]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318410 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[78th Primetime Emmy Awards]]
**[[78th Primetime Creative Arts Emmy Awards]]
***[[Rob Reiner]] wins a [[posthumous award]] for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series|Outstanding Guest Actor in a Comedy Series]] for his role in ''[[The Bear (TV series)|The Bear]]'' nine months after [[Killing of Rob and Michele Reiner|his killing]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/06/arts/television/rob-reiner-emmy-the-bear.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Pacific hurricane season]]
**A [[state of emergency]] is declared in [[Hawaii]], [[United States]], as [[Hurricane Lowell (2026)|Hurricane Lowell]] approaches the [[U.S. state|state]] as a [[Saffir–Simpson scale|Category 3 storm]], with heavy rain, [[High surf advisory|high surf]], and dangerous coastal conditions forecasted. [[Tropical storm]] warnings are issued for [[Kauaʻi]] and [[Niʻihau]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/06/hawaii-hurricane-lowell-state-of-emergency (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2026 Pacific typhoon season]]
**The death toll from [[Mudflow|mudslides]] caused by Typhoon Saudel in [[Suichuan County]], [[Jiangxi]], [[China]], increases to three. [https://apnews.com/article/china-mudslide-jiang-xi-deaths-saudel-typhoon-8e302d3fae97f3b0c2f74dca908039ec (AP)]
*[[21 Air Flight 7598]]
**A [[Boeing]] [[Boeing 767-300|767-300]] [[Cargo aircraft|cargo plane]] operated by [[21 Air]], contracted by [[Amazon Air]], [[Runway excursion|overshoots]] the runway and strikes vehicles while landing at [[Miami International Airport]] in [[Florida]], United States, killing five people and injuring five others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cmqlwrvwzxx5t (BBC News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/06/us/plane-crash-amazon-miami-airport.html (''The New York Times'')]
*Eleven people are killed and seven others are injured when a [[fuel tanker]] hits other cars and explodes, reportedly due to a faulty [[brake|brake system]], near [[Sanandaj]], [[Kurdistan province]], [[Iran]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-road-accident-death-toll-90148bfbc4007e09d4ad5130aecd1ed6 (AP)]
*Eleven [[Mountaineering|climbers]] are killed and six others are injured after an avalanche struck a group of 33 on Mount Mizhirgi in [[Kabardino-Balkaria]], [[Russia]]. Six other climbers are missing as rescuers continue search operations. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/russia-avalanche-tragedy-11-climbers-killed-after-snow-slide-hits-group-in-kabardino-balkaria-14043837.html (''Firstpost'')]
*[[Jakarta metropolitan area|Jakarta]]'s [[Soekarno–Hatta International Airport]], [[Indonesia]]'s busiest airport, suspends flight operations after volcanic ash from [[Anak Krakatoa]] reaches the airport. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/9/6/indonesia-s-main-airport-suspends-operations-after-volcanic-eruption-1218 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak]]
**Three more children are reported to die from suspected [[measles]] in [[Bangladesh]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the total death toll to 997. [https://www.thedailystar.net/health/news/three-more-die-measles-symptoms-4267171 (''The Daily Star'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Saxony-Anhalt state election]]
**[[Exit poll]]s show the [[Far-right politics|far-right]] [[Alternative for Germany]] party winning the [[Saxony-Anhalt]] state election in [[Germany]] but failing to secure an absolute majority of seats. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/6/far-right-afd-wins-vote-in-germanys-saxony-anhalt-state-exit-polls (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/06/saxony-anhalt-germany-afd-exit-poll-ulrich-siegmund (''The Guardian'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Formula One World Championship]]
**[[2026 Italian Grand Prix]]
***In [[Formula One]] racing, [[Mercedes-Benz in Formula One|Mercedes]] driver [[Kimi Antonelli]] wins the [[Italian Grand Prix]], becoming the first [[Formula One drivers from Italy|Italian driver]] in 60 years to win on [[Autodromo Nazionale Monza|home soil]] after [[Ludovico Scarfiotti]] in [[1966 Italian Grand Prix|1966]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/formula1/antonelli-takes-sensational-home-italian-gp-win-back-grid-2026-09-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Leagues Cup]]
**[[2026 Leagues Cup final]]
***In [[association football]], [[Toluca FC|Toluca]] defeat [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]] 2–0 in the final to claim their first [[Leagues Cup]] championship. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2026/09/07/toluca-rayados-leagues-cup-final/91646771007/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[2026 NASCAR Cup Series]]
**[[2026 Cook Out Southern 500]]
***In [[NASCAR]] racing, [[Joe Gibbs Racing|Joe Gibbs]] driver [[Christopher Bell (racing driver)|Christopher Bell]] wins the [[Southern 500]] race at [[Darlington Raceway]] in [[South Carolina]], U.S., snapping a 33-race winless streak. [https://www.espn.com/racing/story/_/id/49854635/christopher-bell-passes-kyle-larson-win-southern-500 (ESPN)]
*[[2026 World Nomad Games]]
**The final day of the [[World Nomad Games]] is held, with hosts [[Kyrgyzstan]] defeating [[Kazakhstan]] 12–0 to win the [[kok-boru]] final in [[Cholpon-Ata]]. Kyrgyzstan wins the [[gold medal]] in kok-boru, Kazakhstan wins the [[Silver medal|silver]], and [[Russia]] wins the [[Bronze medal|bronze]]. [https://timesca.com/kyrgyzstan-beats-kazakhstan-12-0-to-win-world-nomad-games-kok-boru-gold/ (''The Times of Central Asia'')] [https://24.kg/english/388167_Kyrgyzstan_defeats_Kazakhstan_12-0_for_6th_World_Nomad_Games_kok-boru_victory_/ (24.kg)]
**Kazakhstan finishes first in the medal standings at the World Nomad Games. [https://qazinform.com/news/kazakhstan-tops-medal-standings-at-world-nomad-games-dbbb7c/amp (Qazinform)]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=5|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Peace negotiations in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Russia]] and [[Ukraine]] agree to halt strikes on [[Kyiv]] and [[Moscow]], respectively, during [[United States]]-mediated [[peace talks]], as [[Ambassadors of the United States#Special envoys, representatives, and coordinators|U.S. envoys]] [[Jared Kushner]] and [[Steve Witkoff]] meet [[President of Russia|Russian president]] [[Vladimir Putin]] in Moscow before traveling to Kyiv. [https://www.dawn.com/news/2027693 (AFP via ''Dawn'')]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile strike kills two people and damages multiple residential buildings in [[Bucha, Ukraine|Bucha]], [[Kyiv Oblast]], Ukraine. [https://ua.news/en/war-vs-rf/na-kiyivshchini-cherez-ataku-rf-zaginuli-dvoie-liudei (UA News)]
**[[Russian occupation of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]]
***A Russian [[airstrike]] on [[Kamianske]], [[Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]], Ukraine, kills four people and injures five others, including one critically, according to [[Governor of Dnipropetrovsk Oblast|Dnipropetrovsk governor]] Oleksandr Hanza. [https://sana.sy/en/international/2340576/ (SANA)]
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**The [[United States Central Command]] says [[United States Armed Forces|its forces]] have destroyed three [[Petroleum industry in Iran|Iranian]] [[oil tanker]]s linked to the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]], including one in the [[Gulf of Oman]], after alleged [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|Iranian missile]] attacks on [[United States Navy ships|U.S. naval vessels]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260905-us-military-says-destroys-iranian-oil-tankers-after-missile-attacks (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cj64rrne643o (BBC News)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Two [[Federal Police (Mexico)|federal agents]] are killed in a [[shootout]] with an armed group in [[Omealca]], [[Veracruz]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.democrata.es/en/international/two-agents-murdered-in-an-organized-crime-attack-in-veracruz/ (''Demócrata'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Saudel (2026)|Typhoon Saudel]]
***One person is killed and eleven others are reported missing after a mudslide buries a village and damages 12 homes in [[Suichuan County]], [[Jiangxi]], [[China]]. [https://apnews.com/article/china-jiangxi-mudslide-missing-typhoon-saudel-f129132156a3bf65d493c7af356b41bf (AP)]
*[[2026 Indonesia wildfires]]
**[[Indonesia]]'s [[National Agency for Disaster Countermeasure|disaster agency]] and [[Indonesian Air Force|air force]] conduct [[aerial firefighting]] operations to contain [[wildfire]]s near the planned capital [[Nusantara]] in [[East Kalimantan]], following a request from the [[Nusantara Capital City Authority]]. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/337147/indonesia-uses-water-bombing-to-contain-wildfires-near-future-capital (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*[[Cape Verde bus crash]]
**Twenty-five people are killed and several others are injured after a bus carrying mostly secondary school students plunges down a slope in [[Fogo, Cape Verde|Fogo]] island, [[Cape Verde]]. [https://apnews.com/article/cape-verde-bus-crash-8c726e98d4709db1d48f9bb2a81c622b (AP)]
*Ten people are killed and 64 others are injured after an accidental [[fireworks]] explosion during a religious celebration in a [[parish]] in [[Temascalcingo]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/6/at-least-10-killed-in-central-mexico-fireworks-blast-during-festival (Al Jazeera)]
*Ten people are killed and six others are injured after a [[tank truck]] suffers a brake failure and explodes on the [[Hamedan]]–[[Sanandaj]] highway, [[Iran]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2026/09/06/fuel-tanker-explosion-after-traffic-accident-kills-10-in-western-iran-state-media-says (AFP via ''The Star'')]
*A [[Hellenic Air Force|Greek]] [[F-4 Phantom]] jet crashes during an [[air show]] at [[Tanagra Air Base]] near [[Athens]], [[Greece]], killing both pilots. [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/greek-f-4-crashes-during-an-air-show-near-athens-ert-reports-2026-09-05 (Reuters)]
*A five-story [[hostel]] building collapses in [[New Delhi]], [[India]], killing seven people. At least 12 people are rescued from the rubble. [https://apnews.com/article/india-new-delhi-building-collapse-7cb4420ce1808209044300131cb1de45 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**[[Uganda]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Uganda)|health ministry]] bans mourners from the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] from attending the burial ceremony of the late [[Tooro Kingdom]] [[Omukama of Tooro|king]] [[Rukidi IV of Tooro|Rukidi IV]] amidst the [[Ebola]] outbreak. [https://www.independent.co.ug/mourners-from-drc-barred-from-king-oyos-burial/ (''The Independent Uganda'')] [https://ugmirror.com/index.php/2026/09/05/health-ministry-blocks-eastern-drc-mourners-as-tooro-buries-king-oyo/ (''Uganda Mirror'')]
* Tens of thousands of people rally in [[Zagreb]], [[Croatia]], demanding the removal of about 37,000 tonnes of [[Illegal dumping|illegally dumped]] [[hazardous waste]] from [[Gospić]] and a ban on [[Global waste trade|waste imports]] amid concerns over [[Soil contamination|soil]] and [[Groundwater pollution|groundwater contamination]]. [https://apnews.com/article/croatia-protest-toxic-waste-environment-1db8bad3c3d03d352d99c3cb2d6afd24 (AP)]
*The [[National Food Agency]] of [[Indonesia]] reports that nearly 2,000 people, mostly students, have fallen ill across the country this week in suspected [[food poisoning]] outbreaks linked to [[President of Indonesia|president]] [[Prabowo Subianto]]'s new [[Free Nutritious Meals]] program. [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-free-meals-poisoning-outbreak-fc1dfade9dca3b819a907fbbc0d63f98 (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*The 128 [[List of parties to the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons|parties]] to the [[Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons]] agree on a non-binding text defining [[lethal autonomous weapon]]s systems, potentially enabling negotiations on international rules governing their use. [https://www.reuters.com/world/states-reach-agreement-autonomous-weapons-talks-geneva-2026-09-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Peruvian security crisis]]
**[[Peru]] declares a 60-day [[state of emergency]] in five [[supermax prison]]s, authorizing [[National Police of Peru|police]] and [[Peruvian Armed Forces|military]] forces to control the facilities and surrounding [[airspace]] and [[Telecommunications in Peru|communications]] to disrupt [[Crime in Peru|criminal]] organizations operating from prisons. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-declares-state-emergency-five-high-security-prisons-combat-criminal-gangs-2026-09-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[United Kingdom anti-immigration protests (2025–present)|United Kingdom anti-immigration protests]]
**Hundreds of masked [[anti-immigration]] protesters block the [[Port of Dover]] in [[Kent]], [[England]], and chant "[[English Channel illegal migrant crossings (2018–present)|stop the boats]]", causing massive disruption to traffic and [[Southeastern (train operating company)|train services]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cmwyzxlzxpzgt (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/05/europe/england-dover-port-protest-intl-gbr (CNN)]
*[[Philippine]] [[Vice President of the Philippines|vice president]] [[Sara Duterte]] posts [[Philippine peso|₱]]360,000 ([[US$]]5,740) [[bail]] on three counts of [[Death threat|grave threats]], prompting a [[regional trial court]] to lift her arrest warrant. The charges concern alleged threats against [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]], [[First Lady of the Philippines|first lady]] [[Liza Araneta Marcos]], and former [[Speaker of the House of Representatives of the Philippines|House speaker]] [[Martin Romualdez]]. [https://apnews.com/article/philippines-vice-president-sara-duterte-bail-253a1caa41ef2b831d307fbe2b0489df (AP)]
*In [[Egypt]], twelve people are [[Capital punishment in Egypt|sentenced to death]] for [[Illegal drug trade|drugs trafficking]], including television presenter [[Sarah Khalifa]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-06/sarah-khalifa-egyptian-tv-presenter-sentenced-to-death-drugs/107121306 (AFP via ABC News Australia)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Formula One World Championship]]
**[[2026 Italian Grand Prix]]
***In [[Formula One]], [[Aston Martin in Formula One|Aston Martin]] driver [[Lance Stroll]] becomes the first driver to be knocked out in [[Formula One race weekend#Qualifying|Q1]] 100 times after doing so at the 2026 [[Italian Grand Prix]]. [https://www.motorsport.com/f1/news/lance-stroll-hits-unwanted-100-q1-eliminations-milestone-in-f1-10852655/10852655/ (''Motorsport'')]
***At the same Grand Prix, [[Alpine F1 Team|Alpine]] driver [[Pierre Gasly]] achieves [[List of Formula One polesitters|his maiden]] [[pole position]] after qualifying first, the first [[Formula One drivers from France|French driver]] to do so since [[Jean Alesi]] in [[1997 Italian Grand Prix|1997]]. [https://www.formula1.com/en/latest/article/gasly-charges-to-sensational-maiden-f1-pole-at-monza-over-russell-and-piastri.4CKkkbvgmqL04ijMNBfuXF (F1)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/motor/formula1/2026/09/05/pierre-gasly-gets-first-career-formula-1-pole-position/91634145007/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[2026 Diamond League]]
**[[2026 Memorial Van Damme]]
***In [[track and field]], Swiss [[Sport of athletics|athlete]] [[Audrey Werro]] wins the women's [[800 metres]] at the [[Diamond League]]'s [[Memorial Van Damme]] in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]], with a meeting record of 1:54.75. [https://athleticsweekly.com/news/werro-holds-off-broeders-bol-in-closest-800m-yet-in-brussels-1040012934/ (''Athletics Weekly'')]
*[[2026 China GT Championship]]
**Dutch [[Loek Hartog]] rescues fellow driver {{ill|Ollie Millroy|de}} from a burning car following an accident at the [[Shanghai International Circuit]]. [https://www.motorsport.com/gt/news/hartog-hailed-as-hero-after-rescuing-millroy-from-fiery-shanghai-crash/10852780/ (Motorsport Network)]
*[[2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup]]
**In [[Women's basketball|women's]] [[basketball]], the [[Mali women's national basketball team|Mali women's national basketball team]] [[Upset (competition)|upsets]] [[Spain women's national basketball team|Spain]] 82-73, making it [[Mali]]'s second ever victory in the [[FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup]] after its 2010 victory against [[Senegal women's national basketball team|Senegal]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/sep/05/mali-spain-womens-basketball-world-cup-hungary-nigeria (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.espn.com/wnba/story/_/id/49834051/mali-shocks-spain-fiba-women-basketball-world-cup (ESPN)]
*[[2026 MLS season]]
**In [[association football]], [[Major League Soccer]]'s [[Columbus Crew]] wins their 400th game in franchise history. [https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/mls/columbus-crew/2026/09/05/columbus-crew-vs-colorado-rapids-mls-live-updates-highlights-stats--live/91629431007/ (''The Columbus Dispatch'')] [https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/crew-blanks-rapids-3-0/n-6410204 (Our Sports Central)]
* In [[Women's boxing|women's]] [[boxing]], [[Katie Taylor]] retires as the undisputed super lightweight champion after defeating previously unbeaten [[Flora Pili]] by unanimous decision before a crowd of 83,000 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]]. [https://www.espn.com/boxing/story/_/id/49844006/dublin-croke-park-shows-appreciation-katie-taylor-retirement-fight (ESPN)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=4|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Battle of Sufa#Aftermath|Aftermath of the Battle of Sufa]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] state that Mohammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, a [[Nukhba forces|Nukhba Force]] commander who participated in the [[October 7 attacks]] on the [[Battle of Sufa|Sufa post]], was killed in an [[airstrike]] in [[Khan Yunis]], [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-says-it-killed-a-hamas-commander-who-led-oct-7-assault-on-border-post/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire]]
****[[Israel]] frees four [[Lebanese prisoners in Israel|prisoners]], including two [[Syrians|Syrian]] citizens, via [[International Committee of the Red Cross]] as part of efforts to revive [[United States|U.S.]]-backed [[2026 Israel–Lebanon peace talks|peace talks]] signed between Israel and [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/4/israel-frees-four-more-lebanese-prisoners-in-red-cross-mediated-handover (Al Jazeera)] [https://thehill.com/homenews/ap/ap-international/ap-israel-frees-4-more-lebanese-prisoners-in-a-deal-tied-to-missing-jews-from-lebanons-civil-war/amp/ (''The Hill'')]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensive]]
****Over 120 people are confirmed to have been killed since yesterday during the clashes between [[Houthis]] and the [[Yemeni Armed Forces]] in western [[Yemen]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260904-more-than-120-killed-in-yemen-s-worst-clashes-in-years-sources (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***A [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] strikes the [[Security Service of Ukraine]] (SSU) headquarters in central [[Kyiv]], injuring five people. [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says the attack targeted acting [[Head of the Security Service of Ukraine|SSU head]] [[Oleksandr Poklad]], who was unharmed. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/04/europe/russia-strikes-ukraine-security-service-kyiv-intl (CNN)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**At least three [[National Army of Colombia|soldiers]] are killed and four are wounded by [[Loitering munition|explosives]] dropped from [[drone warfare|drones]] in [[Ocaña, Colombia|Ocaña]], [[Norte de Santander Department|Norte de Santander]], [[Colombia]]. Local authorities blame the attack on the [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]]. [https://apnews.com/article/colombia-drone-attack-army-eln-dff0b8f7af030e0c6b97112f8a76d7d5 (AP)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**The [[Pakistan Armed Forces|Pakistani military]] says it has killed 48 [[Baloch nationalism|Baloch separatists]] in a series of raids on hideouts over the past 72 hours in [[Balochistan, Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-militants-killed-multiple-raids-balochistan-339bdaaaca592d2d9f19a9509708aa0a (AP)]
*[[Kidnapping in Nigeria]]
**Nine people, including five [[State Security Service (Nigeria)|Department of State Services]] personnel, are killed during a security operation to rescue kidnapped victims in [[Oyo State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/09/nine-killed-in-oyo-kidnap-victims-rescue-operation-dss-dg/ (''Vanguard'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*An [[Argentina|Argentine]] judge orders the [[Repatriation (cultural property)|repatriation]] of [[Giacomo Ceruti]]'s 18th-century painting ''[[Portrait of a Lady (Ceruti)|Portrait of a Lady]]'', [[Nazi plunder|looted]] by [[Nazi Germany]] from [[Dutch Jewish]] art dealer [[Jacques Goudstikker]] during [[World War II]], to Goudstikker's daughter-in-law Marei von Saher. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260904-argentina-to-return-nazi-looted-painting-to-jewish-collector-s-heir (AFP via France 24)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iran war fuel crisis]]
***The [[American Automobile Association]] reports that the average [[Petroleum in the United States|U.S. diesel]] price reached a record [[United States dollar|$]]5.85 per gallon, up from $3.71 a year earlier, amid disruptions to [[global energy market]]s caused by the [[2026 Iran war|Iran war]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260904-us-diesel-price-hits-new-high-on-iran-war-squeezing-voters (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 European drought]], [[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[France]] allocates more than [[€]]1 billion to support [[Agriculture in France|farms]] affected by [[drought]] and [[heatwave]]s, including compensation for crop losses, [[liquidity assistance]], [[tax relief]], and support for fertilizer and agricultural diesel costs. [https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/04/09/2026/france-allocates-more-than-eur-1-billion-to-support-agricultural-sector (''The Peninsula'')]
*[[Tajikistan]]'s [[Capital city|capital]] [[Dushanbe]] begins construction on the 340-meter-high [[Dushanbe Tower]], which is set to become the [[List of tallest structures in Central Asia|tallest building]] in [[Central Asia]]. [[President of Tajikistan|President]] [[Emomali Rahmon]] and [[Mayor of Dushanbe|Mayor]] [[Rustam Emomali|Rustami Emomali]] lay the building's foundation stone. [https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/09/04/tajikistans-capital-will-build-the-dushanbe-tower-with-a-height-of-340-meters-emomali-rahmon-launched-the-construction-of-a-large-scale-architectural-complex/ (Asia-News)] [https://caspianpost.com/tajikistan/dushanbe-tower-set-to-become-central-asia-s-tallest-building (''Caspian Post'')] [https://thegulfobserver.com/tajikistan-begins-construction-of-multi-purpose-modern-architectural-and-services-complex-in-dushanbe/ (''The Gulf Observer'')]
*The U.S. [[National Highway Traffic Safety Administration]] opens an investigation into whether [[Tesla, Inc.|Tesla]]'s new [[Tesla Cybercab|Cybercab]] [[robotaxi]] models are properly certified and demonstrate compliance with motor vehicle safety standards. [https://reuters.com/business/autos-transportation/us-auto-safety-regulator-opens-probe-into-nearly-1000-tesla-cybercabs-2026-09-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**The [[Nepali Army]] rescues two people from a tunnel at the [[Upper Trishuli 3A Hydropower Station]] in [[Rasuwa District]], a week after floods ravaged [[Nepal|the country]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/two-trapped-workers-rescued-alive-tunnel-nepal-rcna596050 (NBC News)]
*Around 22 people are killed in a blaze of unknown origin at a wedding party in [[Lingwala]], [[Kinshasa]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-wedding-fire-dd585caa5bc1b990bdefa6b33e3ff446 (AP)]
*At least two people are killed, 62 others sustain injuries, and 14 others remain unaccounted for after a blast at a [[Armed Forces of Bolivia|military]] base storing [[pyrotechnic]] material in [[Viacha]], [[Bolivia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/explosion-bolivia-military-base-kills-least-10-official-says-2026-09-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 East Malaysia haze]]
**[[Malaysia]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in [[Serian Division]], [[Sarawak]], after [[haze]] from [[2026 Indonesia wildfires|wildfires]] in nearby [[Kalimantan]], [[Indonesia]], pushed [[Air pollution in Malaysia|air pollution]] above hazardous levels, closing 647 schools. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260904-malaysia-declares-haze-emergency-in-sarawak-state-on-borneo (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] issues an updated 180-day response to the [[Ebola]] outbreak in the country. [https://english.news.cn/20260905/5d9fa2a1b92b4a31b1639efb29b4806a/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[New Zealand]] becomes the second country after [[Australia]] to authorize [[Medication|pharmaceutical-grade]] [[MDMA]] for severe [[post-traumatic stress disorder]], with [[Medsafe]] allowing two [[Mental health in New Zealand|psychiatrists]] to prescribe it alongside [[MDMA-assisted psychotherapy|psychotherapy]] in controlled clinical settings. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260904-new-zealand-approves-use-of-party-drug-mdma-to-treat-trauma (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cambodia–United States relations]]
**The [[Royal Cambodian Army]] announces that they will resume joint [[military exercise]]s with the [[United States Armed Forces|United States]] beginning in February 2027 after they were suspended in 2017. The exercise will be codenamed Exercise Angkor Sentinel. [https://apnews.com/article/cambodia-us-military-exercise-china-manet-colby-bffea503a189e25ee1d01d4a5764ee0a (AP)]
*The [[United Nations General Assembly]] adopts a [[United Nations resolution|resolution]] supporting the [[Equal Earth projection|Equal Earth]] [[map projection]] over the [[Mercator projection]], with 164 countries voting in favor, one against ([[United States and the United Nations|United States]]), and six abstaining. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/04/un-vote-world-map-mercator-equal-earth-africa (''The Guardian'')]
*[[European Union]] [[European Commissioner for Enlargement|enlargement chief]] [[Marta Kos]] cancels a visit to [[Serbia]] after a [[Government of Serbia|Serbian government]] plane took the remains of [[Trial of Ratko Mladić|convicted]] [[war crime|war criminal]] [[Ratko Mladić]] to [[Belgrade]] for his funeral. [https://apnews.com/article/serbia-mladic-eu-funeral-belgrade-vucic-96408e87f62243f7a81d2a3b8a8bafbe (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/eu-commissioner-kos-cancels-trip-serbia-after-planned-tribute-mladic-2026-09-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Killing of the Clancy children]]
**In the [[United States]], [[Massachusetts Superior Court]] associate justice [[William F. Sullivan]] declares a [[mistrial]] in Lindsay Clancy's [[Murder in United States law|murder]] trial after [[Juries in the United States|jurors]] were [[Hung jury|deadlocked]] following more than 38 hours of deliberations, with the panel split 11–1. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cm3v49dg61gxt (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/04/lindsay-clancy-mistrial (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**[[Mexico]]'s [[Mexican Navy|navy]], the [[Attorney General of Mexico|attorney general]], and the [[Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection]] seize approximately 16.8 tonnes of [[methamphetamine]] and dismantle three [[Clandestine chemistry|clandestine drug laboratories]] in [[Sinaloa]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/world/mexico-seizes-17-tons-of-amphetamines-in-sinaloa-govt-3000534 (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Mexican federal deputy]] [[Zenyazen Escobar García]] is found dead inside his vehicle in his home state of [[Veracruz]] with at least one gunshot wound. State prosecutors open an investigation without determining whether his death is [[Suicide in Mexico|suicide]] or [[homicide]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/09/05/world/asia-oceania/mexican-lawmaker-found-dead-with-gunshot-wound/2419000 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*A [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[regional trial court]] issues an arrest warrant for [[Vice President of the Philippines|vice president]] [[Sara Duterte]] on three counts of [[Death threat|grave threats]] against [[President of the Philippines|president]] [[Bongbong Marcos]], [[First Lady of the Philippines|first lady]] [[Liza Araneta Marcos]], and former [[Speaker of the House of Representatives of the Philippines|House speaker]] [[Martin Romualdez]], setting bail at [[Philippine peso|₱]]120,000 ([[US$]]2,000) per count. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/philippine-court-issues-warrant-vp-dutertes-arrest-in-grave-threats-case-2026-09-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[People's Police (China)|Police]] in [[Guangxi]], [[China]], arrest 52 [[Singaporeans]] over suspected involvement in illegal [[Pyramid scheme|pyramid-scheme]] activities as part of a broader [[Law enforcement in China|law-enforcement]] operation. [[Singapore]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Singapore)|foreign ministry]] says it is providing [[consular assistance]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/china-arrests-52-singaporeans-alleged-pyramid-scheme-activities-singapore-2026-09-04/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sri Lanka]]n [[Member of Parliament (Sri Lanka)|MP]] [[Namal Rajapaksa]] is arrested over alleged [[Corruption in Sri Lanka|corruption]] involving [[SriLankan Airlines]]' 2013 [[Airbus]] purchases. A [[Judiciary of Sri Lanka|court]] in [[Colombo]] remands him until September 18. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sri-lanka-ex-presidents-son-arrested-graft-charges-2026-09-04/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Tunisia]]n judge orders [[Mass media in Tunisia|journalist]] [[Mohamed Ali Yousfi]] detained on allegations of [[illicit enrichment]], [[money laundering]], and [[Criminal conspiracy|conspiracy]] after [[Tunisian National Guard|police]] arrest him outside [[Express FM]] in [[Tunis]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/tunisia-judge-orders-arrest-of-journalist-mohamed-yousfi/a-79040802 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Meloni government]]
**[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Giorgia Meloni]]'s government becomes the longest serving in [[Italy]] during the [[History of the Italian Republic|postwar]] era. [https://amp.dw.com/en/meloni-government-becomes-longest-serving-in-postwar-italy/a-78910642 (DW)]
*The remains of [[Omukama of Tooro|King]] [[Rukidi IV of Tooro|Rukidi IV]] of the [[Tooro Kingdom]] return to [[Uganda]] for his burial. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clylwgn8jk3o (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/body-king-oyo-nyimba-once-worlds-youngest-monarch-returns-uganda-burial-2026-09-04/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup]]
**The opening ceremony for the [[FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup]] is held in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]], with the defending champions [[United States women's national basketball team|United States]] defeating [[China women's national basketball team|China]] 94–61. [https://apnews.com/article/us-china-world-cup-score-9ff47b0711e2b4b5a36f3e051e568367 (AP)]
*[[Palestinian sports during the Gaza war]]
**[[Football in Palestine|Palestinian football]] resumes after nearly three years due to the [[Gaza war]], with the [[Palestinian Football Association]] launching a tournament involving more than 200 teams from [[Palestinian refugee camps|refugee camps]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260906-with-joy-and-grief-palestinian-football-marks-return (AFP via France 24)]
