{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=3|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war]], [[United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[Iranian Armed Forces|Iran's military]] launches [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|drones]] and [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|missiles]] on [[Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base]] in [[Kuwait]] and [[Al Minhad Air Base]] in the [[United Arab Emirates]], targeting [[United States military]] facilities and equipment to retaliate for the recent [[U.S.]] [[September 2026 United States strikes on Iran|bombardment]] of [[Iran]] that killed at least 19 people. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/middle-east/article/3366202/iran-targets-us-bases-kuwait-despite-warnings-trump (AFP via ''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[2026 Kuhestak wedding airstrike]]
****[[Vice President of the United States|U.S. vice president]] [[JD Vance]] says that [[United States|the country]] will investigate its military strike against a wedding in [[Bandar Sirik]] that killed five people. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/vance-us-investigating-strike-iran-wedding-very-fully (''Middle East Eye'')] [https://www.jpost.com/international/article-907552 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire]]
****[[Israel]] releases [[Lebanese prisoners in Israel|prisoner]] Malek Ghazi and hands him over to the [[Lebanese Armed Forces|Lebanese army]], the first release since the war started in March, as part of an effort to revive [[2026 Israel–Lebanon peace talks|peace talks]]. [https://apnews.com/article/lebanon-israel-prisoner-malek-ghazi-release-hezbollah-bfe8abeb4f713332a543e23dd9d2bba5 (AP)] [https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/israel-frees-lebanese-detainee-as-hopes-rise-of-reviving-stalled-rome-talks-3000348 (''Arab News'')]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[2026 Yemen offensive]]
****The [[Houthis]] launch an offensive in western [[Yemen]], clashing with the [[Yemeni Armed Forces]] and aiming to reach and cut the road linking [[Taiz]] to [[Al-Makha district]]. Fourteen [[balistic missile]]s and several [[drone warfare|drones]] are launched in Taiz and [[Hodeidah]]. At least 18 Houthi fighters and 13 government troops are killed in the clashes. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/3/houthi-fighters-clash-with-yemeni-government-forces-in-countrys-southwest (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo–Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kharkiv Oblast campaign (2024–present)|Kharkiv Oblast campaign]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] say they have captured several settlements in northeastern [[Kharkiv Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], encircling [[Ukrainian forces]]. [https://understandingwar.org/research/russia-ukraine/russian-offensive-campaign-assessment-september-3-2026/ (ISW)]
**The [[Security Service of Ukraine]] open fire against agents of the [[Main Directorate of Intelligence (Ukraine)|Main Directorate of Intelligence]] in [[Kyiv]] during a search at an apartment related to an arrest against a [[Russia]]n national fighting for Ukraine, wounding three people. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/03/zelenskyy-shootout-kyiv-between-ukrainian-spy-services-disgraceful- (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Sudanese refugee crisis]]
***The [[International Organization for Migration]] reports the first operation of a [[Voluntary return|voluntary repatriation]] flight for stranded migrants in [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]], since the war [[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|started]] three years ago. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318309 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[Colombia]]n [[Judiciary of Colombia|judge]] orders [[President of Colombia|president]] [[Abelardo de la Espriella]]'s government to suspend [[airstrike]]s on [[Guerrilla movements in Colombia|guerrilla]] camps in the [[Guaviare Department]] when [[National Intelligence Directorate (Colombia)|intelligence]] indicated that minors may be present, after recent bombings killed at least three teenagers. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260903-colombian-judge-bans-strikes-on-guerrillas-if-minors-are-present (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Insurgency in Cabo Delgado]]
**At least one person is killed and no less than 11 people are abducted by [[Islamic State – Mozambique Province|ISM]] militants in an attack on a hunting camp in [[Niassa Province]], [[Mozambique]]. [https://apnews.com/article/mozambique-south-africa-attack-niassa-cabo-delgado-4d14c1f705b0d106dbaeec8cef2bf8d9 (AP)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**Five people are killed and several other residents are abducted during a bandit attack in [[Kebbe]], [[Sokoto State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://dailypost.ng/2026/09/04/bandits-kill-five-abduct-several-residents-in-fresh-attack-on-sokoto-community/ (''Daily Post Nigeria'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Indonesia wildfires]]
**[[2026 East Malaysia haze]], [[Endangerment of orangutans]]
***Authorities in [[Indonesia]] rescue a mother [[orangutan]] and her baby from [[wildfire]] smoke on the island of [[Borneo]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260905-indonesia-rescues-second-orangutan-mother-and-baby-from-wildfire (AFP via RFI)] [https://www.theborneopost.com/2026/09/03/indonesia-rescues-orangutan-mother-and-baby-from-wildfire-haze/ (''The Borneo Post'')]
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**[[President of the United Arab Emirates|United Arab Emirates president]] [[Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan]] announces that [[United Arab Emirates|the country]] will deploy an emergency relief mission to [[Nepal]] to support people affected by the deadly floods and landslides. [https://gulfnews.com/uae/government/uae-sends-rescue-mission-to-nepal-after-deadly-floods-landslides-2-1.500662318 (''Gulf News'')]
*At least 37 people are killed after inhaling [[Petroleum industry in Nigeria|petroleum]] fumes while allegedly [[siphon]]ing fuel from an [[Gasoline theft|illegally tapped]] [[pipeline]] in [[Rivers State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260903-37-people-die-from-fumes-during-oil-pipeline-theft-in-nigeria-ngo (AFP via France 24)]
*Six crew members are referred to court as part of the investigation into the ship collision in the [[Sea of Marmara]] yesterday, while the search continues for the ten [[Turkey|Turkish]] crew members aboard the sunken MV ''Tuğberk İmamoğlu'' [[cargo ship]]. [https://www.bbc.com/turkce/articles/cx2z034d3pdo (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 East Malaysia haze]]
**[[Malaysia]]'s [[National Disaster Management Agency|disaster agency]], [[Malaysian Meteorological Department|meteorological agency]], and [[Royal Malaysian Air Force|air force]] launch [[cloud-seeding]] operations in [[Sarawak]] to reduce [[haze]] and increase [[water reserve]]s. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260903-malaysia-starts-cloud-seeding-to-help-clear-toxic-haze (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Aftermath of the Syrian civil war]]
**[[Syrian chemical weapons program]], [[Use of chemical weapons in the Syrian civil war]]
***Officials at a [[United Nations Security Council]] meeting say that [[Syria]] has started the process of destroying clandestine [[chemical weapon|chemical weapons]] from [[Fall of the Assad regime|former]] [[President of Syria|president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]]'s [[Presidency of Bashar al-Assad|regime]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/3/syria-begins-destroying-al-assad-era-chemical-weapons-materials (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/syria-begins-destroying-assad-era-chemical-weapons-2026-09-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Germany–Russia relations]]
**[[2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents]]
***[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian foreign minister]] [[Sergey Lavrov]] says that [[Russia]] will close [[Goethe-Institut]] [[cultural center]]s in [[Moscow]], [[Saint Petersburg]], and [[Yekaterinburg]] in response to [[Germany]] closing [[List of diplomatic missions of Russia|Russia's consulate]] in [[Bonn]] and the [[Russian House (Berlin)|Russian House]] in [[Berlin]] following the [[drone attack]]s at [[Leipzig/Halle Airport]] last month. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-germany-goethe-institute-close-airport-drone-1e72ac4fd59f4a1f44859bd2e78dbde6 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Tacloban school shooting]], [[2026 Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting]]
**The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Department of Education (Philippines)|education department]] initiates nationwide [[school safety]] drills to prepare students and staff for armed intruders, involving [[Philippine National Police|police]] and [[emergency responders]] after two [[school shooting]] incidents. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260903-philippines-holds-drills-to-safeguard-students-from-armed-intruders (AFP via France 24)]
*A [[Judiciary of Russia|court]] in [[Moscow]], [[Russia]], places [[children's hospice]] founder [[Lida Moniava]] under judicial supervision, imposing a nightly curfew, [[Internet censorship in Russia|internet ban]], and contact restrictions over a 2023 post prosecutors said spread [[Russian disinformation|false information]] about [[Russian Armed Forces|the military]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260903-russia-slaps-curfew-on-charity-director-over-army-criticism (AFP via France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025–2026 United States redistricting]]
**In the [[United States]], the [[Supreme Court of Missouri]] blocks the use of a [[2025 Missouri redistricting|congressional map]] intended to favor [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]], despite the map having already been used for [[2026 United States House of Representatives elections in Missouri|primary elections]] in the state. A [[2026 Missouri Proposition A|referendum]] on the 2025 map will appear on the ballot for the November election in [[Missouri|the state]]. [https://apnews.com/article/redistricting-congress-missouri-trump-gerrymandering-5034c87f2161baa933ea337408e4c5b4 (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/sep/03/missouri-supreme-court-trump (''The Guardian'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[AI boom]]
**[[OpenAI]] releases [[GPT-6 Astra]], the latest version of [[ChatGPT]]. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/technology/2026/9/4/openai-begins-rollout-of-new-powerful-ai-model-gpt-6-astra-0838 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)] [https://www.axios.com/2026/09/03/openai-astra-gpt-6-agi-brockman (''Axios'')]
*The ''[[BepiColombo]]'' begins its final mission to [[Mercury (planet)|Mercury]], eight years after its launch by the [[European Space Agency]] and the [[JAXA|Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency]]. [https://www.space.com/space-exploration/missions/a-new-mission-starting-today-8-years-after-launch-bepicolombo-begins-mercury-arrival (Space.com)]
*[[NASA]] discovers a 10–sided pattern on the south pole of [[Saturn]] using its [[Hubble Space Telescope]] from the [[Goddard Space Flight Center]] in [[Maryland]], [[United States]]. [https://thepeninsulaqatar.com/article/03/09/2026/saturn-has-a-new-mystery-scientists-discover-giant-10-sided-shape-at-south-pole (''The Peninsula'')] [https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/09/260903064229.htm (''ScienceDaily'')]

'''Sports'''
*In [[association football]], the [[French Football Federation]] upholds [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]]'s [[relegation]] to [[Régional 1]], the sixth tier of the [[French football league system]], rejecting the club's request for reinstatement in [[Championnat National 2|National 2]] following its exclusion from national competitions over financial concerns. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260903-bordeaux-facing-sixth-tier-football-after-french-federation-upholds-relegation (AFP via France 24)]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=2|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**[[Israeli settler violence]]
***[[Palestine|Palestinian]] officials say two teenagers were killed during an incident involving [[Israeli settlers]] and [[Israeli Ground Forces|soldiers]] in [[Al-Mughayyir, Ramallah|al-Mughayyir]], [[Ramallah and al-Bireh Governorate]], [[West Bank]]. The villiage council states that the Palestinian teenagers were killed when they were trying to prevent the Israeli settlers from stealing livestock. [[Israel]]'s [[Israel Defense Forces|military]] says troops shot [[Stone throwing|stone-throwers]] while protecting an Israeli civilian and [[Israel Police|police]] retrieving livestock. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj6482r6yl4o (BBC News)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[2026 SBU{{endash}}HUR Kyiv shootout]]
***In [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]], the [[Security Service of Ukraine]] and [[Defence Intelligence of Ukraine]] (HUR) have a shootout, injuring three HUR officers. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/3/ukrainian-intel-agencies-in-kyiv-firefight-what-happened-and-why (Al Jazeera)] [https://kyivindependent.com/ukraine-prevents-fsb-plot-against-russian-opposition-figure/ (''Kyiv Independent'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[War crimes in the Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|War crimes in the Sudanese civil war]]
***The [[World Food Programme]] reports that an [[airstrike]] hit two [[United Nations|UN]] food aid trucks in [[Dilling, South Kordofan|Dilling]], [[South Kordofan]], [[Sudan]], over the weekend, destroying emergency supplies. [https://www.arabnews.com/middle-east/two-un-aid-trucks-destroyed-in-sudan-attack-wfp-3000264 (AFP via ''Arab News'')] [https://sudantribune.com/article/318242 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**Twenty-one insurgents and six Pakistani personnel, including five security forces and a [[Pakistan Customs|customs]] official, are killed in separate [[shootout]]s across multiple [[Districts of Pakistan|districts]] in [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/2026635 (''Dawn'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**The [[Stock market index|global stock index]] rises following recent declines amidst the war in [[Iran]] including [[September 2026 United States strikes on Iran|renewed tensions]] with the [[Japanese yen]] gaining against the [[United States dollar]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-wrapup-1-2026-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[De Nederlandsche Bank|central bank]] reallocates 86 tonnes of [[gold reserve]]s from [[Ottawa]], [[Canada]], and [[New York City]], [[United States]], to [[London]], [[United Kingdom]], increasing the share held there to 32.1%, citing "increasing [[Geopolitics|geopolitical]] unrest". [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260902-dutch-shift-86-tonnes-of-gold-from-us-canada-to-uk (AFP via France 24)] [https://en.sedaily.com/international/2026/09/02/dutch-central-bank-shifts-86-tons-of-gold-to-london (''Seoul Economic Daily'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Dahab-Nuweiba bus crash]]
**At least 22 people, including ten [[Jordanians]], are killed and 28 others are injured in a bus accident in [[South Sinai]], [[Egypt]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260902-bus-crash-in-egypt-s-sinai-kills-22-including-10-jordanians (AFP via France 24)]
*The MV ''Tuğberk İmamoğlu'' [[cargo ship]] sinks in the [[Sea of Marmara|Marmara Sea]] after a collision with an [[oil tanker]], leaving ten people missing. [https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/02/cargo-ship-with-10-crew-sinks-off-istanbul-after-collision-maritime-authorities-say (Euronews)]
*At least 13 people are killed and five others sustain critical injuries after two [[minivan]]s collide head-on in [[Greater Accra]], [[Ghana]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260902/f0109d4b64f849d7a13c7f8997cc5e38/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Five people are killed and 20 others injured after a passenger bus collides with a tanker truck on the [[National Highway 39 (India)|National Highway 39]] in [[Rewa District]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/mp-highway-crash-5-killed-20-hurt-after-bus-collides-with-bulker-pm-modi-mourns-deaths/articleshow/133715684.cms (''Times of India'')]
*An explosion at the [[Augsburg Hauptbahnhof|Augsburg train station]] in [[Swabia]], [[Germany]], injures two people. The cause is unknown. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2026/09/02/at-least-two-people-injured-in-explosion-at-german-train-station-police-say (Euronews)]
*A crew member is killed, six others are missing, and one is rescued when a [[tugboat]] capsizes and sinks off the coast of [[Busan]], [[South Korea]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-korea-tugboat-sinks-busan-crew-search-842629f4f2721a1b71d8e7737bfc6ecc (AP)] 

'''International relations'''
*[[Norway–Russia relations]], [[Russian shadow fleet]]
**[[Norway]] seizes the [[Russia]]n-owned ''[[Professor Molchanov]]'' ship near [[Svalbard]] to enforce a [[US$]]4.22 billion compensation award owed to [[Ukraine]]'s [[Naftogaz]] for assets expropriated in [[Crimea]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/3/norway-seizes-russian-ship-in-arctic-over-crimea-compensation-claim (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents]]
**Following the [[Drone warfare|drone attacks]] at [[Leipzig/Halle Airport]] last month, [[National security of Germany|German security]] authorities are focusing on several suspects with ties to [[Russia]]. According to investigations by the [[Norddeutscher Rundfunk|NDR]], [[Westdeutscher Rundfunk|WDR]], and [[Süddeutsche Zeitung|SZ]], the suspects are two men from [[Belarus]] and [[Lithuania]] who are also said to hold [[Russian passport]]s. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20260902-eu-summons-russia-envoys-eyes-sanctions-after-germany-drone-attack (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-says-russia-behind-attempted-drone-attack-at-leipzig-airport/a-78584589 (DW)]
*[[Birthright citizenship in the United States]]
**[[United States federal judge|U.S. federal judge]] [[Deborah Boardman]] of [[Maryland]]'s [[United States District Court for the District of Maryland|district court]] blocks an attempt by the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] from implementing an [[executive order]] aimed at ending [[Jus soli|birthright citizenship]] in [[United States|the country]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/02/us/politics/judge-trump-birthright-citizenship.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-judge-blocks-trumps-newest-order-limiting-birthright-citizenship-2026-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Malta|Maltese]] [[jury]] acquits businessman [[Yorgen Fenech]] of [[complicity]] in the 2017 [[car-bomb]] killing of journalist [[Daphne Caruana Galizia]] and of [[criminal association]], finding him not guilty by an 8–1 vote. [https://www.npr.org/2026/09/02/nx-s1-5954420/daphne-caruana-galizia-case-yorgen-fenech-acquitted-malta (AP via NPR)]
*Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and six others are injured in a [[Mass shootings in the United States|mass shooting]] in [[Loring Park, Minneapolis|Loring Park]], [[Minneapolis]], United States. [https://apnews.com/article/minneapolis-shooting-police-wounded-3ff6046fde9edd1c764701c10aa4a1ac (AP)] [https://www.dw.com/en/us-3-dead-including-suspect-in-minneapolis-shooting/a-78815092 (DW)]
*[[Digital rights]] organization SHARE Foundation documents at least 14 [[Serbia]]n students and [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] activists targeted with [[Pegasus (spyware)|Pegasus]] or NoviSpy [[spyware]] in 2026, while [[Citizen Lab]] confirms Pegasus infection in at least one case. [https://www.ft.com/content/c9c3a0ef-98d5-4aeb-9d20-e6250d6fcf99?syn-25a6b1a6=1 (''Financial Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Estonian presidential election]]
** [[Chancellor of Justice (Estonia)|Chancellor of Justice]] [[Ülle Madise]], the only candidate, is elected by the [[Riigikogu]] as [[President of Estonia|President]] of [[Estonia]]. She will be sworn into office on October 12, succeeding [[Alar Karis]]. [https://news.err.ee/1610126071/estonia-elects-new-president (ERR)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/estonia-elects-human-rights-ombudsman-madise-its-next-president-2026-09-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2027 U.S. Open Cup]]
**In [[association football]], [[Major League Soccer]] announces that all 27 teams from the [[Soccer in the United States|United States]] will return to the [[U.S. Open Cup]] beginning in 2027, making it the first full participation in the tournament since [[2023 U.S. Open Cup|2023]]. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49795119/us-mls-teams-make-full-return-open-cup-2027 (ESPN)] [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/01/mls-us-open-cup-participation (''The Guardian'')]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=09|day=1|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[September 2026 United States strikes on Iran]]
*****The [[United States]] carries out additional [[airstrike]]s against [[Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corp]] (IRGC) targets in [[Iran]], in response to recent attempted attacks on commercial shipping vessels in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and on [[U.S. troops]] in [[Middle East|the region]], according to the [[United States Central Command|U.S. Central Command]]. Five members of the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force|IRGC Aerospace Force]] are killed in [[Kermanshah]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/9/2/iran-war-live-us-bombs-iran-tehran-retaliates-on-gulf-neighbours-jordan?update=4909793 (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj06q4ynpmjo (BBC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/01/politics/us-military-strikes-iran?utm_source=cnn_Breaking_News&utm_medium=email (CNN)]
***[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
****[[President of Iran|Iranian president]] [[Masoud Pezeshkian]] says that [[Iran|his country]] is ready to return to the [[Islamabad Memorandum]] signed in June if the [[United States]] does the same amidst renewed fighting between the two countries. [https://fortune.com/2026/09/01/iran-ceasefire-hormuz-japan/ (''Fortune'')]
***[[2026 Kuhestak wedding airstrike]]
****[[Iranian state media]] reports that five civilians were killed and 63 more were wounded at a [[wedding]] party at a home in [[Kuhestak]], [[Hormozgan province]], during an American airstrike against [[Iranian military]] targets. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/2/iran-says-us-strikes-hit-a-wedding-party-in-sirik-killing-five (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***Four people are killed in [[Israel]]i strikes during a ground operation in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] says that [[Israeli forces]] captured a senior [[Hamas]] internal security official in the operation. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-israeli-strikes-kill-four-in-operation-to-seize-hamas-figure-in-gaza-officials (AFP via France 24)]
**[[War against the Islamic State]], [[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
***[[Abu Hudhayfah al-Ansari]], the [[spokesperson]] for the [[Islamic State]], is killed during a security operation by the [[Yemeni Armed Forces]]. [https://www.voiceofemirates.com/en/politics/2026/09/01/a-joint-security-operation-resulted-in-the-death-of-the-isis-spokesman-in-yemen/ (Voice of Emirates)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***[[Government of Ukraine|Ukrainian officials]] say that [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile and [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|drone]] attacks on [[Kyiv]] and surrounding areas killed at least 12 people, including an [[Indian diaspora|Indian national]], and injure dozens, while damaging residential buildings and other civilian [[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure|infrastructure]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/indian-among-12-killed-in-russian-attack-on-kyiv-says-ukraines-zelensky-11985931 (NDTV)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[car bomb]] explodes outside a police station in [[Norte de Santander Department]], [[Colombia]], killing a person and wounding eleven more. [https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/one-dead-and-eleven-injured-in-terrorist-attack-on-police-station-in-colombia/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX09XRUZWQzcwMDE2MDkyNjMwMDE (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The 75,000-seater [[KJC King Dome|Kingdome]], built by the [[Christianity in the Philippines|Christian]] sect [[Kingdom of Jesus Christ (church)|Kingdom of Jesus Christ]], opens in [[Davao City]], [[Philippines]], becoming the [[List of indoor arenas by capacity|largest indoor arena in the world]]. It surpasses the 55,000-seater [[Philippine Arena]] in [[Bulacan]]. [https://mb.com.ph/2026/09/02/davao-city-council-cites-kingdome-as-emerging-city-landmark (''Manila Bulletin'')] [https://mindanews.com/top-stories/2026/09/kojcs-75000-seater-kingdome-opens-nearly-2-years-after-siege-that-led-to-quiboloys-arrest/ (''MindaNews'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Senegal hidden debt scandal]]
**The [[International Monetary Fund]] reaches a staff-level agreement with [[Senegal]] on a new [[US$]]2.2 billion, 36-month loan program supporting [[economic reform]]s after an earlier arrangement was suspended over previously unreported [[government debt]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-imf-reaches-agreement-with-senegal-on-new-2-2-bn-loan-programme (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Ghana]] begins requiring [[Artisanal mining|artisanal]] [[doré bar]]s purchased by privately financed [[Gold as an investment|gold buyers]] to undergo [[Mining industry of Ghana|domestic refining]] before export, with [[Ghana GoldBod|GoldBod]] considering export applications only after processing at approved refineries. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/ghana-bars-unrefined-artisanal-gold-dore-exports-september-1-2026-08-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Japan]] eases [[Japanese labour law#Working time|overtime enforcement]] by ending pressure on [[List of companies of Japan|companies]] with special labor-management agreements to keep monthly [[overtime]] below 45 hours, as businesses face [[Labor market of Japan|labor shortages]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-japan-to-relax-overtime-regulation-under-workaholic-pm (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**[[Nepal–South Korea relations]]
***[[South Korea]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (South Korea)|foreign ​ministry]] announces that the country will deploy a 44-member [[Incident response team|emergency relief team]] to [[Nepal]] to support [[Search and rescue|search-and-rescue]] operations after [[flash flood|flash floods]] hit the [[South Asia]]n country. [https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10858444 (''The Korea Herald'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-says-send-disaster-relief-team-nepal-2026-09-01/ (Reuters)]
**The [[Nepali Army]] reports that around 119 people have been rescued. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/01/briton-among-119-more-people-rescued-in-nepal-after-flash-floods (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2026 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**Tropical Storm Edouard makes landfall on the [[Gulf Coast of the United States|Gulf Coast]] of the [[United States]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/31/weather/tropical-storm-edouard-texas-louisiana-path-climate?utm_source=cnn_Breaking_News&utm_medium=email (CNN)]
*Seven people are killed and 13 others are injured when a speeding passenger [[van]], with an [[Ipil, Zamboanga Sibugay|Ipil]]–[[Pagadian]] route, crashes into a [[motorcycle]] and a wing van in [[Dumalinao]], [[Zamboanga del Sur]], [[Philippines]]. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2297371/zamboanga-del-sur-highway-crash-death-toll-climbs-to-7-13-hurt (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*Four people are killed and more than ten others are injured when a car crashes into a gathering of [[Government of Iran|government]] and [[Iranian Armed Forces|military]] supporters in [[Mashhad]], [[Razavi Khorasan province|Razavi Khorasan]], [[Iran]]. [[Iranian Traffic Police|Traffic police]] arrest the driver and say the incident was unintentional. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/car-hits-pro-government-gathering-iran-killing-four-2026-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*Six [[pilgrims]] are killed and 14 others sustain serious injuries after a pickup truck carrying devotees collides with a truck along an expressway in [[Palwal district]], [[Haryana]], [[India]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/gurgaon/6-devotees-killed-14-injured-after-pickup-truck-rams-into-parked-truck-on-kmp-expressway-in-haryana/amp_articleshow/133668708.cms (''The Times of India'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*The [[Department of Conservation (New Zealand)|New Zealand Conservation Department]] reports that the amount of critically endangered [[kākāpō]] have reached 325 in [[New Zealand|the country]] following the addition of 90 chicks, exceeding 300 for the first time in 75 years. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/sep/01/record-breeding-worlds-heaviest-parrot-nz-endangered-kakapo (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/kakapo-parrot-baby-boom-worlds-heaviest-bird-rise-new-zealand-rcna595479 (NBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Germany–Russia relations]], [[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[2026 Leipzig Airport drone incidents]]
***[[Germany]] raises [[National security of Germany|its threat assessment]] to "high", orders the closure of [[Russia]]'s [[List of diplomatic missions of Russia|consulate]] in [[Bonn]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia]], and the [[Russian House (Berlin)|Russian House]] in [[Berlin]], and tightens [[Border control|entry control]]s for Russian nationals after attributing the [[Drone warfare|drone attack]]s at [[Leipzig/Halle Airport]], [[Saxony]], last month to Russia. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/09/01/europe/leipzig-drone-germany-russia-intl (CNN)]
*[[Reactions to the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[Peru]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Peru)|foreign ministry]] says that the country has cut off ties with [[Iran]], accusing it of escalating the [[war]] in the [[Middle East]]. [https://apnews.com/article/peru-iran-relaciones-diplomaticas-5c2f381543084e3745542995b55e1d54 (AP <small>in Spanish</small>)] [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/09/02/peru-says-it-cut-ties-with-iran-accusing-tehran-of-escalating-mideast-war (Al-Arabiya)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Assassination of Charlie Kirk]]
**An [[Judiciary of the United States|American judge]] rules that the case against Tyler James Robinson, accused of [[Murder in United States law|murdering]] [[Politics of the United States|political]] activist [[Charlie Kirk]] in September 2025, can [[United States criminal procedure|go to trial]], citing sufficient [[probable cause]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj4jn9q7evpo (BBC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/01/us/live-news/charlie-kirk-tyler-robinson-hearing (CNN)]
*[[LGBTQ rights in the United States]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Department of Justice]] files a lawsuit against [[Kansas City, Kansas Public Schools|the public schools district]] of [[Kansas City, Kansas|Kansas City]], [[Kansas]], over its policies that allow [[transgender]] students to share their [[preferred name]], [[gender]], and [[pronoun]]s with school staff. [https://www.kcur.org/education/2026-09-01/justice-department-sues-kansas-city-kansas-public-schools-transgender-policies (KCUR)] [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-sues-kansas-school-district-aiding-transgender-students-transitions-2026-09-01/ (Reuters)]
*A [[Honduras|Honduran]] judge dismisses a [[Corruption in Honduras|corruption]] case against former [[President of Honduras|president]] [[Juan Orlando Hernández]], ruling that he neither authorized nor managed the public funds allegedly diverted to [[Campaign finance|finance]] his [[2013 Honduran general election|2013 presidential campaign]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-honduran-judge-drops-corruption-charges-against-ex-leader-hernandez (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Mexico|Mexican]] musician Jonathan Meléndez of the band [[Camilo Séptimo]], his pregnant wife, their three-year-old daughter, a [[domestic worker]], and their pet dog are shot dead in a penthouse outside [[Mexico City]], while Meléndez's six-year-old son is found unharmed. Prosecutors arrest two suspects. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/mexican-musician-family-members-slain-gruesome-shooting-upscale-penthouse-2026-09-02/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Death and state funeral of Harald V]]
**[[Haakon VIII]] takes the oath as [[King of Norway]] before the [[Storting]] following the death of his father, [[Harald V]]. His daughter, [[Ingrid Alexandra, Crown Princess of Norway|Ingrid Alexandra]], takes the oath as [[Crown Princess of Norway|Crown Princess]]. [https://apnews.com/article/norway-king-haakon-oath-allegiance-constitution-harald-0c4e5de3b7bcc7069af52500e34ec86c (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/norways-new-king-swear-oath-before-parliament-after-haralds-death-2026-09-01/ (Reuters)]
*[[Nicaragua]]'s [[National Assembly (Nicaragua)|National Assembly]] approves on [[first reading]] a [[Constitution of Nicaragua|constitutional]] amendment barring [[List of political parties in Nicaragua|opposition parties]] from [[Elections in Nicaragua|elections]] and extending [[Co-presidents of Nicaragua|presidential]] and other elected [[Term limits in Nicaragua|terms]] from six to seven years. A second legislative vote is required for [[ratification]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/nicaraguan-congress-passes-ortega-backed-reform-excluding-opposition-elections-2026-09-02/ (Reuters)]
*Former [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|prime minister]] [[Keir Starmer]] [[resignation from the House of Commons of the United Kingdom|resigns]] as a [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|member]] of the [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|House of Commons]] for [[List of stewards of the Chiltern Hundreds|his appointment to the Chiltern Hundreds]]; a [[2026 Holborn and St Pancras by-election|by-election will be held]] to fill his parlimentary seat of [[Holborn and St Pancras]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/1/ousted-uk-prime-minister-keir-starmer-to-quit-domestic-politics (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgy4258kgyo (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Syria and weapons of mass destruction]]
**The [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] reports that [[Syria]]'s [[Presidency of Bashar al-Assad|former government]] under [[Bashar al-Assad]] failed to declare [[nuclear material]] and [[Nuclear power plant|facilities]], confirming that infrastructure at [[Deir ez-Zor]] is consistent with an unfinished [[nuclear reactor]] and identifying about 73 tonnes of [[natural uranium]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-syria-site-infrastructure-consistent-with-nuclear-reactor-iaea (AFP via France 24)]
*The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Turkey)|Turkish foreign ministry]] reports that [[Turkey]] has joined the U.S.-led [[Artemis Accords]], becoming the 71st country to do so. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/science-technology/turkiye-joins-nasa-s-artemis-accords-as-71st-signatory-to-peaceful-space-exploration-pact/4043176 (AA)] [https://www.firstpost.com/world/turkey-becomes-71st-country-to-join-us-led-artemis-accords-for-space-exploration-14042345.html (''Firstpost'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026–27 NBA season]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] announces that the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] had [[Los Angeles Clippers salary cap scandal|violated]] the [[NBA salary cap|league salary cap]] by signing [[Kawhi Leonard]] in 2022 via a series of external dealings. Penalties include fines of [[US$]]30 million for the Clippers and $700,000 for Leonard, the loss of the Clippers' [[Draft (sports)|first-round picks]] in each [[NBA draft|draft]] from 2029 to 2033, and a one-year suspension for Clippers owner [[Steve Ballmer]]. [https://tribune.net.ph/2026/09/03/nba-cracks-whip-on-clippers-over-salary-cap-row (AFP via ''Daily Tribune'')] [https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49806356/nba-announces-punishments-clippers-kawhi-probe (ESPN)]
*In [[baseball]], the [[Los Angeles Angels]] of the [[Major League Baseball|MLB]] are sold to [[Stan Kroenke]] of [[Kroenke Sports & Entertainment]] for an unspecified price, ending 23 years of ownership by [[Arte Moreno]]. The deal is pending regulatory review and is expected to be complete by 2027. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/stan-kroenke-controlling-stake-los-angeles-angels.html (CNBC)] [https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/kroenke-reaches-deal-add-angels-sports-portfolio-2026-09-01/ (Reuters)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=31|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] (IRGC) says that a [[Oil tanker#The supertanker era|supertanker]] caught fire after hitting two [[naval mine|naval mines]] in the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. The IRGC accuses the [[United States]] of responsibility for the attack, which the [[United States Central Command]] on an [[X (social network)|X]] post denies. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/aug/31/us-iran-israel-hormuz-oil-donald-trump-larak-kharg-island-uae-jordan-latest-news-updates?CMP=share_btn_url&page=with%3Ablock-6a957d358f089f2cda79ab60#block-6a957d358f089f2cda79ab60 (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2656391/amp (Reuters via ''Arab News'')]
****[[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] shipping company [[Bahri (company)|Bahri]] says that two [[Filipino seamen|Filipino crew members]] were killed after unidentified [[projectile]]s struck the oil tanker ''SIDR'' while it transited the Strait of Hormuz. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/9/2/two-filipinos-killed-in-attack-on-saudi-oil-tanker-in-hormuz-shipping-firm-1702 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
***[[United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] defense ministry reports that an [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|Iranian drone]] has been intercepted over the country's airspace. Additionally, [[Islamic Republic of Iran Army|Iran's army]] says that they have attacked the [[Al Minhad Air Base]], which the UAE denies. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-us-war-uea-august-31-2026-9f34873bad9a928574c36ee984c3f96b (AP)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israel]]i attacks across the [[Gaza Strip]] kill ⁠at least five people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/31/israeli-air-strikes-on-gaza-kill-at-least-five-people (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Aerial warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***[[Ukraine]] tightens security measures for [[Kyiv]]'s [[Transport in Kyiv|public transport]], [[Education in Ukraine|schools]], and [[Verkhovna Rada|parliament]] amid increased [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] attacks, including restrictions on large [[School assembly|school gatherings]], possible [[remote learning]], and expanded [[Points of Invincibility|shelter arrangements]]. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/world/3311733/kyiv-orders-heightened-security-amid-intense-russian-drone-strikes (AFP via ''Bangkok Post'')]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**Twelve civilians are killed in an attack by alleged armed [[People's Defence Force (Myanmar)|People's Defence Force]] members after they claim to have entered a village in [[Mahlaing Township]], [[Mandalay Region]], [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.mdn.gov.mm/en/12-civilians-slain-brutal-pdf-attack (Myanmar Digital News)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[car bomb]] outside a [[National Police of Colombia|police]] station in [[Los Patios]], [[Norte de Santander Department|Norte de Santander]], [[Colombia]], kills one civilian and injures 11 others, including two officers. Police attribute the attack to the [[National Liberation Army (Colombia)|National Liberation Army]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-car-bomb-at-colombian-police-station-kills-one-injures-11 (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**A car bomb outside a [[National Guard (Mexico)|police]] station in [[Ojocaliente, Zacatecas]], [[México]], leaves ten people injured. Authorities arrest one suspect related to the attack. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/mexico-security-chief-cites-cartel-dispute-in-zacatecas-car-bomb/4047889 (AA)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Dale Sanders (hiker)|Dale Sanders]] reclaims his record of being the oldest person to hike the entire [[Appalachian Trail]], one of the world's longest [[List of long-distance trails in the United States|hiking-only trails]], after completing it at age 91. [https://apnews.com/article/appalachian-trail-oldest-hiker-grey-beard-fd7a9a735c2cc1d31412535a2d36f6d8 (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**It is reported that [[Head teacher|school principal]] Rajendra Dawadi saved over 900 students and 16 faculty members at the Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in [[Bidur]], [[Nuwakot District|Nuwakot]] [[List of districts of Nepal|District]], [[Nepal]], 10 minutes before [[flash flood|flash floods]] hit the area last week. [https://apnews.com/article/nepal-flash-floods-school-principal-rajendra-dawadi-de0b24519de6514dd150737c2a729d97 (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/last-minute-flood-warning-saved-over-900-nepal-students-school-head-says-2026-08-31/ (Reuters)]
**The death toll from the flash floods in Nepal has reached past 950. Additionally, hundreds are reported to be feared stuck in [[hydropower]] tunnels in wake of the floods. [https://apnews.com/article/nepal-tibet-china-flash-floods-744fe6e15ae7751e15efcd6dff70170c (AP)] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/nepal-tibet-flood-rescue-9.7326270 (CBC)]
*[[2026 Grand Canyon flood]]
**The death toll from the flash flood in [[Grand Canyon National Park]], [[Arizona]], [[United States]], last Saturday rises to two, while the number of people missing falls from more than 20 to one after [[United States Park Rangers|park rangers]] locate most of those previously unaccounted for. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260831-heavy-rain-at-grand-canyon-after-flood-kills-2-dozen-missing (AFP via France 24)]
*[[2026 Indonesia wildfires]]
**The [[Mount Sinabung]] [[stratovolcano]] in [[North Sumatra]], [[Indonesia]], erupts, sending ash 3,500 meters into the air. Residents and visitors around Lake Lau Kawar are ordered to evacuate. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/indonesias-mount-sinabung-erupts-spewing-ash-3-500-meters-into-sky/4042457 (AA)] [https://en.antaranews.com/amp/news/429175/mount-sinabung-raised-to-alert-level-after-3500-meter-ash-eruption (Antara News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The total amount of cases of [[ebola]] in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] exceeds 6,000. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/8/31/over-6000-ebola-cases-confirmed-in-drc-as-death-toll-nears-3000 (Al Jazeera)]
*A data from the [[International Methane Emissions Observatory#Methane Alert and Response System (MARS)|Methane Alert and Response System]] reports that [[Turkmenistan]] has started the process of clearing [[methane]] [[Methane leak|leaks]] from [[Oil and natural gas refining in Turkmenistan|its oil and gas facilities]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/aug/31/turkmenistan-methane-leaks-un-alerts-mars (''The Guardian'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2026 Bishkek SCO summit]]
**The 26th [[Shanghai Cooperation Organisation]] summit is held in [[Bishkek]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], which coincides with the country's [[Independence Day (Kyrgyzstan)|Independence Day]] and the opening ceremony of the [[2026 World Nomad Games|2026]] [[World Nomad Games]]. [https://timesca.com/kyrgyzstan-hosts-sco-summit-as-bloc-marks-25-years/ (''The Times of Central Asia'')] [https://english.news.cn/20260901/45d53fa50821414f97f62777866497fc/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Greece–Israel relations]], [[2020s European rearmament]]
**[[Israel]] and [[Greece]] sign a {{Euro}}3 billion (US$3.48 billion) arms export deal that will enable the [[Ministry of Defense (Israel)|Israeli defense ministry]] to build the "Achilles Shield", a multi-layered air defense array similar to the [[Iron Dome]], made entirely by [[Defense industry of Israel|Israeli systems]], including [[David's Sling]], [[SPYDER]], and [[Barak MX]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/israel-signs-3-billion-arms-export-deal-with-greece/a-78572062 (DW)] [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-907112 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[India–Pakistan wars and conflicts]]
**The [[Permanent Court of Arbitration]] in [[The Hague]], [[Netherlands]], orders [[India]] to comply with the [[Indus Waters Treaty]] and restrict work on two [[Hydroelectric power in India|hydroelectric projects]] that could violate it. India rejects the ruling and maintains that the treaty remains suspended. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260831-tribunal-says-india-cannot-withdraw-from-water-treaty-with-pakistan (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Italy–Spain relations]], [[2026 Ceuta migrant crisis]]
**[[Prime Minister of Italy|Italian prime minister]] [[Giorgia Meloni]] announces that [[Italy]] will extend its suspension of the [[Schengen Area|Schengen]] [[Schengen Agreement|free movement agreement]] with [[Spain]] for another 15 days in response to the [[migrant crisis]] event at the [[Ceuta]] [[Ceuta border fence|border fence]] with [[Morocco]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/italy-extends-border-curbs-with-spain-month-after-migrant-rush-2026-08-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in South Korea]], [[Unification Church and politics]]
**A [[South Korea]]n [[Judiciary of South Korea|court]] sentences [[Unification Church]] leader [[Hak Ja Han]] to two years in prison for [[bribing]] officials, including former [[First Lady of South Korea|first lady]] [[Kim Keon Hee]], in an effort to obtain [[Politics of South Korea|policy]] favors. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260831-south-korea-court-gives-unification-church-leader-2-years-prison-1 (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-court-finds-unification-church-leader-han-guilty-2026-08-31/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kidnapping of Shelly Kittleson]]
**A [[Judiciary of Iraq|judiciary]] in [[Iraq]] sentences [[Kata'ib Hezbollah]] member Amir Rahim Jabbar to 15 years in prison for his role in the kidnapping of [[Americans|American]] journalist [[Shelly Kittleson]]. [https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5313105-iraq-sentences-kidnapper-us-journalist-15-years-prison (''Asharq Al Awsat'')]
*[[Murder of Tupac Shakur]]
**A [[Juries in the United States|jury]] in [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], United States, finds former [[Crips]] [[Gangs in the United States|gang]] leader Duane Davis guilty of [[first-degree murder]] for orchestrating the [[Murder in United States law|murder]] of rapper [[Tupac Shakur]] during a [[drive-by shooting]] in [[Paradise, Nevada|Paradise]] in 1996. [https://abcnews.com/US/jury-begins-deliberating-trial-murder-tupac-shakur/story?id=136099547 (ABC News)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c24j5192j7jo (BBC News)]
*A [[Tribunal of first instance (Belgium)|tribunal of first instance]] in [[Brussels]], [[Belgium]], orders [[biometrics]] company [[Semlex Group|Semlex]] and 13 other defendants to stand trial over alleged [[Corruption in Belgium|corruption]], [[money laundering]], and [[tax fraud]] linked to a [[Democratic Republic of the Congo passport|passport]] contract in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/belgian-court-orders-trial-corruption-money-laundering-linked-congo-passport-2026-09-01/ (Reuters)]
*A suspect is arrested in relation to a [[mass shooting]] over the weekend at a rave in [[Aarau]], [[Aargau]], [[Switzerland]], which killed a woman and injured five other people. [https://www.dw.com/en/swiss-police-arrest-man-over-deadly-rave-shooting/a-78575110 (DW)]
*[[2026 Times Square stabbing attack]]
**A woman stabs two people in [[Times Square]], [[New York City]], U.S., killing a [[Bank of America]] vice president and injuring another person, before [[New York City Police Department|police]] fatally shot her after she refused commands to drop her knives. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260901-two-dead-after-stabbing-in-new-york-s-times-square (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/1/bank-of-america-vice-president-identified-as-killed-in-times-square-attack (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025–2026 Kosovo political deadlock]]
**[[Kosovo]]'s [[Vetëvendosje]] and [[Democratic League of Kosovo|Democratic League]] parties agree to support former [[Constitutional Court of Kosovo|Constitutional Court]] judge [[Bekim Sejdiu]] for [[President of Kosovo|president]], potentially ending nearly two years of [[political deadlock]] and enabling the formation of a new [[Government of Kosovo|government]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/kosovo-parties-strike-deal-elect-president-breaking-deadlock-2026-08-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[AI boom]]
**[[Adobe Inc.]] reaches a [[US$]]4 billion deal to offer free access to [[Artificial intelligence|AI]] tools in [[Saudi Arabia]] with its [[Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (Saudi Arabia)|Ministry of Communications and Information Technology]] and [[Humain]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/adobe-offer-free-access-ai-tools-saudi-arabia-4-billion-deal-2026-08-31/ (Reuters)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=30|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan]]
****[[Iran]] launches [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|ballistic missile]]s at [[List of American military installations|U.S. military bases]] in [[Jordan]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-irgc-says-it-launched-attack-two-us-bases-jordan-2026-08-30/ (Reuters)]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****A spokesperson for the [[United States Central Command]] reports that the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] has launched strikes on two [[Iranian Armed Forces|Iranian]] [[rocket launcher]]s at [[Larak Island]] in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] that were used by [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]], its first strikes against the country since [[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran|July]]. [https://www.axios.com/2026/08/30/us-iran-strike-hormuz-mines (''Axios'')] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/us-forces-strike-iranian-rocket-launchers-strait-hormuz-first-military-rcna595194 (NBC News)]
**[[Aftermath of the Syrian civil war]]
***Syrian security forces says that they have killed Firas Abdul Karim Hammoud, a [[Syrian Army|army]] commander who served under [[Fall of the Assad regime|ousted]] former [[President of Syria|Syrian president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]], after he opened fire on forces as they tried to arrest him. [https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5312802-syrian-authorities-say-killed-assad-era-officer-after-clash (''Asharq Al Awsat'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Ukrainian Air Defence Forces|Ukrainian missile]] strike on [[Belgorod]], [[Russia]], kills two people and injures 16 others, according to [[Belgorod Oblast|regional]] acting [[Governor of Belgorod Oblast|governor]] [[Alexander Shuvaev]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/missile-attack-kills-two-injures-16-russias-belgorod-authorities-say-2026-08-30/ (Reuters)] [https://english.news.cn/europe/20260831/0618e80ed77f4a0282c21b69122071f7/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]], [[Battle of Barah]]
***[[Sudan]]'s doctors network reports that five civilians are killed and thousands are displaced during attacks by [[Rapid Support Forces]] in [[Barah, Sudan|Bara]], [[North Kordofan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318063 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[2026 Nigerien coup attempt]]
**[[Niger]]'s [[Niger Armed Forces#Niger Army|army]] says that they have regained control of an airbase after it was attacked by mutinous soldiers yesterday. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/niger-says-it-regains-control-airbase-after-soldiers-mutiny-2026-08-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**[[Mexican Armed Forces|Mexican security forces]] kill [[Los Reyes, Michoacán|Los Reyes]] [[Crime in Mexico|cartel]] leader [[:es:Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez|Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez]] and his bodyguard during an operation in [[Tocumbo Municipality|Tocumbo]], [[Michoacán]], after coming under gunfire. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/mexico-confirms-killing-of-los-reyes-cartel-leader-in-michoacan/4044257 (AA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Indonesia wildfires]]
**[[2026 East Malaysia haze]], [[Endangerment of orangutans]]
***An [[orangutan]] named Sampurna is reported to be rescued from a [[haze]] fire zone in [[Ketapang]], [[West Kalimantan]], on [[Indonesia]]'s [[Borneo]] island. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/orangutan-rescued-fire-zone-indonesias-borneo-battles-respiratory-illness-2026-08-30/ (Reuters)]
**The [[Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force|Japanese military]] ship [[JS Kunisaki|JS ''Kunisaki'']] departs from a port in [[Kure, Hiroshima|Kure]], [[Hiroshima Prefecture|Hiroshima]], to help fight [[wildfire]]s in [[Indonesia]]. [https://en.tempo.co/read/2118581/japans-kunisaki-ship-departs-to-help-fight-indonesia-wildfires (''Tempo'')]
*[[2026 Grand Canyon flood]]
**The body of one man is found near the [[Colorado River]] while 15 other people remain missing after a [[flash flood]] at [[Bright Angel Creek]] in the [[Grand Canyon]] in [[Arizona]], United States. [https://www.euronews.com/2026/08/31/body-of-46-year-old-man-recovered-after-grand-canyon-flash-flood-park-service-says (Euronews)]
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**Following the floods that killed over 1,000 people in [[Nepal]] and [[Tibet]], several countries and organizations pledge over $19.8 million total in emergency [[humanitarian aid]], including [[Canada]], the [[European Union]], the [[United Kingdom]], the United States, and the [[International Red Cross and Red Crescent Society]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/gallery/2026/8/30/photos-nepal-issues-fresh-flood-alerts-as-regional-death-toll-hits-750 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Sinking of the Filo Jet|Sinking of the ''Filo Jet'']]
**At least eight people are killed and 18 others are missing when a [[Ferry|passenger ferry]] sailing from [[Northern Cyprus]] to [[Turkey]] capsizes in the eastern [[Mediterranean sea]]. The ship was carrying 259 passengers and 8 crew members, of which 237 people have been rescued. [https://news.sky.com/story/boat-capsizing-latest-vessel-with-270-people-on-board-capsizes-off-northern-cyprus-13577576 (Sky News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/boat-with-around-270-people-capsizes-off-north-cyprus-media-says-2026-08-30/ (Reuters)]
* The body of the last missing individual aboard a boat capsized on Thursday on [[Mapanuepe Lake]] in [[San Marcelino, Zambales]], [[Philippines]], is recovered, concluding [[Search and rescue|search operations]] with the final death toll at nine. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2295047/body-of-missing-pregnant-aeta-found-after-4-day-search-in-zambales-lake (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2026 state visit by Xi Jinping to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt]]
**[[China|Chinese]] [[Paramount leader|leader]] [[Xi Jinping]] and [[First Lady of China|his wife]] [[Peng Liyuan]] arrive in [[Bishkek]], [[Kyrgyzstan]], for the [[2026 Bishkek SCO summit|upcoming]] [[Shanghai Cooperation Organisation]] summit and a [[state visit]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260831-russia-s-putin-and-china-s-xi-to-attend-summit-in-kyrgyzstan (AFP via RFI)] [https://english.news.cn/20260831/3ca97fc981694636957e9bcd18df2dfc/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Law and crime'''
*One person is killed and five others are injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[rave]] in [[Aarau]], [[Aargau]], [[Switzerland]]. The perpetrator is on the run. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/30/europe/switzerland-shooting-rave-aargau-hnk-intl (CNN)]
*Two people are killed and nine injured during a [[mass shootings in the United States|mass shooting]] at a gathering in [[Trenton, New Jersey|Trenton]], [[New Jersey]], [[United States]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/at-least-2-killed-9-injured-in-new-jersey-mass-shooting/4041840 (AA)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/2-dead-9-hurt-trenton-mass-shooting-rcna595106 (NBC News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Guinea-Bissau constitutional referendum]]
**[[Guinea-Bissau|Bissau-Guineans]] vote on a [[constitutional referendum]] that proposes to expand [[List of presidents of Guinea-Bissau|presidential]] powers. [https://apnews.com/article/guinea-bissau-referendum-elections-presidential-powers-e3596d7ae2ad62f6f380af99d5bfe9ce (AP)]
*[[2026 Zambian general election]]
**[[Zambia]]n [[President of Zambia|presidential]] candidate [[Brian Mundubile]] is charged with [[treason]] amid an election dispute. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c20lwqpx70qo (BBC News)]
*The [[Korean Central News Agency]] reports that [[Jiang (rank)|general]] [[No Kwang-chol]] has been dismissed as [[Ministry of National Defence (North Korea)|defence minister]] of [[North Korea]], with [[Korean People's Army]] [[General Political Bureau of the Korean People's Army|General Political Bureau director]] [[Kim Song-gi]] replacing him. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/north-korea-defence-minister-dismissed-state-media-6349961 (AFP via CNA)] [https://www.nknews.org/2026/08/north-korea-reshuffles-top-military-leadership-replaces-defense-minister/ (''NK News'')] 

'''Science and technology'''
*[[NASA]] launches the [[Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope]] aboard a [[Falcon Heavy]] rocket from [[Florida]], [[United States]], to survey the universe, study [[dark matter]] and [[dark energy]], and search for [[exoplanet]]s and [[supernova]]e. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260830-nasa-s-roman-telescope-set-to-launch-on-cosmic-mapping-mission (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/nasa-roman-space-telescope-launch-success-on-a-spacex-falcon-heavy-rocket-spectacular-launch-video (Space.com)]
<!-- All news items above this line -->

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup]]
**In [[field hockey]], [[Germany men's national field hockey team|Germany]] defeats [[Spain men's national field hockey team|Spain]] 1–0 in the [[2026 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup final|final]] to secure their fourth [[Men's FIH Hockey World Cup|FIH Men's World Cup]] title. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/germany-edge-spain-retain-world-cup-2026-08-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 World Rowing Championships]]
**In [[rowing (sport)|rowing]], the 2026 [[World Rowing Championships|World Championships]] conclude in [[Amsterdam]], [[Netherlands]], with [[Royal Dutch Rowing Federation|the host nation]] as the most successful team with 4 gold medals and 10 medals overall. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/rowing/articles/cp80ne8168zo (BBC Sport)] [https://worldrowing.com/2026/08/30/historic-sunday-brings-2026-world-rowing-championships-to-a-close/ (World Rowing)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=29|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****A [[tanker (ship)|tanker]] is struck by a unknown projectile while transiting through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] near [[Khasab]], [[Oman]], according to the [[United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/tanker-struck-projectile-hormuz-ukmto-says (''Middle East Eye'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Attacks on health facilities during the Gaza war]]
****[[Israel]] strikes the [[Shuhada al-Aqsa Hospital]] in the [[Deir al-Balah]] area of the [[Gaza Strip]], killing three people, in violation of the [[Gaza peace plan|October 2025]] [[ceasefire]]. The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) stated that they targeted a [[Hamas]] commander who, according to it, was hiding within the compound of the [[hospital]]. [https://www.newarab.com/news/israeli-army-bombs-hospital-kills-three-gaza-strip (MENA via ''The New Arab'')]
***The IDF confirms that they have killed [[Nukhba forces|Nukhba Force]] commander [[Hani Abd al-Hai Fakhri Mazloum]] and [[Hamas]] sniper Hassan Zidan Hassan Deiri in separate strikes in the [[North Gaza Governorate|northern]] [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-hamas-commander-and-sniper-killed-in-strike-in-north-gaza-yesterday/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian drone]] attack on [[Shebekino]], [[Belgorod Oblast]], [[Russia]], kills three people and damages residential buildings, according to the regional [[Ministry of Emergency Situations (Russia)|emergency response center]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260829/263a4d21732c4e139600bcc0383ba4ab/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Somali Civil War]]
**[[Piracy off the coast of Somalia]]
***The [[Cameroon]]-[[Flag state|flagged]] [[Turkey|Turkish]] [[cargo ship]] MV ''LUTUF'', which was hijacked on August 17, is freed by [[Somali Armed Forces|Somali]] and [[Turkish Armed Forces|Turkish forces]] off the coast of [[Somalia]]. Conversely, the [[Puntland]] [[Ministry of Security (Puntland)|ministry of security]] says a ransom was paid. [https://apnews.com/article/somalia-pirates-turkish-vessel-freed-4e271b3e63921d7589864ce17b23eedb (AP)] [https://garoweonline.com/en/news/puntland/somalia-puntland-says-somali-officials-phoned-pirates-facilitated-ransom-for-hijacked-mv-lutuf-ship (Garowe Online)] [https://www.hiiraan.com/news4/2026/Aug/206122/puntland_state_accuses_somalia_trkiye_of_paying_pirates_after_mv_lutuf_freed.aspx (Hiiraan Online)]
*[[2026 Nigerien coup attempt]]
**[[Niger]]ien television confirms that dissenting elements of the [[Niger Armed Forces]] attempted a [[Coup d'état|coup]] in the nation's capital, [[Niamey]]. Attacks are reported on [[Diori Hamani International Airport]] and the [[Presidential Palace, Niamey|Presidential Palace]]. [https://apnews.com/article/niger-niamey-gunfire-explosions-airport-presidential-district-77d0c701e5729f2779580ea557e0a2c3 (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/gunfire-blasts-heard-several-areas-niger-capital-niamey-witness-says-2026-08-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Tuareg people|Tuareg]] rebels free 60 [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian soldiers]] in exchange for army officer-turned-defector Inkinane Ag Attaher. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/29/tuareg-rebels-free-more-malian-soldiers-in-prisoner-swap-sources-say (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**[[Nepal–United States relations]]
***The [[United States Department of State|U.S. State Department]] says that the [[United States|U.S.]] will provide [[United States dollar|US$]]3.6 million in humanitarian aid to [[Nepal]] in wake of the [[flood|floods]]. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2026/08/30/us-steps-up-nepal-flood-aid-with-us36m-package/233226 (''Malay Mail'')]
**The death toll from [[flash flood|flash floods]] in [[Nepal]] rises to 669, with more than 2,400 people reported missing. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/asia/nepal-floods-death-toll-climbs-missing-rescue-efforts-rcna594990 (NBC News)]
*[[2026 Grand Canyon flood]]
**A flash flood in the [[Grand Canyon National Park]] in [[Arizona]], [[United States]], leaves about 15 people missing and prompts the evacuation of at least 62 others. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260830-about-15-people-missing-after-grand-canyon-flash-flood (AFP via France 24)]
*A person is rescued while four people are missing when a [[sport utility vehicle]] plunges into [[Tarlac River|a river]] after a bridge in [[Tarlac City]], [[Philippines]], collapses. The bridge has been serving as an alternative route as another partially collapsed days prior amid [[monsoon]] rains. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2295013/4-missing-1-rescued-after-suv-falls-as-another-tarlac-bridge-collapses (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Icelandic European Union membership negotiations referendum]]
**[[Iceland]] rejects restarting membership negotiations with the [[European Union|EU]] in a referendum. [https://www.ruv.is/english/2026-08-29-iceland-rejects-eu-accession-talks-485377 (RÚV)]
*[[Pope]] [[Leo XIV]] publishes a ''[[motu proprio]]'' to amend the [[Code of Canons of the Eastern Churches|Code of Canons]] of the [[Eastern Catholic Churches|Eastern Churches]], granting them the ability to remove their respective [[Patriarchs of the East|Patriarchs]] via a [[two-thirds vote]] with papal approval, if the relationship between them and the council is broken beyond repair. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2026-08/pope-leo-grants-eastern-synods-the-faculty-to-remove-patriarchs.html (Vatican News)] [https://www.ncregister.com/cna/pope-leo-eastern-patriarchs (''National Catholic Register'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup]]
**[[2026 Women's FIH Hockey World Cup final]]
***In [[field hockey]], [[Argentina women's national field hockey team|Argentina]] beat the [[Netherlands women's national field hockey team|Netherlands]] in the final after a 1–1 draw and a [[Penalty shoot-out (field hockey)|penalty shoot-out]] to secure their third [[Women's FIH Hockey World Cup|Women's World Cup]] title. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/argentina-lift-womens-hockey-world-cup-title-break-dutch-dominance-2026-08-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Women's NORCECA Volleyball Championship]]
**[[Canada at the 2028 Summer Olympics]], [[Volleyball at the 2028 Summer Olympics]]
***In [[volleyball]], the [[Canada women's national volleyball team|Canadian women’s national team]] qualifies for the [[2028 Summer Olympics|upcoming]] [[Summer Olympics]] in [[Los Angeles]], [[California]], [[United States|U.S.]], their first qualification since [[1896 Summer Olympics|1996]] following a victory against the [[Dominican Republic women's national volleyball team|Dominican Republic]] in the [[Women's NORCECA Volleyball Continental Championship]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/volleyball/canada-women-volleyball-dominican-republic-recap-olympic-qualifier-9.7325709 (CBC)]
*[[Moses Itauma vs Filip Hrgovic]]
**In [[boxing]], [[Filip Hrgović]] defeats [[Moses Itauma]] by ninth-round stoppage to win the vacant [[International Boxing Federation|IBF]] [[heavyweight]] title. Hrgović becomes the first [[Croatia]]n heavyweight boxing world champion. [https://www.philstar.com/sports/2026/08/30/2552848/hrgovic-wins-ibf-world-heavyweight-title-itauma-hospitalized (AFP via ''The Philippine Star'')]
*In [[tennis]], former player [[Roger Federer]] is inducted into the player category, while former player and current [[sportscaster]] [[Mary Carillo]] is inducted into the contributor category of the [[International Tennis Hall of Fame]] respectively. [https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/Articles/2026/08/30/intl-tennis-hof-holds-star-studded-induction-for-federer-carillo/ (''Sports Business Journal'')]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=28|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign|Blue Nile campaign]]
***[[Sudan]]'s [[Rapid Support Forces]] says that they have seized the Bakori and Surkum [[Sudanese Army]] bases in the southeastern [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] [[States of Sudan|region]] alongside [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/318007 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***Emergency Lawyers, an independent group documenting atrocities in Sudan, reports that eight civilians have been killed in [[drone warfare|drone strikes]] in the [[Sowdari District]] of [[North Kordofan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-north-korodfan-drone-strikes-civilians-killed-51bbdafbbc96601c085aec8c7b951870 (AP)] [https://english.aawsat.com/arab-world/5312104-drone-strikes-kill-8-civilians-sudan%E2%80%99s-north-kordofan (''Asharq Al Awsat'')]
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) says that they have killed three [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] militants, including [[Palestinian Islamic Jihad|Islamic Jihad]] (PIJ) senior member Qais Bitawi, in a [[drone strike]] in the [[Israel]]-[[Israeli occupation of the West Bank|occupied]] [[West Bank]] city of [[Jenin]]. The PIJ later confirms Bitawi's death. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-strike-kills-three-west-bank-israel-says-it-targeted-hamas-operative-2026-08-28/ (Reuters)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-it-killed-3-palestinian-terror-operatives-in-rare-west-bank-airstrike/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***A [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone]] strike hits a [[supply depot]] in [[Bucha Raion|Bucha]], [[Kyiv Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], triggering explosions and a fire, killing at least 37 people and forcing the evacuation of almost 400 residents. [[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says explosives stored near homes worsened the disaster. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c86xwqez4npo (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/29/europe/ukraine-kyiv-russia-war-attack-intl (CNN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Ministry of Finance (Japan)|Japanese finance ministry]] says it spent a record ¥15.4 trillion ([[US$]]96 billion) between July 30 and August 26 to support the [[Japanese yen|yen]], marking [[Japan|the country]]'s largest monthly [[currency intervention]] on record. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260828-japan-spent-record-96-bn-in-yen-interventions-ministry (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twenty-seven people are killed and seven people are injured after a vehicle carrying churchgoers collides head-on with a truck in [[Chivhu]], [[Zimbabwe]]. [https://www.msn.com/en-gb/public-safety-and-emergencies/traffic-and-transportation-incidents/zimbabwe-crash-involving-church-minibus-kills-27/ar-AA2baNtQ (MSN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Seventh cholera pandemic]]
**[[Nigeria]] records 65,000 cases of [[cholera]], across 35 [[States of Nigeria|states]], alongside 10,000 cases of [[diphtheria]]. Additionally, [[Nigeria Centre for Disease Control|NCDC]] director Jide Idris reports a decline in cholera cases but also warn that transmission of cases remain ongoing. [https://thenationonlineng.net/nigeria-records-65000-cholera-cases-over-10000-diphtheria-cases-in-one-year/ (''The Nation NG'')] [https://dailytrust.com/cholera-cases-decline-but-outbreak-not-over-ncdc/ (''Daily Trust'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**The [[United States]] and [[Venezuela]] agree to expand U.S. access to [[Oil reserves in Venezuela|Venezuelan oil reserves]] under a deal involving US$100 billion in private investment, while Venezuela retains ownership of [[Energy in Venezuela|its petroleum resources]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260830-venezuelans-view-us-oil-deal-with-doubt-hope (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Corruption in Ecuador]]
**An [[Ecuador]]ian court convicts former [[President of Ecuador|president]] [[Lenín Moreno]] of [[bribery]] linked to the construction of the [[Coca Codo Sinclair Dam|Coca Codo Sinclair plant]] in [[Napo Province]]. His wife, [[Rocío González Navas]], and daughter are also found guilty. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/ecuador-finds-ex-president-moreno-guilty-hydro-plant-bribery-case-2026-08-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[Protests against Donald Trump]]
**Demonstrators gather in [[Washington, D.C.]], [[United States]], to [[Protests against the second Trump administration|protest]] against the [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]'s alleged efforts to rollback [[Election law and voting rights under the second Trump administration|voting]] and [[civil rights]], 63 years after the [[March on Washington]] rally by [[Civil rights movement|civil rights]] leader [[Martin Luther King Jr.|Martin Luther King Jr]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/thousands-march-washington-leaders-warn-voting-civil-rights-rollbacks-2026-08-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[Scam centers in Cambodia]]
**The [[Cambodia]]n [[Government of Cambodia|government]] says that they have closed more than 700 [[online scam]] [[Scam center|centers]] and arrested nearly 30,000 suspects, including 15 senior officials and [[Law enforcement in Cambodia|law-enforcement]] officers, during a year-long crackdown on [[cybercrime]] networks. [https://www.euronews.com/2026/08/28/cambodia-shuts-over-700-cyberscam-locations-over-past-year-government-says (Euronews)]
*Two men steal a 200-carat platinum-and-diamond necklace from the [[Museum of Applied Arts, Vienna|Museum of Applied Arts]] in [[Vienna]], [[Austria]], after smashing a display case with a hammer and fleeing, according to [[Federal Police (Austria)|Austrian police]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/carat-platinum-diamond-necklace-heist-vienna-museum/ (AFP via CBS News)]
*Two teenagers are arrested in [[Israel]] for allegedly pledging allegiance to [[Islamic State|ISIS]] and plotting an attack on security forces at the [[Temple Mount]] and an IDF base in [[Northern District (Israel)|northern Israel]]. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/r1cnn3avfx (Ynetnews)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/two-northern-israel-teens-indicted-for-planning-isis-inspired-attacks-on-security-forces/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Death and state funeral of Harald V]]
**[[Monarchy of Norway|King]] [[Harald V]] of [[Norway]] dies at the age of 89 after a 35-year reign and is succeeded by his son [[Haakon VIII]]. [https://apnews.com/article/king-harald-norway-228366941b7c48c59ececf004cc3c467 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/clykn5p5172o (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/28/europe/king-of-norway-harald-v-oldest-monarch-dead-intl (CNN)]
*[[Forced contraception of women in Greenland]]
**[[Greenland]] establishes a [[truth and reconciliation commission]] after experts conclude that a decades-long [[Denmark|Danish]] [[contraceptive]] program violated [[Inuit women]]'s rights but disagree on whether it constituted [[genocide]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/28/forced-birth-control-in-greenland-violated-womens-rights-experts-find (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Serbia]] [[Ministry of Justice (Serbia)|justice minister]] [[Nenad Vujić]] says that [[Trial of Ratko Mladić|convicted]] [[war criminal]] [[Ratko Mladić]] will be buried with [[State funeral|state]] and [[Military funeral|military honors]] following his death at the [[United Nations Detention Unit]] at the [[The Hague|Hague]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/28/europe/serbia-mladic-burial-war-crimes-intl (CNN)] [https://serbiantimes.info/en/serbian-justice-minister-mladic-will-be-buried-with-the-highest-state-honors/ (''Serbian Times'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026–27 NHL season]]
**In [[ice hockey]], the [[Colorado Avalanche]] [[2026–27 NHL transactions|sign]] [[defenceman]] and [[Captain (ice hockey)#Alternate captains|alternate captain]] [[Cale Makar]] to an eight-year extension worth [[United States dollar|US$]]163.2 million, the largest contract in [[National Hockey League]] history. He is the first player to exceed $20 million in average annual value. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7546811/2026/08/28/cale-makar-contract-nhl-record/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')] [https://www.cbssports.com/nhl/news/cale-makar-colorado-avalanche-contract-record/ (CBS Sports)] [https://www.espn.com/nhl/story/_/id/49756170/avalanc-makar-agrees-record-deal-worth-204-annually (ESPN)]
