parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=27|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)| Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza–Israel conflict]]
***[[Gaza war]]
****[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
*****Three [[Palestinians]] are reported to be killed in strikes in the [[Gaza Strip]], violating the [[Gaza peace plan|October 2025]] [[ceasefire]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/27/three-killed-in-strikes-on-gaza-as-israel-renews-threats-over-kite-flying (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/israeli-strikes-kill-three-people-gaza-medics-say-2026-08-27/ (Reuters)]
****[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
*****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) and its [[IDF Spokesperson's Unit|Spokesperson's Unit]] confirms [[Al-Qassam Brigades]] commander Ismail Mohammad Ibrahim Barim, who held [[Edan Alexander]], [[Avera Mengistu]], and [[Matan Zangauker]] as [[List of Gaza war hostages|hostages]], was killed in a strike in [[Khan Yunis]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-hamas-commander-who-held-3-israelis-hostage-killed-in-gaza-airstrike/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/432335 (''Israel National News'')] [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-906742 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
****The IDF also confirms that they have recently killed two [[Hamas]] militants that invaded the [[Battle of Re'im|Re'im Base]] in [[Re'im]] during the [[October 7 attacks]] in separate strikes in the [[Gaza Strip]], including a body guard to [[Killing of Yahya Sinwar|former leader]] [[Yahya Sinwar]] and a [[Nukhba forces]] militant. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-former-bodyguard-of-slain-hamas-leader-yahya-sinwar-killed-in-southern-gaza-strike/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***It is reported that [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] held secret meetings with [[Hamas]] during the [[2014 Gaza War]]. The [[Prime Minister's Office (Israel)|Prime Minister's Office]] denies the reports. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/netanyahu-held-secret-talks-with-hamas-during-2014-gaza-war-report-says-pms-office-denies/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/hyqmr110wmx (Ynetnews)]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
****[[Qatar as a mediator in conflict]]
*****[[Prime Minister of Qatar|Qatari prime minister]] [[Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani]] talks with [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] in [[Tehran]], including on the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and efforts to end the war. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/27/iran-qatar-hold-hormuz-talks-amid-intl-hopes-dialogue-with-us-will-resume (Al Jazeera)]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****[[United States Central Command]] commander [[Brad Cooper (admiral)|Brad Cooper]] says that [[United States Armed Force|the military]] has cleared all [[Iran|Iranian]] [[naval mine|naval mines]] in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and its routes. [https://thehill.com/policy/defense/6056395-centcom-us-clears-iranian-sea-mines/amp/ (''The Hill'')]
****[[Iran]]'s [[Supreme National Security Council]] [[Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council|secretary]] [[Mohsen Rezaei]] says that Iran is preparing a set of conditions for reopening the [[Strait of Hormuz]] after mediators called for them to do so. [https://www.reuters.com/3fec1b0a85a0/world/middle-east/irans-security-chief-denies-allegations-iranian-plot-assassinate-trumps-son-al-2026-08-27/ (Reuters)]
****The [[United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations]] reports that a [[tanker (ship)|tanker]] in the Strait of Hormuz was [[List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war|hit]] by an "unknown projectile", causing a fire that was later extinguished. [https://www.marineinsight.com/tanker-catches-fire-after-being-hit-by-unknown-projectile-in-strait-of-hormuz/ (Marine Insight)]
*[[Sudanese Civil Wars]]
**[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
***[[2026 Blue Nile campaign|Blue Nile campaign]]
****[[Sudan]]'s [[Sudanese Army|army]] repels a [[Rapid Support Forces]] attack on the town of Al-Keli in the [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] region. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317979 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
***[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
****[[Sudan]]'s Security Affairs Coordination Committee lifts the curfew and state of emergency on the [[Capital city|capital]] [[Khartoum]] after two years. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260827-sudan-lifts-khartoums-2-year-old-curfew-state-of-emergency/ (Middle East Monitor)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c2076gxr0llo (BBC)]
***Around 12 people are reported killed in a airstrike near the [[Chad–Sudan border|border]] with [[Chad]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/8/28/chad-accuses-sudan-of-deadly-air-strike-near-shared-border (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Sudanese nomadic conflicts]]
***Around 49 people are killed in a [[Cattle raiding|cattle raid]] on the Machar-Pakuek cattle camp in Mading Juer Boma in [[Tonj North County]] of [[South Sudan]]'s [[Warrap State|Warrap]] [[States of South Sudan|state]]. [https://www.newarab.com/news/armed-raiders-kill-49-south-sudan-cattle-raid-local-official?amp (MENA via ''The New Arab'')]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***Four people are killed after an unconfirmed civilian or military airplane is shot down with a [[surface-to-air missile]] near [[Minembwe]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.nouveaumedia.cd/sud-kivu-un-avion-civile-pris-pour-cible-abattu-pres-de-laeroport-de-minembwe/ (Noveau Media)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**[[NORAD]] and the [[United States Northern Command|U.S. Northern Command]] say that the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] used a [[laser weapon]] against three drones belonging to [[Mexico|Mexican]] [[List of Mexican cartels|drug cartels]]. [https://www.militarytimes.com/industry/techwatch/2026/08/28/us-military-uses-laser-to-down-three-mexican-cartel-drones-near-border/ (''Military Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[South Korea]]n company [[SK Group|SK Gas]] pays a record [[US$]]5.3 million for priority passage of the [[LPG tanker]] ''G. Spirit'' through the [[Panama Canal]] before [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation|El Niño]]-related transit restrictions reduced daily crossings. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260828-tanker-pays-record-5-3-mn-to-transit-panama-canal-administrator (AFP via France 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2026]]
**[[2026 Canadian wildfires]]
***In [[Canada]], [[British Columbia]] ends its [[state of emergency]] previously imposed on August 8 in response to [[wildfire]]s that killed one person. [https://www.thecanadianpressnews.ca/business/b-c-ends-fire-state-of-emergency-after-20-days-thousands-of-evacuations-one-death/article_e1affe53-ab50-5f18-a2cc-a5dc027c6547.html (''The Canadian Press News'')] [https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/bc-to-end-off-roading-ban-citing-decreased-wildfire-risk/ (CTV News)]
***A [[British Columbia Highway 1|section]] of the [[Trans-Canada Highway]] in the [[Fraser Canyon]] reopens after being closed for seven weeks due to the wildfires. [https://redfm.ca/en-ca/vancouver/news-articles/trans-canada-highway-reopens-near-boston-bar-after-seven-week-wildfire-closure (Redfm)] [https://www.ctvnews.ca/vancouver/article/highway-1-reopens-through-fraser-canyon-after-wildfire/ (CTV News)]
**[[Algeria|Algerian]] [[President of Algeria|president]] [[Abdelmadjid Tebboune]] declares three [[National day of mourning|days of national mourning]] after 12 people were reported to be killed in [[wildfire|wildfires]] in northeastern [[Jijel]]. [https://www.africanews.com/2026/08/28/algeria-declares-3-days-of-national-mourning-as-wildfire-death-toll-rises-to-12/ (Africanews)]
*[[2026 Flores earthquake]]
**The death toll from the [[earthquake]] that struck the [[Flores]] island in [[East Nusa Tenggara]], [[Indonesia]], rises to 111, with 176,000 people displaced. [https://www.anews.com.tr/asia/2026/08/27/indonesia-earthquake-death-toll-rises-to-111-over-176000-displaced/amp (A News)] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/indonesia-earthquake-death-toll-rises-to-111-over-176-000-displaced/4039350 (AA)]
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**The [[United States Geological Survey]] says a [[glacial]] collapse and [[debris flow]], not an earthquake, caused the seismic event near the [[Nepal]]–[[Tibet]] border and subsequent flooding that killed at least 392 people and left over 900 more missing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/c6y8mjmnpxv0t (BBC News)]
* Six people die after a [[pump boat]] carrying 13 passengers capsizes while crossing the [[Mapanuepe Lake]] in [[San Marcelino, Zambales]], [[Philippines]]. Three others remain missing. [https://www.philstar.com/nation/2026/08/28/2552406/6-aetas-including-3-minors-die-boat-capsizes-zambales (''The Philippine Star'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] begins [[Ebola vaccine|vaccination]] for the [[Ebola]] outbreak in [[Kisangani]], [[Tshopo]], with healthcare and front line workers among the first to receive the [[vaccine]]. [https://www.africanews.com/amp/2026/08/28/dr-congo-begins-ebola-vaccinations-as-deadliest-outbreak-on-record-spreads/ (Africanews)]
**The [[World Health Organization]] declares the Ebola outbreak in [[Uganda]] over after the country went 42 days without a new case of the virus. [https://www.euronews.com/health/2026/08/27/who-declares-uganda-ebola-free-after-42-days-without-new-cases (Euronews)]
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[Germany]]'s [[Robert Koch Institute]] estimates 15,800 [[heat-related death]]s during summer 2026, the highest total in a decade of monitoring, as repeated [[heat wave]]s push temperatures above {{convert|40|C|F}}. [https://www.kurdistan24.net/en/story/935403/germany-records-15800-heat-related-deaths-in-record-breaking-summer (Kurdistan 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Malaysia–Myanmar relations]]
**[[Malaysia]] says that 1,476 [[Burmese in Malaysia|Burmese people]] will be [[Voluntary return|voluntarily repatriated]] on September 29 in the first phase of a return program agreed with [[Myanmar]], using [[Myanmar Navy|Myanmar naval]] vessels. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/08/29/world/asia-oceania/malaysia-to-repatriate-first-group-of-myanmar-citizens-in-september/2414148 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*Two people are killed in a stabbing at a private school in [[Gosen-Neu Zittau]], [[Brandenburg]], [[Germany]]. A suspect is arrested. [https://english.news.cn/20260828/b117398c9d8b4cbd857445a187616b5a/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Zambian general election]]
**[[Zambia]]n [[President of Zambia|presidential]] candidate [[Brian Mundubile]] surrenders to [[Zambia Police Service|police]] and is questioned over an alleged [[national security]] threat after two weeks in hiding following the disputed [[Elections in Zambia|presidential election]], in which he finished second. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260827-zambia-opposition-leader-surrenders-to-police-state-media (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Forced contraception of women in Greenland]]
**[[Denmark]]'s [[Folketing|parliament]] passes [[Law of Denmark|legislation]] granting 300,000 [[Danish krone|kr.]] ([[US$]]46,758) in compensation to each [[Greenland]]ic woman affected by [[non-consensual]] [[contraception]] administered under a Danish birth-control program in the 1960s and 1970s. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/czxzv29p12lo (BBC News)]
*[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] signs an [[executive order]] directing [[List of federal agencies in the United States|federal agencies]] to call [[Lake Ontario]] "Lake America." The change applies only to [[Federal government of the United States|U.S. federal]] usage; [[Canada]] need not adopt it, and no international authority exclusively determines names of shared waters. [https://apnews.com/article/lake-ontario-canada-america-trump-trade-war-3ac58dca0ca83c15605d4dbff146b28a (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/27/trump-renames-lake-ontario-america (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Omukama of Tooro|King]] [[Rukidi IV of Tooro|Rukidi IV]] of [[Uganda]]'s [[Tooro Kingdom]], the youngest person to reign as a monarch, dies at the age of 34. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0j38d9v40po (BBC News)] [https://ntv.co.ug/news/king-oyo-nyimba-kabamba-iguru-rukidi-iv-of-tooro-dies-at-34 (NTV Uganda)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[August 2026 lunar eclipse]]
**A near-total partial [[lunar eclipse]] occurs over [[Africa]], the [[Americas]], and [[Europe]]. [https://www.timeanddate.com/eclipse/lunar/2026-august-28 (TimeandDate)]
*The [[Korea AeroSpace Administration]] says that the [[Nuri (rocket)|Nuri]] will launch 15 satellites, a record, into space from the [[Naro Space Center]] in [[South Korea]]'s [[Goheung County]] on October 7. [https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/amp/business/tech-science/20260827/korea-to-launch-homegrown-nuri-rocket-on-oct-7 (''Korea Times'')] [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20260827005051320 (Yonhap)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 Diamond League]]
**In [[Sport of athletics|athletics]], [[Brazil]]ian [[Alison dos Santos]] and [[United States|American]] [[Masai Russell]] break the world records in men's [[400 metres hurdles]] (45.80 seconds) and women's [[100 metres hurdles|100 metres]] [[Hurdling|hurdles]] (12.09 seconds), respectively, at the [[2026 Weltklasse Zürich]] in [[Zurich]], [[Switzerland]]. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/brazils-dos-santos-races-world-record-400m-hurdles-zurich-2026-08-27/ (Reuters)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=26|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Iran–Oman negotiations]]
*****The [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] say [[Iran]] and [[Oman]] have agreed to share revenues from the [[Strait of Hormuz]] and define their respective [[Territorial waters|maritime area]]s, while negotiations continue over reopening the waterway amid the war. [https://www.theborneopost.com/2026/08/26/iran-guards-say-agreed-with-oman-to-share-revenues-from-hormuz/ (AFP via ''The Borneo Post'')]
*****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian deputy foreign minister]] [[Kazem Gharibabadi]] says that Iran will not allow [[Naval ship|military vessels]] to transit through the strait under the proposed agreement. [https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-iran-israel-west-bank-august-26-2026-cb19bc3f0b467db591edbef52d0db273 (AP)] [https://www.military.com/iran-negotiates-with-oman-warns-military-ship-ban-strait-hormuz (Military.com)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] says that they have killed several [[Hamas]] members in [[airstrike|airstrikes]] in the [[Gaza Strip]] city of [[Jabalia]], including on a structure allegedly used as a storage facility for weapons. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-906650 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***An overnight [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[drone warfare|drone attack]] "completely destroys" a [[Wildberries]] depot in [[Tambov Oblast]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/drone-sets-wildberries-warehouse-ablaze-russias-tambov-region-governor-says-2026-08-26/ (Reuters)]
***A man and a 14-year-old child are killed in [[Lipetsk Oblast]], and a woman is killed in [[Belgorod Oblast]], in [[Unmanned Systems Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian drone]] strikes. The [[Ministry of Defence (Russia)|Russian defence ministry]] says [[Russian Armed Forces|its forces]] have shot down 426 Ukrainian drones overnight. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/26/ukrainian-drone-attacks-kill-3-as-fire-destroys-wildberries-warehouse (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Luhansk Oblast campaign]]
***Nine people are killed after a Ukrainian strike on a bus in [[Russian occupation of Ukraine|Russian-occupied]] [[Luhansk Oblast|Luhansk]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/nine-killed-ukrainian-strike-bus-russian-controlled-luhansk-region-russia-says-2026-08-26/ (Reuters)]
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**[[Cambodia]] deploys 184 peacekeepers, including 28 women, to the [[Central African Republic]] as part of a peacekeeping mission by the [[United Nations]]. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/502013556/cambodia-deploys-184-peacekeepers-to-un-mission-in-car/ (''Khmer Times'')] [https://english.news.cn/20260826/2c20e85a442944d8a633b30815fce425/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[2026 anti-immigrant movement and xenophobia in South Africa]]
**A spokesperson for [[Mali|Malian]] singer [[Salif Keita]] confirms that he has cancelled all upcoming concerts in [[South Africa]] over its response to anti-migrant protests in the country. [https://www.channelstv.com/2026/08/26/mali-singer-salif-keita-sancels-s-africa-shows-over-xenophobic-violence/ (Channels TV)] [https://arbiterz.com/malian-music-legend-salif-keita-cancels-south-african-tour-over-xenophobic-attacks/ (Arbiterz)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Nepal–Tibet floods]]
**[[Flash flood]]s and [[Mudflow|mudslide]]s along the [[Trishuli River]] impact between [[Nepal]] and [[Greater Tibet|Tibet]], [[China]]. At least 160 people are killed, hundreds are injured and 463 others, including over 200 [[Tourism in Nepal|tourists]], are reported missing in Nepal, while [[Chinese Communist Party]] officials report three deaths and 265 missing in Tibet, severely affecting [[Gyirong County]] and [[Gyirong Port|its port]]. [https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2026/08/26/massive-flood-near-tibet-border-kills-least-95-nepal/ (AFP via ''Jamaica Observer'')] [https://apnews.com/article/climate-change-nepal-flash-floods-7262dac22e31258955efa5c28c8fe917 (AP)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cd948kn02e5o (BBC News)]
**[[Government of Nepal|Nepali officials]] say bridges, roads, [[power station]]s, and entire villages have been swept away by the [[flash flood]]ing with some areas still completely cut-off from [[search and rescue]] efforts. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/26/at-least-eight-killed-in-nepal-flash-floods-that-swept-away-villages-roads (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/asia/2026/08/26/nepal-tibet-flash-floods/ (''The National'')]
*At least 15 infants are killed and another is injured after a fire at a [[Healthcare in Pakistan|state-run hospital]] in [[Islamabad]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/article-at-least-15-infants-killed-in-pakistan-hospital-fire-local-media/ (''The Globe and Mail'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/newborn-babies-die-fire-pakistan-hospital-maternity-ward (''The Guardian'')]
*Twelve people are killed and at least 54 others are injured as [[wildfire]]s spread across northeastern [[Algeria]] during a severe [[heat wave]], with deaths reported in [[Béjaïa Province|Béjaïa]], [[Jijel Province|Jijel]], and [[Tizi Ouzou Province|Tizi Ouzou]] provinces. [https://gulfnews.com/world/africa/algeria-wildfires-kill-12-as-154-fires-rage-across-country-1.500653548 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Artificial intelligence in healthcare]]
**The [[University College London]] reports that neurosurgeons in [[London]], [[England]], have performed the first [[Artificial intelligence|AI]]-assisted [[Neurosurgery|brain surgery]] at the [[National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery]] in a 48-year old patient who was diagnosed with a [[brain tumor]] in 2024. [https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/aug/27/london-neurosurgeons-ai-assisted-operation-brain-tumour (''The Guardian'')] [https://news.sky.com/story/ai-helps-perform-brain-surgery-on-british-man-in-world-first-13577615 (Sky News)] [https://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/2026/aug/first-patient-live-ai-assisted-sight-saving-brain-surgery (UCL)]
*Nineteen cases of [[Japanese encephalitis]] are confirmed in [[Madhesh Province]], Nepal, causing six deaths. [https://english.nepalnews.com/s/health/japanese-encephalitis-in-madhesh-19-infected-6-dead/ (Nepal News)]
*The [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] approves the [[daraxonrasib]] drug as a treatment for [[Metastasis|metastatic]] [[pancreatic cancer]], making it the first [[Ras GTPase#RAS inhibitors|RAS inhibitor]] drug to be approved for the disease. This came after a previous study showed that it nearly doubled the survival rate for patients compared to [[chemotherapy]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/26/fda-approves-new-pancreatic-cancer-drug (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/revolution-medicines-gets-fda-nod-targeted-pancreatic-cancer-drug-2026-08-26/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[South Korea–United States relations]], [[Japan–United States relations]]
**The [[United States Indo-Pacific Command|U.S. Pacific Command]] announces that the [[United States]] will conduct trilateral [[military exercise]]s with [[South Korea]]'s [[Republic of Korea Armed Forces|armed forces]] and [[Japan]]'s [[Japan Self-Defense Forces|self-defense forces]] despite [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] scaling back on the recent [[Ulchi-Freedom Guardian]] exercises. [https://www.trtworld.com/article/54c23fef9520 (AA via TRT World)] [https://koreaherald.com/article/10852624 (''Korea Herald'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the September 11 attacks]]
**The [[Courts-martial of the United States|U.S. military trial]] for [[al-Qaeda]] militant [[Khalid Sheikh Mohammed]], the alleged mastermind of the [[September 11 attacks]], is set for June 2028 alongside three co-conspirators. [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/national-security/military-trial-date-set-alleged-mastermind-sept-11-attacks-ksm-rcna594621 (NBC News)] [https://news.sky.com/story/alleged-9-11-mastermind-to-go-on-trial-almost-27-years-after-attacks-13577612 (Sky News)]
*[[Lawsuits involving Meta Platforms]]
**[[Meta Platforms]] agrees to pay up to [[United States dollar|$]]16.7 billion to settle [[Cause of action|claims]] by 29 [[U.S. state]]s over alleged harms to young users and to impose new usage limits and safeguards for teenagers on its [[social media]] platforms [[Facebook]] and [[Instagram]]. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/technology/2026/8/26/meta-us-states-agree-16-7-b-settlement-in-landmark-teen-safety-case-2211 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*[[Terrorism in the United States]]
**The [[United States]] designates the [[Italy]]-based [[Hacktivism in Italy|Autistici/Inventati]], the [[UK]]-based [[Palestine Action]], and [[Palestinian nationalism|pro-Palestinian]] group Masar Badil as [[United States Department of State list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations|terrorist organizations]], citing alleged involvement in [[Political violence in the United States|politically motivated violence]] and [[extremist]] activity. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260826-us-designates-uk-based-palestine-action-as-foreign-terrorist-group (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Russia]] orders the arrest of [[Germany|German]] ''[[Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung]]'' journalist {{ill|Michael Martens|de}}, charging him [[Trial in absentia|in absentia]] over comments interpreted as calling for the killing of Russians, a [[Crime in Russia|crime]] punishable by up to six years in [[Prisons in Russia|prison]]. [https://news.az/news/russia-places-faz-journalist-martens-on-international-wanted-list (News.az)]
*Two people are killed and nine others are seriously injured in a [[vehicle-ramming attack]] against pedestrians after a fight near a [[train station]] in [[Caen]], [[Normandy]], [[France]]. The perpetrator is arrested. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20260827-man-drives-car-into-group-of-pedestrians-in-french-city-of-caen-killing-one (France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States Department of State]] suspends [[Visa policy of the United States#Immigrant visa|immigrant visa]] appointments at [[List of diplomatic missions of the United States|all embassies and consulates]] worldwide while training [[Bureau of Consular Affairs|consular staff]] on screening applicants for potential dependence on [[Social programs in the United States|public benefits]]. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/8/27/us-issues-global-pause-for-immigration-visa-appointments-0809 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*[[Deogratius Ndejembi]] is appointed as [[Vice-President of Tanzania|Vice President]] of [[Tanzania]], replacing [[Emmanuel Nchimbi]] who resigned yesterday. [https://tanzaniatimes.net/energy-minister-deogratius-ndenjembi-becomes-the-13th-vice-president-of-tanzania/ (''The Tanzania Times'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[Pro Bowl Games]]
**In [[American football]], the [[National Football League]] announces the elimination of the [[Pro Bowl Games]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7540770/2026/08/26/nfl-pro-bowl-eliminated-ending/ (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/sports/nfl-ends-pro-bowl-selection-best-best-continue--flm-2026-08-26/ (Reuters)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 25
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=25|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Iran–Oman negotiations]]
*****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] and [[Foreign Ministry (Oman)|Omani foreign minister]] [[Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi]] say that [[Iran]] and [[Oman]] have discussed a proposal to establish a temporary joint shipping route for ships in the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/25/iran-oman-strait-hormuz-oil.html (CNBC)]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****[[United States]] [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[United States Navy|the navy]] say that all mines have been cleared from the Strait of Hormuz. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/08/trump-says-hormuz-mine-free-iran-oman-agree-clear-them (''Al-Monitor'')]
****The [[United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations]] reports that an [[oil tanker]] has been [[List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war|struck]] by a unknown projectile off the coast of [[Oman]] near the strait. No casualties are reported. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2655749/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')] [https://gulfnews.com/business/energy/unknown-projectile-hits-oil-tanker-off-oman-ukmto-1.500651171 (''Gulf News'')]
***[[Analysis of the 2026 Iran war]]
****''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reports that U.S. president Trump launched [[2026 Iran war|Operation Epic Fury]] in February despite warnings from [[Vice President of the United States|U.S. vice president]] [[JD Vance]] and then-[[Director of National Intelligence|intelligence director]] [[Tulsi Gabbard]]. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260825-trump-ignored-top-level-warnings-before-launching-iran-war-report/ (Middle East Monitor)]
**[[Aftermath of the Syrian civil war]]
***The [[Kurds in Syria|Kurdish]]-led [[Syrian Democratic Forces]] announce they have officially dissolved and completed a merger with the [[Syrian Armed Forces|Syrian army]] following the end of [[Syrian civil war|the civil war]] [[Fall of the Assad regime|in 2024]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syrian-democratic-forces-dissolution-mazloum-abdi-1b7d210c96d2c608007b0411db25f453 (AP)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] and [[Shin Bet]] say that they have struck five [[Hamas]] weapons storage systems and a launch site in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], including in [[mosque|mosques]]. [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/sk5ahxjpze (Ynetnews)]
*[[Operation Southern Spear]]
**[[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***The [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] launches a strike against a vessel in the [[Caribbean Sea]] allegedly carrying [[drug smuggling|drug smugglers]], killing four people. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/26/us-military-kills-four-boat-strike-caribbean (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***Around 27 people, including four children, are reported to be killed by [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North]] (SPLM-N) militants in the [[South Kordofan]] areas of [[Kadugli]] and Abu Hitan. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260825-dozens-killed-in-attacks-by-rsf-aligned-group-in-sudans-south-kordofan-local-medical-group/ (Middle East Monitor)]
**[[War crimes in the Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|War crimes in the Sudanese civil war]]
***[[Sudan]]’s [[Kamil Idris government#Ministers|social welfare ministry]] reports that 224 cases of [[Child sexual abuse|child]] [[Wartime sexual violence|sexual violence]] have been documented since the conflict. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317889 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[AI boom]], [[Artificial intelligence in music]]
**The [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] bans wholly [[AI-generated music]] from appearing on [[ARIA Charts|its charts]] starting in September 2026. The ruling aims to distinguish fully AI-generated music and AI-assisted music, where the track is human-created but uses AI as a supporting tool. [https://www.dw.com/en/australias-music-chart-bars-fully-ai-generated-music/a-78491743 (DW)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico]]
***[[Canada]] announces retaliatory [[tariff]]s on about [[US$]]20 billion worth of [[List of imports of the United States|U.S. annual imports]] in response to the 50% [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs]] by [[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] and [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|his administration]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/canada-announces-20-bln-retaliatory-tariffs-us-goods-unveils-support-measures-2026-08-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Economic consequences of the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Boycott of Russia and Belarus]], [[Belarus–Latvia relations]], [[Latvia–Russia relations]]
***[[Latvia]]'s [[Kulbergs cabinet|cabinet ministry]] announces that the country will ban imported goods from [[Belarus]] and [[Russia]] starting September 1. [https://news.liga.net/en/amp/sanctions/news/latvia-has-banned-the-import-of-goods-from-russia-and-belarus (LIGA)]
*[[South Korea|South Korean]] automaker [[Hyundai Motor Company]] reaches a deal to end a month of [[walkout]]s by workers. [https://www-pp.afp.com/en/hyundai-reaches-tentative-deal-workers-after-strikes (AFP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Flores earthquake]]
**The toll from the [[earthquake]] in [[Flores]], [[Indonesia]], ten days ago, increases to 103 people dead and 1,666 injured. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-8633936/update-gempa-ntt-103-korban-tewas-185-ribu-orang-masih-mengungsi (Detik News)]
*[[2026 Venezuela earthquakes]]
**The death toll for the earthquakes in [[Venezuela]] this June exceeds past 6,500, with a total of 6,509 deaths reported. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/venezuela-quake-death-toll-surpasses-6500?ref=latest (''The Straits Times'')]
*At least 40 people are injured and over 300 homes are damaged in a [[tornado]] in [[Pomas]], [[Occitania (administrative region)|Occitania]], [[France]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/tornado-in-france-damages-homes-injures-dozens/a-78491206 (DW)]
*[[El Salvador]] declares a nationwide red alert for meteorological and [[Agriculture in El Salvador|agricultural]] drought, while [[Panama]] declares an [[El Niño–Southern Oscillation|El Niño]] emergency as severe dry conditions damage [[Agriculture in Panama|crops]] and reduce traffic through the [[Panama Canal]]. [https://globalnation.inquirer.net/335894/el-salvador-panama-sound-alarm-on-el-nino-fueled-drought (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**U.S. [[Central Intelligence Agency]] (CIA) [[Director of the Central Intelligence Agency|director]] [[John Ratcliffe]] visits [[Moscow]], [[Russia]], on an unscheduled military flight to meet with [[Foreign Intelligence Service (Russia)|Russian intelligence]] officials, marking the first known visit by a U.S. CIA director to Russia since 2021. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/26/kremlin-says-cia-head-met-russian-intelligence-officials-but-not-putin (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c87vg9x5d7do (BBC News)]
**[[The Wall Street Journal|''The Wall Street Journal'']] reports Ratcliffe's visit was to formally warn Russia against attacking [[NATO]] after [[military intelligence]] suggested Russia is preparing for a "limited assault" on a NATO member state. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/cia-director-john-ratcliffe-russia-visit-nato-kremlin-6342771 (AFP via CNA)] [https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/cia-chiefs-surprise-moscow-trip-was-to-warn-russia-not-to-attack-nato-c2d997f3 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[Israel and the United Nations]], [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank]]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] take control of the [[UNRWA]]'s [[vocational training]] centre in [[Qalandia]], [[East Jerusalem]], [[West Bank]], and begin removing the [[United Nations]] agency under [[Israeli law|legislation]] banning its operations in [[Israel]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260825-israel-begins-evicting-un-training-centre-for-palestinians (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
**[[Hungary]] [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Hungary)|foreign]] and [[Deputy Prime Minister of Hungary|deputy prime minister]] [[Anita Orbán]] files a [[Crime in Hungary|criminal]] complaint against the [[Second premiership of Viktor Orbán|government]] of former [[Prime Minister of Hungary|prime minister]] [[Viktor Orbán]] (no relation) over its purchase of 300 billion [[Hungarian forint|Ft]] (US$965 million) in ventilators during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] in [[Hungary|the country]]. [https://apnews.com/article/hungary-china-fraud-orban-covid19-ventilator-deal-db5dae40f252e4ba325c9505913c1ef2 (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/hungary-foreign-ministry-files-report-964-mln-pandemic-era-ventilator-deals-2026-08-25/ (Reuters)]
*[[Lawsuits involving TikTok]]
**[[Brazil]]'s [[national data protection authority]] fines [[TikTok]] [[Brazilian real|R$]]153.7 million (US$29.9 million) for inadequate [[Child safety on social networking websites|child-safety]] measures and orders its developer, [[ByteDance]], to delete [[Data privacy|improperly collected data]] and strengthen protections for users under 16. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260825-brazil-fines-tiktok-30-mn-in-powerful-signal-over-child-safety (AFP via France 24)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Hijab and burqa controversies in Europe]]
**The [[Grand Council of Aargau]] votes 78–54 to ban [[Islam in Switzerland|Islamic]] [[hijab]]s for girls aged under 16 in the [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[Cantons of Switzerland|canton]] of [[Aargau]]. The motion was sponsored by the [[The Liberals (Switzerland)|Radical-Liberal Party]]. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/swiss-politics/swiss-canton-approves-motion-to-ban-headscarves-for-girls-under-16/91955557 (Swiss Info)]
*[[Emmanuel Nchimbi]] announces his resignation as the [[Vice-President of Tanzania|vice president]] of [[Tanzania]]. [https://www.africanews.com/amp/2026/08/26/tanzanias-vice-president-emmanuel-nchimbi-resigns/ (Africanews)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tanzanias-vice-president-resigns-less-than-year-2026-08-26/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 WNBA season]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[Women's National Basketball Association]]'s [[Chicago Sky]] bans [[Enes Kanter Freedom]] from attending [[Wintrust Arena|home games]] following his altercation with [[Natasha Cloud]]. [https://www.espn.com/wnba/story/_/id/49725856/sky-ban-kanter-freedom-arena-clash-cloud (ESPN)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=24|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Operation Southern Spear]]
**[[United States strikes on alleged drug traffickers during Operation Southern Spear]]
***The [[United States Southern Command]]'s [[Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere]] launches a strike on a vessel in the eastern [[Pacific Ocean]] on alleged [[drug traffickers]], killing two people. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/24/politics/us-military-strike-alleged-drug-boat-intl-hnk (CNN)] [https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/u-s-forces-strike-vessel-in-pacific-killing-2-accused-of-trafficking-drugs (PBS)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Ukraine–United Kingdom relations]]
***[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British prime minister]] [[Andy Burnham]], during [[List of international prime ministerial trips made by Andy Burnham|a visit]] to [[Kyiv]], confirms that he has approved supplying [[Ukraine]] with the classified blueprints to produce [[Storm Shadow]] [[cruise missile]]s despite [[Russia]]n threats against such a move, which will give [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] the ability to strike key targets deep inside Russian territory. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/clyqypkrzq5o (BBC News)] [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/08/24/world/politics/burnham-world-stage-debut-ukraine/ (''The Japan Times'')]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Kharkiv strikes]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile strike on the outskirts of [[Kharkiv]] kills three people and leaves eight others wounded. [https://www.trtworld.com/article/bc04b964fde0 (TRT World)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***[[Drone warfare|Drone strike]]s by the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] hits several [[Rapid Support Forces]] [[Paramilitary]] targets in [[Nyala, Sudan|Nyala]], [[South Darfur]], [[Sudan]], hours after a cargo aircraft [[Nyala Airport|landed]] in the area. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317809 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[South Sudanese Civil War]]
**[[Jonglei clashes (2025–present)|Jonglei clashes]]
***Two [[United Nations peacekeeping|peacekeepers]] from [[Ethiopia]] of the [[United Nations Mission in South Sudan]] are killed in an [[ambush]] by unknown gunmen in [[Jonglei State]], [[South Sudan]]. Three more peacekeepers, two policemen and two civilians are also wounded. [https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique/20260824-soudan-du-sud-deux-casques-bleus-%C3%A9thiopiens-tu%C3%A9s-dans-une-embuscade-dans-le-centre-du-pays (RFI <small>in French</small>)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[International sanctions against Iran]]
***[[United States sanctions against Iran]]
****[[United States Secretary of the Treasury|U.S. treasury secretary]] [[Scott Bessent]] announces [[Economic D-Day|Operation Economic Outcast]], a campaign involving new [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] against [[Iran]], in an effort to isolate [[Government of the Islamic Republic of Iran|the regime]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0qxew81y83o (BBC News)] [https://www.politico.com/news/2026/08/24/bessent-iran-economy-01047365 (''Politico'')]
**[[Iranian economic crisis]]
***The [[Iranian rial]] reaches 2.02 million rials ahead of the [[United States dollar|U.S. dollar]], a record-low, ahead of U.S. sanctions. [https://time.com/article/2026/08/24/iranian-rial-hits-record-low-new-us-sanctions/ (''Time'')]
*[[France–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**[[President of France|French president]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] and [[Saudi Arabia]] [[Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia|crown prince]] [[Mohammed bin Salman]] reach an agreement to build a ''[[Dragon Ball Z]]'' [[Amusement park|theme park]] worth [[Euro|€]]6 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]7 million) in [[Paris]], [[France]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20260824-saudi-arabia-to-invest-%E2%82%AC6-billion-theme-parks-near-paris-macron-says (France 24)] [https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/08/25/dragon-ball-z-theme-park-france-paris.html (CNBC)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak]]
**The [[Arkansas Department of Health]] reports seven new cases of [[cyclosporiasis]] in [[Arkansas|the state]], including the first cases in [[Ashley County, Arkansas|Ashley]] and [[Cleburne County, Arkansas|Cleburne]] counties, amidst a decline in the outbreak across the [[United States]]. [https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2026/aug/24/arkansas-reports-7-new-cyclosporiasis-cases-since/ (''Arkansas Democrat-Gazette'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Syria–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] formally removes [[Syria]] from [[US-designated state sponsors of terrorism|its designated state sponsors of terrorism]] list. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/middle-east/us-removes-syria-from-state-sponsor-of-terrorism-list (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')] [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-906461 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[War crimes in the Syrian civil war]]
**[[Grand Mufti of Syria|Syria's Grand Mufti]] [[Ahmad Badreddin Hassoun]] is [[found guilty]] of committing [[war crimes]] spanning nearly 14 years of [[Syrian Civil War|civil war]] under [[Bashar al-Assad]]'s former regime and is [[Sentence (law)|sentenced]] to [[Life imprisonment|life]] in [[Imprisonment|prison]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-court-mufti-assad-sentenced-e1d6078e20fdee13f2c77c72a5b9f9a3 (AP)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/24/hold-ahmad-hassoun-assads-barrel-bomb-mufti-faces-death-penalty (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.dw.com/en/syria-sentences-assad-era-top-muslim-cleric-to-life-in-prison/a-78485344 (DW)]
*Former British [[snooker]] player [[Graeme Dott]] is found guilty of [[Child sexual abuse in the United Kingdom|sexually abusing]] two primary school children. [https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/8/24/former-snooker-world-champion-graeme-dott-convicted-of-child-sex-abuse (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/aug/24/former-world-snooker-champion-graeme-dott-found-guilty-of-sexually-abusing-children (''The Guardian'')] 
*[[South Africa]]n [[South African Police|police]] arrests four people in connection of the murder of former [[Professional boxing|professional boxer]] [[Zolani Tete]]. [https://saharareporters.com/2026/08/24/four-persons-arrested-south-african-police-murder-renowned-boxer-zolani-tete (''Sahara Reporters'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/sports/2026/8/24/four-arrested-over-fatal-shooting-of-south-african-boxer-zolani-tete (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Kazakh legislative election]]
**The [[Central Election Commission (Kazakhstan)|Central Election Commission]] of [[Kazakhstan]] declares the preliminary results from yesterday's election, stating that [[Ädilet (political party)|Ädilet]] secured 71% of the vote. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pro-presidential-party-kazakhstan-won-71-votes-weekend-election-electoral-2026-08-24/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*In [[tennis]], [[Philippine Tennis Association|Philippine]] tennis player [[Alexandra Eala]] becomes the highest-ranked [[WTA Tour|female player]] in [[Southeast Asia]]n history after reaching rank 18. [https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/alex-eala-sends-6-word-184230740.html (Yahoo! Sports)] [https://www.wtatennis.com/players/330332/alexandra-eala WTA)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 23
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=23|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Iran]] claims to have blacklisted 45 tankers in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] that breached its rules for crossing the waterway, with the [[Persian Gulf Strait Authority]] threatening fines, detainments, and confiscations against the named vessels. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-warns-vessels-violating-hormuz-transit-rules-fines-detention-2026-08-24/ (Reuters)]
****The [[Islamic Consultative Assembly|Iran parliament]]'s [[Commission on National Security and Foreign Policy|National Security and Foreign Policy Commission]] approves a draft allowing Iran to charge ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/iranian-parliamentary-committee-approves-provision-charge-ships-hormuz (Middle East Eye)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
****Two [[Israel|Israeli]] [[airstrike|airstrikes]] kill two people, including a four-year-old boy, in the [[Gaza Strip]] in violation of the [[Gaza peace plan|October 2025]] [[ceasefire]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/israeli-airstrikes-gaza-kill-two-people-including-4-year-old-boy-medics-say-2026-08-23/ (Reuters)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]]
***At least ten people are killed and several others injured in clashes between [[Somali Armed Forces|federal forces]] and residents protesting a controversial demolition and forced eviction in [[Yaqshid, Mogadishu|Yaaqshid neighbourhood]] of [[Mogadishu]]. [https://www.ftlsomalia.com/violence-erupts-in-mogadishu-as-residents-protest-demolition-of-homes-in-tookiyo-neighbourhood/ (FTL Somalia)] [https://garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/somalia-heavy-weapons-reported-used-during-mogadishu-evictions-as-turkish-f-16s-fly-over-capital (''Garowe Online'')] [https://shabellemedia.com/mogadishu-protests-turn-violent-as-residents-resist-home-demolitions/ (Shabelle Media)]
**The [[Turkish Armed Forces]] carries out an [[airstrike]] in [[Garmaal]], [[Puntland]], killing at least four people, in response to the previous [[Piracy|hijacking]] of a [[Cameroon]]-flagged [[Watercraft|vessel]] by [[Piracy off the coast of Somalia|Somali pirates]], which was transporting military equipment to the [[Camp TURKSOM]] in [[Mogadishu]]. The [[Puntland Security Force|authorities of Puntland]] identified the victims as civilian [[Fisherman|fishermen]]. [https://www.somaliguardian.com/news/somalia-news/somalia-defends-turkish-drone-strike-puntland-civilians/ (Somali Guardian)]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***The [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] and the [[March 23 Movement|M23]] rebel group agree on a roadmap for further peace negotiations under the [[2025 DRC–Rwanda peace agreement|Doha Framework Agreement]] after talks in [[Switzerland]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/dr-congo-m23-fighters-agree-roadmap-for-peace-talks-joint-statement/article71381809.ece (AFP via ''The Hindu'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Sudan]]'s [[Ministry of Defence (Sudan)|defence ministry]] says that the country's [[Sudanese Armed Forces|armed forces]] (SAF) have shot down a "hostile" drone from [[Ethiopia]] entering its airspace, which was seen flying over the [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] region. [https://saudigazette.com.sa/article/663972/world/sudan-says-it-shot-down-hostile-drone-launched-from-ethiopia (''Saudi Gazette'')] [https://sudanhorizon.com/saf-shoots-down-drone-entering-sudanese-airspace-from-ethiopia/ (''Sudan Horizon'')]
**The SAF-allied [[Darfur Joint Protection Force|Joint Forces]] says that they have destroyed a [[Rapid Support Forces]] convoy in the northern desert [[Libya–Sudan border|bordering]] [[Libya]], along with capturing several vehicles and drone equipment. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317787 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Haitian crisis (2018–present)|Haitian crisis]]
**At least 47 people are killed and over 50 others are kidnapped by [[Gangs in Haiti|armed gangs]] in [[Kenscoff]], [[Ouest (department)|Ouest department]], [[Haiti]], in one of the largest mass kidnappings in the conflict. [https://apnews.com/article/haiti-kenscoff-gangs-killed-kidnapped-attack-1690b1523421eb72aa260d9d56b5d521 (AP)]
*[[Mali War]]
**The [[Tuareg people|Tuareg]]-led [[Azawad Liberation Front]] releases 22 [[Mali]]an [[Malian Armed Forces|soldiers]], some held for more than three years, in exchange for at least eight of its fighters and several civilian detainees. [https://macaubusiness.com/tuareg-rebels-release-22-mali-soldiers-security-sources/ (AFP via ''Macau Business'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Iván Manjarrez, a [[La Línea (gang)|La Línea]] ringleader accused of controlling [[illegal logging]] in the Chihuahua Mountains, is killed during a security operation in [[Bocoyna Municipality]], [[Chihuahua (state)|Chihuahua]], [[Mexico]]. [https://oem.com.mx/elheraldodechihuahua/local/abaten-al-lider-criminal-el-19-tras-enfrentamiento-en-san-juanito-31706703 (''El Heraldo de Chihuahua'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 United States wildfires]]
**[[2026 Nevada wildfires]]
***The Hawk Fire near [[Reno, Nevada|Reno]], [[Nevada]], [[United States|U.S.]], grows to more than 20 square miles (53 sq. km.) and spreads across the [[Peavine Peak]] of [[Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest]], prompting evacuations. [https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/human-caused-wildfire-approaches-reno-nevada-forcing-thousands-of-evacuations (PBS)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/tens-thousands-ordered-evacuate-nevada-fire-threatens-reno-2026-08-23/ (Reuters)]
*A {{M|w|5.9}} earthquake strikes southern [[Ibaraki Prefecture]] in [[Japan]], injuring 45 people. [https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUD222HP0S6A820C2000000/ (''The Nikkei'')] [https://www.fnn.jp/articles/-/1099791 (FNN)]
*At least 30 people are killed and six more are wounded when a [[landfill]] collapses in [[Conakry]], [[Guinea]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4g3g36z7p6o (BBC News)]
*The [[Indian Coast Guard]] and [[Indian Navy|Navy]]'s [[Eastern Naval Command]] reports that two crew members from the [[Panama]]-[[Flag state|flagged]] ''MV Ocean Winner'' have been rescued after it sank off the coast of [[Bay of Bengal]] in eastern [[India]]. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/vijayawada/2-rescued-22-missing-after-china-bound-panama-flagged-cargo-ship-sinks-off-odisha-coast/amp_articleshow/133446127.cms (''Times of India'')] [https://www.newindianexpress.com/amp/story/states/odisha/2026/Aug/24/navy-icg-step-up-search-operations-as-mv-ocean-winner-still-untraceable-with-22-crewmen (''New Indian Express'')]
*Four people are found dead after a fire at a restaurant in [[Thusis]], [[Switzerland]], two days ago. The search and rescue operation are concluded. [https://www.rsi.ch/info/ticino-grigioni-e-insubria/Incendio-a-Thusis-il-bilancio-%C3%A8-di-4-morti--4006539.html (RSI)]

'''Law and crime'''
* [[Billings, Montana massacre]]
**Eight people, including four children, are killed in a domestic shooting and house fire in [[Billings, Montana|Billings]], [[Montana]], United States. The gunman kills himself at the scene. [https://apnews.com/article/billings-montana-family-killed-house-burned-e977fa5e9cd635eea4e111ad8b2c79ff (AP)]
*The [[Israel Defense Forces]]'s [[Duvdevan Unit]] says that they arrested four [[Palestinians]] over the weekend, including two allegedly affiliated with the [[Islamic State]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-arrests-4-palestinian-terror-suspects-in-ramallah-area-including-2-affiliated-with-isis/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Kazakh legislative election]]
**[[Kazakhstan]]is vote to elect 145 members to the [[1st Kurultai|1st convocation]] of the [[unicameral]] [[Kurultai (Kazakhstan)|Kurultai]] following the [[2026 Kazakh constitutional referendum|passage]] of the new [[Constitution of Kazakhstan|constitution]] on 15 March. Contesting parties must get at least five percent of the vote in order for lists to gain [[proportional representation]]. [https://apnews.com/article/kazakhstan-election-tokayev-ef0cb883baa7344cc89fc1e655edbd5d (AP)] [https://www.dw.com/en/kazakhstans-future-after-the-elections-russia-eu-or-china/a-78449637 (DW)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 IndyCar Series]]
**[[Freedom 250 Grand Prix]]
***In [[open-wheel racing]], American [[auto racing]] driver [[Kyle Kirkwood]] wins the [[IndyCar]] [[Freedom 250 Grand Prix]] event at the [[National Mall]] in [[Washington D.C.]], United States. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7533879/2026/08/23/kyle-kirkwood-wins-indycar-freedom-250-washington-dc/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')] [https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/motor/2026/08/23/indycar-race-dc-freedom-250-leaderboard-timeline-president-trump-alex-palou/91431154007/ (''The Indianapolis Star'')]
*[[2026 WNBA season]]
**In [[basketball]], former [[National Basketball Association]] player [[Enes Kanter Freedom]] is ejected from a [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]] game between the [[Chicago Sky]] and [[Indiana Fever]] at [[Wintrust Arena]] after being confronted by [[Natasha Cloud]] for his controversy in declaring for the [[WNBA draft|2027 WNBA draft]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sky-enes-kanter-natasha-cloud-8bf4dc50c06a01c402c1c4dc75f313eb# (AP)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 22
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=22|top=yes}}

<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Aftermath of the Syrian civil war]]
***[[Israeli invasion of Syria (2024–present)|Israeli invasion of Syria]]
****The [[Israeli Army Radio]] reports that the [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) launched a [[Drone warfare|drone strike]] against a militant in [[Southern Syria|southern]] [[Syria]] whom they accuse of prepping an [[improvised explosive device]] (IED) attack against Israeli troops currently [[military occupation|occupying]] the region. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-906244 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[Media in Syria|Syrian state media]] reports that an IED struck a bus carrying [[Internal Security Forces (Syria)|security forces]] on the [[Maarounah]]–[[Al-Tall, Syria|Al-Tall]] road near [[Damascus]], injuring several passengers. [https://www.arabnews.jp/en/middle-east/article_176527/ (AFP via ''Arab News Japan'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Tunnel warfare in the Gaza Strip]]
****The IDF says that Sharif al-Hasanat, an alleged [[Hamas]] company commander affiliated with the [[Deir al-Balah]] Battalion of the [[Al-Qassam Brigades]], was killed in an [[airstrike]] in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]], violating the ongoing [[ceasefire]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-strike-on-gaza-earlier-killed-hamas-commander-involved-in-attempts-to-restore-tunnels/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.jfeed.com/latest-news/israeli-strike-kills-hamas-commander-in-deir-al-balah-gaza-50000 (JFeed)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Canada–United States relations]]
**[[2025–2026 United States trade war with Canada and Mexico]]
***The [[United States]] imposes 50% [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs]] on about [[US$]]20 billion of [[Economy of Canada|Canadian goods]] after [[Multilateral trade negotiations|trade talks]] fail to produce an agreement. [[Prime Minister of Canada|Canadian prime minister]] [[Mark Carney]] says [[Canada]] will impose equivalent retaliatory tariffs. [https://tribune.net.ph/2026/08/22/us-canada-fail-to-reach-tariff-pact (AFP via ''Daily Tribune'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Sudan]]'s [[Ministry of Industry and Trade (Sudan)|industry ministry]] establishes a high-level committee to rehabilitate industrial zones in [[Khartoum State]] that were damaged during the ongoing [[civil war]] along with helping shuttered factories resume production. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317747 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Zamboye mine collapse]]
**The [[Central African Republic]]'s [[Politics of the Central African Republic|government]] closes down a [[Gold mining|gold mine]] site  in [[Zamboye]] that killed over 100 people after it collapsed, citing non-compliance with regulatory procedures. [https://apnews.com/article/central-african-republic-gold-mine-closed-bf3cfcdbad6dae8a43fc0ec250a30aab (AP)]
*The [[Indian Coast Guard]] launches a rescue operation after a [[Panama]]–[[Flag state|flagged]] cargo bulk carrier sunk off the coast of eastern [[India]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/panamaflagged-cargo-ship-sinks-off-eastern-india-coast-guard-says-2026-08-22/ (Reuters)]
*Seven people are killed, including two [[Law enforcement in the United Kingdom|police officers]], and several others are injured in a three-vehicle collision on the [[A66 road]] in [[Middlesbrough]], [[North Yorkshire]], [[England]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cq6151gdp50t (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/multiple-deaths-after-uk-police-car-crash-police-say-2026-08-22/ (Reuters)]
*Five people are killed in a head-on road collision along the [[Lagos–Badagry Expressway]] near [[Lagos]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://dailypost.ng/2026/08/22/five-killed-in-fatal-head-on-collision-on-lagos-badagry-expressway/ (''The Daily Post Nigeria'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[List of pastoral trips made by Pope Leo XIV|Pastoral trips made by Pope Leo XIV]]
**[[Pope]] [[Leo XIV]] makes a half-day [[papal travel|papal visit]] to [[San Marino]], including meeting with the [[Captains Regent]], the local religious community, and visiting the [[Basilica di San Marino|Basilica of Saint Marinus]]. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2026-08/pope-leo-xiv-republic-san-marino-civil-leaders-human-person.html (Vatican News)] [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2026/08/22/260822a.html (Holy See)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Pacific Islands Forum Fisheries Agency]] reports that authorities in [[Kiribati]], [[Palau]], and [[Papua New Guinea]] have detained four [[Fishing industry in China|Chinese]] and [[Aquaculture in Indonesia|Indonesian fishing]] vessels for alleged [[illegal fishing]] or licence violations during a regional enforcement operation across the [[Pacific Ocean]]. [https://tribune.net.ph/2026/08/21/pacific-nations-detain-chinese-indonesian-boats-over-illegal-fishing (AFP via ''Daily Tribune'')]
*American far-right activist [[Jake Lang]], who was [[Pardon of January 6 United States Capitol attack defendants|pardoned]] last year for his role in the [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riot]] at the [[United States Capitol]], is arrested during a protest in [[Minneapolis]], [[Minnesota]], [[U.S.|U.S]]. [https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/nation/2026/08/23/jake-lang-arrested-suspicion-of-rioting-muslim-minneapolis-dearborn/91431272007/ (''The Detroit News'')] [https://www.startribune.com/far-right-agitator-jake-lang-arrested-on-suspicion-of-rioting-in-minneapolis/601881529 (''Minnesota Star Tribune'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*A humanoid robot at the [[World Humanoid Robot Games]] in [[Beijing]], [[China]], runs 100 meters in 9.39 seconds, surpassing a record set by [[Usain Bolt]] of 9.58 seconds at the [[World Athletics Championships]] in [[2009 World Championships in Athletics|2009]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/chinese-humanoid-robot-lightning-beats-human-100m-world-record-rcna593869 (NBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 IndyCar Series]]
**In [[open-wheel racing]], the [[Freedom 250 Grand Prix]] kicks off in [[Washington, D.C.]] on the [[National Mall]] to commemorate the [[United States Semiquincentennial|250th anniversary]] of the [[United States Declaration of Independence|U.S. Declaration of Independence]], with former [[NASCAR]] driver [[Jeff Gordon]] winning the [[International Race of Champions]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7531751/2026/08/22/jeff-gordon-wins-iroc-race-freedom-250-grand-prix/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')] [https://www.motorsport.com/general/news/jeff-gordon-sweeps-iroc-races-in-washington-dc/10848440/ (Motorsport)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 21
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=21|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Kryvyi Rih strikes (2022–present)|Kryvyi Rih strikes]]
****[[Unmanned Systems Forces of Russia|Russian drone strikes]] on a shopping center in [[Kryvyi Rih]], [[Dnipropetrovsk Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], kill at least 16 people and injure more than 130 others, including 22 children. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/five-killed-52-wounded-russian-strike-ukraines-kryvyi-rih-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]
***[[Mykolaiv strikes (2022–present)|Mykolaiv strikes]]
****A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] strike on a neighborhood in [[Mykolaiv Oblast]], Ukraine, kills four people, including three children, according to [[Ministry of Internal Affairs (Ukraine)|Ukrainian interior minister]] [[Ivan Vyhivskyi]]. [https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4156420-russian-strike-on-mykolaiv-region-kills-four-including-three-children.html (Ukrinform)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[Pakistan Armed Forces|Pakistani forces]] raid multiple militant hideouts, killing 12 suspected [[Pakistani Taliban]] militants in [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]] and 37 suspected Baloch separatist militants in [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-security-forces-widen-operation-against-militants-e5dadb257138c1b59b3d821d23fe2fff (AP)]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[List of ethnic armed organisations in Myanmar|Resistance fighters]] and a local activist say [[Myanmar]]'s [[Tatmadaw|military]] deployed hundreds of troops around the proposed [[Dawei Special Economic Zone]] in the [[Tanintharyi Region]], burning villages and pushing resistance groups back as [[Government of Myanmar|the government]] seeks to revive the project. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmar-military-offensive-targets-land-russia-backed-port-project-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]
**At least 14 people are reportedly killed and 20 others are injured after Myanmar's military launched an [[airstrike]] on a [[Buddhism|Buddhist]] [[monastery]] compound in [[Myaung Township]] during a religious gathering. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/myanmar-military-airstrike-monastery-kills-14-6334766 (AFP via CNA)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**The annual [[Ashenda]] festival in [[Mekelle]], [[Tigray Region]], [[Ethiopia]], is cancelled over [[Drone warfare|drone strike]] fears. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c24me64n31qo (BBC News)] [https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/358147480654073 (Binance)]
*[[American film industry|American]] fantasy film ''[[The Odyssey (2026 film)|The Odyssey]]'' reaches [[US$]]1.35 billion at the worldwide [[box office]] to become the [[List of highest-grossing R-rated films|highest-grossing R-rated film]], surpassing ''[[Deadpool & Wolverine]]''. [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/aug/21/the-odyssey-highest-grossing-r-rated-film-of-all-time (''The Guardian'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Panama Canal]] announces it will limit the number of ships allowed to cross the passage over the next month due to [[El Niño]] causing droughts in the region. [https://www.dw.com/en/panama-canal-el-nino/a-78453054 (DW)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The death toll of a boat capsizing off the coast of [[Zambezia Province]], [[Mozambique]] from August 16 rises to 12 after five bodies of those unaccounted for are found by search teams. [https://clubofmozambique.com/news/mozambique-death-toll-reaches-12-after-pebane-boat-sinking-as-bodies-of-last-five-missing-people-recovered/ (Club of Mozambique)]
*Three people are killed and six more wounded in an explosion at a house in the Ain al-Qasab village of [[Idlib]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/explosion-at-house-kills-3-injures-6-in-northwestern-syria/4033386 (AA)] [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/blast-syrias-idlib-kills-least-three?topic=War%2520on%2520Iran&nid=442386&fid=557639 (''Middle East Eye'')]
*Five people are reported missing and eight others are injured after a fire at a restaurant with apartments in [[Thusis]], [[Grisons]], [[Switzerland]]. [https://kuwaittimes.com/article/48470/world/five-missing-eight-injured-in-swiss-apartment-fire/ (AFP via ''Kuwait Times'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cy8e6g13497o (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Project Elephant]]
**[[India]]'s [[Supreme Court of India|Supreme Court]] orders [[States and union territories of India|states]] to protect [[Indian elephant|elephant]] corridors, identify and remove obstructions, and prohibit groups from using fire to drive wild elephants away amid increasing [[habitat loss]] and [[human-elephant conflict]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260821-top-india-court-orders-new-steps-to-protect-threatened-elephants (AFP via France 24)]
*Around 16 people in [[Sudan]]'s [[Red Sea State|Red Sea]] [[States of Sudan|state]] have reportedly died from a [[heat stroke]] amidst a rise in temperatures in the state. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260821-16-killed-by-heatstroke-in-sudans-red-sea-state/ (Middle East Monitor)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Fagersta school stabbing]]
**A person is killed and three other people are injured in a [[mass stabbing]], carried out with a [[sword]], at a [[Secondary school|high school]] in [[Fagersta]], [[Sweden]]. The perpetrator is arrested at the scene. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/several-people-injured-sword-attack-swedish-school-municipality-says-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Capital punishment in Japan]]
**[[Japan]] executes a 58-year-old man for a 2009 [[arson]] attack that killed five people at a [[pachinko parlor]] in [[Osaka]]. It is the first execution under [[Sanae Takaichi]]'s [[Premiership of Sanae Takaichi|premiership]]. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2026/08/22/osaka-arsonist-hanged (AFP via ''The Star'')] [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/08/21/japan/crime-legal/death-penalty-execution/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*[[Lawsuits involving TikTok]]
**[[TikTok]] agrees to pay $400 million to settle a [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] lawsuit alleging violations of [[Children's Online Privacy Protection Act|federal children's privacy law]] through the collection of personal data from users under 13 without [[parental consent]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260821-tiktok-to-pay-400-mn-settlement-in-us-children-s-privacy-case (AFP via France 24)]
*[[War crimes in the Gaza war]], [[Humanitarian aid during the Gaza war]], [[Gaza genocide]]
**[[Ministry of Justice (Turkey)|Turkish justice minister]] [[Akın Gürlek]] announces that [[Turkey]] has issued an [[Interpol]] arrest warrant for [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] for his role in attacks on activists seeking to deliver [[Humanitarian aid to Gaza|humanitarian aid]] to [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20260821-middle-east-live-hormuz-shipping-traffic-falls-as-iran-us-talks-stall (France 24)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-seek-interpol-notice-netanyahu-gaza-flotilla-case-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Hong Kong]] [[Hong Kong Court of First Instance|Court of First Instance]] convicts [[Lee Cheuk-yan]] and [[Chow Hang-tung]] of [[Inciting subversion of state power|incitement to subversion]] over their leadership of [[Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China|a group]] that organized annual [[1989 Tiananmen Square protests and massacre|Tiananmen crackdown]] vigils. They face up to 10 years in [[Prisons in Hong Kong|prison]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260821-hong-kong-tiananmen-activists-found-guilty-of-inciting-subversion (AFP via RFI)]
*The [[Russia]]n [[Ministry of Justice (Russia)|justice ministry]] designates independent [[Mass media in Russia|news outlet]] [[Mediazona]] a "[[Russian foreign agent law|foreign agent]]" for a second time, accusing it of publishing [[Russian fake news laws|false information]] about [[Law enforcement in Russia|law enforcement]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/russia-designates-independent-mediazona-news-outlet-foreign-agent-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*In [[Mexico]], [[Sinaloa]]n [[Governor of Sinaloa|governor]] [[Rubén Rocha Moya]] resumes office after a four-month suspension while contesting [[Illegal drug trade in the United States|U.S. drug-trafficking]] charges and an [[Extradition law in the United States|extradition]] request. Mexican prosecutors say they find insufficient evidence linking him to criminal conduct. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260821-mexican-governor-wanted-on-us-drug-charges-returns-to-job (AFP via France 24)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026–27 Malaysia Super League]]
**In [[association football]], [[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]] claims a [[List of world association football records|world record]] for the longest unbeaten run in top-flight league play, reaching 109 matches after defeating [[Kuching City F.C.|Kuching City]] 3–0 in [[Malaysia]]'s [[Malaysia Super League|Super League]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260821-malaysia-s-jdt-claims-unbeaten-run-world-record (AFP via RFI)]
*[[2026–27 DFB-Pokal]]
**85 people were injured, including 35 police officers, after Kaiserslautern fans launched flares towards the main stand, while Mannheim fans stormed the pitch, causing the match between [[1. FC Kaiserslautern|Kaiserslautern]] and [[SV Waldhof Mannheim|Mannheim]] to be temporarily interrupted. [https://www.goal.com/en/news/video-pitch-invasion-clashes-and-85-injuries-german-cup-match-descends-into-utter-chaos/blt0ce28fb431648f95 (Goal)]
