{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=20|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East]]
****The {{USS|George Washington|CVN-73|6}} arrives in the [[Middle East]] to relieve the {{USS|Abraham Lincoln|CVN-72|6}} amidst a nine-month deployment and reports of [[USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72)#Mental_health_on_the_Lincoln_during_Iran_War|mental health challenges]] among the crew and supply shortages on the [[aircraft carrier]] during the Iran war. [https://apnews.com/article/aircraft-carrier-washington-lincoln-iran-war-trump-10ddf7b55104e0eeec2e9213e1021b98 (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/20/uss-lincoln-washington-sailors-military (''The Guardian'')]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****Data from [[MarineTraffic|Kpler]] shows that seven ships have passed through the [[Strait of Hormuz]], with four entering and three exiting the [[waterway]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/hormuz-ship-crossings-hover-single-digits-data-shows-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza war]], [[Palestinian war crimes]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] accuses [[Hamas]] of using the [[Nasser Hospital]] in [[Khan Yunis]] to carry out interrogations and [[Torture during the Gaza war|torture]] [[Palestinians]]. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-906118 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2026 Mali offensives]]
***[[Human Rights Watch]] reports that [[Africa Corps (Russia)|Africa Corps]] forces [[Summary execution|summarily killed]] nine civilians, including four children, in [[Mali]] last month. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/20/russian-paramilitaries-in-mali-kill-nine-including-children-hrw (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/08/20/mali-russias-africa-corps-massacres-villagers (HRW)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North]] led by [[Abdelaziz al-Hilu]] regains control of [[Kauda, Sudan|Kauda]], [[South Kordofan]], following two days of clashes with [[Otoro language|Otoro]] fighters. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317666 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Unexploded ordnance]] from past fighting is detonated after being tampered with in [[Maungdaw Township]], [[Rakhine State]], [[Myanmar]], injuring ten children. [https://www.bnionline.net/en/news/unexploded-grenade-explosion-injures-10-children-northern-rakhine (Burma News International)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[London Stock Exchange Group|LSEG]] data shows that a vessel in [[France]] is loading wheat destined for [[Sudan]], marking the first export of wheat from France to Sudan since August 2008. [https://www.bairdmaritime.com/shipping/dry-cargo/bulkers/france-loads-first-wheat-shipment-to-sudan-in-18-years (Baird Maritime)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Security Aviation Flight 45]]
**Eight people are killed when a [[Cessna 441 Conquest II]] aircraft crashes at the [[Cape Newenham Long Range Radar Site]] in Western [[Alaska]], [[United States]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/charter-plane-crash-in-us-state-of-alaska-claims-all-8-lives-on-board-report/4033450 (AA)] [https://apnews.com/article/alaska-charter-plane-crash-army-cd21190cad6b7246d903677685f1e928 (AP)] [https://www.alaskasnewssource.com/2026/08/21/report-plane-crashes-western-alaska-with-multiple-people-board/ (KTUU-TV)]
*A {{M|w|6.7}} earthquake strikes the [[Parinacochas province]] in [[Peru]]. [https://apnews.com/article/peru-earthquake-andes-mountains-0018e250224f1cd86fc4c99cb33a9537 (AP)]
*Four railway workers on the [[Tōbu Nikkō Line]] are killed after being struck by a [[Limited express]] train in [[Kanuma, Tochigi|Kanuma]], [[Tochigi Prefecture]], [[Japan]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5yrnz24j22o (BBC News)] [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/08/20/japan/workers-struck-by-train/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*[[Mauritania]]'s [[coast guard]] rescues more than 300 migrants, including 40 children, from an overcrowded boat off the country's coast after finding them in distress. [https://today.lorientlejour.com/article/1545233/more-than-300-migrants-including-40-children-rescued-off-mauritania-coastguard.html (AFP via ''L'Orient–Le Jour'')]
*At least 13 [[Tunisia]]ns are missing and two are rescued after their boat capsized off [[Tunisia]] while sailing toward [[Italy]], according to the Tunisian Observatory for Human Rights. One survivor is in critical condition. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/least-13-tunisians-missing-after-migrant-boat-sinks-off-tunisia-group-says-2026-08-22/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] says that the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] will receive 70,000 doses of the [[Ebola vaccine]] candidate developed by [[Merck & Co.|Merck]] to combat the [[Ebola]] outbreak in the country. [https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/congo-set-to-receive-70000-ervebo-vaccines-to-contain-ebola-outbreak-who-says (CNBC)] [https://www.africanews.com/amp/2026/08/20/dr-congo-receives-70000-ebola-vaccine-doses-for-outbreak-response/ (Africanews)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Ecuador–United States relations]], [[Mexico–United States relations]]
**The [[U.S. Department of the Treasury|U.S. Treasury Department]] issues [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] on 15 people allegedly involved in a [[drug trafficking]] [[illegal drug trade|network]] shipping thousands of kilograms of [[cocaine]] from [[Ecuador]] through [[Mexico]] to the United States. [https://apnews.com/article/us-treasury-ecuador-mexico-drug-trafficking-choneros-lobos-82270ff419944177276b7d655647739d (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2025 Mexican fuel smuggling scandal]], [[Argentina–Mexico relations]]
**[[Argentina]] deports a [[Mexican Armed Forces|Mexican]] Rear Admiral accused of leading a fuel-smuggling network inside the [[Mexican Navy]] to [[Mexico]] after the [[Federal government of Mexico|Mexican government]] withdraws its [[extradition]] request. He is taken to the [[Federal Social Readaptation Center No. 1|Altiplano maximum-security prison]], where his brother and alleged co-leader, Vice Admiral Manuel Roberto Farías Laguna, is also imprisoned. [https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2026/08/21/fgr-revela-la-operacion-de-la-red-de-huachicol-fiscal-integrada-por-los-hermanos-farias-laguna/ (Infobae <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[Corruption in China]], [[Chinese real estate crisis (2020–present)|Chinese real estate crisis]]
**A [[China|Chinese]] [[Judicial system of China|court]] sentences [[Evergrande Group|Evergrande]] founder [[Hui Ka Yan]] to [[Life imprisonment in China|life imprisonment]] for [[fraud|financial fraud]], [[bribery]], and [[embezzlement]], and fines Evergrande and its real estate arm a combined [[Renminbi|¥]]15.8 billion ([[United States dollar|US$]]2.35 billion). [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/east-asia/china-evergrande-founder-hui-ka-yan-sentenced-life-in-prison-6330256 (AFP via CNA)]
*Two [[ANC]] members including a former Knysna councillor are shot dead, one day after a sitting Knysna councillor is shot dead in a suspected internal ANC faction fight in [[Knysna]], [[Western Cape]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.knysnaplettherald.com/News/Article/Local-News/3-murders-follow-long-history-of-political-strife-in-knysna-anc-202608210113 (Knysna-Plett Herald)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bangladeshi presidential election]]
**The [[Jatiya Sangsad]] elects [[Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir]] as the [[President of Bangladesh|President]] of [[Bangladesh]] in the first contested [[Presidential elections in Bangladesh|presidential election]] in 35 years. Alamgir will take office tomorrow. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/20/bangladesh-elects-ruling-party-veteran-alamgir-as-president (Al Jazeera)] [https://apnews.com/article/bangladesh-president-hasina-tarique-khaleda-9884e60119d1ba29053cb883fd75234b (AP)] [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/417930/mirza-fakhrul-islam-alamgir-elected-bangladesh%E2%80%99s (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
*[[President of Cameroon|Cameroon President]] [[Paul Biya]] returns to [[Cameroon|the country]] following a two-and-a-half-month absence. [https://www.africanews.com/2026/08/20/cameroons-president-biya-returns-home-after-unexplained-10-week-absence/ (Africanews)]
*[[Syrian Kurdish]] leader [[Mazloum Abdi]] says the integration of [[Syrian Democratic Forces|Kurdish military]], security, and administrative institutions into the [[Syria]]n state is complete following an agreement reached with [[President of Syria|president]] [[Ahmed al-Sharaa]] in January. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260820-syrian-kurds-announce-completion-of-civil-military-integration-with-damascus (AFP via France 24)]

'''Sports'''
*In [[American football]], the [[National Football League]] fines the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and the [[New Orleans Saints]] $500,000 each after they started a brawl after a joint practice session at the Cowboys' facility in [[Oxnard, California|Oxnard]], [[California]], United States. [https://apnews.com/article/cowboys-saints-practice-fines-379642b637ebef52f0147757a61aba01 (AP)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=19|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Strait of Hormuz campaign]]
*****''[[Axios (website)|Axios]]'' reports that the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] has created a new [[shipping lane]] in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] to help ships transit through the [[waterway]], including the facilitating of 10 million [[Barrel (unit)#Oil barrels|barrels of oil]] per day. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-906042 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.axios.com/2026/08/19/hormuz-iran-oil-gulf-trump (''Axios'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Gaza peace plan]], [[Qatar as a mediator in conflict]]
****[[Prime Minister of Qatar|Qatari prime minister]] and [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Qatar)|foreign minister]] [[Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani]] meets with [[List of leaders of Hamas|Hamas leader]] [[Khalil al-Hayya]] and other senior leaders in [[Doha]], [[Qatar]], to discuss the situation in the [[Gaza Strip]] and other occupied [[Palestine|Palestinian]] territories. [https://dohanews.co/qatar-pm-fm-meets-hamas-leaders-as-gaza-ceasefire-roadmap-faces-hurdles/ (''Doha News'')]
***[[War crimes in the Gaza war]], [[Gaza genocide]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) launches an investigation into troop conduct for their roles in the [[Killing of Hind Rajab|2024 killing]] of five-year-old [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] girl [[Hind Rajab]], her family, and 15 [[Killing of health workers in the Gaza war|paramedics]]. [https://apnews.com/article/israel-military-hind-rajab-gaza-parademics-investigations-c0a733a3ac78660b474e5bdb47154f8b (AP)]
***Around ten people are reported killed in an [[Israel]]i [[airstrike]] on a police station in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/gaza-israel-kills-nine-gaza-police-station-bombing (Middle East Eye)]
***The IDF says that the [[Israeli Air Force|Air Force]] have targeted two [[Hamas]] commanders, including one who participated in the [[October 7 attacks]], along with [[Tunnel warfare in the Gaza Strip|Hamas tunnels]] in the [[Gaza Strip]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-906011 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***The IDF also confirms that they have killed four [[Nukhba forces|Nukhba force]] commanders from the [[Al-Qassam Brigades]] wing of [[Hamas]] in an airstrike on a cafe yesterday in [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-905915 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-4-of-6-people-killed-in-gaza-cafe-strike-were-nukhba-fighters/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[President of Ukraine|president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] says that a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile and [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] on [[Kyiv]] killed at least 15 people and injured 40 others, damaging residential buildings, a children's hospital, and a school. [https://abcnews.com/International/massive-russian-missile-strike-kyiv-kills-12-people/story?id=135797221 (ABC News)] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c98vzmden5yo (BBC News)]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
** Nine [[Jalisco New Generation Cartel|CJNG]] members, including four ringleaders, are arrested during a [[Mexican Armed Forces|military]] operation in Tinaja de Vargas y Colesio, municipality of [[Tanhuato]] and [[Ecuandureo]]. Among the detained is Heraclio Guerrero aka "Tio Lako", leader identified as behind the operation of cartel training camps and the offensive during the [[2026 Jalisco operation]]. [https://cnnespanol.cnn.com/2026/08/19/mexico/bloqueos-violencia-michoacan-detencion-objetivos-orix (CNN en Español <small>in Spanish</small>)] [https://www.democrata.es/en/international/expansion-nine-members-of-the-jalisco-new-generation-cartel-arrested-in-a-large-operation-in-michoacan/ (''Democrata'')]
*The [[United Nations]] reports that 36 humanitarian workers and contractors in [[South Sudan]] have been killed since the start of [[2026|the year]], surpassing the 31 killed [[2025|last year]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-sudan-violence-humanitarian-workers-54617e70313b9ee79a2bae923258084a (AP)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[Iranian economic crisis]], [[Economic D-Day]]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces an [[economic warfare|economic war]] against [[Iran]], along with new sanctions for countries trading with Iran. [https://thehill.com/homenews/administration/6040249-trump-announces-economic-warfare-iran/ (''The Hill'')]
**The [[Office for National Statistics]] reports that inflation in the [[United Kingdom]] rose to 2.9% last month amidst the [[2026 Iran war|Iran war]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/aug/19/uk-inflation-rise-iran-war-energy-consumer-prices-index-interest-rates (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Economy of the United States]]
**The [[United States Department of the Treasury]] reports that [[national debt of the United States|the national debt]] surpassed [[List of countries by external debt|$40 trillion for the first time]] the previous day, and is currently at $40.047 trillion. [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-debt-crosses-40-trillion-threshold-after-doubling-under-trump-biden-2026-08-19/ (Reuters)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/us-government-debt-passes-40-trillion-mark-for-the-first-time.html (CNBC)] [https://apnews.com/article/treasury-national-debt-limit-a27a8d3651ff810b25c610d3e1b6259d (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Mount Ololokwe helicopter crash]]
**Six passengers, including [[Ecuador]]ian intelligence head [[Michele Sensi-Contugi]] and his wife, and the pilot are killed in a helicopter crash on [[Mount Ololokwe]] in [[Samburu County]], [[Kenya]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/4-americans-killed-helicopter-crash-kenya-rcna593384 (NBC News)]
*At least 52 people are killed when a boat carrying farm workers capsizes in [[Goronyo]], [[Sokoto State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://lagostelevision.com/52-bodies-buried-after-sokoto-boat-accident/ (Lagos Television)]
*Twenty-three people are killed and five others are injured in a [[head-on collision]] between a bus and a truck on the [[BR-373 (Brazil highway)|BR-373]] near [[Ipiranga, Paraná|Ipiranga]], [[Paraná (state)|Paraná]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/bus-truck-head-on-collision-parana-brazil-kills-least-21-2026-08-19/ (Reuters)] [https://noticias.uol.com.br/cotidiano/ultimas-noticias/2026/08/19/acidente-br-373-parana.ghtm (UOL)]
*Nine people, including eight [[Bangladesh]]i nationals, are killed and six others are injured in a hotel fire in [[Kolkata]], [[West Bengal]], [[India]]. [https://apnews.com/article/india-west-bengal-kolkata-hotel-fire-bcad29dde1b8eab369f3c182e6ede4e5 (AP)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/asia/india/kolkata-hotel-fire-bangladeshi-nationals-killed-b3035576.html (''The Independent'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Bangladesh measles outbreak]]
**Amidst the ongoing [[measles]] outbreak in [[Bangladesh]], [[Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Bangladesh)|health minister]] [[M. A. Muhit]] says that the outbreak will need 2-3 months for it to be under control. [https://www.jagonews24.com/en/national/news/95309 (Jagonews24)]
**In a study from the [[Bangladesh Shishu Hospital & Institute]], around 82% of children who died from measles during the outbreak in Bangladesh did not receive adequate or exclusive [[breastfeeding]] during their first 6 months of their life. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/health/417833/82%25-of-children-who-died-from-measles-lacked (''Dhaka Tribune'')] [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/health/82-children-who-died-measles-were-not-exclusively-breastfed-study-1519491 (''The Business Standard'')]
**Four more children are reported to have died from measles in 24 hours, bringing the death toll in the country from the outbreak past 922. [https://www.tbsnews.net/bangladesh/health/measles-death-toll-reaches-922-4-more-children-die-24-hours-1519286 (''The Business Standard'')]
*[[Merck & Co.|Merck]] and [[Moderna]] report that their [[cancer vaccine|cancer]] [[vaccine]] candidate showed positive results in their late-stage trial in preventing a [[Cancer recurrence|recurrence]] of [[melanoma]], including in high-risk patients. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260819-merck-and-moderna-s-tailored-cancer-drug-curbs-melanoma-recurrence-in-trial (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/19/moderna-merck-cancer-vaccine-shows-initial-late-stage-melanoma-data.html (CNBC)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Former [[Vice President of Liberia|Liberian vice president]] [[Jewel Taylor]] is charged for [[drug trafficking]], [[money laundering]] ‌and other offenses as part of an investigation of a [[Transnational organized crime|transnational narcotics network]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/liberias-former-vice-president-charged-transnational-narcotics-investigation-2026-08-19/ (Reuters)]

'''Science and technology'''
*A [[U.S.]]-led research team grows human brain [[organoid]]s for seven years, the longest reported period, and finds that their cells continue [[Timeline of human brain development|maturing]] in patterns similar to normal [[brain development]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260819-oldest-human-brain-cells-grown-in-lab-recorded-passage-of-time (AFP via France 24)]

'''Sports'''
* [[2026 Sydney Swans player investigation]]
** In [[Australian football]], the [[Sydney Swans]] suspend five of their players for the remainder of [[2026 AFL season|the season]] who are under police investigation over allegations of [[sexual assault]] against multiple women. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-19/afl-sydney-swans-ban-five-players-amid-police-investigation/107053398 (ABC News Australia)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=18|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***The [[United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations]] reports that a cargo vessel has come under attack off the [[Oman]]i coast in the [[Strait of Hormuz]], leaving one dead. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/18/vessel-hit-by-unknown-projectile-in-strait-of-hormuz-ukmto-says (Al Jazeera)]
**[[United Arab Emirates in the 2026 Iran war]]
***The [[United Arab Emirates]]'s [[Ministry of defence|defence ministry]] detects two missiles fired from [[Iran]] towards the country, including one that fell outside territorial waters and another that fell within it. [https://gulfnews.com/uae/uae-detects-two-missiles-from-iran-one-falls-in-territorial-waters-1.500645007 (''Gulf News'')] [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/world/mena/us-israel-iran-lebanon-war-peace-deal-day-62-live-updates (''Khaleej Times'')] [https://www.emirates247.com/uae/uae-air-defence-detected-two-ballistic-missiles-launched-from-iran/4670 (Emirates 24/7)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Russia–United Kingdom relations]]
***[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|British prime minister]] [[Andy Burnham]] confirms that the [[United Kingdom]] will continue to [[Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war|militarily support]] [[Ukraine]] after [[Russia]] warned the UK will face "consequences" for allowing Ukraine to use British-made drones to strike targets deep inside Russian territory. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cy5dz0kkn0wo (BBC News)]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[ballistic missile]] strike kills ten [[civilian]]s and injures eight others in [[Pechenihy]], [[Kharkiv Oblast]]. Several homes are completely destroyed. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-war-drone-attack-moscow-5f1f84bfb064942d7b7fe9be1bd4693c (AP)]
**[[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant crisis]]
***A [[drone warfare|drone strike]] hits a [[bus stop]] near the [[Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant]] in [[Enerhodar]], killing one plant worker and injuring several others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/iaea-drone-exploded-zaporizhzhia-nuclear-plant-bus-stop-killing-one-2026-08-18/ (''Reuters'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign|Blue Nile campaign]]
***The Sudan Doctors Network reports that recent attacks in [[Geissan District|Geissan]] of [[Sudan]]'s [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] region has displaced over 5,000 people to [[Ad-Damazin|Damazin]]. [https://sudanhorizon.com/5000-people-displaced-to-damazin-following-attack-on-geissan/ (''Sudan Horizon'')]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***The [[Rapid Support Forces]] launches a major crackdown in [[Nyala, Sudan|Nyala]], [[South Darfur]], its largest security and military mobilization since [[Battle of Nyala|seizing the city]] in 2023. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317590 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 24 bandits are killed by a force of [[Nigerian Army]], [[State Security Service (Nigeria)|State Security Service]], and [[Vigilantism|vigilante]] groups during a foiled kidnapping attempt in [[Bakori]], [[Katsina State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://dailypost.ng/2026/08/19/twenty-four-bandits-neutralized-as-army-dss-foil-mass-abduction-in-katsina/ (''Daily Post'')]
**Fourteen kidnapping victims are rescued by the Nigerian Army in [[Sabuwa]], Katsina State. [https://punchng.com/soldiers-rescue-14-kidnapped-victims-in-katsina/ (''The Punch'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**Five gunmen are killed by members of the [[Mexican Army]] after an encounter in Los Palillos locality, [[Los Reyes, Michoacán|Los Reyes]], [[Michoacán]]. [https://latinus.us/mexico/2026/8/18/ejercito-abate-cinco-hombres-armados-en-michoacan-suman-once-muertos-en-cinco-dias-181954.html (Latinus <small>in Spanish</small>)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[Iran–United Arab Emirates relations]]
***The [[United Arab Emirates]] suspends commercial exchanges, and financial transactions with [[Iran]] after Iran launched two ballistic missiles at the country. [https://time.com/article/2026/08/19/uae-suspends-trade-with-iran-after-reported-missile-strikes/ (''Time'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Zamboye mine collapse]]
** At least 100 people are killed when a [[Gold mining|gold mine]] collapses in [[Zamboye]], [[Baboua, Central African Republic|Baboua]], [[Central African Republic]], [[Cameroon–Central African Republic border|at the border]] with [[Cameroon]]. [https://www.rte.ie/news/world/2026/0819/1588552-gold-mine-collapse/ (RTÉ)]
*At least eight people are killed and more than 20 others are injured after a vehicle rams into a truck in [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260818/3e120bbde84f461a813f37a3c9593422/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Five people are killed and 17 others sustain injuries after a parapet wall collapses due to excessive rainfall during a [[Education in China|college]] [[Entrance examination|entrance]] celebration in [[Changning County, Sichuan|Changning County]], [[Sichuan]], [[China]]. [https://www.news.cn/local/20260819/266a8f9cbc2d49e9a06203f3fbca7095/c.html (Xinhua <small>in Chinese</small>)]
*Four people are killed and 16 others are injured when a passenger bus crashes due to a [[brake failure]] in [[Kirehe District]], [[Eastern Province, Rwanda|Eastern Province]], [[Rwanda]]. [https://en.igihe.com/news-40/article/kirehe-four-killed-16-injured-in-passenger-vehicle-crash (IGIHE)]
*Three people are killed after an explosion at a [[Thermal power station|thermal power plant]] in [[Baniyas]], [[Syria]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260818/f53de581912240d2a89ef4611c7eeae8/c.html (Xinhua)]
*A second {{M|w|4.7}} earthquake strikes the [[province of Granada]], in [[Spain]]. Damage and injures are reported in [[Granada]] and the surrounding area, while the [[Alhambra]] is evacuated. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cdx755dyy1yo (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*The [[UK Health Security Agency]] confirms that an outbreak of [[salmonella]] in the [[UK]] has left one person dead and hundreds more ill. The outbreak is believed to be linked to imported eggs. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cqx7vp77g0jo (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[United States and the International Criminal Court]]
**The [[United States]] imposes [[United States government sanctions|sanctions]] on [[International Criminal Court]] (ICC) president [[Tomoko Akane]] and senior trial lawyer Abdoulaye Seye over their alleged involvement in proceedings against officials from countries that do not recognize ICC jurisdiction. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260818-us-sanctions-international-criminal-court-chief-tomoko-akane-of-japan (AFP via France 24)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Ateneo de Zamboanga University shooting]]
**A student is killed while nine other people are injured in a [[Mass shooting|mass]] [[School shooting|shooting]] at a junior secondary school building of the [[Ateneo de Zamboanga University]] in [[Zamboanga City]], [[Philippines]]. The perpetrator, also a student, later kills himself.  [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/mayor-says-shooting-incident-school-southern-philippines-reports-two-casualties-2026-08-18/ (Reuters)] [https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2026/08/18/2550109/2-reported-dead-9-injured-ateneo-de-zamboanga-shooting/ (''The Philippine Star'')]
*[[Imprisonment of Imran Khan]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s [[Supreme Court of Pakistan|Supreme Court]] orders imprisoned former [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|prime minister]] [[Imran Khan]] transferred from [[Central Jail Rawalpindi|the central jail]] in [[Rawalpindi]], [[Punjab, Pakistan|Punjab]], to [[Shifa International Hospitals|Shifa International Hospital]] in [[Islamabad]] for medical examinations following a petition by his lawyers concerning his health. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260818-pakistan-supreme-court-orders-ex-pm-khan-moved-from-jail-to-hospital (AFP via RFI)]
*[[Singapore]] begins requiring major [[Internet messaging platform]]s to restrict unsolicited [[Social networking service|contacts]] and [[social media]] services to verify [[Online advertising|advertisers]] and block suspected [[Internet fraud|scam advertisements]] under new anti-scam rules, with penalties of up to [[Singapore dollar|S$]]1 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]780,000) for non-compliance. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/08/18/world/singapore-tightens-anti-scam-rules-on-social-media-messaging-platforms/2407426 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Zambian general election]]
**[[Zambia]]n [[President of Zambia|president]] [[Hakainde Hichilema]] is declared the winner by the electoral commission, re-electing him to a second term. [https://apnews.com/article/zambia-election-hichilema-victory-562c0ee56653c8dc835af7556c913aab (AP)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=17|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Iranian strikes on the Kurdistan Region]]
***[[Kurdistan Region]] [[Prime Minister of the Kurdistan Region|prime minister]] [[Masrour Barzani]] reports that [[Iran]] has launched a drone attack on the [[Government of the Kurdistan Region|Kurdistan Regional Government]]’s (KRG) prime minister’s office. No casualties are reported. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/17/iraqi-kurdish-pm-barzanis-office-targeted-in-drone-attack (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[S8000 Banderol|Banderol]] [[cruise missile]] explodes in [[Ștefan Vodă District]], [[Moldova]], after entering from Ukrainian [[airspace]], triggering a [[wildfire]] in a corn field. Moldovan authorities condemn the strike as "a serious violation of Moldova’s sovereignty". [https://english.nv.ua/russian-war/russian-missile-explodes-in-moldova-50633452.html (''The New Voice of Ukraine'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] says that it has shot down a long-range drone used by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] in [[Sudan]]'s [[North Kordofan]] [[States of Sudan|state]], the second drone shot down this month in the region. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317518 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[President of South Sudan|South Sudanese president]] [[Salva Kiir]] meets with [[Darfur]] [[Darfur Regional Government|governor]] [[Minni Minnawi]] in [[Juba]], [[South Sudan]], to discuss efforts to end the conflict in [[Sudan]]. [https://www.eyeradio.org/kiir-meets-darfur-governor-to-discuss-renewed-efforts-for-peace-in-sudan/?amp (Eye Radio)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**[[Constitutional crisis in Somalia]], [[Controversies of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]]
***Several fighters from both sides are killed after [[Somalia|Somali]] [[Somali Armed Forces|federal forces]] and opposition groups clash in the [[South West State of Somalia|South West State]]. Two civilians are also killed. Militias loyal to former [[List of leaders of South West State of Somalia|state president]] [[Abdiaziz Laftagareen]] enter the regional capital [[Baidoa]], challenging two battalions of the [[Somali National Army]] loyal to [[President of Somalia|Somali president]] [[Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/somalia-federal-troops-armed-opposition-clash-baidoa-city-2026-08-17/ (Reuters)] [https://garoweonline.com/en/news/somalia/somalia-baidoa-erupts-in-heavy-fighting-as-laftagareen-forces-claim-to-seize-city (Garowe Online)] [https://www.i24news.tv/en/news/international/africa/artc-somalia-federal-troops-armed-opposition-clash-in-baidoa-city-report (i24 news)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]]
**At least 22 people are killed in a [[mass shooting]] in [[Kebbe]], [[Sokoto State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://tribuneonlineng.com/22-killed-as-bandits-attack-ungushi-community-in-sokoto/ (''Tribune'')]
*[[Terrorism in Afghanistan]]
**An explosion is reported at a school in the [[Dashte Barchi]] neighborhood of [[Kabul]], [[Afghanistan]], injuring several people. The perpetrator is unknown. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/8/17/explosion-reported-at-school-in-afghan-capital-kabul (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Pacific hurricane season]]
**A 90-year-old woman is confirmed dead in [[Nāʻālehu, Hawaii|Nāʻālehu]], [[Hawaii]], [[United States]], and over 100,000 people remain without power after [[Hurricane Lala]] struck [[U.S. state|the state]]. [https://apnews.com/article/hawaii-lala-hurricane-tropical-storm-damage-446cc73e6f3f72636cd593aa61f100cc (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/aug/17/storm-lala-hawaii-damage (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2026 Pacific typhoon season]]
**Floods and landslides caused by the southwest [[monsoon]] and [[Tropical Storm Kujira (2026)|Tropical Storm Kujira]] kill at least 23 people and displace thousands across the [[Philippines]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/asia-pacific/23-dead-as-monsoon-cyclones-displace-thousands-in-philippines/4029160 (AA)]
*A [[crowd crush]] at the [[Ashokdham Temple]] in [[Bihar]], [[India]], kills at least seven people and injures 19 others. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/world/2026/8/17/india-temple-stampede-kills-seven-authorities-1427 (AFP via ABS-CBN News)]
*Seven people are killed and several others are injured after a fire breaks out in a hotel in [[Birbhum District]], [[West Bengal]], India. [https://english.news.cn/20260817/67efeec788de4e05ac45b7ede2fe2b79/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Humanitarian [[NGO]] [[Emergency (organization)|Emergency]] rescues 50 [[Libyan refugees|migrants]] from a wooden boat in international waters off [[Libya]] and recovers seven bodies. Two survivors require urgent medical evacuation, and 29 of those rescued are unaccompanied minors. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/charity-boat-rescues-50-migrants-off-libya-seven-found-dead-2026-08-17/ (Reuters)]
*Three people are killed when a private helicopter crashes on [[Sifnos]], [[South Aegean]], [[Greece]]. [https://apnews.com/article/greece-sifnos-helicopter-crash-6aa05a47d228812c0702db922ab1658a (AP)]
*Torrential rainfall causes widespread flooding in [[Geoje-si]], [[South Gyeongsang Province|South Gyeongsang]], [[South Korea]], killing at least one. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cvgww971nn2o (BBC News)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/18/south-korea-rain-deadly-landslide-philippines-major-flooding (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[United Nations]] reports that at least 2,325 people have died from the current [[Ebola]] outbreak in the [[Democratic Republic of Congo]], making it the deadliest in the country's history. [https://www.dw.com/en/drc-ebola-outbreak-becomes-deadliest-in-countrys-history/a-78394992 (DW)]
*[[Seventh cholera pandemic]]
**A city official reports that at least 500 people have been hospitalized for severe [[diarrhea]], with nearly 150 testing positive for [[cholera]], in [[Yangon]], [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/yangon-myanmar-diarrhoea-hospital-cholera-6324451 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[California]]'s [[California Energy Commission|energy commission]] approves the [[United States]]'s first energy-efficiency standards for replacement tires, aiming to reduce rolling resistance and lower driver fuel costs by 2029. However, manufacturers warn the strict limits could eliminate up to 70% of current replacement tire options by 2033. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/18/us/california-tires-energy-efficient-standards.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.foxbusiness.com/politics/california-regulators-pass-rules-limiting-what-replacement-tires-drivers-purchase (Fox Business)]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–Iran relations]]
**[[Iran]] says it barred two [[French embassy]] employees from returning for allegedly violating the [[Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations|Vienna Convention]] through activities supporting Iranian [[civil society]]. [[France]] says their work involved programs for civil society, students, and artists. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-says-two-french-embassy-employees-barred-returning-2026-08-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**[[United States president]] [[Donald Trump]] orders the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] to substantially reduce the [[Ulchi-Freedom Guardian]] [[military exercise]]s with [[South Korea]], citing their cost and his relationship with [[North Korea]]n [[Supreme Leader (North Korean title)|supreme leader]] [[Kim Jong Un]]. The drills begin as scheduled. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/trump-instructs-pentagon-to-reduce-military-exercises-with-south-korea (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[War on drugs]]
**[[Mexican drug war]]
***Members of the [[Mexican Navy]] seize 3.2 million doses of [[cocaine]] floating off the coasts of the state of [[Michoacán]]. This action represents a financial blow of [[Mex$]]340.2 million ([[US$]]20.11 million) to [[Organized crime in Mexico|organized crime]]. [https://lopezdoriga.com/nacional/marina-asegura-3-millones-dosis-cocaina-costas-michoacan/ (López Doriga <small>in Spanish</small>)]
**[[Indonesia]]'s [[National Narcotics Board]], [[Indonesian National Police|police]], and [[Directorate General of Customs and Excise|customs]] arrest 10 [[Myanmar]] nationals after seizing 2.6 metric tons of liquid [[methamphetamine]] from a [[Tanzania]]n-flagged vessel in waters off the [[Riau Islands]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/indonesia-arrests-10-myanmar-nationals-following-liquid-meth-bust-2026-08-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia]], [[Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Protests against the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**A [[Russia]]n [[Judiciary of Russia|court]] sentences [[Yabloko]] deputy chairperson [[Lev Shlosberg]] to 11 years and one month in [[Prisons in Russia|prison]] for discrediting [[Russian Armed Forces|the armed forces]] and spreading [[Disinformation in the Russian invasion of Ukraine|disinformation]] after he publicly condemned the [[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/russia-jails-opposition-politician-11-years-anti-war-comments-mediazona-says-2026-08-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Discord]] suspends [[live streaming]], [[screen sharing]], and [[video calls]] in [[Brazil]] to comply with an order from the [[national data protection authority]] following the death of a 13-year-old girl allegedly encouraged to [[Suicide in Brazil|kill herself]] during an online broadcast. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260818-discord-suspends-livestreams-in-brazil-after-teen-s-suicide (AFP via RFI)]
*The trial of Duane "Keffe D" Davis for his alleged role in [[murder of Tupac Shakur|the murder]] of rapper [[Tupac Shakur]] begins in [[Las Vegas]], [[Nevada]], [[United States]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgmkl1j3dwvo (BBC News)] [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/09/us/duane-davis-tupac-murder-trial (CNN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]]
**[[United States Customs and Border Protection]] (CBP) commissioner [[Rodney S. Scott]] pauses construction of a [[United States dollar|$]]1.7 billion [[Border control|border-security]] project in [[Big Bend National Park]], [[Texas]], while the CBP reviews the plan amid [[Bipartisanship in United States politics|bipartisan]] local opposition and [[Environmental issues in the United States|environmental concerns]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260818-us-pauses-construction-of-border-project-in-texas-national-park (AFP via RFI)]
*Former [[Prime Minister of South Korea|South Korean prime minister]] [[Kim Min-seok (politician)|Kim Min-seok]] is elected as the new leader of the [[Democratic Party (South Korea, 2015)|Democratic Party]] with 54.08% of the vote against its former leader [[Jung Chung-rae]]. [https://thediplomat.com/2026/08/kim-min-seok-wins-democratic-party-chair-in-ranked-choice-runoff/ (''The Diplomat'')] [https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10843221 (''The Korea Herald'')]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=16|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[Russia–NATO relations]]
***[[2026 drone incidents in Romania]] 
****A [[Spanish Air and Space Force|Spanish]] [[McDonnell Douglas F/A-18 Hornet|F/A-18 Hornet]] jet shoots down a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] drone in [[Romania]]n [[airspace]]. The drone was downed near [[Galați]] after entering from [[Moldova]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/nato-fighter-jet-shoot-drone-romania/ (''Politico'')]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] launch 822 drones at [[Russia]], including over 600 towards [[Moscow]], killing at least seven people and injuring 39 others. A [[Wildberries]] warehouse is also destroyed. [[Government of Russia|Russian officials]] say it is the largest Ukrainian drone attack launched this year. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1411pgje8xo (BBC News)]
*[[Insurgency in Balochistan]]
**Seven suspected members of the [[Pakistani Taliban]] are killed in a intelligence-based joint operation in [[Kharan District]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2624165/security-forces-kill-seven-terrorists-in-balochistans-kharan (''The Express Tribune'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2026 Mali offensives]]
***[[Tuareg people|Tuareg]] separatist [[Azawad Liberation Front]] releases six wounded [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian troops]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2654913/world (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**[[Rakhine offensive (2023–present)|Rakhine offensive]]
***Two civilians are killed and several homes are damaged by a government airstrike in [[Thandwe]], [[Rakhine State]], [[Myanmar]]. [https://www.narinjara.com/news/detail/6a812e19a41afa325cd71954 (Narinjara News)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**The [[African Union]] (AU) holds a meeting with [[Government of Sudan|Sudanese officials]] in an effort to end the war, marking the first talks by the AU in [[Sudan|the country]] since the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|military]] led by [[Abdel Fattah al-Burhan]] seized power in the [[2021 Sudanese coup d'état|October 2021 coup]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317489 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Federal Government of Somalia]] announces that [[Somali Airlines]] will resume flights beginning next month, ending a 35-year pause after the country [[Somali Civil War|entered a civil war]] in 1991. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-16/somalia-national-airline-to-resume-service-after-35-years (Bloomberg)] [https://www.dawan.africa/news/somali-airlines-expected-to-resume-flights-in-mid-september (Dawan Africa)] [https://airlinegeeks.com/2026/08/17/somali-airlines-to-fly-again-after-35-year-pause/ (Airline Geeks)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*The death toll of the [[Lake Kariba]] vessel capsizing in [[Zimbabwe]] from last week rises to 72 after twelve more bodies are recovered. [https://apnews.com/article/zimbabwe-ferry-capsize-death-toll-rises-children-cfd6c6df88f0d72b3ab227d8f41214f4 (AP)]
*A passenger bus carrying tourists from [[Poland]] crashes in to a [[ditch]] in [[Mezőkeresztes]], [[Hungary]], killing 12 people and injuring ten more. [https://apnews.com/article/hungary-tourist-bus-crash-poland-5d7ea3649f0af2dab9b45a08671f79b7 (AP)]
*Ten people are killed after a tourist bus overturns near [[Petrópolis]], [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260817/17a964b8bdb64ab8a6cfb6b2a0142445/c.html (Xinhua)] [https://g1.globo.com/rj/rio-de-janeiro/noticia/2026/08/16/onibus-tomba-em-petropolis.ghtml (''O Globo'' {{Small|in Portuguese}})]
*Five teenagers are killed and four others, including a child, are injured in a [[head-on collision]] caused by a [[wrong-way driving]] vehicle on the [[M9 motorway (Ireland)|M9 motorway]] in [[County Kildare]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ce8lx172kero (BBC News)]
*[[St. Nicholas' Church, Bączal Dolny|St. Nicolas' Church]] is completely destroyed by a fire at the [[Museum of Folk Architecture, Sanok|Museum of Folk Architecture]] in [[Sanok]], [[Podkarpackie Voivodeship]], [[Poland]]. [https://tvpworld.com/94878049/poland-skansen-fire-in-sanok-guts-church-from-1667 (TVP World)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Three people, including a teenager, are killed and two others are injured in a shooting in [[Isla Cristina]], [[Andalusia]], [[Spain]]. [[Law enforcement in Spain|Police]] investigate the attack as a possible dispute between rival [[Illegal drug trade in Spain|drug-trafficking]] groups and search for the gunman. [https://www.reuters.com/world/suspected-gang-leaders-mother-in-law-sister-killed-drug-related-shooting-spain-2026-08-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 IFAF Women's Flag Football World Championship]], [[Canada at the 2028 Summer Olympics]]
**In [[flag football]], [[Canada]]'s [[Canada women's national flag football team|women's team]] defeats the [[2024 IFAF Women's Flag Football World Championship|defending champion]] [[United States women's national flag football team|United States]] to win its third [[IFAF Flag Football World Championship]] title. Additionally, the [[Canada men's national flag football team|men's football team]] qualifies for the [[2028 Summer Olympics|upcoming]] [[Summer Olympics]]. [https://globalnews.ca/news/12023402/canada-flag-football-olympics/ (Global News)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=15|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***[[2026 Iran–Oman negotiations]]
****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign ministry]] [[Spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Iran|spokesperson]] [[Esmail Baghaei]] says that [[Iran]] and [[Oman]] have reached an agreement on a safe route for vessels transiting through the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.iranintl.com/en/202608156799 (''Iran International'')] [https://saudigazette.com.sa/article/663756/world/iran-says-deal-reached-with-oman-on-strait-of-hormuz-shipping-route-map (''Saudi Gazette'')]
***The [[Emirates News Agency]] reports that a third [[Abu Dhabi National Oil Company]] vessel was [[List of ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war|attacked]] by [[Iran]] while transiting through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] a day earlier. No injuries were reported. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/uaes-adnoc-says-one-its-vessels-came-under-attack-while-transiting-hormuz-2026-08-14/ (Reuters)] [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/08/uae-says-iran-attacked-adnoc-vessel-hormuz-urges-waterways-reopening (Al-Monitor)]
*[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[Israel]]i airstrikes in [[southern Lebanon|southern]] [[Lebanon]] kill eleven people, including three children. [https://news.sky.com/story/israeli-airstrikes-in-lebanon-kill-nine-people-including-three-children-health-ministry-says-13573242 (Sky News)]
**The [[Israel Defense Forces]] says that they have killed Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a [[Hezbollah]] commander in the [[Radwan Force]], during a airstrike in [[Ansar, Lebanon|Ansar]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-battalion-commander-in-hezbollahs-radwan-force-killed-in-early-morning-strike-near-tyre/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*A {{convert|180|ft|m|adj=on}} the [[Our Lady of Mercy monument, Konotopie|Our Lady of Mercy monument]] dedicated to the [[Mary, mother of Jesus|Virgin Mary]] and the [[List of tallest statues|tallest]] of its kind in [[Europe]], is inaugurated in [[Konotopie]], [[Poland]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/europe/giant-180-ft-statue-virgin-mary-inaugurated-small-polish-village-rcna592669 (NBC News)] [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/pope/news/2026-08/europe-s-tallest-statue-of-mary-blessed-in-poland.html (''Vatican News'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Indiana floods]]
**Authorities in [[Indiana]], [[United States]], report that six people have died in recent floods from storms. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/six-dead-indiana-after-storms-floods-emergency-officials-say-2026-08-15/ (Reuters)]
*The death toll of the [[Lake Kariba]] vessel capsizing in [[Zimbabwe]] from last week rises to 72 after 26 more bodies are recovered. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/15/africa/zimbabwe-ferry-disaster-dead-children-latam-intl (AP via CNN)]
*Six people are killed and several others wounded after a container truck crashes into an [[auto rickshaw]] in [[Latehar district]], [[Jharkhand]], [[India]]. [https://www.etvbharat.com/en/state/several-killed-in-road-accident-in-latehar-truck-auto-collision-enn26081506300 (ETV Bharat)]
*A minibus carrying a wedding party overturns in [[Diyarbakir Province]], [[Türkiye]], killing five and injuring eleven others. [https://english.aawsat.com/world/5307174-five-dead-turkish-wedding-party-road-crash (Asharq al-Awsat)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Ceuta migrant crisis]]
**Police in [[Morocco]] arrest 111 migrants who attempted to enter [[Spain]]'s [[Autonomous communities of Spain|autonomous community]] [[Ceuta]], amidst tightened security on both sides of [[Morocco–Spain border|the border]] with Spain. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/morocco-arrest-migrants-spain-ceuta-9.7308697 (CBC)]
*Four artwork by [[Renaissance art|Renaissance]] artist [[Antonello da Messina]] are reportedly stolen from the [[Regional Museum of Messina]] in [[Messina]], [[Sicily]], [[Italy]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2026/aug/16/antonello-da-messina-renaissance-paintings-stolen-sicilian-museum-holiday (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/four-antonello-da-messina-works-stolen-renaissance-painters-hometown-2026-08-16/ (Reuters)]
*Three people are shot dead and two others are wounded in a mass shooting in a flat in Newclare, [[Johannesburg]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.ewn.co.za/2026/08/17/gauteng-police-probing-fatal-weekend-mass-shooting (EWN)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Succession to the Liechtensteiner throne]]
**[[Crown prince|Hereditary Prince]] [[Alois, Hereditary Prince of Liechtenstein|Alois]] announces that [[Liechtenstein]] will gradually transition its [[line of succession]] to [[absolute primogeniture]], stating that any future descendant of him and [[Sophie, Hereditary Princess of Liechtenstein|Hereditary Princess Sophie]], regardless of sex, will inherit the [[House of Liechtenstein|throne]], allowing future women to inherit the throne. [https://apnews.com/article/liechtenstein-prince-royal-female-succession-3d890116a71754ee50aa960e94543da6 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 European Aquatics Championships]]
**In [[swimming]], [[Johannes Liebmann]] sets a men's [[1500 metres freestyle|1,500-metre freestyle]] world record of 14:26.79 at the [[LEN European Aquatics Championships|European Championships]], improving [[Bobby Finke]]'s [[Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's 1500-metre freestyle|2024 Olympic]] record by nearly four seconds. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260815-marchand-wins-first-euros-gold-as-liebmann-breaks-1500m-free-world-record (AFP via RFI)]
*[[2026 Pan Pacific Swimming Championships]]
**In swimming, [[Kate Douglass]] sets a women's [[50 metres freestyle|50-metre freestyle]] world record of 23.49 seconds in the [[Pan Pacific Swimming Championships|Pan Pacific Championships]] heats, surpassing [[Gretchen Walsh]]'s 23.55-second mark set in June. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260815-american-kate-douglass-reclaims-50m-freestyle-world-record (AFP via RFI)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 14
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=14|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] announce that [[Al-Qassam Brigades]] commander Muhammad Bassam Mushtaha, who was accused of taking [[List of Gaza war hostages|hostages]] during and after the [[Hamas]]–led attacks against [[Israel]] on [[October 7 attacks|October 7]], was killed in a recent airstrike last month in northern [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/idf-confirms-killing-hamas-commander-who-held-multiple-israelis-hostage-in-gaza/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***Heavy fighting erupts in [[El Obeid]], [[North Kordofan]], [[Sudan]], between the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] and [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF). Clashes also break out in Umm Arda. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317390 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
***Around 14 people are reported to be killed following an attack by RSF militants on the North Kordofan town of Umm Arda. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2654719/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')] [https://english.news.cn/africa/20260815/34cada1407eb4ebeb3feb02918b35e0c/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[National Army of Colombia|Colombian soldier]] is killed and four more wounded following a [[drone strike]] in the rural area of [[El Carmen, Norte de Santander]]. [https://www.elcolombiano.com/colombia/ataque-drones-explosivos-militar-muerto-cuatro-heridos-norte-de-santander-GG39959924#google_vignette (''El Colombiano'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**A constable [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police|policeman]] is killed and another is injured after a group of suspected insurgents attacked a police post in [[Bajaur district]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/2022779/cop-martyred-another-injured-in-terrorist-attack-on-police-post-in-bajaur (''Dawn'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
** Three gunmen are killed and a child is wounded in an attempted ambush on a highway in [[La Piedad]], [[Michoacán]], [[Mexico]]. Authorities seize four long guns, magazines, ammunition, and improvised explosives. [https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2026/8/14/hombres-armados-disparan-contra-soldados-en-la-piedad-hay-tres-muertos-un-adolescente-lesionado-869374.html (''El Heraldo de México'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[War in the Sahel]]
**American missionary Kevin Rideout is released from captivity after being kidnapped by an unidentified organisation front in [[Niger]] nine months prior. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/14/world/africa/american-missionary-niger-rideout-released.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Croatia wildfires]]
**One person dies and at least 40 others are injured after a severe wildfire breaks out on [[Croatia]]'s coastline. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c9342wn2x27o (BBC News)]
*[[2026 Flores earthquake]]
**At least 47 people are killed and several more are injured when a {{M|w|7.7}} earthquake strikes the coast of the island of [[Flores]] in [[East Nusa Tenggara]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-earthquake-magnitude-77-c31ad3cf07fa83d2d443e8d85e5c9d84 (AP)]
*A {{M|w|4.8}} earthquake strikes the [[province of Granada]] in [[Spain]], with damage reported in [[Granada]] and the surrounding area, and being felt in [[Madrid]]. [https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1412340-spain-rocked-by-48-magnitude-earthquake-with-epicentre-near-granada (''The News International'')]
*Sixteen people are killed and 40 others injured on the [[Yaounde]]-[[Bafoussam]] highway after a passenger bus crashed into a parked truck carrying planks in [[Mbam-et-Inoubou]], [[Cameroon]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260814/a2db5088bb1844e391b54cc3f48a8e9e/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Thailand|Thai]] rescuers find a French [[Tourism in Thailand|tourist]] and his two sons alive after they spend more than 16 hours at [[Gulf of Thailand|sea]] when their rented jet ski capsizes off [[Ko Samui]]. The family receives medical checks and is discharged. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/thailand-jet-ski-family-rescue/ (CBS News)]
*Heavy rainfall persists in [[Eastern China]] due to the remnants of [[Typhoon Dolphin]], resulting in flooding in [[Zhejiang]] province, [[China]], killing atleast one. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/mudslide-eastern-china-kills-one-more-heavy-rain-expected-2026-08-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Internet censorship in France]]
**The [[Constitutional Council (France)|Constitutional Council]] of [[France]] blocks a bill proposing a ban on [[social media]] access for minors under the age of 15. [[President of France|President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] orders [[Prime Minister of France|prime minister]] [[Sebastien Lecornu]] to re-work the draft legislation and resubmit it to the Council. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20260814-top-french-court-scraps-social-media-ban-for-children-under-15 (RFI)] [https://www.businessoffashion.com/news/media/frances-top-court-blocks-social-media-ban-for-under-15s/ (''Business of Fashion'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 political prisoner release in Venezuela]]
**[[Venezuela]] releases 131 detainees under alternative custody measures as part of a national reconciliation program following former [[President of Venezuela|president]] [[Nicolás Maduro]]'s [[2026 United States intervention in Venezuela|removal]]. [[Human rights in Venezuela|Human rights]] group [[Foro Penal]] confirms that at least 45 of those freed are [[Political prisoners in Venezuela|political prisoners]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260814-venezuela-frees-more-political-prisoners-amid-post-maduro-talks (AFP via RFI)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 NFL season]]
**In [[American football]], the [[National Football League]] suspends [[Atlanta Falcons]] [[linebacker]] [[James Pearce Jr.]] for eight games for violating the league's personal conduct policy after his arrest in February on [[domestic violence]] charges. [https://apnews.com/article/nfl-atlanta-falcons-b5eb71e5108fd4e5002b686a63427f84 (AP)] [https://www.fox5atlanta.com/sports/nfl-atlanta-falcons-defender-james-pearce-jr-suspended-8-games (WAGA-TV)]
*[[2026 Volta a Portugal]]
**In [[road bicycle racing]], the eighth stage at the [[Volta a Portugal]] race is neutralised after British cyclist [[Finlay Tarling]] is killed in an accident during the race. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7513762/2026/08/14/finlay-tarling-dies-volta-a-portugal/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 13
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=13|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] says that two vessels linked to the [[Abu Dhabi National Oil Company]] were attacked in the [[Strait of Hormuz]], accusing [[Iran]] of being behind the attacks. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/14/uae-accuses-iran-of-attacks-on-two-adnoc-vessels-in-strait-of-hormuz (Al Jazeera)] [https://thenewregion.com/posts/6207 (The New Region)]
***[[2026 United States military buildup in the Middle East]]
****''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reports that the {{Sclass|Nimitz|aircraft carrier|0}} {{USS|George Washington|CVN-73|6}} will deploy to the [[Middle East]] to replace the {{USS|Abraham Lincoln|CVN-72|6}} following a nine-month deployment and amidst reports of conditions on the aircraft carrier. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/aircraft-carrier-uss-george-washington-uss-lincoln-iran-middle-east/ (CBS News)] [http://thehill.com/policy/defense/6028854-george-washington-replaces-abraham-lincoln/ (''The Hill'')] [https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/u-s-sending-fresh-aircraft-carrier-to-middle-east-amid-iran-war-strain-d0d6e98d?msockid=0602fb23e44264c40559ec96e5eb658d (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) and [[Shin Bet]] says that they have killed [[Hamas]] commander and Gaza District Police chief Jamal Mahmoud Abu Kamil in a airstrike in [[Gaza City]]. Additionally, the IDF also kills a Hamas company commander in a separate strike in [[Khan Yunis]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-905483 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/431670 (''Israel National News'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Crimea attacks (2022–present)|Crimea attacks]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian military]] [[Officer (armed forces)|officer]] Robert Shagaev, who commanded the submarine [[Ukrainian submarine Zaporizhzhia|''Zaporizhzhia'']] before defecting to [[Russia]] after [[2014 Russian annexation of Crimea|its annexation]] of [[Crimea]], is reported to have been killed by an explosive planted in a trash can in [[Sevastopol]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/13/europe/crimea-bomb-kills-ukrainian-submarine-commander-intl (CNN)] [https://www.ynetnews.com/article/syhtjpouzl (Ynet)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign|Blue Nile campaign]]
***The [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF) says that they have retaken control of the [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] town of [[Kurmuk]], a month after being recaptured by the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] (SAF). [https://www.sudanspost.com/rsf-says-it-regained-kurmuk-in-renewed-southern-blue-nile-fighting/ (''Sudans Post'')]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The SAF and [[Darfur Joint Protection Force|Joint Forces]] repels a major assault by RSF on the [[Jebrat al Sheikh District|Jebrat al Sheikh]] district in [[North Kordofan]], [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317338 (''Sudan Tribune'')] [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/sudanese-army-says-it-repelled-rsf-attack-in-north-kordofan-state/4026673 (AA)]
**Renewed drone attacks by the RSF are reported in [[Khartoum]], [[Sudan]], for a second consecutive day, with the SAF intercepting several drones targeting the area. [https://www.lapresse.ca/international/afrique/2026-08-13/soudan/les-paramilitaires-attaquent-khartoum-pour-une-deuxieme-journee-consecutive.php?utm_source=dlvr.it&utm_medium=twitter&utm_campaign=international (''La Presse'')] [https://sudantribune.com/article/317334 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Pacific hurricane season]]
**In the [[United States]], [[Hawaii]] [[Governor of Hawaii|governor]] [[Josh Green (politician)|Josh Green]] declares a [[state of emergency]] ahead of [[Tropical Storm]] Lala's expected [[landfall]] on the state over the weekend. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/hawaii-declares-state-emergency-ahead-tropical-storm-lala-6318906 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[2026 United Kingdom wildfires]]
**Multiple wildfires break out across [[England]] on the hottest day of the year in the [[United Kingdom]] so far, with widespread damage in [[Stourbridge]], [[West Midlands (region)|West Midlands]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c04k20w7lr6o (BBC News)]
*[[Lewes derailment]]
**At least 20 people are injured when a [[Southern (Greater Thameslink Railway)|GTR Southern]] [[Commuter rail|commuter train]] derails near [[Lewes]], [[East Sussex]], United Kingdom. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cly5252xqdvt (BBC News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/13/world/uk-train-derailment-intl (CNN)]
*At least eleven people are killed and 13 others are injured after two trucks, two minibuses, two cars and a tricycle collided on the [[Accra–Kumasi Expressway]], [[Ghana]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260813/1a7577468f1142e08da2cee34f9b990f/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Seven people are killed after an under-construction tunnel collapsed in [[Chamoli District]], [[India]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260814/d703472d3388461d9a320c6633c1177e/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Unprecedented torrential rainfall due to severe thunderstorms causes widespread flooding in [[Chiba Prefecture]], [[Japan]], leaving at least eight people dead. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cq561gpen8lo (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/thousands-stranded-japans-narita-airport-after-record-rain-kills-four-2026-08-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[Romania]] begins shutting down the second [[Nuclear reactor|reactor]] at the [[Cernavodă Nuclear Power Plant]], the country's only [[Nuclear power in Romania|nuclear power]] plant, after a drought lowered the [[Danube]] river below the level required for [[Nuclear reactor coolant|cooling]], leaving both reactors offline. [[Bolojan cabinet|The government]] says alternative sources and imports will cover [[Electricity sector in Romania|electricity demand]]. [https://apnews.com/article/romania-europe-drought-energy-weather-4239b119af1153fc0a57093b04df555b (AP)]
*[[Greece]]'s [[National Public Health Organization (Greece)|public health agency]] reports 110 [[West Nile virus]] infections and nine deaths in 2026, including 45 new cases in one week, as authorities increase [[mosquito control|mosquito control]] measures in the [[Athens metropolitan area]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/greece-reports-significant-rise-in-west-nile-virus-cases-with-9-dead (AFP via ''Daily Sabah'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Russian spies in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Poland|Polish]] [[Prime Minister of Poland|prime minister]] [[Donald Tusk]] says authorities, working with [[United States|U.S.]] services, foiled an alleged Russian plot to kill a [[Ukrainian-American]] citizen in [[Warsaw]] and arrest a suspect accused of acting for [[Russian intelligence]]. Tusk says it is the first such Russian-directed plot in another [[NATO]] country. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/russian-plot-kill-american-thwarted-poland/ (CBS News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2027 Kyrgyz presidential election]]
**[[Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyz]] [[President of Kyrgyzstan|president]] [[Sadyr Japarov]] announces that he will run for a second term in the upcoming presidential election in January 2027. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/kyrgyz-president-says-he-will-run-second-term-2026-08-13/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Zambian general election]]
**[[Zambia]]ns vote to elect a [[President of Zambia|president]] and 280 seats of the [[National Assembly of Zambia|National Assembly]]. Incumbent president [[Hakainde Hichilema]] is running for re-election to a second term in office. [https://apnews.com/article/zambia-election-hichilema-mundubile-c2e3a627284296099089e03d2454e3b7 (AP)]
**[[Zambia Police Service|Zambian police]] arrest several senior [[Opposition (politics)|opposition]] figures during the elections, accusing them of possessing [[Zambian Defence Force|military]] weapons and planning [[Rebellion|armed insurrection]]. Opposition leader [[Brian Mundubile]] says security forces raided his residence after voting ended. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/zambia-says-it-arrested-opposition-figures-night-elections-2026-08-17/ (Reuters)]

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=12|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]], [[Siege of El Obeid]]
***The [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF) launch eight [[Drone warfare|drone]] and land attacks across [[El Obeid]], [[North Kordofan]]. Two people are reported to be killed during the attacks. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/rsf-renews-assault-sudans-al-obeid-drones-strike-capital-witnesses-say-2026-08-12/ (Reuters)] 
**The RSF launch drone strikes across multiple cities in [[Sudan]], including its [[Capital city|capital]] [[Khartoum]], [[Khartoum North|Bahri]], and [[Omdurman]] in [[Khartoum State]], and the [[River Nile State|River Nile]] cites of [[Ad-Damir]] and [[Atbara]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2654334/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')] [https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/mena/2026/08/12/suspected-rsf-drones-attack-areas-in-sudan-including-khartoum-and-al-obeid/ (''The National News'')]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**Two [[National Army of Colombia|Colombian soldiers]] are killed and 17 more are wounded in an [[ambush]] by [[FARC dissidents]] in [[Algeciras, Huila]]. [https://www.elcolombiano.com/colombia/ataque-explosivos-huila-ejercito-muertos-OF39879869 (''El Colombiano'' <small>in Spanish</small>)] [https://www.sociedadmedia.com/algeciras-huila-ambush-farc-dissidents-2026/ (Sociedad Media)]
*[[Libyan crisis]]
**A drone strike is reported on a [[Substation|electrical substation]] in [[Zawiya, Libya|Zawiya]], western [[Libya]], causing a fire and power outages. [https://thehill.com/homenews/ap/ap-international/ap-drone-strike-in-western-libya-torches-a-power-substation-triggering-outages/mlite/ (''The Hill'')]
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**A failed attack against the [[Tayoltita Airfield]], in [[San Dimas Municipality]], [[Durango]], [[Mexico]], leaves one gunman killed and two [[Mexican Army|soldiers]] wounded. Authorities deploy an operation in the zone to secure the area and search for the remaining attackers. [https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/12/estados/un-muerto-y-dos-militares-lesionados-deja-enfrentamiento-armado-en-tayoltita-durango (''La Jornada'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[Red Sea crisis]]
**[[Minister for Foreign Affairs (Pakistan)|Pakistani foreign minister]] [[Ishaq Dar]] reports that three [[Pakistanis]] were killed in a attack on a commercial vessel in the [[Red Sea]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/pakistan-says-3-nationals-killed-in-houthi-red-sea-attack/a-78330015 (DW)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Central African Republic]] inaugurates a 50-[[megawatt]] [[Photovoltaic power station|photovoltaic]] [[solar power]] [[Solar power plant|plant]] built by [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]]-based company Global South Utilities that would boost the country's [[electricity]] by 60%. [https://www.cnbcafrica.com/2026/central-african-republic-inaugurates-uae-built-50-mw-solar-plant (CNBC Africa)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A woman is killed and 172 other people are rescued after a ferry catches fire off the coast of [[Bali]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260812-passengers-rescued-as-second-ferry-in-days-catches-fire-in-indonesia (AFP via RFI)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Four people are killed, including the perpetrator, in shooting and stabbing attacks at a [[daycare]] and a house in [[Hopkins, Minnesota|Hopkins]], [[Minnesota]], [[United States]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/police-presence-hopkins-neighborhood/ (CBS News)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Cook Islands general election]]
**[[Cook Islands|Cook Island]]ers vote to elect all 24 seats of [[Parliament of the Cook Islands|Parliament]] amid a [[cost-of-living crisis]] and debate regarding a past [[China–Cook Islands relations#2025 partnership agreement|partnership agreement]] with [[China]]. Incumbent [[Prime Minister of the Cook Islands|prime minister]] [[Mark Brown (Cook Islands politician)|Mark Brown]] faces a challenge from [[Cook Islands United Party|Cook Islands United]] leader [[Teariki Heather]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/pacific/970743/cost-of-living-water-tariffs-mining-on-cook-islanders-minds-ahead-of-election (RNZ)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/12/cook-islands-election-mark-brown-pm-prime-minister (''The Guardian'')]
*The [[Rapid Support Forces]]-appointed [[Government of Peace and Unity#Regions|governor]] of [[Sudan]]'s [[Kordofan]] region, Hamad Mohammad Hamad Khalifa, resigns and announces he will defect. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317318 (''Sudan Tribune'')] [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/08/12/rsfappointed-kordofan-governor-defects-urges-fighters-to-return-to-homeland- (Al-Arabiya)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Solar eclipse of August 12, 2026]]
**A total [[solar eclipse]] occurs in [[Greenland]], [[Iceland]], and [[Spain]], with partial eclipses visible over much of northern [[North America]], [[Europe]] (except most of [[Ukraine]], [[Greece]], [[Bulgaria]] and [[Russia]]), northwestern [[Africa]] and northern [[Asia]]n [[Russia]]. It is the first total eclipse observable in mainland Europe since [[solar eclipse of August 11, 1999|August 1999]]. [https://www.timeanddate.com/eclipse/solar/2026-august-12 (Time and Date)] [https://eclipsewise.com/solar/SEprime/2001-2100/SE2026Aug12Tprime.html (EclipseWise)]
*[[MoM-BH*-1]]
**Astronomers studying a [[Little red dot (astronomical object)|little red dot]] found by the [[James Webb Space Telescope]] announce in ''[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]'' the discovery of the first [[black hole star]]. The first object classed as such, [[MoM-BH*-1]], in the constellation of [[Cetus (constellation)|Cetus]], is the size of the [[Solar System]] and emits a light that outshines its host galaxy. [https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/aug/12/astronomy-discovery-new-cosmic-object-black-hole-star (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.popsci.com/science/black-hole-star-discovery/ (''PopSci'')]
