{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=11|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
****[[Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war]]
*****[[Minister of Defence (Pakistan)|Pakistani defence minister]] [[Khawaja Asif]] says that a deal between [[Iran]] and the [[United States]] is "close", including an arrangement over the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-11/trump-hardens-stance-iran-clouding-hopes-hormuz-deal?srnd=homepage-uk (Bloomberg News)] [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/11/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz-control-reparation-talks-.html (CNBC)]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 United States naval blockade of Iran]]
*****''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' reports that a [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] [[List of United States military helicopters|helicopter]] has fired at the rudder of the [[Panama]]-[[flag state|flagged]] [[container ship]] ''Vela ​Nova'' after crews ignored the naval blockade re-imposed in July, contradicting British maritime management that it was hit by a missile in the [[Gulf of Oman]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/us-fired-panama-flagged-ship-that-tried-break-blockade-iranian-ports-wsj-reports-2026-08-11/ (Reuters)]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***[[March–May 2025 United States attacks in Yemen|Operation Rough Rider]]
****The [[United States Department of Defense|U.S. Department of Defense]] reports to [[United States Congress|Congress]] that the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]] strikes against [[Houthis|Houthi]] rebels in [[Yemen]] in 2025 killed 153 civilians and injured another 243. [https://thehill.com/policy/defense/6023883-pentagon-report-yemen-civilian-casualties/amp/ (''The Hill'')]
***The [[Government of Yemen|Yemeni government]] reports that six people have been killed in strikes on a cargo ship by the [[Houthis]] in the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/11/world/middleeast/deadly-houthi-strike-red-sea.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israeli Army Radio]] reports that the [[Israel Defense Forces]] launched a strike targeting a [[Hamas]] sniper near the [[Yellow Line (Gaza)|Yellow Line]] in the [[Gaza Strip]], its first strike on the enclave in 10 days. [https://allisraelnews.com/brief/idf-announces-first-gaza-strike-in-10-days-kills-hamas-sniper-who-threatened-troops (AIN)] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-it-targeted-hamas-sniper-who-posed-immediate-threat-to-troops-in-gaza/ (''The Times of Israel'')] [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-905210 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Sudanese Civil War]]s
**[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
***[[2026 Blue Nile campaign|Blue Nile campaign]]
****A heavy attack on civilians by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF) and [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North]] (SPLM-N) is reported in [[Geissan District|Geissan]] in [[Sudan]]'s [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] [[States of Sudan|state]], including on the main market, surrounding farms, and other shops. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317261 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
****The [[International Organization for Migration]] reports that 2,300 people in the Blue Nile region has been  [[Forced displacement|displaced]] following recent clashes. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260812-iom-2500-people-displaced-by-clashes-in-sudans-blue-nile-state/ (Middle East Monitor)]
****Attacks by the RSF and SPLM-N are also reported in [[Qaysān]] on its provincial headquarters and a market. [https://sudantribune.net/article/317259 (''Sudan Tribune'' <small>in Arabic</small>)]
**[[Sudanese nomadic conflicts]]
***Around 60 people are killed and around 50 others injured in an armed attack during a [[Cattle raiding|cattle raid]] in [[Tonj North County]], [[Warrap State]], [[South Sudan]]. [https://arab.news/r5ma9 (AFP via ''Arab News'')] [https://www.radiotamazuj.org/en/news/article/communal-clashes-leave-60-dead-and-50-wounded-in-tonj-north (Radio Tamazuj)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Colombia earthquake]]
**The casualty toll from the {{M|w|7.4}} earthquake in [[Colombia]] yesterday increases to over 240 people killed, 570 injured, and at least 3,000 others still missing. [[President of Colombia|President]] [[Abelardo de la Espriella]] declares a national [[state of emergency]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/11/colombia-earthquake-dead-amid-hunt-for-survivors (''The Guardian'')]
*At least 44 people are killed when a ferry sinks on [[Lake Kariba]], [[Zimbabwe]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260812-44-lives-lost-after-ferry-capsizes-on-zimbabwe-s-lake-kariba (AFP via RFI)]
*Search operations for the landslide from Sunday conclude in [[Baguio]], [[Philippines]], placing the final death toll at ten people. Meanwhile, the [[Philippine National Police|national police]] places the nationwide toll from the [[tropical cyclone]]s and monsoons at 26. [https://www.abs-cbn.com/news/regions/2026/8/11/10-dead-3-rescued-in-baguio-landslide-as-search-ends-0659 (ABS-CBN News)] [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2282502/death-toll-from-habagat-storms-maymay-and-luis-now-at-26-pnp/ (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*At least 18 people are killed and around 30 others are injured in a two-vehicle collision in [[Ismailia Governorate]], [[Egypt]]. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/1/1235/574404/Egypt/Urban--Transport/Death-toll-rises-to--in-Ismailia-crash-.aspx (''Al Ahram'')]
*Four people are killed and five others are injured after an old residential building collapses in [[Cairo]], Egypt. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/four-killed-five-injured-in-cairo-residential-building-collapse-1.500637365 (''Gulf News'')]
*Three people are killed following a commercial building fire in [[Giza]], Egypt. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/1/1235/574466/Egypt/Urban--Transport/-bodies-recovered-after-fire-engulfs-commercial-bu.aspx (''Al Ahram'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Syria and weapons of mass destruction]]
**The [[Syrian transitional government]] confirms their cooperation with the [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] to purge [[nuclear material]]s at a hidden facility following a report by ''[[Axios (website)|Axios]]'' on such plan after an agreement between [[Israel]], Syria, and the [[United States]]. Conversely, Israel threatens to bombard the site again if the materials remain, and to prevent access to the site. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iaea-to-remove-nuclear-material-from-clandestine-syrian-site-report/4023605 (AA)] [https://www.axios.com/2026/08/10/syria-nuclear-israel-turkey-iaea (''Axios'')] [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-905121 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Presidency of Ahmed al-Sharaa]], [[War crimes in the Syrian civil war]],[[‪ Prosecution of Syrian civil war criminals]]
**The [[Judiciary of Syria|Criminal Court]] in [[Damascus]], [[Syria]], sentences [[Fall of the Assad regime|deposed]] [[President of Syria|president]] [[Bashar al-Assad]] and his brother [[Maher al-Assad|Maher]] to [[Capital punishment in Syria|death]] [[Trial in absentia|in absentia]], and former [[Daraa Governorate|Daraa]] political security director [[Atef Najib]] in person, and issue [[Interpol notice|international]] [[arrest warrant]]s for all for [[premeditated murder]] and [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://www.thestandard.com.hk/world/article/339643/Syria-sentences-Bashar-al-Assad-to-death-in-absentia-over-atrocities (AFP via ''The Standard'')] [https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/2026/08/11/damascus-court-sentences-bashar-al-assad-and-others-to-death/ (''The National'')]
*[[Capital punishment in Lebanon]]
**The [[Lebanon|Lebanese]] [[Parliament of Lebanon|parliament]] votes to abolish [[Capital punishment in Lebanon|the death penalty]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c8enj8p1xwgo (BBC News)]
*A [[United States Marine Corps]] soldier is released from [[Russia]] after having been detained there since 2022. [https://kyivindependent.com/russia-releases-ailing-ex-us-marine-after-4-years-in-detention/ (''Kyiv Independent'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Hungarian presidential election]]
**Former [[Curia of Hungary|Supreme Court]] president [[András Baka]] is elected as [[Hungary|Hungarian]] [[President of Hungary|president]] through a [[supermajority]] and is scheduled to take office on 19 August. He ran [[Uncontested election|uncontested]] as the [[Tisza Party]]'s candidate, as neither [[Fidesz]] nor its partner [[Christian Democratic People's Party (Hungary)|KNDP]] nominated a candidate. [https://www.reuters.com/world/hungary-parliament-elects-former-supreme-court-head-andras-baka-president-2026-08-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Thousand Martyrs' Cup]], [[Palestinian sports during the Gaza war]]
**[[Palestinian Football Association]] president [[Jibril Rajoub]] announces that all [[Association football|football]] and sport activities will resume in September following a three-year suspension that began after the outbreak of the [[Gaza war]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/8/10/palestinian-club-football-to-restart-in-september-after-gaza-war-suspension (Al Jazeera)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 10
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=10|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***[[2026 United States naval blockade of Iran]]
****The [[United States Central Command]] says that they have redirected 55 vessels linked to [[Iran]] since reinstating the blockade in July. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/us-says-it-has-rerouted-55-iran-linked-vessels (''Middle East Eye'')]
**[[Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran]]
***[[Supreme Leader of Iran|Iranian supreme leader]] [[Mojtaba Khamenei]] appoints new leaders for [[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Republic of Iran Armed Forces|military]] to replace their predecessors after they were [[List of Iranian officials killed during the 2026 Iran war|killed]] during the initial [[Israel]] and [[U.S.]] airstrikes, including [[Ali Abdollahi]] as [[General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran|chief of staff]], [[Kioumars Heydari]] as deputy commander, and [[Hossein Taeb]] as [[Basij]] commander. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/iran-news/article-905101 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/08/irans-khamenei-appoints-six-military-commanders-what-know (Al-Monitor)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***Аt least 13 people are killed, including a child, and 39 others were injured in a [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] on an oil refinery in [[Nizhnekamsk]], [[Tatarstan]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-kills-12-drone-strikes-russian-city-nizhnekamsk-state-media-reports-2026-08-10/ (Reuters)]
*[[Libyan crisis]]
**{{ill|Fawzi al-Mansouri|ar|فوزي المنصوري}}, head of [[military intelligence]] for the [[Libyan National Army]], is [[Assassination|assassinated]] as a bomb exploded [[Car bomb|inside his car]] in [[Benghazi]], [[Libya]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/middle-east/20260811-car-bomb-kills-haftar-intel-chief-in-eastern-libya (AFP via RFI)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/11/east-libya-military-intelligence-chief-killed-in-car-bomb (Al Jazeera)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Colombia earthquake]]
** A {{M|w|7.4}} earthquake strikes [[Chocó Department]], [[Colombia]], causing widespread and heavy damage, and leaving at least 288 people dead. [https://english.elpais.com/international/2026-08-10/at-least-25-people-dead-as-magnitude-74-earthquake-hits-colombia.html (''El Pais'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c20e360lx0vo (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/earthquake-pacific-coast-shakes-colombian-capital-2026-08-10/ (Reuters)]
**The [[Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary, Manizales|Cathedral Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary]] in [[Manizales]] is confirmed to be among the buildings damaged after one of the towers collapsed following the earthquake. [https://www.independent.co.uk/tv/news/colombia-earthquake-cathedral-collapse-video-b3030635.html (''The Independent'')] [https://thecitypaperbogota.com/news/powerful-7-4-earthquake-strikes-colombia-collapsing-buildings-across-western-cities/ (''The City Paper Bogota'')] [https://www.elcolombiano.com/amp/colombia/temblor-hoy-colombia-catedral-manizales-JL39761954 (''El Colombiano'' <small>in Spanish</small>)]
*[[Wildfires in 2026]]
**A recent [[wildfire]] at the [[Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park]] in [[East Java]], [[Indonesia]], is extinguished after {{cvt|550|ha|acres|abbr=on}} were burnt. However, new hotspots are also reported near [[Mount Bromo|the caldera]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/fire-near-indonesias-mount-bromo-extinguished-after-550-hectares-burnt-new-2026-08-10/ (Reuters)]
*The [[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Office of Civil Defense (Philippines)|civil defense office]] reports that at least 16 people were killed across [[Luzon]], including seven in [[Baguio]], by floods, landslides and [[Climate of the Philippines|weather]]-related accidents after nine days of heavy [[monsoon]] rain, while three others remain missing. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260810-days-of-heavy-rain-leave-at-least-13-dead-in-philippines (AFP via RFI)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The [[World Health Organization]] reports that the [[Ebola]] outbreak in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] started in February before its declaration, with some cases attributed to [[malaria]] and [[Typhoid fever|typhoid]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/10/drcs-ebola-outbreak-began-months-before-officially-declared-says-who (Al Jazeera)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Colombia–Israel relations]], [[Colombia–Syria relations]]
**[[Colombia]] becomes the second country to [[international recognition|recognize]] the [[Golan Heights]], a region in southwestern [[Syria]] that has been [[Israeli occupation of the Golan Heights|under Israeli occupation]] since [[Six-Day War|1967]], as part of Israel's sovereignty. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/colombia-recognises-israeli-claim-over-golan-heights-6310936 (AFP via CNA)] [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-905102 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Nonthaburi shootings]]
**[[Nonthaburi province#Administrative divisions|Nonthaburi Provincial Administrative Organization]] president Thongchai Yenprasert is killed in a shooting at a government building in [[Nonthaburi province]], [[Thailand]]. Former [[National Assembly (Thailand)|parliament]] member Chalong Riewrang is taken into custody over [[Corruption in Thailand|corruption]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cqvg08287pz4t (BBC News)] [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/thailand-ex-mp-shooting-kills-local-official-gun-6309301 (AFP via CNA)] [https://en.thairath.co.th/news/crime/2951779 (''Thairath'')]
*[[Murder of Mir Raza Ali]]
**The [[Sindh government|government]] of [[Sindh]], [[Pakistan]], announces that a [[Judicial Commission of Pakistan|judicial commission]] headed by a judge of the [[Sindh High Court]] would investigate businessman Mir Raza Ali's death. The decision followed a recommendation by the [[Sindh Assembly]]. [https://www.dawn.com/news/2021701 (''Dawn'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Russian legislative election]]
**Upon petition from [[Rodina (political party)|Rodina]], the liberal [[Yabloko]] party is barred from participating in the [[2026 Russian legislative election]] on charges of unregistered funding, a controversial [[copyright infringement]], and [[List of organizations designated as terrorist or extremist by Russia|extremism]] by the [[Supreme Court of Russia]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/11/ukraine-war-briefing-russia-bans-voting-against-conflict (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/08/10/russian-supreme-court-bars-yabloko-party-from-election-a93452 (''The Moscow Times'')]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 9
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=9|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Gaza peace plan]]
****[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] rejects a [[United States]]-led plan for peace accepted by [[Hamas]], saying [[Israel]] will not withdraw [[Israeli Defense Force|forces]] until Hamas fully [[Disarmament|disarms]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/middle-east/20260809-netanyahu-rejects-gaza-plan-in-new-break-from-trump (AFP via RFI)]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***At least eleven people are killed and at least 40 others are injured in a [[Houthi]] missile and [[Military drone|drone]] attack on [[Mokha]], [[Taiz Governorate]], [[Yemen]]. [https://www.newarab.com/news/least-11-killed-houthi-strikes-yemens-mokha (MENA via ''The New Arab'')]
***The Governor of [[Al-Hudaydah Governorate]], Yemen, survives an [[assassination attempt]] after the Houthis shelled his residence in [[Al Khawkhah district]]. [https://yemenonline.info/special-reports/13398 (''Yemen Online'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2026 Mali offensives]]
***Around ten [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian soldiers]] are reportedly killed in a [[Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin]] attack in central [[Mali]]. [https://arab.news/bju3p (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
***Authorities say that they have repelled an attack by militants on a military base in [[San, Mali|San]], Mali. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cly8j7ygwvlo (BBC)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[2026 Blue Nile campaign|Blue Nile campaign]]
***[[Mass grave|Mass graves]] of 25 civilians executed by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] are discovered in [[Kurmuk]] in [[Sudan]]'s [[Blue Nile State|Blue Nile]] region. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317193 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**[[Colombia]]n [[President of Colombia|president]] [[Abelardo de la Espriella]] reports that [[Military Forces of Colombia|military forces]] killed four [[FARC dissidents]] in [[Meta Department|Meta]] and two [[Gulf Clan]] members in [[Antioquia Department|Antioquia]]. [https://www.thedailystar.net/news/world/news/colombia-president-says-6-armed-rebels-killed-clashes-4244221 (AFP via ''The Daily Star'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Canadian wildfires]]
**[[Royal Canadian Mounted Police|Police]] report that a woman was killed while evacuating the Summerland [[wildfire]] in [[British Columbia]], [[Canada]], which has burned more than {{convert|13600|ha|acre}} and forced over 20,000 people to evacuate. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260810-one-woman-confirmed-dead-in-western-canada-wildfire (AFP via RFI)]
*[[2026 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Dolphin (2026)|Typhoon Dolphin]] makes landfall in eastern [[China]], evacuating 1 million people and cancelling 1,300 flights from [[Shanghai]]. Monsoon rains are also reported in parts of the [[Philippines]], causing flooding. [https://www.scmp.com/video/china/3363511/powerful-typhoon-dolphin-makes-landfall-eastern-china (''South China Morning Post'')] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/10/world/asia/typhoon-dolphin-china-evacuations.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://apnews.com/article/typhoon-dolphin-d40f4d49b0d89935366f360f1f13afd8 (AP)]
*At least 16 migrant workers are killed in a major fire at a sofa manufacturing factory in [[Riyadh]], [[Saudi Arabia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/fire-saudi-factory-kills-16-bangladeshi-migrant-workers-2026-08-10/ (Reuters)]
*Six people, all members of the same family, are killed after an [[drunk driving|intoxicated]] truck driver collides head-on with their vehicle in [[Dhar district]], [[Madhya Pradesh]], [[India]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/madhya-pradesh/several-killed-as-container-truck-collides-with-car-in-madhya-pradeshs-dhar/article71324605.ece (''The Hindu'')]
*Five people are killed, at least three others survive, and five are still missing in a landslide that hits a residential area in [[Baguio]], Philippines. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/2281379/baguio-landslide-death-toll-rises-to-5-after-toddler-recovered/ (''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 cyclosporiasis outbreak]], [[Salmonellosis in the United States]]
**[[Taylor Farms]] extends its [[product recall|recall]]s to products containing [[jalapeño]]s after they were linked to the ongoing [[salmonellosis]] outbreak in the [[United States]]. Taylor Farms currently has a recall for [[iceberg lettuce]] linked to [[cyclosporiasis]]. [https://arstechnica.com/health/2026/08/taylor-farms-recalls-jalapeno-products-for-salmonella-amid-cyclospora-outbreak/ (''Ars Technica'')] [https://www.huffpost.com/entry/salsa-guacamole-recall-jalapeno-salmonella_n_6a7918d7e4b01ec88690947e (''HuffPost'')]
*The [[Hong Kong Observatory]] records {{convert|36.9|C|F}} in [[Hong Kong|the city]], the [[Climate of Hong Kong|highest temperature]] since records began in 1884. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2026/08/09/so-hot-hong-kong-weather-observatory-posts-record-high-temperature/230729 (AFP via ''Malay Mail'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–Syria relations]]
**[[Russia]] and [[Syria]] reach a [[memorandum of understanding]] to reorganize Russia's presence on the [[Geography of Syria|Syrian coast]], including transferring civilian facilities to Syrian state management and converting [[Russian military]] bases into joint training centers. [https://sana.sy/en/syria/2335254/ (SANA)]

'''Law and crime'''
*At least eleven people are killed and two others are injured in three separate shootings in [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/11-killed-in-separate-shootings-in-south-africas-cape-town/4022686 (AA)]
*[[Afghanistan]]'s [[General Directorate of Intelligence|intelligence agency]] arrests two staff members of the [[United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan]] in [[Herat]], according to the office of [[Secretary-General of the United Nations|UN secretary-general]] [[António Guterres]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260811-un-says-2-staff-arrested-by-afghan-intelligence-agency (AFP via RFI)]
*Suspected crime boss [[Daniel Kinahan]] is arrested upon arrival at [[Baldonnel, County Dublin]], [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]], following his extradition from the [[United Arab Emirates]], and is brought to the [[Special Criminal Court]] in [[Dublin]]. Kinahan is charged with directing the operations of [[Kinahan Organised Crime Group|a criminal organisation]] from 2015 to 2017. [https://www.rte.ie/news/ireland/2026/0809/1587120-daniel-kinahan/ (RTÉ)]
*The boat operator involved in a capsizing that killed two people, including a 5-month-old toddler, and injured 12 others near the [[Statue of Liberty]], [[New York City]], [[United States]] on August 8 has been arrested on 13 counts of [[reckless endangerment]]. [https://abcnews.com/US/2-dead-12-injured-after-boat-capsizes-new/story?id=135496017 (ABC)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Impact of the 2026 Iran war on Iran]]
**[[Iranian state media]] reports that [[Supreme Leader of Iran|Iranian supreme leader]] [[Mojtaba Khamenei]] met [[President of Iran|president]] [[Masoud Pezeshkian]] in July, his first publicly reported meeting since [[2026 Iranian supreme leader election|taking over]], amidst ongoing speculation about his health and future. Additionally, a rare video is released of him. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260809-iran-releases-rare-video-of-mojtaba-khamenei-after-reports-of-deteriorating-health/ (Middle East Monitor)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/irans-pezeshkian-recently-met-supreme-leader-khamenei-state-media-says-2026-08-09/ (Reuters)] [https://shafaq.com/en/World/Mojtaba-Khamenei-holds-first-reported-meeting-with-Pezeshkian (Shafaq)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2027 FIFA Women's World Cup]]
**In [[association football]], [[Malawi]]'s [[Malawi women's national football team|women's national football team]] defeats [[Ghana women's national football team|Ghana]] 2–1 at the [[Women's Africa Cup of Nations]] in the [[2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] at [[Al Medina Stadium]] in [[Morocco]], [[2027 FIFA Women's World Cup qualification|qualifying]] for the upcoming [[FIFA Women's World Cup]] in [[Brazil]] and will make their debut at the tournament. [https://www.nyasatimes.com/history-made-malawis-scorchers-stun-ghana-to-book-place-at-world-cup-for-the-very-first-time-as-nation-erupts-in-wild-celebration/ (''Nyasa Times'')] [https://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/SportsArchive/Malawi-stun-Ghana-to-end-Black-Queens-WAFCON-title-hopes-2046946 (Ghanaweb)] [https://www.espn.com/espn/story/_/id/49571953/malawi-ranked-153-stun-ghana-wafcon-quarterfinals-qualify-women-world-cup (ESPN)]
*[[2026 CONCACAF U-20 Championship]]
**[[Mexico national under-20 football team|Mexico]] defeats the [[United States men's national under-20 soccer team|United States]] 2–0 at the [[Estadio Azteca]] to win the [[CONCACAF Under-20 Championship]], its second in a row after winning the [[2024 CONCACAF U-20 Championship|previous one]]. [https://africa.espn.com/football/story/_/id/49571657/mexico-beats-us-concacaf-u20-final (ESPN)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=8|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2026 Iran war]]
**[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
***The [[Abu Dhabi National Oil Company]] says that one of their vessels was attacked by a missile while transiting through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] during the early hours. No injuries were reported. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/uae/adnoc-vessel-targeted-missile-transit-hormuz-strait?_refresh=true (''Khaleej Times'')]
***[[Supreme National Security Council]] [[Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council|secretary]] [[Mohammad Bagher Zolghadr]] says that [[Iran]] will reopen the [[Strait of Hormuz]] if the [[United States]] lifts [[United States sanctions against Iran|sanctions against the country]], ends the [[2026 United States naval blockade of Iran|naval blockade]], and halts [[United States Armed Forces|military action]] against the country. [https://aje.news/b0vimc?update=4838689 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***[[President of Ukraine|Ukrainian president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] reports that a 3-year-old boy and his grandparents were killed by a [[drone warfare|drone strike]] by [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] in [[Kyiv]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/three-killed-russian-strikes-kyiv-region-official-says-2026-08-08/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***[[Darfur]] [[Darfur Regional Government|governor]] [[Minni Minnawi]] says that the [[Sudanese Armed Forces|SAF]]-allied [[Darfur Joint Protection Force|Joint Forces]] have repelled an attack in [[Sudan]]'s [[West Darfur]] [[States of Sudan|state]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317171 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***A tribe leader in the [[Nuba Mountains]] in [[South Kordofan]] accuses the [[Sudan People's Liberation Movement–North]] of launching attacks on [[Otoro language|Otoro]] villages in [[Kauda, Sudan|Kauda]]. Additionally, four aid workers are reported to be detained. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317174 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2026]]
**[[2026 United States wildfires]]
***[[2026 Utah wildfires]]
****The [[National Interagency Fire Center]] reports that two people were killed yesterday in a [[Sikorsky S-64 Skycrane]] [[helicopter]] crash in [[Fishlake National Forest]], [[Utah]], [[U.S.]], while trying to battle the Widemouth 2 [[wildfire|fire]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/08/us/two-killed-wildfire-helicopter-crash.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.thehansindia.com/news/international/two-killed-in-helicopter-crash-fighting-wildfire-in-us-state-of-utah-1107126 (''The Hans India'')]
**[[2026 Canadian wildfires]]
***In [[Canada]], [[British Columbia]] declares a [[state of emergency]] after 105 [[wildfire|wildfires]] were reported across [[Provinces and territories of Canada|the province]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/canada-british-columbia-declares-emergency-as-fires-spread/a-78291841 (DW)]
*[[2026 Pacific typhoon season]]
**[[Typhoon Dolphin (2026)|Typhoon Dolphin]] makes landfall in the [[Ryukyu Islands]] of [[Japan]], which encompass the entirety of [[Okinawa Prefecture]] and parts of [[Kagoshima Prefecture]]. Additionally, [[China]] shuts down [[List of ports in China|ports]] and ferry routes in preparation for the typhoon. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/08/08/japan/typhoon-dolphin-okinawa/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*A helicopter crashes in [[Tijuca National Park]] in [[Rio de Janeiro (state)|Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]], killing three [[Colombians|Colombian]] [[Tourism in Brazil|tourists]] and the pilot. [https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/four-killed-in-helicopter-crash-in-rio-de-janeiro-1.500635018 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]
*Satellite images show that the [[United Kingdom|British]]-sanctioned [[oil tanker]] ''Caroline Bezengi'', believed to be part of the [[Russian shadow fleet]], which was carrying 1 million barrels of oil, is [[Oil spill|leaking oil]] and sinking further off the coast of [[Oman]], after an explosion was reported on the vessel on June 8. The oil leaks have reportedly reached the shore of [[Khuriya Muriya Islands|Al-Qibliyah Island]]. [https://apnews.com/article/oman-russia-oil-tanker-f445bfd4110dd2e44e010dc0b95c825e (AP)]

'''International relations'''
*[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]], [[Italy–Spain relations]]
**[[Spain]] imposes temporary [[border control|border checks]] on travelers from [[Italy]] after Italy introduced similar controls on arrivals from Spain amid a dispute over [[Migration and asylum policy of the European Union|migration policy]] following the [[Migrant crisis|mass arrival]] of [[Immigration to Spain|migrants]] in [[Ceuta]]. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-italy-ceuta-migrants-schengen-border-controls-f3fc82cadf7dce39d553126a47d61fd7 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*4 men and one woman are shot and killed in a house in [[Langa, South Africa|Langa]], [[Cape Flats]], [[Cape Town]], [[South Africa]] on Saturday night. [https://www.ewn.co.za/five-killed-in-langa-mass-shooting/ (EWN)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 7
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=7|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Operation Urja Suraksha]]
*****[[India]]n [[Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways|shipping minister]] [[Sarbananda Sonowal]] reports that more than 4,000 seafarers from India have been repatriated and 62 Indian vessels have successfully transited through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] during the Iran war. [https://www.lokmattimes.com/international/62-india-bound-ships-sailed-safely-out-of-hormuz-amid-west-asia-crisis-minister-2/ (''Lokmat Times'')] [https://indianewengland.com/62-india-bound-ships-transit-strait-of-hormuz-safely-amid-regional-tensions/ (India New England News)]
****The [[Abu Dhabi National Oil Company]] reports that 15 of its vessels have been attacked by missiles or drones while transiting through the Strait of Hormuz since the war with [[Iran]] started on February 28. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/adnoc-says-attacks-vessels-staff-significantly-impacting-operations-2026-08-07/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war]]
****[[Israel]]i [[Israel Defense Forces|forces]] withdraw from the [[Qalandia Camp|Qalandiyah refugee camp]] and [[Kafr 'Aqab]] neighborhood in [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank|occupied]] [[West Bank]] following a two-day raid, with [[Palestinian Authority]] reporting 51 injuries. [https://www.haaretz.com/west-bank/2026-08-07/ty-article/.premium/israeli-forces-withdraw-from-palestinian-refugee-camp-after-two-day-operation/0000019f-db17-d9df-af9f-fb97787c0000 (''Haaretz'')]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***[[Houthi]] attacks in [[Marib Governorate|Marib]], [[Yemen]], kill at least eight [[Yemeni Armed Forces|government soldiers]] and two civilians and injure 26 others, as the group launches missiles, drones and shelling against military positions, residential areas, and [[refugee camp]]s. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/08/09/world/americas-emea/10-killed-in-houthi-attack-on-oil-rich-marib-yemen/2401431 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Odesa strikes (2022–present)|Odesa strikes]]
***A [[Russia]]n drone strike hits the [[Chornomorets Stadium]] in [[Odesa]], [[Ukraine]], with [[Odesa Oblast]] [[Governor of Odesa Oblast|governor]] [[Oleh Kiper]] reporting that two people are injured in the strikes. [https://kyivindependent.com/russian-strike-on-odesa-damages-one-of-ukraines-largest-football-stadiums-injures-one/ (''Kyiv Independent'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***[[Sudan]]ese [[Sudanese Armed Forces|armed forces]] repel a surprise [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] in [[Dilling, South Kordofan|Dilling]], [[South Kordofan]]. Additionally, five civilians are reported to be killed [[Siege of El Obeid|in]] [[El Obeid]], [[North Kordofan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317129 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twenty people are killed and several others are injured after a fuel tanker overturns in [[Bangui]], [[Central African Republic]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260808/18168539da8b405abde74f17d8b039c5/c.html (Xinhua)]
*Sixteen people are killed and dozens others are injured in two separate road accidents in [[Sylhet Division]] and [[Bogra District]], [[Bangladesh]]. [https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20260807/a9e2a200aa3944fd8d919cbb8d1a34c4/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak]]
**[[Michigan Department of Health and Human Services|Michigan health officials]] lift an advisory against the consumption of [[lettuce]] in the [[Michigan|U.S. state]] after reporting a decline in cases of [[cyclosporiasis]], which is caused by ''[[Cyclospora cayetanensis]]''. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/cyclosporiasis-cases-michigan-climb-over-12400-health-officials-say-2026-08-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Brazil]]'s [[National Institute for Space Research]] reports that [[Deforestation of the Amazon rainforest|deforestation]] of the [[Amazon rainforest]] fell to {{convert|2874|sqkm|ha}} from August 2025 to July 2026, a 37% annual decline and the lowest level since the institute's [[satellite monitoring]] began in 2016. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/deforestation-hits-record-low-in-brazilian-amazon (AFP via ''The Straits Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[United States and the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**The [[United States Senate]] votes 86–11 to pass a bill imposing [[Sanctioning Russia Act|sanctions on Russia]]'s [[Energy in Russia|energy]] revenues, [[Banking in Russia|financial institutions]], [[Government of Russia|officials]], and [[Russian shadow fleet|shadow fleet]], while authorizing [[Tariffs in the second Trump administration|tariffs]] of up to 100% on major buyers of [[Russian oil]] and [[Natural gas in Russia|gas]]. The legislation will head to the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House of Representatives]] for a vote. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/sweeping-russia-energy-sanctions-head-toward-us-senate-passage-2026-08-07/ (Reuters)]
*[[Pakistan–Saudi Arabia relations]], [[Pakistan–Turkey relations]], [[Saudi Arabia–Turkey relations]]
**[[Pakistan]], [[Saudi Arabia]], and [[Turkey]] mutually sign the [[Mecca Joint Defence Agreement]], declaring that an attack on one will constitute an attack on all three. [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/saudi-arabia/2026/08/07/saudi-arabia-pakistan-and-turkey-sign-mecca-joint-defense-agreement (Al Arabiya)]
*[[Mexico–Peru relations]]
**The governments of [[Mexico]] and [[Peru]] reinstate diplomatic relations after agreeing to allow former Peruvian [[Prime Minister of Peru|prime minister]] [[Betssy Chávez]] to seek [[Asylum seeker|asylum]] in Mexico. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peru-mexico-resume-diplomatic-relations-2026-08-07/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Karachi]]
**[[Murder of Mir Raza Ali]]
***A judge of the [[Karachi High Court]] in [[Pakistan]] allows the [[exhumation]] of [[Mir Raza Ali]]'s body. [https://www.dawn.com/news/2021005 (''Dawn'')]
*[[2026 Nonthaburi shootings]]
**Nine people are killed, including the shooter, and 15 others are injured in a [[Spree killer|shooting spree]] between a home and the [[Debsirin School|Debsirin Nonthaburi School]] in [[Bang Kruai district]], [[Nonthaburi province]], [[Thailand]]. [https://apnews.com/article/thailand-nonthaburi-school-shooting-7939000dbad098198a9fc77169028762 (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/07/thailand-school-shooting-debsirin-nonthaburi-bangkok (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Inauguration of Abelardo de la Espriella]]
**[[Abelardo de la Espriella]] is sworn in as the [[president of Colombia]] after winning [[2026 Colombian presidential election|the presidential election]] in June. [https://apnews.com/article/colombia-inauguration-de-la-espriella-president-cali-bogota-petro-6a062df06d20e440ba0e4f7ee7587af6 (AP)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Investigation of UFO reports by the United States government]]
**The [[United States Department of Defense|U.S. defense department]] releases more [[Classified information in the United States|classified]] videos and files of [[unidentified flying object]]s, including an incident in the [[Gulf of Oman]] in 2021 when [[United States Air Force]] pilots encountered a swarm of "cold orbs", describing each orb as measuring around 4 feet (1.2 metres) in diameter and moving in irregular patterns. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ce8kr7p2pmdo (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026–27 Ukrainian Premier League]]
**The [[Ukrainian Premier League]]'s [[FC Chornomorets Odesa]] announces on [[Telegram]] that its match against [[FC Kolos Kovalivka]] is postponed after [[Chornomorets Stadium|its home stadium]] was hit by a Russian strike. [https://intent.press/en/news/society/2026/chornomorets-returned-to-the-premier-league-with-a-loss-to-polissya/ (Intent)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=6|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Politics of Uganda|Ugandan authorities]] approve a measure to send troops from [[Uganda]] to the [[Gaza Strip]] as part of the [[International Stabilization Force]] proposed by the [[Board of Peace]] to secure the enclave following the war. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/gaza/uganda-approves-sending-troops-international-force-gaza-rcna591177 (NBC News)]
**[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
***The [[Houthis]] announce a [[Offensive (military)|military offensive]] against [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]]-backed [[Yemeni Armed Forces|government forces]] in [[Marib Governorate]] and [[Hadhramaut Governorate]], with over 30 soldiers being killed in two missile attacks. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/6/houthis-claim-to-have-killed-45-in-attacks-on-yemeni-government-forces (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] launch [[drone warfare|drone attacks]] on two [[oil refinery|oil refineries]] in [[Russia]], the [[Yaroslavl refinery]] and a [[Bashneft-Novoil]] refinery in [[Bashkortostan]], causing large fires at the facilities. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwymv212xrxo (BBC News)]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure]]
***Six people are killed in [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[airstrike]]s across [[Ukraine]], including three civilians in [[Kharkiv Oblast]], while a total [[power outage]] occurs in the city of [[Kherson]] after [[critical infrastructure]] was targeted overnight by Russian drones. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/6/russian-strikes-kill-six-in-ukraine-as-moscow-intercepts-hundreds-of-drones (Al Jazeera)] [https://antikor.info/en/articles/854970-posle_nochnoj_ataki_rf_herson_ostalsja_bez_elektrosnabhenija__ova (Antikor)]
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**[[2026 Ethiopia–TPLF clashes]]
***It is reported that the situation on [[Ethiopia–Sudan border|the border]] between [[Ethiopia]] and [[Sudan]] is calm following recent clashes between the [[Ethiopian Army]] and [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]] that sparked fears of a new conflict four years after a [[Ethiopia–Tigray peace agreement|peace agreement]] was signed in 2022 to end the [[Tigray War|war]] in [[Tigray Region|Tigray]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317095 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Haitian conflict]]
**The [[United Nations Mission for Justice Support in Haiti|United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti]] reports that 613 people were killed and 375 others injured between March 6 and July 31 amid intensifying gang violence across the country. [https://www.cbc.bb/news/caribbean-news/over-600-killed-in-renewed-gang-violence-in-haiti-since-march/ (Caribbean Broadcasting Corporation)]
**Two people are killed and 13 others are injured when an explosive device detonates on a passenger [[minibus]] in [[Jaramana]], [[Syria]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/bomb-explosion-aboard-passenger-minibus-kills-2-injures-13-near-damascus-state-media/4020507 (AA)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance]]
**The [[Competition and Markets Authority]] of the [[United Kingdom]] clears [[Paramount Skydance]]'s [[United States dollar|US$]]110 billion [[Mergers and acquisitions|acquisition]] of [[Warner Bros. Discovery]], while [[Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport|culture secretary]] [[Lisa Nandy]] declines a [[Public interest law|public-interest]] review after receiving commitments on [[editorial independence]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/economy/uk-clears-paramount-s-stalled-110b-warner-bros-discovery-takeover/4020298 (AA)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Civil officials state that ten children passengers are reported missing after a wooden boat capsized on the [[Lulua River]], [[Demba Territory]], [[Kasai-Central]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/more-than-10-children-missing-after-boat-capsizes-in-dr-congo/4020879 (AA)]
*Six people are killed and 19 others are injured after a bus crashed in [[Constantine Province]], [[Algeria]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260806/fc47b5b6575f4cd0b35f6c615173a96a/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**[[Ministry of Public Health (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|Congolese health authorities]] monitor passengers from a boat near [[Kinshasa]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], after a traveler died from [[Ebola]] complications. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/08/06/congo-ebola-outbreak-ituri-protest-health-workers/6b8ab3b6-9175-11f1-9fdc-0a725c989a7b_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]]
**[[Mayor-President of Ceuta|Ceuta mayor-president]] [[Juan Jesús Vivas]] confirms that at least 100 people died during last week's [[Migrant crisis|migrant surge]] into the [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Autonomous communities of Spain|autonomous city]] of [[Ceuta]], while around 3,500 to 5,000 [[Illegal immigration|undocumented migrants]] remain in the city. [https://www.reuters.com/world/100-people-died-during-ceuta-border-rush-says-ceuta-leader-2026-08-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Mexican drug war]]
**[[Iguala mass kidnapping]]
***Former [[Guerrero]] [[Governor of Guerrero|governor]] [[Ángel Aguirre Rivero]] is arrested on charges of [[Missing persons in Mexico|forced disappearance]] and obstruction of justice. He is accused of ordering the concealment of security camera footage that showed police intercepting a bus carrying [[Ayotzinapa Rural Normal School|students]] in [[Iguala]] in 2014, who have never been found. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/former-mexican-governor-arrested-allegedly-destroying-evidence-tied-43-missing-2026-08-06/ (Reuters)]

{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=5|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Iran–Oman negotiations]]
*****[[Iran]] and [[Oman]] reach an agreement understanding on [[Geographic coordinate system|geographic coordinates]] for shipping routes through the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-oman-reach-understanding-coordinates-route-through-hormuz-iran-ministry-2026-08-05/ (Reuters)] [https://www.euronews.com/2026/08/05/iran-and-oman-agree-route-for-ships-in-strait-of-hormuz-tehran-says (Euronews)]
**[[2026 Lebanon war]]
***[[2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire]]
****[[2026 Israel–Lebanon peace talks|Talks]] between [[Israel]] and [[Lebanon]] are on pause following alleged leaks and will resume tomorrow. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/08/israel-lebanon-talks-suspended-over-alleged-leaks-set-resume-thursday (Al-Monitor)]
***[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) says they have launched strikes in [[southern Lebanon|southern]] [[Lebanon]] after alleged [[ceasefire]] violations by [[Hezbollah]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-it-launched-strikes-in-south-lebanon-after-alleged-ceasefire-violation-by-hezbollah/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
****Two [[Israeli Ground Forces|Israeli soldiers]] are [[killed in action]] and four others are wounded in an [[improvised explosive device]] bombing in [[Majdal Zoun]], [[South Governorate]], Lebanon. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/2-israeli-soldiers-killed-in-explosive-device-blast-in-southern-lebanon/4019715 (Anadolu Ajansı)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Chief of the General Staff (Israel)|IDF chief]] [[Eyal Zamir]] visits the [[Gaza Strip]] to conduct an assessment in the enclave. He also states that the military will continue to operate proactively. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-904710 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] launch dozens of [[ballistic missile]]s and drones at [[Kyiv]], [[Ukraine]], killing at least 17 people, including eight [[civilian]]s at a [[railway station]] in [[Kyiv Oblast]], and wounding dozens more. None of the missiles were intercepted by [[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] due to a shortage of [[MIM-104 Patriot|Patriot missile]]s, according to [[President of Ukraine|president]] [[Volodymyr Zelenskyy]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/05/russia-kyiv-attack-kills-at-least-14-people-ukraine-authorities (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Five people are killed after two vehicles collided head-on and burst into flames on the [[Stuart Highway]], [[Australia]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260806/f01d2b00c03240888cbb74e023b162a2/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''Health and environment'''
*The [[Food and Drug Administration|U.S. Food and Drug Administration]] approves [[Moderna]]'s [[mRNA vaccine|mRNA]] [[influenza vaccine]] for people aged 50 and older. [https://time.com/article/2026/08/06/fda-approves-first-mrna-flu-vaccine/ (''Time'')] [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/us-fda-approves-first-mrna-flu-shot-moderna-2026-08-06/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[International sanctions against Iran]]
**The [[United States Treasury Department]] lifts [[United States sanctions against Iran|sanctions]] against [[Fly Baghdad]], which were previously imposed in 2024 over its links to [[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] [[Quds Force]]. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/08/us-lifts-sanctions-fly-baghdad-previously-linked-irans-irgc (Al-Monitor)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-removes-sanctions-three-irgc-linked-entities-treasury-website-shows-2026-08-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[List of pastoral trips made by Pope Leo XIV|Pastoral trips made by Pope Leo XIV]], [[Argentina–Holy See relations]], [[Holy See–Peru relations]], [[Holy See–Uruguay relations]]
**The [[Holy See]] [[Holy See Press Office|Press Office]] announces [[Pope]] [[Leo XIV]] will make an [[papal travel|apostolic journey]] to [[Argentina]], [[Uruguay]], and his home country of [[Peru]], in November, marking his first trip to [[Latin America]] in his papacy. [https://apnews.com/article/vatican-pope-leo-peru-argentina-uruguay-latin-701f20187f230f504f15a2b2fb52a89b (AP)] [https://press.vatican.va/content/salastampa/en/bollettino/pubblico/2026/08/05/260805b.html (Holy See)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Karachi]]
**[[Murder of Mir Raza Ali]]
***[[Sindh Police]] detain 19 people for questioning as part of the investigation into the murder of Karachi entrepreneur and Wafflix founder [[Mir Raza Ali]]. [https://en.dailypakistan.com.pk/04-Aug-2026/mir-raza-murder-case-cctv-shows-scavenger-at-crime-scene-19-detained (Daily Pakistan)] [https://arynews.tv/mir-raza-ali-case-police-detain-18-for-questioning-in-karachi-raids (ARY News)]
*[[Far-right politics in Germany (1945–present)|Far-right politics in Germany]]
**The [[Hanseatisches Oberlandesgericht|Hanseatic Higher Regional Court]] in [[Hamburg]], [[Germany]], convicts seven members and one supporter of a [[right-wing extremist]] group called ''Last Defense Wave'' and sentences them to [[Prisons in Germany|prison]] for [[attempted murder]], [[arson]], [[aggravated assault]], and being members of a [[Terrorism in Germany|terrorist organisation]] for planning and carrying out arson and bomb attacks on [[refugee shelter|asylum seeker shelters]]. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-far-right-group-conviction-prison-sentences-2eae8375b7c427ff1e945eb935ca0882 (AP)]
*[[War on drugs]], [[Illegal drug trade in Latin America]], [[Crime in Spain]]
**The [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Civil Guard (Spain)|Civil Guard]] and the [[Ecuador]]ian [[National Police of Ecuador|National Police]] announce they have arrested 44 people and confiscated 21 tons of [[cocaine]] as part of a multiyear investigation on a [[drug trafficking]] ring financed by investors in [[Dubai]], [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://apnews.com/article/drugs-spain-ecuador-cocaine-6a8f4fd0e6ff23f5be9224933e092662 (AP)]
*A drone loaded with explosives is found and defused at [[Leipzig/Halle Airport]] in [[Germany]], while a cargo [[Boeing 757]] had a collision with another supposed UAV at the same airport. [https://www.reuters.com/world/german-police-examine-suspicious-object-leipzig-airport-2026-08-05/ (Reuters)] [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-news-explosive-drone-defused-at-leipzig-airport/live-78241747 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Aftermath of the July Uprising]]
**Former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|Bangladesh prime minister]] [[Sheikh Hasina]] announces that she plans to return to [[Bangladesh|the country]] from exile in [[New Delhi]], [[India]], despite facing a [[capital punishment in Bangladesh|death sentence]] for her role during a [[July massacre|violent crackdown]] on [[July Uprising|protesters]] that led to [[Resignation of Sheikh Hasina|her resignation]] two years ago. [https://news.sky.com/story/bangladeshs-ousted-ex-prime-minister-sheikh-hasina-says-she-will-return-despite-facing-death-sentence-13570122 (Sky News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[2026 SpaceX lunar impact]]
**The spent upper stage ([[International Designator|COSPAR ID]] 2025-010D) of a [[SpaceX]] [[Falcon 9]] rocket [[List of artificial objects on the Moon|collided with the Moon]] near [[Einstein (crater)|Einstein Crater]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/science/2026/jul/31/spacex-rocket-moon-collision (The Guardian)]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 4
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=4|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]], [[Qatar as a mediator in conflict]]
*****Mediators from [[Qatar]] reports that progress has been made in efforts to end the [[war]] between the [[United States]] and [[Iran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/status-us-iran-talks-uncertain-ship-struck-hormuz-2026-08-04/ (Reuters)]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****The [[Liberia]]n-flagged [[bulk carrier]] ''Minoan Pioneer'' is reported to be missing in the [[Strait of Hormuz]] after it was struck by a unknown projectile northeast of [[Oman]]. [https://www.seatrade-maritime.com/security/cargo-ship-struck-in-the-strait-of-hormuz (''Seatrade Maritime News'')] [https://english.alarabiya.net/News/middle-east/2026/08/04/dry-bulk-ship-struck-by-projectile-near-strait-of-hormuz-crew-abandon-ship-sources (Al Arabiya)] [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-security/2026-08-04/ty-article-live/as-board-of-peace-urges-de-escalation-idf-strikes-reportedly-kill-two-in-gaza/0000019f-ca64-db33-a5ff-fa7420cf0000?liveBlogItemId=69731044#69731044 (''Haaretz'')]
****Shipping data show that [[Iraq]] has exported over 30 million [[Barrel (unit)#Oil barrel|barrels]] of [[Petroleum|crude oil]] through the [[strait]] between July 4 and August 4. [https://english.aawsat.com/business/5303393-iraq-exported-30-mn-barrels-crude-hormuz-month-monitor (''Asharq Al-Awsat'')]
***It is reported that the [[United States Army]] has used most of its [[ATACMS]] and [[Precision Strike Missile|Precision Strike]] missiles during the [[war]] in [[Iran]] including [[Operation Epic Fury]]. [https://www.militarytimes.com/industry/techwatch/2026/08/04/us-used-virtually-all-long-range-precision-missiles-during-iran-war-sources-say/ (''Military Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us-has-used-virtually-all-its-long-range-precision-missiles-during-iran-war-2026-08-04/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Casualties of the Gaza war]]
****A mass funeral is held for 112 bodies that were recovered from a [[Israel]]i strike in the [[Sabra, Gaza City|Sabra]] neighborhood of [[Gaza City]] during the early weeks of the war. [https://www.haaretz.com/gaza/2026-08-04/ty-article/.premium/mass-funeral-held-in-gaza-for-112-people-recovered-from-2023-strike-rubble/0000019f-cc03-db33-a5ff-fe77b7df0000 (''Haaretz'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***[[Yemen]]'s [[Presidential Leadership Council|internationally recognized government]] says a [[projectile]] attack sank the [[India]]n-flagged cargo ship MSV ''Faize Noore Oliya'' in the [[Red Sea]] near the coast of [[Hodeidah]], with all 14 crew members rescued. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2653392/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***[[Rapid Support Forces]] senior commander and [[Brigadier general|brigadier general]] [[Mahdi Adam Ismail]], also known as ''Jebel Moon'', is confirmed to be killed during clashes with the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]] and the [[Darfur Joint Protection Force|Joint Forces]] in [[West Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. His death is confirmed by [[Sudan Liberation Movement/Army|Sudan Liberation Movement]] leader and [[Darfur Regional Government|Darfur governor]] [[Minni Minnawi|Minni Arko Minnawi]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/317039 (''Sudan Tribune'')] [https://sudannabaa.com/en/news-en/killing-of-militia-commander-mahdi-adam-ismail-known-as-jabal-moon/88013/?amp=1 (Sudan Nabaa)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**[[Health Canada]] announces it has given [[Moderna]] the green light for authorization to launch a clinical trial for a [[mRNA vaccine|mRNA]] [[Ebola vaccine|Ebola]] [[vaccine]] aimed at targeting the [[Bundibugyo ebolavirus|Bundibugyo strain]] of the [[Ebola|ebola]][[ebolavirus|virus]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/health/ebola-vaccine-trial-health-canada-moderna-9.7295616 (CBC)]
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[Austria]] records {{convert|41|C|F}} in [[Vienna]], the [[List of weather records|highest temperature]] in [[Climate of Austria|the country's history]], as a [[heat wave]] also brings [[wildfire]]s and historically low [[Danube]] water levels. [https://english.news.cn/20260805/d3f2f716b706406ab32cdae25faa1eb2/c.html (Xinhua)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Brazil–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] revokes the [[Visa policy of the United States|visa]] of [[List of ambassadors of Brazil to the United States|Brazilian ambassador]] [[Maria Luiza Ribeiro Viotti]] to [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] [[Brazil]]'s denial of [[Visa policy of Brazil|visas]] to two U.S. diplomats. The [[State Department]] says the action does not expel Viotti from the country. [https://www.nst.com.my/world/world/2026/08/1504316/us-revokes-visa-brazilian-ambassador-washington (AFP via ''New Straits Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**The [[Colombia]]n [[Special Jurisdiction for Peace]] charges 27 former [[FARC]] members, including ex-commander [[Timoleón Jiménez]], with [[crimes against humanity]] and [[Wartime sexual violence|sexual violence]] committed during the conflict, including killings, [[Kidnappings in Colombia|disappearances]], [[Forced displacement|displacement]], and [[Rape statistics#Colombia|rape]]. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/08/05/world/americas-emea/27-ex-guerrillas-charged-with-crimes-against-humanity-in-colombia/2398570 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
*[[President of Kyrgyzstan|Kyrgyz president]] [[Sadyr Japarov]] signs a law banning the use of [[cremation]] for deceased human bodies in [[Kyrgyzstan]]. [https://akipress.com/news:910655:Kyrgyzstan_bans_cremation_of_human_bodies/?place=main1 (AKIPress)] [https://en.kabar.kg/news/kyrgyzstan-officially-bans-cremation/ (Kabar)]
*[[South Sudan]]ese [[South Sudan Police Service|police]] arrest 60 suspected gang members in a series of operations targeting criminal gangs, [[Illegal drug trade|drug trafficking]] and [[Juvenile delinquency|youth delinquency]] in [[Juba]]. [https://www.sudanspost.com/south-sudan-police-arrest-60-in-anti-gang-operation-in-juba/ (''Sudans Post'')]
*Four people are killed and four others are injured in a [[shooting spree]] by a [[Desertion|rogue]] [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian soldier]] in [[Sevastopol]], [[Russian occupation of Crimea|Russian-occupied Crimea]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/serviceman-shoots-civilians-soldiers-crimea-deaths/ (CBS News)]
*A 37-year-old man [[2026 Plovdiv murder|is killed]] in [[Plovdiv]], [[Bulgaria]] after being [[lure]]d through a dating app by a group of teenagers posing as an underage girl. [https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/1181579-plovdiv-court-leaves-teenage-killers-in-custody (BTA)]

'''Sports'''
*[[Timeline_of_the_WNBA#2025–future:_Expansion_era|Expansion of the WNBA]]
**In [[basketball]], the [[Women's National Basketball Association]] announces that the expansion team in [[Cleveland]], [[Ohio]], [[United States|U.S.]], will be called the [[Cleveland Sirens|Sirens]]. The organization will debut in 2028. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7490965/2026/08/04/cleveland-sirens-wnba-expansion-2028/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')]

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 3
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=3|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Gaza peace plan]]
****A [[Board of Peace]] envoy meets [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] and urges a halt in strikes across the [[Gaza Strip]]. However, they also announce that [[Israel]] will not withdraw from the enclave until [[Hamas]] completely disarms. [https://thenewregion.com/posts/6091 (''The New Region'')] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/08/03/mideast-gaza-disarmament-hamas-netanyahu/28ac67ae-8f6f-11f1-9fdc-0a725c989a7b_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[Casualties of the Gaza war]]
****The [[United Nations]] [[United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs|Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs]] reports that dozens of [[Effect of the Gaza war on children in the Gaza Strip|children]] and civilians have been killed in Israeli attacks on Gaza over the weekend, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [https://english.news.cn/20260804/31d80575cde444acb07d23159b82d4c3/c.html (Xinhua)]
****Two [[Palestinian]] civilians are killed in an Israeli missile strike near a [[mosque]] which targeted a civilian vehicle southwest of [[Gaza City]]. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/two-palestinians-killed-israeli-strike-southwest-gaza-city (Middle East Eye)]
***[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) claim that they have killed [[Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] commander [[Mahmoud Fatair]], who took part in the [[Kidnapping of Rom Braslavski|abduction]] of [[Rom Braslavski]], in the [[Deir al-Balah]] area of the [[Gaza Strip]] during the [[Nova music festival massacre]] on [[October 7 attacks|October 7, 2023]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/article-904464 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***The IDF claim that they have killed two Hamas militants in separate [[airstrike|airstrikes]] in central Gaza and the [[Al-Shati refugee camp|Shati camp]] in [[Gaza City]] respectively, violating the ongoing ceasefire. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-it-killed-2-senior-hamas-members-one-of-whom-took-part-in-oct-7/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***Shipping data shows that two [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]] ships carrying oil from [[Saudi Arabia]], the [[Suezmax]] [[Malta]]-[[Flag state|flagged]] ''Lesvos'' and the [[Oil tanker#Size categories|VLCC]] ''Desh Vaibhav'', have exited the [[Red Sea]] through the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]] [[strait]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/two-tankers-with-saudi-oil-exit-red-sea-over-weekend-data-shows-2026-08-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***At least seven people, including three children, are killed and 40 others are injured when drone debris falls on a crowded beach in [[Gelendzhik]], [[Krasnodar Krai]], [[Russia]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/03/europe/ukrainian-drone-southern-russia-beach-intl (CNN)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Venezuela earthquakes]]
**The death toll from the two [[earthquake]]s that hit [[Venezuela]] in June exceeds 6,000 people according to figures from lawmaker [[Jorge Rodríguez (Venezuelan politician)|Jorge Rodríguez]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/death-toll-venezuela-june-earthquakes-tops-6000-2026-08-03/ (Reuters)]
*At least fourteen people are killed in a series of floods in [[southern India]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/fourteen-dead-thousands-displaced-rains-floods-strike-southern-india-2026-08-03/ (Reuters)]
*[[Guatemala]]'s [[Coordinadora Nacional para la Reducción de Desastres|disaster agency]] declares a nationwide orange alert following a major eruption of [[Volcán de Fuego|Fuego volcano]] and begins evacuating two nearby villages. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/world/885758/guatemala-issues-danger-alert-after-fuego-volcano-erupts (AFP via RNZ)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2020–2026 H5N1 outbreak]]
**[[Scotland]]'s [[NatureScot]] denies a 2026 licence for hunting [[northern gannet]]s on [[Sula Sgeir]], citing possible harm to the local gannet population after recent [[bird-flu]] deaths. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/international-news/20260804-last-scottish-island-bird-hunt-banned-after-almost-500-years (AFP via RFI)]
*[[2026 European heatwaves]]
**[[Italy]] experiences its fourth [[heatwave]] of the summer with the [[Ministry of Health (Italy)|health ministry]] issuing [[extreme heat warning|red alerts]] for a record 25 cities. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/italy-s-4th-heat-wave-peaks-with-red-alerts-in-record-25-cities/4016831 (AA)]
*[[2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak]]
**[[Michigan]], [[United States|U.S.]], reports the first two deaths of the current [[cyclosporiasis]] outbreak, which is caused by ''[[cyclospora cayetanensis]]''. [https://apnews.com/article/michigan-cyclospora-outbreak-deaths-cf058908cdfd1bfd405d15e7079bed14 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
**The [[Poland|Polish]] [[Ministry of Health (Poland)|health ministry]] appeals a [[Brussels]] [[Tribunal of first instance (Belgium)|court]] ruling that ordered the country to accept and pay approximately [[Euro sign|€]]1.3 billion for unwanted [[COVID-19 vaccine]] doses [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|produced]] by [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/poland-appeal-pfizer-vaccine-ruling/ (''Politico EU'')]
*South African news outlets report that over 170 people have been murdered in the [[Western Cape]], [[South Africa]] in the past 2 weeks. [https://iol.co.za/capeargus/news/2026-08-02-western-cape-in-turmoil-with-over-170-murders-in-two-weeks-sparking-urgent-calls-for-action/ (''Independent Online'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Human rights in Russia]]
**[[Russia]]n [[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|opposition]] politician [[Boris Nadezhdin]], who attempted to contest the [[2024 Russian presidential election|2024 presidential election]] on a platform against the [[Russo-Ukrainian war]], announces that he has fled the country to [[France]] following growing pressure on him and his family. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/08/03/boris-nadezhdin-leaves-russia-a93401 (''The Moscow Times'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 WTA Tour]]
**[[2026 Mubadala DC Open]]
***In [[tennis]], [[Alexandra Eala]] becomes the first [[Philippines|Filipino]] player and the first player from [[Southeast Asia]] to win a [[WTA Tour]] title after defeating [[Jessica Pegula]] 4–6, 6–4, 6–0 to win the [[2026 Mubadala DC Open – Women's singles|women's singles]] title at the 2026 [[Washington DC Open]]. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/sports/20260803-eala-powers-past-pegula-for-first-wta-title-in-washington (AFP via RFI)] [https://www.espn.com/tennis/story/_/id/49521788/alex-eala-claims-first-title-dc-open-becomes-first-filipina-win-wta-500-crown (ESPN)]
*In [[horse racing]], [[Churchill Downs Incorporated]] and the [[New York Racing Association]] announce a new championship series for 3-year old [[Thoroughbred]]s beginning in 2027, involving the [[Kentucky Derby]] and [[Belmont Stakes]], but notably omitting the traditional middle leg of the [[Triple Crown of Thoroughbred Racing (United States)|U.S. Triple Crown]], the [[Preakness Stakes]]. [https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/horses/horse-racing/2026/08/03/churchill-downs-nyra-thoroughbred-championship-series-kentucky-derby-belmont-stakes-horse-racing/91149294007/ (''Courier Journal'')] [https://www.dailygazette.com/horse_racing/nyra-churchill-downs-collaborate-on-championship-series/article_7b75745c-563e-43ae-938c-1f374084cb75.html (''The Daily Gazette'')]
* [[Major League Soccer]], the top flight of men's [[Association football|soccer]] in the [[Soccer in the United States|U.S.]] and [[Soccer in Canada|Canada]], announces that [[Larry Berg]], currently a co-owner of [[Los Angeles FC]] (LAFC) in that league, will succeed [[Don Garber]] as league commissioner at the start of 2027. Berg will sell his interest in LAFC before assuming his new position. [https://apnews.com/article/mls-new-commissioner-berg-867851cd4d30855a5e1217bdc619cb0e (AP)] [https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/03/larry-berg-mls-commissioner-vote (''The Guardian'')]
