parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 2
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=2|top=yes}}
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]]
*****[[Iranian Parliament|Iranian lawmaker]] [[Hassan Ghashghavi]] says that efforts to restore the [[Islamabad Memorandum]] deal between [[Iran]] and the [[United States]] are underway. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2653137/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[2026 Iran–Oman negotiations]]
*****[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Iranian foreign minister]] [[Abbas Araghchi]] says that Iran and [[Oman]] are nearing a deal to manage the [[Strait of Hormuz]] after the U.S. halted its [[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran|recent strikes]] against the country. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/2/iran-says-negotiations-with-oman-over-strait-of-hormuz-in-final-stages (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) confirm that they killed three militants in separate strikes last week, including a [[Army of Islam (Gaza)|Jaish al-Islam]] militant in [[Gaza City]], a [[Hamas]] commander in the Jabalya Battalion, and a [[Palestinian Islamic Jihad]] militant. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-904348 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***The IDF's [[401st Brigade (Israel)|401st Brigade]] says that they have destroyed 1,200 [[Hezbollah]] [[Hezbollah tunnels|tunnels]] and concluded their mission in [[southern Lebanon|southern]] [[Lebanon]], ending their eight-month deployment. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/431114 (''Israel National News'')] [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-904328 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)|Ethiopian civil conflict]]
**[[Ethiopia-TPLF clashes (2026–present)|Ethiopia-TPLF clashes]]
***New clashes are reported across the [[Tigray Region]] in northern [[Ethiopia]] between the [[Ethiopian Army|Ethiopian federal army]] and [[Tigray People's Liberation Front]], four years after the [[Tigray War|previous war]] in the region ended, prompting hundreds to flee to war-torn [[Sudan]] amidst fears of a new [[civil war]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cdrv6r3xgyeo (BBC)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/8/3/tigray-refugees-flee-into-sudan-after-deadly-violence-on-ethiopia-border (Al Jazeera)]
***Several Ethiopian refugees are reportedly killed after projectiles have hit refugee camps across the [[Ethiopia–Sudan border]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316940 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]], [[Darfur genocide (2023–present)|Darfur genocide]]
***A [[Drone warfare|drone strike]] hits a [[customary law|customary court]] in [[Kabkabiya District]], [[North Darfur]], [[Sudan]], killing at least 37 people. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/2/sudan-army-drone-attack-on-darfur-kills-35-rights-group-says (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**[[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police|Police]] say a suspected [[suicide bombing]] outside a police station in [[Kabal, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa|Kabal]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]], [[Pakistan]], killed at least 17 people, including seven officers and the suspected bomber, and injured at least 34 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/suspected-suicide-bombing-police-station-kills-least-14-pakistan-officials-say-2026-08-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mali War]], [[Mali–Russia relations]]
**The [[BBC]] reports that [[Russia]] shipped military equipment to the [[Mali]]an [[Government of Mali|government]] on the sanctioned [[Cargo ship|cargo vessel]] ''Mikhail Britnev'' last month. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cgk4rdley0ko (BBC News)] [https://newsukraine.rbc.ua/news/bbc-russia-shipped-armored-vehicles-to-mali-1785672943.html (RBC-Ukraine)]
*[[Papua conflict]]
**Five road construction workers are killed in an ambush by armed separatist insurgents at a workers' camp in [[Tolikara Regency]], [[Highland Papua]], [[Indonesia]]. [https://en.antaranews.com/news/425187/five-workers-killed-by-insurgents-in-highland-papua-manhunt-ongoing (Antara News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Greece wildfires]]
** Two people are killed when two [[Hellenic Fire Service|firefighting]] helicopters collide near [[Athens]], [[Greece]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c1417713ve6o (BBC News)]
*[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]]
**[[Government of Spain|Spanish officials]] say at least 72 people died during the [[Migrant crisis|mass migrant crossing]] from [[Morocco]] into the [[Autonomous communities of Spain#Autonomous_cities|autonomous city]] of [[Ceuta]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/death-toll-migrant-rush-into-ceuta-rises-72-2026-08-02/ (Reuters)]
*Six people are killed and 27 more injured in a traffic collision between a bus, a camper, and three cars in [[Colli sul Velino]], [[Province of Rieti]], [[Italy]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260803/e330a1c742a244308007cc7b022d5836/c.html (Xinhua)]
*A ferry catches fire off the coast of [[Madura]], [[Indonesia]], leaving at least five people dead and 41 others missing. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c74g0wjvlrxo (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[South Korea]]'s [[Korea Meteorological Administration|weather agency]] records {{convert|42.5|C|F}} in [[Yangsan]], [[South Gyeongsang Province|South Gyeongsang]], the country's [[List of weather records|highest temperature]] since observations began. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260802-south-korea-records-its-highest-ever-temperature-of-42-5c (AFP via France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Foreign relations of the Dominican Republic]], [[Foreign relations of Venezuela]]
**The [[Dominican Republic]] and [[Venezuela]] agree on a framework to gradually restore diplomatic relations, which deteriorated after the Dominican Republic [[International reactions to the 2024 Venezuelan presidential election|questioned]] the results of the [[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]]. [https://www.jamaicaobserver.com/2026/08/02/venezuela-dominican-republic-agree-restore-ties-dispute-maduro/ (AFP via ''Jamaica Observer'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Brazilian general election]]
**Incumbent [[Brazil]]ian [[President of Brazil|president]] [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]] formally announces his candidacy for a fourth term as the [[Workers' Party (Brazil)|Workers' Party]]'s nominee in October’s [[Presidential elections in Brazil|presidential election]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260802-brazil-s-lula-launches-fourth-term-bid-as-trump-looms-over-campaign (AFP via France 24)]
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=2|bottom=yes}}

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 August 1
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=08|day=1|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****The [[Bermuda]]-flagged [[LNG carrier|LNG tanker]] ''Gaslog Shanghai'', which was carrying [[Liquefied natural gas|LNG]] [[Natural gas in Qatar|oil]] from [[Qatar]], is reported to have been among the two vessels hit yesterday in the [[Strait of Hormuz]]. [https://www.arabtimesonline.com/news/qatari-lng-tanker-struck-by-projectile-in-strait-of-hormuz-bloomberg-reports/ (''Arab Times Kuwait'')] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-01/tanker-carrying-qatari-lng-struck-while-transiting-hormuz (Bloomberg)]
****A [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]] near [[Oman]] is hit by an unknown projectile. [https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/01/tankers-near-oman-come-under-fire.html (CNBC)]
***[[Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war|2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait]]
****The [[Ministry of Defense (Kuwait)|Kuwaiti defense ministry]] reports that [[Kuwait Armed Forces|its military]] has detected and intercepted [[Iran]]ian [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|drones]] entering [[Kuwait|the country]]'s [[airspace]]. [https://kuwaittimes.com/article/47424/kuwait/kuwait-military-thwarts-hostile-iranian-drone-attack-reports-no-casualties/ (''Kuwait Times'')]
***[[United States]] [[List of diplomatic missions of the United States#Asia|embassies]] in the [[Middle East]] warn [[Americans]] to depart the region amidst fears of a potential escalation in the war. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2653013/middle-east (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
***[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] cancels a planned attack against Iran, citing progress in [[2026 Iran war ceasefire|ceasefire]] [[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations|negotiations]]. [https://www.axios.com/2026/08/02/trump-iran-attack-cancelled (''Axios'')] [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2026/08/02/world/trump-cancels-iran-attacks/ (''The Japan Times'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Casualties of the Gaza war]], [[Israeli bombing of the Gaza Strip]]
****[[IDF|Israeli]] airstrikes kill three [[Palestinians]] in [[Gaza City]], bringing the total casualties in the past 24 hours to seven. [https://english.ahram.org.eg/NewsContent/58/1262/573873/War-on-Gaza/War-on-Gaza/Three-Palestinians-killed-in-Israeli-drone-strikes.aspx (''Al-Ahram'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/1/israeli-strikes-kill-four-across-gaza-destroy-medical-supply-warehouse (Al Jazeera)]
***[[Gaza peace plan]]
****A [[Board of Peace]] official reports that [[Hamas]] will disarm its weapons in the coming days. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/board-of-peace-says-hamas-to-start-disarming-in-coming-days-idf-hits-gaza-arms-depots/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***[[2026 Lebanon war]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] says it has killed several [[Hezbollah]] fighters in an [[Israeli-occupied territories|Israeli-held area]] of [[southern Lebanon]], despite a [[2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire|ceasefire framework]] between [[Israel]] and [[Lebanon]]. [https://www.scmp.com/news/world/middle-east/article/3362660/israel-says-it-killed-several-hezbollah-fighters-south-lebanon (AFP via ''South China Morning Post'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***The [[Houthis]] in [[Yemen]] deny reports of imposing tolls on vessels passing through the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]] strait. [https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/2026/8/1/yemens-houthis-deny-plan-to-charge-ships-transiting-red-sea (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Foreign involvement in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***''[[The Washington Post]]'' reports that [[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli prime minister]] [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] blocked a request by former [[United States Senate|United States senator]] [[Lindsey Graham]] to transfer an [[Iron Dome]] system from the [[U.S.]] to [[Ukraine]]. [https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/israel-security/2026-08-01/ty-article/report-netanyahu-blocked-lindsey-grahams-request-to-send-iron-dome-to-ukraine/0000019f-bd7f-d3b5-a99f-bdffdd7b0000 (''Haaretz'')]
**[[Kyiv strikes (2022–present)|Kyiv strikes]]
***[[Kyiv]] [[Mayor of Kyiv|mayor]] [[Vitali Klitschko]] says an overnight [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile attack [[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|has killed]] at least nine people and injured 24 others, while damaging buildings and causing fires across several [[Subdivisions of Kyiv|districts]] of the [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[capital city|capital]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/1/russian-missile-attack-kills-three-in-ukraines-kyiv (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/aerospace-defense/russia-pounds-kyiv-with-missiles-2026-07-31/ (Reuters)]
**[[Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Naval warfare in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Armed Forces of Ukraine|Ukrainian forces]] sink a [[Rosatom]]-owned [[container ship]] in the [[Black Sea]], forcing its 17-member crew to abandon it. Rosatom says it had been transporting civilian goods, including frozen food and construction materials. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/ce973yvk7pko (BBC News)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Battle of Khartoum (2023–2025)|Battle of Khartoum]]
***[[Egypt]] and [[Sudan]] reach an agreement on a 16-month plan to rehabilitate the [[Jebel Aulia Dam]] south of [[Khartoum]], including the construction of a temporary bridge, after the [[dam]] was damaged in November 2023 during shelling by the [[Rapid Support Forces]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316907 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Terrorism in Colombia]]
**[[2026 Attack on the Norte de Santander Police Command|2026 attack on the Norte de Santander Police Command]]
***A [[truck bomb]] explodes beside a [[National Police of Colombia|police]] station in [[Cúcuta]], [[Norte de Santander Department|Norte de Santander]], [[Colombia]], injuring eleven police officers and three civilians. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260801-11-injured-in-colombia-bombing-days-before-presidential-inauguration (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Terrorism in Russia]] 
**[[2026 Moscow restaurant bombing|2026 Moscow bombing]]
***A woman attempts to set off a bomb inside a [[coffeehouse]] in [[Moscow]], [[Russia]], but is stopped at the entrance and detonates the explosive. Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and 21 more are injured. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/01/europe/moscow-explosion-restaurant-latam-intl (CNN)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Iraq in the 2026 Iran war]]
**The [[Arba'in pilgrimage|Arba'in]] [[Shia Islam]] pilgrimage in [[Iraq]] is held amidst the Iran war, with Iranian pilgrims attending the event. [https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/08/iranian-pilgrims-flood-iraq-first-arbaeen-war (Al-Monitor)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 United States wildfires]]
**[[2026 Washington wildfires]]
***The [[Old Trails Fire|Old Trails]] [[wildfire]] in northwestern [[Spokane, Washington|Spokane]], [[Washington (state)|Washington]], [[United States]], burns over {{cvt|3,000|acres|km2}}, destroying many structures. Residents near [[Fort Spokane]] are told to evacuate. [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/01/us/spokane-washington-wildfire-old-trails (CNN)] [https://news.az/news/fort-spokane-wildfire-residents-ordered-to-evacuate (News.az)]
*[[2024–2026 Cuba blackouts]]
**[[Cuba]] reports a partial collapse of the national [[power grid]], leaving western [[Provinces of Cuba|provinces]] without electricity after [[transmission line]]s fail between [[Matanzas Province|Matanzas]] and [[Pinar del Río Province|Pinar del Río]]. [https://english.news.cn/20260802/330cc886a90447419b2956dcb0319a0f/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[2026 Aerodiana Cessna 208 crash]]
**Thirteen people, including eleven [[Tourism in Peru|tourists]], are killed when a small aircraft crashes near the [[Nazca Lines]], [[Peru]], after departing [[Pisco, Peru|Pisco]], [[Department of Ica|Ica]]. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/sightseeing-plane-carrying-foreign-tourists-crashes-in-peru-all-13-on-board-killed-14035379.html (''Firstpost'')]
*[[2026 Broad Peak avalanche]]
**All ten climbers, including [[Nirmal Purja]], are confirmed deceased after an [[avalanche]] at [[Broad Peak]] in [[Pakistan]] on July 30. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/1/omani-legend-us-novice-pakistan-recovers-bodies-from-broad-peak (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 heat waves]]
**Protesters block parts of the main highway connecting [[Port Sudan]] and [[Khartoum]] in [[Suakin]] and [[Jubayt]] over severe power cuts amidst a heat wave reported by the {{ill|Sudan Meteorological Authority|de|Sudan Meteorological Authority}} in [[Red Sea State]], [[Sudan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316909 (''Sudan Tribune'')] 
<!-- Do not include heat waves simply because they happen, as happens everywhere. We need something news-worthy -->

'''International relations'''
*[[Morocco–Spain relations]]
**[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]]
***[[Morocco|Moroccan]] [[Royal Moroccan Armed Forces|security forces]] clash with hundreds of migrants as they attempt to storm the [[Spain|Spanish]] enclave of [[Melilla]]. Several Moroccan security personnel are reportedly injured while more than 50 migrants are detained. [https://en.yenisafak.com/world/morocco-melilla-border-clashes-resume-amid-migrant-surge-3721439 (Yeni Safak)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Twin Falls shooting]]
**Four people are killed, including the perpetrator, and seven others are injured in a [[Mass shootings in the United States|mass shooting]] at an [[In-N-Out Burger|In-N-Out]] restaurant in [[Twin Falls, Idaho|Twin Falls]], [[Idaho]], [[United States]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/08/01/us/idaho-shooter-twin-falls (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/us/three-dead-idaho-shopping-center-shooting-2026-08-02/ (Reuters)]
*[[Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war]]
**The [[Federal Bureau of Investigation|U.S. FBI]] opens an investigation after the [[U.S. state]] of [[Michigan]] reports a [[cyberattack]] on [[Water in Michigan|its water systems]], including whether [[Iran]] was behind the cyberattack, a day after [[Minnesota]] reported a [[2026 Minnesota water system cyberattack|similar breach]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/1/michigan-joins-minnesota-in-reporting-cyber-attacks-with-fbi-investigating (Al Jazeera)] [https://abcnews.com/US/wireStory/fbi-investigates-michigan-joins-minnesota-reporting-cyberattacks-water-135291463 (ABC News)]
*Four workers are killed in a [[Mass shootings in South Africa|mass shooting]] in [[Nyanga, Western Cape|Nyanga]], [[Western Cape]], [[South Africa]], while they were repairing a flat tyre. [https://witness.co.za/news/2026/08/02/four-killed-in-western-cape-mass-shooting/ (''The Witness'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[List of 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies|2030 FIFA World Cup controversies]]
**[[UEFA]] gives [[List of presidents of FIFA|FIFA president]] [[Gianni Infantino]] an ultimatum to resign or face an emergency [[no-confidence vote]] following Infantino's plan to sell stakes in [[FIFA Forward Enterprise]], which he has rescinded amidst backlash. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c04kr2nv3v3o (BBC Sport)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/01/uefa-demand-change-fifa-after-infantino-world-cup-sale-plan/?WT.mc_id=tmgoff_tw_post_infantino-world-cup-sale-plan/ (''The Telegraph'')]
<!-- All news items above this line -->}}

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=07|day=31|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****[[Iran]]'s [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] says that it struck two [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]]s trying to pass the [[Strait of Hormuz]] with aerial protection from the [[United States]], and forced four others to turn around. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/31/iran-strikes-tankers-us-escort-hormuz-strait-trump-gathers-cabinet (''The Guardian'')]
***Recent evidence by ''[[The New York Times]]'' show that a [[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran|U.S. strike]] yesterday on [[Qeshm Island]] hit a family home and killed three people. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/31/world/middleeast/us-iran-bomb-mk84-qeshm-island.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Israeli incursions in the West Bank during the Gaza war]], [[Israeli settler violence]]
****At least eleven [[Palestinians]], including four [[Children in the Israeli–Palestinian conflict|children]], are injured during a raid by [[Israeli settler]]s and [[IDF|soldiers]] in [[Nablus]] in the [[Israeli occupation of the West Bank|occupied]] [[West Bank]]. Israeli soldiers also detain at least ten people from [[Bethlehem]], Nablus, [[Salim, Nablus|Salim]], and [[Tell, Nablus|Tell]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/31/at-least-11-including-children-injured-in-israeli-raids-near-nablus (Al Jazeera)]
***[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
****The [[Israel Defense Forces]] (IDF) confirms that they have killed a [[Mujahideen Brigades]] militant who was involved in the [[Kidnapping of Avinatan Or|abduction]] of [[Avinatan Or]] and [[Noa Argamani]] during the [[Nova music festival massacre]], and directing the abduction of [[Sudthisak Rinthalak]] during the [[October 7 attacks]]. [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-904226 (''The Jerusalem Post'')] [https://www.timesofisrael.com/gaza-terrorist-who-kidnapped-noa-argamani-avinatan-or-on-oct-7-killed-in-strike-idf/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[Gaza peace plan]]
****[[Hamas]] says that they will disarm if [[Israel]] withdraws from and ends its military campaign in the [[Gaza Strip]] and if Israel and the U.S. honors the [[ceasefire]] agreement signed in October 2025. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/hamas-disarm-when-israel-keeps-its-word-gazas-weapons-stay-palestinian (Middle East Eye)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/07/31/hamas-disarm-trump-gaza-board-of-peace/c11f461a-8cd0-11f1-8912-d71e69d679d7_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
***The IDF says that killed two [[Hamas]] operatives accused of smuggling weapons into the Gaza Strip in separate strikes. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-two-hamas-operatives-killed-in-precise-aerial-strikes-on-wednesday/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Attacks in Russia during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***Two warehouses in [[Volgograd]] and [[Zelenodolsk, Republic of Tatarstan|Zelenodolsk]], [[Tatarstan]], are attacked and set on fire, causing damage estimated at US$1.5 billion, in the latest of a series of [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] [[Drone warfare|drone strikes]] targeting Russian [[online retail]]er [[Wildberries]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260731-wildberries-russia-s-amazon-targeted-by-ukraine (AFP via France 24)] [https://www.kyivpost.com/post/81431 (''Kyiv Post'')]
*[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
**A [[Migrant workers in India|migrant worker]] is fatally shot and another is injured by insurgents in [[Kulgam district]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], [[India]]. [https://indianexpress.com/article/india/kashmir-kulgam-terror-attack-migrant-worker-killed-10812586/ (''The Indian Express'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[Human Rights Watch]] reports that a [[Sukhoi Su-24]] [[airstrike]] by the [[Russia]]n [[paramilitary]] group [[Africa Corps (Russia)|Africa Corps]] in [[Mali]]'s [[Mopti Region|Mopti]] [[Regions of Mali|region]] killed eight civilians in June. [https://www.africanews.com/amp/2026/07/31/mali-hrw-accuses-russian-paramilitaries-of-killing-8-civilians/ (Africanews)] [https://apnews.com/article/mali-human-rights-watch-africa-corps-airstrike-895b085f097572630dd275d89da2b34f (AP)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**The [[Sudan News Agency]] reports that the Group 26 unit of the [[Rapid Support Forces]] paramilitary group has surrendered its personnel and military equipment to the [[Sudanese Armed Forces]]. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260731-rsf-unit-surrenders-to-sudanese-army-with-full-military-equipment/ (Middle East Monitor)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[AI boom]]
**[[South Korea]]'s [[KOSPI]] index rises by 18%, its largest single-day gain in history, amid a surge of investment in [[Artificial intelligence|AI]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/31/business/korea-stocks-chips-kospi.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*A bus en route to [[Algiers]], [[Algeria]], plunges into a deep [[ravine]] in [[El Kerma]] after skidding off the road, killing 25 people and injuring 44 others. [https://apnews.com/article/algeria-bus-crash-c8aa8bfdc69a0f071aa09b2c4259421d (AP)]
*Twelve people, including five children, are killed and 66 others are injured after a bus overturns on the [[N1 (South Africa)|N1]] highway near [[Trompsburg]], [[Free State (province)|Free State]], [[South Africa]]. [https://iol.co.za/news/crime-and-courts/2026-07-31-breaking-eleven-killed-including-five-children-as-bus-overturns-on-free-state-n1/ (IOL)]
*Two bodies and a body part are recovered after an [[avalanche]] on the [[Broad Peak]] in Pakistan buried ten climbers yesterday, including [[Nirmal Purja]], who remains missing. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/cjd42d4jvxkt (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*A [[cancer]] patient at the [[The Christie|Christie hospital]] in [[Manchester]], [[United Kingdom]], becomes the first to receive the ZI-MA4-1 therapy. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1w1py5e353o (BBC)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1w1py5e353o (''The Independent'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Morocco–Spain relations]]
**[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]]
***[[Ceuta]]n [[Mayor-President of Ceuta|mayor-president]] [[Juan Jesús Vivas]] says that around 60,000 [[Illegal immigration|undocumented migrants]] have entered the [[Spain|Spanish]] exclave in [[North Africa]] in the last 24 hours, as the death toll rises to 57. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/jul/31/cueta-spain-morocco-italy-migration-schengen-europe-latest-news-updates#top-of-blog (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cx2kp639yx4o (BBC News)]
***Videos on [[social media]] appear to show the [[Spanish Army]] deploying military vehicles towards [[Morocco–Spain border|the border]] with [[Morocco]]. [https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/spain-spanish-army-seen-moving-toward-ceuta-border-with-morocco/ (Reuters)]
***[[France|French]] [[Minister of the Interior (France)|interior minister]] [[Laurent Nuñez]] announces that he has ordered increased controls at [[France–Spain border|the border]] with Spain amid fears the thousands of migrants entering Ceuta could make their way to France. [https://www.politico.eu/article/ceuta-crisis-migration-france-spain-border-checks-schengen-unity-morocco/ (''Politico'')]
***[[Austria]]n [[Chancellor of Austria|chancellor]] [[Christian Stocker]] and [[Finland|Finnish]] [[Minister of the Interior (Finland)|interior minister]] [[Mari Rantanen]] join [[Italy|Italian]] [[Prime Minister of Italy|prime minister]] [[Giorgia Meloni]] in calling for Spain to be suspended from the [[Schengen Area]] in response to the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta over the last 24 hours.  [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/finland-austria-join-italys-call-for-schengen-border-closures-after-mass-migrant-arrivals-in-spains-ceuta/4015081 (AA)]
***Spanish authorities close the [[Melilla]] [[Border control|border crossing]] with Morocco after around 400 migrants stormed the [[border barrier]]. [[RTVE]] reports the sound of gunfire and explosions. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/spain-closes-melilla-border-crossing-with-morocco-after-mass-entry-attempt/4014629 (AA)]
***Italy suspends Schengen [[Freedom of movement|border-free]] travel with Spain, introducing [[Border control|checks]] on air and sea passengers and strengthening controls with France along the [[France–Italy border]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/italy-suspends-eu-schengen-free-travel-pact-with-spain-over-ceuta-crisis-2026-07-31/ (Reuters)]
***[[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|Spain's interior ministry]] says authorities have returned about 48,300 of roughly 50,000 migrants who entered Ceuta from Morocco. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/spain-ceuta-morocco-migrants-border-crossings/ (CBS News)]
*[[Belarus–Latvia relations]]
**[[Latvia]] announces the sudden closure of [[Belarus–Latvia border|its border]] with [[Belarus]], citing "technical reasons". [https://www.reuters.com/world/latvia-closes-border-with-belarus-interior-minister-says-2026-07-31/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Crime in Karachi]]
**[[Murder of Mir Raza Ali]]
***[[Pakistani]] entrepreneur and Wafflix founder Mir Raza Ali Khan is found shot dead in [[Karachi]], Pakistan, two days after he went missing. [[Law enforcement in Pakistan|Police]] launch a murder investigation into the case. [https://tribune.com.pk/story/2621007/kidnapped-man-found-murdered-in-jauhar (''The Express Tribune'')]
*[[2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings]]
**A [[Sri Lanka]]n [[Judiciary of Sri Lanka|court]] sentences former [[Sri Lanka Police|police]] [[Inspector General of Police (Sri Lanka)|chief]] [[Pujith Jayasundara]] to [[Capital punishment in Sri Lanka|death]] for [[negligence]] in failing to prevent the 2019 [[Easter]] bombings, which killed 279 people. Sri Lanka has not carried out an execution since 1976. [https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/2026/07/31/sri-lanka-sentences-ex-police-chief-to-death-over-2019-bombings#goog_rewarded (AFP via ''The Star'')]
*[[Indonesia]]n authorities announces it arrested a [[Malaysia Airlines]] pilot for allegedly [[drug trafficking|smuggling]] over {{cvt|26|kg|lbs}} of [[ecstasy (drug)|ecstasy]] and a package of [[methamphetamine]] into [[Jakarta]]'s [[Soekarno–Hatta International Airport]]. [https://apnews.com/article/indonesia-malaysia-airlines-pilot-arrest-drug-smuggling-51e9e268cee90563a4f52e7598e5d069 (AP)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2026 Bulgarian presidential election]]
**The [[Bulgaria]]n [[National Assembly (Bulgaria)|National Assembly]] sets 25 October as the date for the [[President of Bulgaria|presidential]] election. [https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-election-president-radev-yotova-october-01424a34100517745ed30d2c15ffc9a4 (AP)]

'''Sports'''
*[[List of 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies|2030 FIFA World Cup controversies]]
**[[Carlos Cordeiro]], senior [[FIFA]] executive and adviser to [[List of presidents of FIFA|FIFA president]] [[Gianni Infantino]], resigns in protest of Infantino's plans to sell stakes in [[FIFA Forward Enterprise]] to private investors, including American banking institution [[JPMorgan Chase]], calling them "a bad deal for FIFA's members, a bad deal for [[Association football|football]], and a bad deal for the long-term future of the game". [https://news.sky.com/story/gianni-infantinos-senior-adviser-carlos-cordeiro-quits-in-protest-at-fifa-chiefs-world-cup-plan-13568760 (Sky News)]
**The [[Asian Football Confederation]] joins [[UEFA]] in opposing Infantino's plans and vows to [[boycott]] the [[2030 FIFA World Cup|next tournament]] if they go ahead. [https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fifa-world-cup-sale-infantino-afc-uefa-concacaf-b3025187.html (''The Independent'')]
**Infantino reverses his plan to sell stakes in the [[FIFA World Cup]] amidst backlash. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49500782/fifa-world-cup-investment-private-gianni-infantino (ESPN)]
<!-- All news items above this line -->}}

parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=07|day=30|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[2025–2026 Iran–United States negotiations]]
****[[2026 Iran war ceasefire]], [[Pakistan in the 2026 Iran war]]
*****[[Pakistan]] [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Pakistan)|foreign ministry]] spokesman Tahir Andrabi reaffirms that talks between [[Iran]] and the [[United States]] are still ongoing despite [[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran|recent strikes]] by the [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. military]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/mediating-pakistan-insists-us-iran-talks-ongoing-despite-heavy-strikes/amp/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[2026 Iranian strikes on Arab countries]]
****[[2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan]]
*****[[Jordan]]ian [[air defense]]s shoot down five [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|missiles]] from [[Iran]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-us-hormuz-strait-july-30-2026-8dc77ed6a65f389ea4af84635d2473bd (AP)]
****[[Kuwait in the 2026 Iran war|2026 Iranian strikes on Kuwait]]
*****[[Kuwait]]i [[Government of Kuwait|authorities]] confirm that an Iranian attack targeted a building belonging to a [[China|Chinese]] company and killed one person. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/kuwait-says-iranian-strike-hit-chinese-company-building-killing-1/ (AFP via ''The Times of Israel'')] [https://kuwaittimes.com/article/47328/kuwait/kuwait-defense-ministry-iranian-attack-targets-chinese-company-building-killing-worker/amp (''Kuwait Times'')]
***[[Egypt in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[2026 Damietta drone strike]]
*****The [[Cabinet of Egypt|Egyptian cabinet]] confirms a drone has hit two vessels yesterday at a port in [[Damietta]], [[Egypt]], including the [[LNG storage tank|LNG storage]] [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]] ''Energos Winter''. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/egypt-confirms-drone-caused-fire-two-gas-vessels-damietta-2026-07-30/ (Reuters)]
***[[2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis]]
****Data shows that the [[QatarEnergy]]-controlled [[Liquefied natural gas|LNG]] [[gas carrier|tanker]] ''Al Areesh'' exited the [[Strait of Hormuz]], becoming the first LNG vessel from [[Qatar]] visible on ship-tracking data to do so since July 11, when ''Al Hamra'' exited the strait from [[Das Island]], [[United Arab Emirates]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/qatarenergy-controlled-lng-tanker-exits-hormuz-first-nearly-three-weeks-2026-07-30/ (Reuters)]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Gaza peace plan]]
****Mediators and [[Hamas]] reach an agreement to implement the second phase of a [[United States]]-backed [[ceasefire]] signed in October last year during a meeting in [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]]. [https://egyptian-gazette.com/egypt/egypt-hamas-palestinian-factions-accept-roadmap-for-second-phase-of-gaza-ceasefire/ (''Egyptian Gazette'')]
****[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] announces that the [[Board of Peace]] has reached a deal for a complete disarmament of [[Hamas]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cj03m512r4go (BBC News)] [https://jewishinsider.com/2026/07/trump-deal-hamas-disarmament-board-of-peace-idf-withdrawal/ (''Jewish Insider'')]
****Amidst reports of a new plan to disarm Hamas, [[Israel]] reaffirms that it will not withdraw from the [[Gaza Strip]], including the [[Yellow Line (Gaza)|Yellow Line]], until the militant organization is completely disarmed. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-904113 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
***The [[Gaza Health Ministry]] reports that four people, including [[Effect of the Gaza war on children in the Gaza Strip|children]], are killed in an Israeli strike in Gaza, in violation of the ongoing ceasefire. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/30/israeli-strikes-kill-at-least-four-including-children-across-gaza-strip (Al Jazeera)]
***The [[Israel Defense Forces|Israeli military]] claims it has killed two Hamas militants in separate strikes in the Gaza Strip, including a Nuseirat Battalion commander and a Hamas [[Platoon leader|platoon commander]], violating the ongoing ceasefire. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/idf-says-it-killed-hamas-sniper-oct-7-participant-in-separate-gaza-strikes-on-monday/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***[[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[Government of Saudi Arabia|government]] announces the establishment of the [[Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance]] with 14 countries signing the founding document in an effort to keep the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]] strait open. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/live-blog/live-blog-update/saudi-arabia-unveils-plans-multinational-maritime-defence-coalition (''Middle East Eye'')] [https://www.spa.gov.sa/en/N2644911 (Saudi Press Agency)]
***About 25 vessels cross the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]] strait according to data from [[MarineTraffic|Kpler]] shipping data. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/bab-el-mandeb-sees-25-commodity-vessels-transit-hormuz-traffic-stays-thin-2026-07-31/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russian attacks on civilians in the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***[[Russian Armed Forces|Russian forces]] launch hundreds of drones and missiles at [[Ukraine]], killing at least nine people and injuring more than 50 others, including six people killed in a [[ballistic missile]] strike on [[Kryvyi Rih]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/world/ukraine/russian-strikes-ukraine-kill-13-poland-scrambles-fighter-jets-rcna589964 (NBC News)] [https://www.fananews.com/language/en/6-killed-in-russian-attack-on-outskirts-of-ukraines-kryvyi-rih/ (Fana News)]
**[[2026 missile explosion in Poland]], [[Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Violations of non-combatant airspace during the Russo-Ukrainian war]]
***An armed Russian [[Kh-101|Kh-101 cruise missile]] enters [[Poland|Polish]] [[airspace]] around [[Lublin]], prompting [[NATO]] to scramble fighter jets in response. It later explodes in the countryside near [[Tarnawa-Kolonia]]. [https://kyivindependent.com/russian-kh-101-missile-fall-in-poland-during-mass-attack-on-ukraine-official-confirms/ (''The Kyiv Independent'')] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/30/nato-jets-scramble-as-russian-missile-detonates-in-poland (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.dw.com/en/poland-says-russian-ballistic-missile-violated-airspace/a-78172288 (DW)] [https://tvn24.pl/polska/rosyjska-rakieta-naruszyla-polska-przestrzen-powietrzna-opis-zdarzen-minuta-po-minucie-st9166879 (TVN24 <small>in Polish</small>)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[War crimes in the Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|War crimes during the Sudanese civil war]]
***The [[Associated Press]] reports that two former [[Child soldiers in Africa|child soldier]]s said they were trained by [[Colombia]]n mercenaries after being conscripted by the [[Rapid Support Forces]] (RSF) during the ongoing [[civil war]] in [[Sudan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/sudan-war-child-soldiers-colombia-mercenaries-uae-rsf-9730de7a24a28895b2c2c500e7c1fd6b (AP)] [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/07/30/sudan-war-child-soldiers-colombia-mercenaries-uae-rsf/65a1695a-8c29-11f1-8912-d71e69d679d7_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The [[Sudanese Air Force]] launches a series of [[airstrike|airstrikes]] against RSF mobilizations and military positions in the [[North Kordofan|north]] and [[West Kordofan|west]] [[Kordofan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316827 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**The death toll from yesterday's attack in the [[Hangu District, Pakistan|Hangu district]] of northwest [[Pakistan]] rises to at least eleven [[Law enforcement in Pakistan|police officers]]. [https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/deadly-overnight-raid-pakistani-police-post-leaves-11-135216651 (AP via ABC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[Intergovernmental Authority on Development]] [[trade bloc]] reopens its office in [[Khartoum]], Sudan, resuming operations for the first time since the start of the country's civil war in April 2023. [https://sudanhorizon.com/igad-secretary-general-inaugurates-mission-headquarters-in-khartoum-thursday/ (''Sudan Horizon'')] [https://sudantribune.com/article/316833 (''Sudan Tribune'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Kumamoto earthquake]]
**The casualty toll from the {{M|w|6.8}} earthquake in [[Kumamoto]] on [[Kyushu]], [[Japan]], earlier this week rises to 35 people killed and over 134 injured. [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/japans-earthquake-leaves-communities-thirsting-water-relief-heat-2026-07-30/ (Reuters)]
*[[2026 Quetta coal mine explosion]]
**At least 34 miners are killed and more are reported missing after a [[methane]] gas [[explosion]] at a coal mine near [[Quetta]], [[Balochistan, Pakistan|Balochistan]], [[Pakistan]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2652889/amp (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*At least nine people are killed and several others are trapped after an explosion at a four-story building in [[Bhiwandi]], [[Maharashtra]], India. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/loud-cracking-sounds-and-a-collapse-a-blow-by-blow-account-of-maharashtra-building-horror-death-toll-rescue-ops-101785475208435.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*Five people are critically injured and six are missing after a residential building collapses during a [[gas leak]] explosion in [[Messina]], [[Sicily]], [[Italy]]. [https://tg24.sky.it/cronaca/2026/07/30/messina-esplosione-pistunina (SkyNews24)]
*Ten climbers are reported missing, including Nepalese mountaineer [[Nirmal Purja]], after an [[avalanche]] on the [[Broad Peak]] in [[Pakistan]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2026/07/30/asia/climber-nirmal-purja-feared-missing-intl-hnk (CNN)] [https://indianexpress.com/article/world/nirmal-purja-climbers-missing-avalanche-broad-peak-10811321/ (''The Indian Express'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2026 Ebola epidemic]]
**The death toll from the [[Ebola]] epidemic in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] rises to over 1,500 people killed. [https://apnews.com/article/congo-ebola-death-toll-bundibugyo-virus-response-treatment-269eac4d8a93be912459486428ef2f94 (AP)]
**[[Singapore]]-based [[Hilleman Laboratories]] announces plans to advance an [[RVSV-ZEBOV vaccine|rVSV]]-based [[Ebola vaccine|vaccine]] against the [[Bundibugyo ebolavirus|Bundibugyo strain]] of Ebola into [[human trial]]s after [[World Health Organization]] experts identified it as the most promising candidate for the epidemic. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/singapore-ebola-vaccine-hilleman-laboratories-merck-bundibugyo-6288361 (AFP via CNA)]
*[[2026 United States cyclosporiasis outbreak]]
**The [[Michigan Department of Health and Human Services]] reports that the [[Michigan|U.S. state]] has surpassed 10,000 cases of [[cyclosporiasis]], which is caused by [[Cyclospora cayetanensis]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/detroit/news/michigan-cyclosporiasis-cases-193-hospital-cases-july-30/ (CBS News MI)]
*[[Nuclear power in Hungary]]
**The [[Paks Nuclear Power Plant|Paks nuclear power plant]] in [[Hungary]] shuts down for the first time in 44 years amid a drought across the country and extremely low [[Hydrology of Hungary|water levels]] on the [[Danube]] river. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cn0nqv05g0do (BBC News)] [https://www.dw.com/en/danube-water-levels-hungary-romania-cut-nuclear-output/a-78171891 (DW)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Morocco–Spain relations]]
**[[2026 Morocco–Spain border incident]]
***Thousands of [[undocumented immigrants]] cross into the [[Spain|Spanish]] [[Autonomous communities of Spain|autonomous city]] of [[Ceuta]] from [[Morocco–Spain border|neighboring]] [[Morocco]]. The city's [[Mayor-President of Ceuta|mayor-president]], [[Juan Jesús Vivas]], requests the [[Government of Spain|Spanish government]] to declare a [[state of emergency|national emergency]], but is refused by the [[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|interior ministry]]. [https://apnews.com/article/spain-ceuta-tarajal-morocco-migrants-5c864e5f951e2a7cf7a3eac417668e97 (AP)]
***Senior [[Italy|Italian]] politicians, including [[Prime Minister of Italy|prime minister]] [[Giorgia Meloni]], deputy prime minister [[Matteo Salvini]], and [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Italy)|foreign minister]] [[Antonio Tajani]], call for Spain to be kicked out of the [[Schengen Zone]] or the suspension of the [[Schengen Agreement]] entirely, citing the alleged threat of undocumented immigrants spreading throughout the [[European Union]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/migration-crisis-spain-italy-clash-over-schengen-morocco-cueta/ (''Politico EU'')]
*[[Chile–Venezuela relations]]
**[[Chile]] and [[Venezuela]] restore diplomatic relations after a two-year suspension following Chile's call for a review of the [[2024 Venezuelan presidential election]] results. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/07/31/world/chile-and-venezuela-restore-diplomatic-relations/2395619 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]
* [[International recognition of Abkhazia and South Ossetia]]
**[[Naoero]] announces it has withdrawn its recognition of [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]'s [[breakaway state]]s [[Abkhazia]] and [[South Ossetia]], terminating diplomatic relations with these entities "with immediate effect". [https://civil.ge/archives/746547 (Civil Georgia)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[President of Argentina|Argentine president]] [[Javier Milei]] issues a [[decree]] seeking [[Argentine National Congress|parliamentary]] approval to bar or expel foreigners accused of inciting [[Racism in Argentina|hatred]] against [[Argentina]] or [[Argentines|its people]], while exempting protected [[Politics of Argentina|political]], academic, and ideological expression. [https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/07/argentina-president-demands-expulsion-of-foreigners-expressing-hate-against-country/ (AFP via ''Vanguard'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Cyberwarfare during the 2026 Iran war]], [[2026 Minnesota water system cyberattack]]
**The [[Minnesota]] [[Minnesota IT Services|IT Services]] reports a [[cyberattack]] across 30 municipal community water systems across the state, with American authorities accusing [[Iran]] of being behind the [[cyberattack]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/30/us-authorities-probe-cyberattack-on-water-systems-in-minnesota (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/30/us/politics/minnesota-water-cyberattack-iran.html (''The New York Times'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIFA crisis]], [[List of 2030 FIFA World Cup controversies|2030 FIFA World Cup controversies]]
**In [[association football]], [[UEFA]] announces that it will [[boycott]] the [[2030 FIFA World Cup]], scheduled to be hosted by current champions [[Spain national football team|Spain]] along with [[Morocco]] and [[Portugal]], if [[List of presidents of FIFA|FIFA president]] [[Gianni Infantino]] proceeds with plans to sell off stakes in the [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] to private investors. [https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13568511/uefa-will-boycott-fifa-tournaments-if-gianni-infantino-continues-with-plans-to-sell-off-stake-in-world-cup (Sky Sports)]
*[[International sporting sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**In [[boxing]], [[World Boxing]] lifts all restrictions on [[Russia]]n athletes, allowing them to compete with their national symbols. [https://www.reuters.com/sports/world-boxing-lifts-all-restrictions-russians-2026-07-30/ (Reuters)]
**In [[ice hockey]], the [[International Ice Hockey Federation]] extends Russia's ban to the [[2027 Men's Ice Hockey World Championships]], and says that a decision will be made in November for the [[2027 Women's Ice Hockey World Championships]]. [https://www.espn.com/olympics/hockey/story/_/id/49491145/iihf-says-russia-4-world-tournaments-2027 (ESPN)]
<!-- All news items above this line -->}}

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 29
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=07|day=29|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Attacks on religious sites during the Israeli invasion of Gaza]]
****[[Israeli forces]] strike a [[mosque]] in [[Gaza City]] in violation of [[Gaza peace plan|the ongoing ceasefire]] and accuses [[Hamas]] of using it to store [[Palestinian domestic weapons production|weapons]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/29/world/israel-strikes-mosque-gaza-city.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)|Hezbollah–Israel conflict]]
***[[2026 Lebanon war]]
****Israeli forces accuse [[Hezbollah]] of launching a [[Drone warfare|drone attack]] on its forces in the [[Ali al-Taher]] ridge of [[southern Lebanon|southern]] [[Lebanon]], in violation of [[2026 Israel–Lebanon ceasefire|the ceasefire]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/2652721/amp (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
***Israeli forces also claim that their 401st Brigade Combat Team and [[Yahalom (IDF)|Yahalom Unit]] have destroyed an underground headquarters belonging to [[Hezbollah]], located near a [[United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon|UNIFIL]] post. [https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/430934 (''Israel National News'')] 
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***[[Saudi Arabia in the 2026 Iran war]], [[Iraq in the 2026 Iran war]]
****The [[Saudi Arabian Armed Forces]] and [[United States Central Command]] (U.S. CENTCOM) launch [[United States–Saudi strikes on Iraqi militias|strikes]] against [[Iran]]–backed militias in [[Iraq]] in response to [[Unmanned aerial vehicles in the Iranian military|Iranian drone]] attacks against [[Oil reserves in Saudi Arabia|oil facilities]] in [[Saudi Arabia]]'s [[Eastern Province, Saudi Arabia|Eastern Province]]. [https://www.iraqinews.com/iraq/us-saudi-forces-strike-iran-backed-militias-in-iraq/ (''Iraqi News'')] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/saudi-arabia-says-drones-launched-iraq-targeting-oil-facilities-intercepted-2026-07-28/ (Reuters)]
****The [[Popular Mobilization Forces]] reports that 20 militants have been killed in joint Saudi–U.S. strikes. [https://thedefensepost.com/2026/07/29/us-saudi-strikes-iraq-pmf-killed/amp/ (''The Defense Post'')]
****Several members of the [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] are also confirmed to have been killed in the Saudi–U.S. strikes in Iraq. [https://thenewregion.com/posts/6040 (''The New Region'')]
***[[Egypt in the 2026 Iran war]]
****[[2026 Damietta drone strike]]
*****A drone strike targets the [[LNG storage tank|LNG storage]] [[Tanker (ship)|tanker]] ''Energos Winter'', which is leased by the [[Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Company]], at the port of [[Damietta]], [[Egypt]]. Additionally, another vessel is also targeted. The group responsible for the strike is currently unknown. [https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/29/world/middleeast/ships-drone-strike-egypt.html?eafs_enabled=false (''The New York Times'')]
***[[July 2026 United States strikes against Iran]]
****The U.S. CENTCOM launches strikes against [[Iran]] in retaliation of a attempted [[2026 Iranian strikes on Jordan|attack]] by [[Iran]] against [[Jordan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/iran-war-us-hormuz-strait-july-29-2026-e31d249ba6443decdd3e63cd00f0fb84 (AP)]
****A senior officer in U.S. CENTCOM issues an internal email requesting troops to suggest "new creative and unconventional ways to pressure and punish Iran". [https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/03/politics/us-military-iran-war-troops-punish (CNN)]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***Data from Kpler shows that 39 commercial vessels have transited through the [[Bab el-Mandeb]] yesterday, the highest since July 19, while another five transited it today, including the [[Oil tanker#Size categories|VLCC]] ''Sophia'' and the [[Aframax]] tanker ''​Ocean Laureate''. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/ships-transiting-via-bab-el-mandeb-strait-highest-week-data-shows-2026-07-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***The ''[[Sudan Tribune]]'' reports that [[Rapid Support Forces]] militants retreating from [[Umm Sayala]], [[Jebrat al Sheikh District|Jabrat al-Sheikh]], and [[Barah, Sudan|Barah]] have launched retaliatory strikes in [[North Kordofan]]. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316794 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)|Somali Civil War]]
**Five [[Kenya Army|soldiers]] are killed in a [[shootout]] with [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] gunmen in [[Mandera County]], [[Kenya]]. [https://www.garoweonline.com/en/world/africa/five-kenyan-soldiers-killed-in-al-shabaab-attack-near-somalia-border (''Garowe Online'')]
*[[Terrorism in Pakistan]]
**Ten [[Law enforcement in Pakistan|police officers]] are killed in a drone attack and ambush in [[Hangu, Pakistan|Hangu]] district of northwest [[Pakistan]]. Pakistani authorities claim that 15 of the attackers were killed. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/islamist-militants-kill-10-police-officers-northwest-pakistan-say-police-2026-07-30/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Wildfires in 2026]]
**Two [[Hellenic Fire Service|firefighters]] are killed while battling a [[wildfire]] near [[Rethymno]], [[Crete]], [[Greece]], while a third dies near [[Gytheio]], [[Laconia]], during a separate operation. [https://www.malaymail.com/news/world/2026/07/30/three-firefighters-killed-as-gale-force-winds-fan-wildfires-across-greece/229501 (AFP via ''Malay Mail'')]
*A [[Bell 412]] helicopter crashes while on a fire-fighting training operation in [[San Juan, Argentina|San Juan]], [[Argentina]], killing all seven occupants. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/7-killed-in-helicopter-crash-in-argentina-officials-11840494 (AFP via NDTV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Kenya Wildlife Service]] says preliminary tests indicated [[Cyanide poisoning|cyanide-contaminated]] tomatoes may have killed 15 elephants near [[Amboseli National Park]] over the past month, warning that [[Agriculture in Kenya|livestock grazing]] in the area could also be exposed. [https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/07/30/world/americas-emea/kenya-says-15-elephants-died-of-cyanide-poisoning-after-eating-tomatoes-from-nearby-farms/2394577 (AFP via ''The Manila Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2026 Bolivian protests]]
**[[Bolivia]]n prosecutors issue an arrest warrant for former [[President of Bolivia|president]] [[Evo Morales]] for allegedly organizing protests and [[roadblock]]s across the country in May and June. The investigation follows complaints alleging [[armed uprising]] and [[Terrorism in Bolivia|terrorism]]. [https://www.firstpost.com/world/bolivian-prosecutors-issue-arrest-warrant-against-ex-leader-morales-over-protests-14034772.html (AFP via ''Firstpost'')]
* [[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**Russia's [[Federal Security Service]] ​issues an arrest warrant on [[Telegram]] founder [[Pavel Durov]] for facilitating terrorist activity, alleging that Telegram helps [[Ukraine]] plan attacks in Russia. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russias-fsb-charges-telegram-founder-durov-with-facilitating-terrorism-ifax-says-2026-07-29/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[China–Holy See relations]], [[Catholic Church in China]]
**[[Pope]] [[Leo XIV]] consecrates Fr. Francis Xavier Duan Yongkun as the [[coadjutor bishop]] of Bameng in the [[Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region]] under the 2018 provisional framework that cedes authority over its bishops to the [[Chinese government]]. [https://www.vaticannews.va/en/vatican-city/news/2026-07/china-ordination-coadjutor-bishop-bameng-mongolia.html (Vatican News)]
*The [[government of Nauru]] announces the official change of name of [[Nauru|the country]] from Nauru to Naoero. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/pacific/836342/nauru-officially-changes-name-to-naoero-after-thoughtful-deliberation-bypassing-referendum (RNZ)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2026 FIFA World Cup]]
**[[Argentina at the FIFA World Cup]]
***[[FIFA]] opens an investigation into the [[Argentina national football team]] over altercations during the [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] [[2026 FIFA World Cup final|final]] and the display of a banner of the [[Falkland Islands|Falklands]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7477708/2026/07/29/argentina-world-cup-final-investigation-fifa-scrap/ (''The Athletic'' via ''The New York Times'')]
<!-- All news items above this line -->}}

parse.title: Portal:Current events/2026 July 28
parse.wikitext:
{{Current events|year=2026|month=07|day=28|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Middle Eastern crisis (2023–present)|Middle Eastern crisis]]
**[[Gaza war]]
***[[Gaza peace plan]]
****A [[Hamas]] delegation visits [[Cairo]], [[Egypt]], to resume negotiations on the implementation of the next phase of its [[ceasefire]] with [[Israel]]. [https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-903922 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
**[[2026 Iran war]]
***The [[United States Central Command]] says that [[Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps]] forces have launched multiple [[Ballistic missile program of Iran|ballistic missiles]] from [[Iran]] in a "[[surprise attack]]" against [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. forces]] in the [[Middle East]], and that all missiles were successfully intercepted. [https://www.politico.com/news/2026/07/28/iran-attacks-u-s-forces-in-middle-east-01014440 (''Politico'')]
*[[Mali War]]
**[[2026 Mali offensives]]
***[[Malian Armed Forces]] launch strikes against two armed vehicles and [[Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin]] and [[Azawad Liberation Front]] militants in the [[Ségou Region]] near Dagabory as part of Operation Dougoukoloko. [https://apanews.net/mali-armed-forces-strike-armed-groups-near-dagabory/ (APA)]
*[[Sudanese civil war (2023–present)|Sudanese civil war]]
**[[Kordofan campaign (2023–present)|Kordofan campaign]]
***[[Human rights in Sudan|Human rights]] group Emergency Lawyers reports that recent [[airstrike]]s have targeted multiple locations in [[North Kordofan]], [[Sudan]], including a [[Water supply in Sudan|water station]] and civilian vehicles, killing dozens of civilians. [https://sudantribune.com/article/316727 (''Sudan Tribune'')]
**[[Sudanese refugee crisis]], [[Darfur campaign (2023–present)|Darfur campaign]]
***The [[United Nations]] reports that over 20,000 people have been [[Forced displacement|displaced]] [[Refugees and internally displaced people of Sudan|in]] Sudan's [[Darfur]] region over insecurity and violence. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20260729-insecurity-violence-force-20000-to-flee-from-sudans-darfur-un/ (Middle East Monitor)]

''' Arts and culture'''
*[[2026 Booker Prize]]
